project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A payload in a realm, with a state carrying version, strength, decay rate, confidence, access counts, a pin, a tier, a retrieval history, a status and an epistemic status

Storage backend.value: An append-only op log, one segment file per writer process, with in-RAM indexes and full snapshots; segments a certified snapshot covers are deleted

Retrieval strategy.value: A cortical sparse index assigning each memory 64 active features from a dictionary of 16,384 learned atoms, beside semantic HNSW, BM25, HDC, temporal, triplet, symbol-graph, PPR and association-spreading lanes

Write strategy.value: One Op appended to the writer's segment per mutation, hash-chained and CRC'd; state is rebuilt by replay or loaded from a snapshot

Update/delete model.value: Delete is an op and a deleted flag, compacted out of the next full snapshot; supersession, contradiction and archiving are statuses that veto the scored lanes while the payload stays

Scoping model.value: A realm string on every payload, an optional filter on the semantic, BM25, HDC and temporal lanes; None reads every realm and tag selection is global. ClearProject removes code-file and symbol entries, not memories

Agent integration.value: A Rust library with a C FFI, the backing store for the cc-soul daemon in a separate repository

Background processing.value: A maintenance thread that drains touches, checkpoints a full snapshot on a WAL budget and prunes covered segments; decay; an embedding backfill that dedups by cosine; a reconcile pass

Trust/provenance model.value: Statuses that veto on the scored lanes, an epistemic status that only weights, a claim-level contradiction detector served over FFI, a hash chain whose breaks are logged, and a lineage fence

Notable strengths.value: A status that excludes returns `None` rather than a small multiplier, so the scored lanes skip the candidate as control flow — a zero weight is a number a later stage can multiply back up, and an `Option` is not. How a memory was obtained is kept orthogonal to whether it is believed: `EpistemicStatus` produces a multiplier and can never veto. The contradiction detector is "claim-centric, not text-centric": "[t]wo memories contradict when they make incompatible claims under overlapping scope (same subject+predicate), not merely when they are semantically similar". The V3 segment header carries a vector-space id, and replay skips and archives segments written under a different embedding model, dimension or text format instead of returning wrong neighbours. A committed test asserts the three excluding statuses stay out of semantic recall beside an active memory that must come back

Main risks.value: The op log is a recovery log, not a history: every full snapshot, including the one the maintenance thread takes on a WAL budget, deletes the segments it covers, and nothing reads past ops except replay. A broken hash chain is logged as a warning and replay continues. The status veto holds on the scored lanes and not on temporal, HDC or artifact recall. The claim detector and its resolution run only when the FFI caller asks, and resolution returns ops for that caller to apply; the in-tree reconcile pass uses a six-word prefix heuristic. Valid time on triplets is the write clock. Realm is an optional filter. The status and epistemic multipliers are deserialised from scoring.json with no range check

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A node in a SQLite scene graph — type object, room or region, a canonical label over a label-mass distribution, a confidence, a centroid and bounding box in world metres, an EMA feature vector, `n_obs`, `t_first`, `t_last` and a parent — backed by the observation rows that fused into it

Storage backend.value: One `.smem` SQLite file in WAL mode with forward-only migrations: `observations`, `nodes`, `edges`, `node_obs`, `semantic_edges`, `node_properties`, `smem_events`; float32 BLOB features as the source of truth and an optional sqlite-vec `node_vec` index behind the `[vec]` extra

Retrieval strategy.value: A relation phrase plus a whole-word anchor label resolves by edge traversal; otherwise a regex intent router sends the query to recency order, a linear centroid-distance scan, cosine over node features when an encoder is configured, or a label-substring count; a prompt serialiser emits an indented region tree most-recent-first under a token budget that drops whole subtrees and says how many

Write strategy.value: `add_detections` inserts observation rows at once and stages them; `commit` runs the fusion arbiter per observation — candidates by dilated bbox overlap, score = 0.2 geometry + 0.2 IoU + 0.5 cosine + 0.1 label, merge at 0.62, reject below confidence 0.30, otherwise a new node — and every maintenance call fuses the staged rows first

Update/delete model.value: `update` rewrites label, position or confidence in place and resets the label distribution; `forget` hard-deletes a node and its links and leaves its observation rows unlinked; `decay` halves confidence per half-life and prunes below a floor; `resplit` and `consolidate` split and merge nodes; `merge` folds another store's objects in through fusion; nothing records that any of these happened

Scoping model.value: None on the read path. Observations carry an episode row with a `session` string that no query reads

Agent integration.value: A Python library with a six-tool function-calling layer that validates every model-supplied argument and strips control characters from labels, an `answer()` path over a bring-your-own verbalizer, a `PerceptionAdapter` protocol for RGB-D frames, a CLI that inspects a store and exports a read-only HTML viewer

Background processing.value: None. Decay, split, consolidate and relation inference run when the caller invokes them, each over the whole store

Trust/provenance model.value: A confidence float per node that fusion saturates upward and decay pulls down, used for pruning and for a hedging threshold the library documents and does not enforce; no state, no provenance beyond the observation trail

Notable strengths.value: A deterministic arbiter with a fuse-before-persist invariant tested against interleaved maintenance, so the file on disk never holds an observation that is not linked to a node; a tool layer that treats labels as an injection surface; an observation trail that answers where an object was over time

Main risks.value: A rejected observation persists as an orphan row that nothing reads and nothing keys on, so the same low-confidence sighting is re-scored from scratch every time; `forget` leaves the same orphans and no record; `update(label=)` erases the label history; `answer()` serialises the whole scene with no budget and no label sanitisation; and every retrieval is a linear scan over every node

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Two units. A fact row in chump_memory: content, timestamp, source, a confidence float, a verified integer, a sensitivity label, an optional expiry and a memory type. A lesson: a directive in chump_improvement_targets with a priority and an optional tool-domain scope, attached to a reflection that carries an outcome class

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file shared by the fact table with an FTS5 mirror kept by insert, delete and update triggers, an entity-triple graph, the reflection and lesson tables, episodes and causal lessons; embeddings in a positional JSON array beside it; a markdown wiki under a separate brain path

Retrieval strategy.value: Facts: FTS5 with an expiry filter, cosine over embeddings and an entity-graph rank fused by three-way reciprocal rank fusion, multiplied by confidence and freshness, then MMR to a 4,000-character budget. Lessons: frequency over recency, filtered by priority, seed tag, outcome-class quality and tool domain, injected first in the system prompt

Write strategy.value: The agent's memory tool stores a fact with a model-chosen confidence, type and expiry; an opt-in LLM summariser writes a semantic_fact with verified = 1 and expires the episodic rows it consumed. Lessons come from heuristic reflections after autonomy tasks, CI-failure capture and the orchestrator's per-dispatch writer

Update/delete model.value: Expiry, exact-content dedupe and confidence decay floored at 0.05 for unverified facts, all in an operator-run curate mode that nothing in the tree schedules. No forget verb on any surface; lessons are deleted only by an A/B-seed cleanup command, and graph triples and embeddings survive the deletion of their fact

Scoping model.value: No scope key on facts; isolation is one database file per repository root. Lessons carry a tool-domain scope with a universal NULL, and an empty domain returns every lesson. Episode search takes an optional repo argument the caller may omit

Agent integration.value: The built-in agent's memory, memory_brain and graph tools; an MCP server with memory_search, memory_recall, episode_save and episode_search for bring-your-own agents; a briefing command that hands lessons to dispatched agents; a duty-officer peer that reads and writes episodes from shell

Background processing.value: Curation runs only when an operator invokes chump --curate; reflections are written at task and dispatch completion; the duty-officer loop appends an episode per judgment tick

Trust/provenance model.value: A verified integer whose only writers are the two LLM summariser paths, a sensitivity label that is always 'internal' and never read, an outcome-class quality gate on lessons, a hash-chained tool-call ledger capped at 200 rows, per-faculty bypass flags, and a research-integrity directive binding on contributors

Notable strengths.value: Every cognitive faculty has an environment flag read in one place and wired at its single injection point, so each can be measured by its absence; CHUMP_BYPASS_SPAWN_LESSONS short-circuits load_spawn_lessons before any database work. The project ran that A/B, then asked a second question of the same faculties, whether the agent textually references the injected state, and found reference rates of 0 and 1 percent. Its directive prohibits the exit-code scorer, requires an A/A run per series and states the tolerance before a result may be cited, and EVAL-102 records in public why EVAL-101's null may not be cited. The lesson read path is pinned by tests that assert off-domain and failure-derived lessons stay out of the assembled block beside lessons that must appear

Main risks.value: The memory A/B is weaker than its label. The first EVAL-056 run scored exit code and output length while most trials failed on API connectivity, which the write-up says itself; the LLM-judge re-score at n=50 per cell had overlapping intervals and an A/A run of +0.200 against the plus-or-minus 0.03 the directive requires before citing. RESEARCH-022 applied a 5 percent threshold its preregistration states as 10. Embeddings are a positional array aligned with the live rows, and expiry, dedupe and summarisation remove rows without touching it, so semantic scores attach to the wrong facts after the first removal. The MCP search tools omit the expiry predicate. Thirty-nine of the 78 eval write-ups are private stubs

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A Markdown shard named type_slug.md with YAML title, description, type and updatedAt; types user, feedback, project and reference are curated, and digest holds Pi compaction summaries

Storage backend.value: One directory per scope key under the signed-in owner's data root: the shards, a derived MEMORY.md index, meta.json and an fts.db holding an FTS5 table rebuilt from the files on every open. Teammate scopes live in the teammate's Home under memories/

Retrieval strategy.value: MEMORY.md, listing every curated shard's title and description, is snapshotted into the prompt at session start. memory_search runs an FTS5 phrase MATCH ranked by bm25 plus a LIKE scan for CJK substrings; memory_read fetches a shard by filename

Write strategy.value: The model calls memory_write, memory_consolidate or memory_delete through the cindy_memory MCP server, or Pi's bot_memory facade in a teammate session; a nightly routine proposes teammate memory changes and admits a new one only on a verbatim user quote; Pi compaction writes digests; a person edits teammate memories in settings

Update/delete model.value: update overwrites the shard and bumps updatedAt; append concatenates; consolidate writes a target and unlinks the sources; delete unlinks the file and rebuilds the index. Settings and nightly edits are compare-and-swap on updatedAt. Nightly changes keep before and after for undo, for the last 30 runs

Scoping model.value: Physical: one directory and one fts.db per key, the key being the working directory with linked git worktrees folded to the main checkout, ssh:host:path for remote sessions, or bot:id for a teammate, all under a per-account root. The key comes from the host session context and never from a tool argument. session_search in the same server reads account-wide history for ordinary sessions

Agent integration.value: Built into the Cindy desktop host and its headless runner: an in-process MCP server with list_tools and call_tool over seven memory tools plus session_search, injected rules and index for Claude Code and Codex, a bot_memory tool for Pi teammates, and the harnesses' native auto-memory switched off while it is on

Background processing.value: A built-in nightly learning routine per teammate, default on at 03:30 local time, one auxiliary-model call over the owner conversations since its watermark; no background pass touches workdir memory

Trust/provenance model.value: None on a shard. Nightly creates need a quote found verbatim in a user message; nightly updates and deletes need only a reason. Skill drafts wait in a candidate list until they recur or a person promotes them

Notable strengths.value: A scope key derived by the host on every path, failing closed when the account is unknown; a derived index the model never edits; verbatim-quote admission for background memory writes; per-item undo that refuses to overwrite a later edit; an end-to-end test through the real MCP server

Main risks.value: Deletion is a hard unlink with no record outside the nightly path; the injected index has no hard cap; session_search crosses workdirs from an ordinary session; model writes through MCP carry no evidence; a per-reply review and a working-memory ledger stay in the tree with no caller

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A typed graph node keyed by node_id and one of four scopes (local, identity, environment, community), with a free attribute dict and a version; a user is the node user/ID, a channel channel/ID, an approved identity change an identity_amendment node beside agent/identity. Edges carry a relationship and a weight

Storage backend.value: The ciris-persist Rust engine through PyO3, on SQLite or Postgres: cirisgraph_nodes with primary key (node_id, scope) and cirisgraph_edges with no foreign key. No history table, no status, no expiry and no tenant column. Telemetry metrics are written into the same table as local-scope tsdb_data nodes

Retrieval strategy.value: Exact lookup by node_id and scope; a wildcard by scope and type; and search, which takes the newest rows of one scope by updated_at, up to the caller's limit (10 for the model's RECALL), and keeps those whose id or attribute JSON contains a query term. Edges to depth 2 on request. No ranking and no embeddings

Write strategy.value: Explicit: action selection chooses MEMORIZE and supplies a whole node; a second pass shows the model the graph conventions and existing nodes, conscience checks run, and the handler checks consent and managed user attributes before an upsert that merges attributes. The context builder also creates user nodes for anyone it sees

Update/delete model.value: An upsert merges the new attributes over the stored ones under optimistic concurrency on version; no prior version is kept. FORGET hard-deletes the row and its edges in that scope. Expired consent blocks new writes to that user's node and starts a decay record; nothing deletes the data

Scoping model.value: One store per agent. The four scopes are a type of memory, not a boundary between people: the model picks the scope on every read. Identity and environment writes and deletes need a verified approval. API OBSERVER users see only nodes whose created_by is theirs on three routes; the agent's own reads carry no user predicate

Agent integration.value: Ten action verbs chosen by the agent's decision pipeline, three of them memory (MEMORIZE, RECALL, FORGET); a system snapshot injected into every thought with the identity, user profiles and channel; a FastAPI surface for memory, deferrals and consent; Discord, CLI and API adapters

Background processing.value: TSDB consolidation every 6 hours, weekly and monthly, summarising telemetry and pruning summaries; dream and solitude states that run consolidation thoughts. Nothing re-reads or rewrites stored memory content

Trust/provenance model.value: None on memory rows. Identity-scope writes are refused until a person with the AUTHORITY role resolves a deferral and the approval verifies; the approved change is stored as an amendment carrying the approver's id. Secrets in attributes are detected and replaced with references before storage

Notable strengths.value: Identity changes decided in code before any model judges the approval, with one approval per amendment where the node signs it; a signed hash chain over every agent action; secrets encapsulated before write; extensive design rationale in the code for each guard

Main risks.value: The model's RECALL search sees only the 10 most recently updated nodes in a scope, which telemetry floods; naming a user pulls their profile and messages from other channels into the thought; the approved amendment text is written by the model after approval; expiry and DSAR deletion delete nothing; admin API writes are unaudited

Memory unit.value: A fact — entity, predicate, object (text, number or another entity), with valid time, transaction time, retraction, confidence, scope, source and a JSON locator; an object pointing at an entity makes the fact an edge

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file, one binary, no server: facts, entities, aliases, predicates, an FTS5 index and a vec0 table partitioned on scope

Retrieval strategy.value: Four channels — words, names, a graph walk and kinship — with a semantic channel over a static potion-base-8M embedding; every mode carries the same temporal predicate

Write strategy.value: `brain remember --subject --predicate --value --at --until --source`, a batch file, an MCP `remember` tool, and harness hooks that record what a session did from the transcript

Update/delete model.value: A new value closes the old one rather than overwriting it; a correction at the same instant retracts instead, and the write returns which of the four happened

Scoping model.value: `scope` is a column and a vec0 partition key, but the query carries it as an optional argument that defaults to none, so nothing separates namespaces unless the caller asks

Agent integration.value: A CLI, an MCP server, a loopback studio UI, and installable hooks for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Cline, OpenCode and others

Background processing.value: Session hooks that capture what a session did; `brain lint` scans for structurally unreachable facts and `brain repair` acts on it as a separate decision

Trust/provenance model.value: Retraction as never-true, separated from expiry; declared aliases resolve writes and learned ones deliberately do not; a linter that reports what retrieval cannot reach

Notable strengths.value: Two things. First, the single read arm: `for_when` builds one temporal predicate for every mode and `Now` is literally `AsOf(now)`, so "the two cannot drift apart because there is only one arm" — the structural answer to a store whose current-value path works while its as-of path quietly does not. Second, `brain lint`, which reports "[w]hat the brain can see wrong with itself": findings are structural defects where "the fact is stored, it is true, and retrieval still cannot use it", the case that motivated it is named ("a brain where 59 out of 69 `is_a` facts had a string where an entity belonged. Every voucher knew its class and no voucher was reachable from it"), and finding it had required "opening a 3D scene and noticing loose dots". A memory system that can detect its own unreachable contents and does not report them "is failing at its job, so this module exists to make that a command instead of an observation." The alias split is a third: declared aliases resolve where a write lands and learned ones never do, because "they are guesses made from watching questions, and a guess must never decide where a fact is stored" — enforced "by this `WHERE` clause and by nothing else, so it is load-bearing", which is the comment a future reader needs

Main risks.value: Scope is the gap. It is stored on the fact and used as a vec0 partition key, but the read path takes it as `Option<String>` defaulting to `None`, so a caller that forgets it searches everything; the exclusion form is a post-filter on the semantic channel, since a partition key "indexes equality and cannot express an exclusion", which the project documents and tests but which means that channel trims after ranking. There is no mutation audit beyond the fact table itself, and the retraction reason is appended into `source` by string concatenation — `source = COALESCE(source, '') || ' [retracted: ' || ?2 || ']'` — so the field naming who asserted a claim also carries why it was withdrawn, and neither can be parsed back out reliably. And nothing is keyed on a rejected value: `live_facts` excludes retracted rows precisely so that they "must not influence where a new fact lands", so re-asserting a retracted value produces a fresh `created` fact with no sign that the brain once rejected it

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A memory item with a kind, a project, a scope id, a visibility, a session and timestamps — decisions, dead ends and repository-specific traps

Storage backend.value: Local SQLite with FTS5 and `sqlite-vec`, plus optional peer-to-peer replication of selected scopes

Retrieval strategy.value: BM25 lexical and vector semantic search merged and re-ranked, injected automatically into every prompt, with memories already in context not repeated

Write strategy.value: An observer processes sessions through the configured model provider; the README notes this "can incur costs or consume plan usage"

Update/delete model.value: Not the subject of this reading; the epistemic work is in attribution rather than supersession

Scoping model.value: A replication-scope gate every read path enables, with caller filters intersecting it and the disabling flag typed out of the semantic-search context

Agent integration.value: Plugins for OpenCode 1 and 2, Claude Code and Codex hooks, an MCP server, and a viewer server

Background processing.value: Observer processing, peer-to-peer sync, a coordinator for teams, and a retrieval ledger

Trust/provenance model.value: A retrieval ledger of attempts and exposures, an outcome-evidence store, and an attribution layer that separates observational from causal claims

Notable strengths.value: Two gates, both enforced in the type system rather than by convention. The read boundary: every memory read path passes `enforceScopeVisibility: true`, caller scope filters intersect rather than widen, and the context a semantic caller builds has the flag *removed from its type* — `Omit<OwnershipFilterContext, "enforceScopeVisibility">` — so the path most likely to forget it cannot express forgetting. Beside it, one catalog defines every tool-exposed filter key, pinned to the MCP schemas by "an exact parity test", because otherwise "a filter added here [could] be silently omitted from either surface, so exclusion filters can never fail open and return broader results than the client requested" — naming the failure direction, which is what makes the tripwire worth having. The attribution layer is the other reason to read this: retrieval attempts and exposures are ledgered, outcomes carry evidence, and an assessment is labelled helpful, irrelevant, stale, harmful or unknown on one of seven bases — with a claim type of observational or causal, and a gate refusing the second unless the basis is a randomized contrast whose witnesses are retention-pinned and carry both `experiment.cells_complete` and `experiment.uncertainty_reported`. "[C]ausal claims require a linked preregistered randomized contrast with complete retained cells and uncertainty" is a sentence almost nothing in this corpus is in a position to enforce

Main risks.value: That attribution layer is not wired to anything yet, and the file says so: "[t]hese pre-writer validation gates define initial v1 semantics. Once production writers are enabled, semantic rule changes require a contract version bump." `recordAttributionAssessment` has no caller outside its own module, so the contract and its 5,052 lines of tests exist ahead of the writers that would populate it — honest, and it means a reader should not take the taxonomy as describing what the product currently records. The impact label is likewise diagnostic: a `harmful` assessment is counted in a diagnostics view and filters nothing, so nothing withholds a memory that was judged harmful. Retrieval itself has no epistemic state — no status, no provenance class, no supersession found on the read path. And the surface is large for what it does: 375,155 lines of TypeScript across a dozen packages, with a coordinator, enrollment reconciliation, peer-to-peer replication and a viewer server around a local memory store, and eight unpinned dependency surfaces at this pin

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Two kinds. A note is a markdown file with frontmatter carrying an OKF status, a confidence level, a verified list, an optional task_id, an optional reason and verification block, and a type. A task memory is an entry inside a per-user markdown file, headed by a timestamp and a collision-checked 4-char base36 id

Storage backend.value: Files under a repowiki root behind a KnowledgeStore facade, written by temp-file replace under sidecar locks and staged into git on every write; an SQLite analysis cache holds the search index

Retrieval strategy.value: BM25 over notes, wiki pages and raw sources with an authority multiplier folding note type, OKF status, confidence level and source, plus wikilink hops and progressive reading modes; deprecated notes and, by default, shadow notes are dropped and drafts are labelled; task memories have their own per-task BM25 search that skips superseded entries

Write strategy.value: Notes enter as draft through ingest_note or distillation and reach stable through confirm_note, or are ingested as stable with a required free-text reason; task memories are written directly by add_task_memory, which rejects a near-duplicate of a recent live entry

Update/delete model.value: confirm_note, reject_note, batch_set_status and adjudicate_conflict rewrite a note's status in its frontmatter. Supersession inserts a dated marker line naming the successor into a task-memory entry. Compaction moves originals to a per-user archive file and rewrites the live file. delete_task removes the task directory, archives included

Scoping model.value: An optional task_id filter on the default note query and a repo filter for centralized layouts, both caller-supplied; task memories are addressed by task_id and split into per-user files, with other users' files loaded as a summary plus two recent entries

Agent integration.value: 53 MCP tools over an IDE-driven flow, a CLI, SessionStart and SessionEnd hooks, and a web view; the model is the IDE's own, and the installed server updates itself from PyPI in a detached child unless disabled

Background processing.value: No daemon. A SessionEnd hook captures the transcript in a detached subprocess; distillation, consolidation, compaction, lint and telemetry aggregation are tools the agent calls, with compaction handed to an async subagent when the hot layer crosses its threshold

Trust/provenance model.value: An OKF status of draft, stable or deprecated, where deprecated is dropped and draft is labelled; a confidence level of strong, weak or shadow that weights ranking and drops shadow by default; and a trust tier of unverified, machine-confirmed or human-reviewed derived from a self-declared verified.by prefix, attached to results and read by nothing

Notable strengths.value: Three answers to an uncertain claim on one read path: dropped, labelled, or weighted. A supersession marker written into the entry itself, naming the date and the successor. A telemetry chain that reaches past retrieval to whether the work succeeded, and feeds the last five failures into the prompt that writes the next note. A dedup recall exempted from authority weighting so a confidence migration cannot blind it

Main risks.value: Every retirement is keyed on a record: distillation dedup, the conflict search and the task-memory write check all skip retired material, so re-extracting a rejected claim produces a fresh draft. Every lifecycle verb, including confirm and adjudicate, is on the agent's own tool surface, and ingest_note writes stable directly given any reason. Other users' warm-layer entries are loaded without the superseded filter. The telemetry stream is rewritten on every hit. The outcome verdict is self-reported. The installed server pip-installs minor releases from PyPI on its own

Memory unit.value: A point in a fixed 8D manifold — an id, a permanent position projected from its embedding, a mass derived from confidence and affect, and a temperature that cools on a Lorentzian curve; beliefs and memories share the same space

Storage backend.value: JSON belief files beside a pluggable backend (JSONL, SQLite or ChromaDB), with the manifold`s positions and gravity anchors saved and reloaded as engine state

Memory unit.value: An entity — observation, rule, knowledge, or a derived code symbol — stored as a markdown file with YAML frontmatter and mirrored into a SQLite row

Storage backend.value: Markdown files under .cogz/ as the record, optionally committed for a team, with one local SQLite database per repository as a projection carrying FTS5 and a vector extension

Retrieval strategy.value: Hybrid full-text and vector search with graph expansion and git co-change terms, status-filtered before the KNN cut, assembled into a token-budgeted context pack

Write strategy.value: An agent calls create_entity, or a person edits the markdown; MCP writes run title and embedding dedup, a rejected-match pass and NLI contradiction checking after the file is synced

Update/delete model.value: Status moves through a five-value lattice checked on every update of an existing row; reject is a CLI command and an MCP tool; pruned tombstones blank content and are hard-deleted past a retention count

Scoping model.value: The repository directory. There is no tenant, project or user key on an entity; separation is one database per checkout

Agent integration.value: A Rust binary with nineteen CLI subcommands, an MCP server over stdio offering fifteen tools, and hooks configured for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and Copilot

Background processing.value: Session-end consolidation promotes supported observations to rules and merges duplicates; every index recomputes knowledge drift against referenced code; a 30-day telemetry sweep deletes old events at session end

Trust/provenance model.value: A validated status lattice on the update path, a rejected-match warning to the writer, drift annotations against code hashes, delivery hit and miss instrumentation, and a secret scanner at the write and sync boundaries

Notable strengths.value: The status vocabulary is a state machine that the update path honours: `transition_status` fixes the legal moves with a typed `IllegalTransition`, and every sync of an existing row, hand-edited file included, goes through `update_entity_preserving_status`, which refuses an illegal move before the row changes. A file claiming `pruned` while carrying text is refused as a minted tombstone. Rejection has a producer on both surfaces and a consumer at write time: `check_rejected_match` compares a new entity's title and embedding against up to 100 rejected rows of its type and returns the prior verdict and its `rejected_reason`. Every retrieval surface filters the status, the KNN filter runs before the cut so stale rows do not take slots, and `respects_status_filter` pins the behaviour with a positive control. Knowledge carries `verified_against` hashes of the code it describes, and orphaned anchors demote it to stale automatically

Main risks.value: The lattice is checked against the projection, not the record. `cogz reset` deletes the database and `cogz index` inserts every file as a creation, so a status hand-edited from rejected back to active is refused at sync and accepted after a rebuild. The rejected-match pass runs after the new entity is written and synced as active, reaches only the writing agent, and is never stored; once doctor prunes a rejected observation its title is blanked and the match cannot fire. The event table is telemetry rather than an audit: `sweep_old_telemetry` deletes every event older than 30 days at each session end, pruning strips `old_content` from payloads, and the cascade nulls `entity_id`. The agent holds `reject_entity` and `verify_knowledge`, the second clearing the stale review queue, and no event records which actor did either

Memory unit.value: Two things, kept apart. A ledger event — sequence, project, event type, subject kind and id, actor kind and id, an optional cause kind and id, a timestamp, a note, JSONB annotations, and a pointer to a payload — and a semantic record, keyed `(project_id, record_id)` with a `record_role`, a turn id and sequence, and a Cardbox reference. The content itself is in neither: both point at a `cardbox_project_id`/`cardbox_id` pair

Storage backend.value: PostgreSQL, with the schema created in `infra/postgres.py` — agents, credentials, turns, spawn envelopes, semantic records, the kernel ledger and its scope index. Payloads live in CG-Cardbox, which is a git submodule of this repository and is not checked in with it, so the store this kernel indexes is not in this tree

Retrieval strategy.value: No search arm at all — no embedding, no vector column, no full-text index, no `ilike`. Reading is by identity and by sequence: fetch a subject, or page a project feed after a ledger sequence, or read a scope's events through `cg_ledger_scope_index`. That is the right shape for a ledger and it means the kernel offers nothing that resembles recall by meaning

Write strategy.value: Agents act through an HTTP API versioned `v3r1`, authenticated per agent with credentials whose status is `active` or `revoked`. A turn produces semantic records and ledger events; a `ClaimToken` and a `ConflictError` in the contracts give optimistic concurrency, and unique constraints enforce one provision-launch record per turn. Ledger writes are inserts, never updates

Update/delete model.value: Nothing in the tree updates or deletes a ledger row. Semantic records are keyed to a turn and a sequence and carry a `record_role`, so a correction is a later record rather than an edit. Agent credentials are revoked by status rather than removed. What is missing is any statement about the payloads: deletion, retention and correction of the content live in Cardbox, which is not here

Scoping model.value: `project_id` from a request header, applied as a predicate on every repository read and built into the composite primary keys and foreign keys, so a row cannot reference a parent in another project. Beside it a `cg_ledger_scope_index` on `(project_id, scope_kind, scope_id, ledger_seq)` gives a second scope dimension over the ledger

Agent integration.value: An HTTP API at `/v3r1`, a CLI with project, agent, feed and provisioning subcommands, an SDK, an agent client and a projection client, plus adapters and an Integrations directory. Agents are registered into a project with a provenance record and issued credentials

Background processing.value: None in this repository. Projections are read models a client pulls rather than a worker that maintains them, and there is no consolidation, decay or summarisation pass — which is consistent with a kernel that stores facts and leaves interpretation to its participants

Trust/provenance model.value: Structural rather than epistemic. The ledger records an actor and a cause for every event, credentials carry an `active`/`revoked` status, registration carries a provenance kind and reference, and a test asserts creator authority does not leak into the kernel snapshot or public metadata. No memory record carries a confidence, a verification state or a validity interval

Notable strengths.value: An append-only ledger whose rows name the actor and the cause, not just the subject — an audit that answers *why* as well as *what*; a project key that is a composite primary key rather than a filter someone must remember, so a cross-project reference is impossible at the schema level; a deliberate refusal to offer search, leaving recall by meaning to participants; a test asserting that the authority which created a project does not appear in the kernel's own snapshot

Main risks.value: The payload store is a submodule this repository does not contain, so what the ledger references — and every question about retention, correction and deletion of content — is outside the tree that was read; there is no retrieval by meaning, so a participant needing recall must build it; no memory record carries a trust state or a validity interval; twenty commits from February to May 2026 and nothing since, against a `v3r1-preview` label, so this is an early cut of an ambitious design rather than a settled one

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A dated block in `contexts/memory/OBSERVATIONS.md` holding lines marked 🔴 High, 🟡 Medium or 🟢 Low, under a `Date: YYYY-MM-DD` header. Above it, a promoted rule: an axiom file with `id`, `category`, `created` and `updated` frontmatter, or a skill, or a section of one of the four rule files. Below it, `contexts/daily_records`, `survey_sessions` and `thought_review`

Storage backend.value: Markdown files in a git checkout, plus an embedding index the search tool builds beside them — `embeddings.npy`, `chunks.pkl` and a `manifest.json` under a lock file. No database and no service; `rules/`, `contexts/`, `periodic_jobs/`, `adhoc_jobs/` and `tools/` are the whole store

Retrieval strategy.value: Two paths and a routing table. `AGENTS.md` is the root index an agent reads at session start, pointing at `rules/WORKSPACE.md` for directory routing. `tools/semantic_search` builds a forward index of chunks and embeddings and queries it. `OBSERVATIONS.md` opens with an instruction not to load itself whole — *"不要全文加载这个文件"* — and to retrieve on demand instead

Write strategy.value: An L1 observer runs on a schedule: an 84-line Python trigger hands a prompt to an OpenCode agent, which scans the workspace for the day's changes, filters them, and appends a dated block to `OBSERVATIONS.md` under the three priority marks. The prompt carries the idempotency rule — read the file first, and if a block for that date exists, change nothing — and instructs the agent to append with `>>` or `tee -a` rather than rewriting a large file

Update/delete model.value: An L2 reflector runs weekly on the same trigger pattern: read the 🔴 and high 🟡 entries, promote the generalisable ones into `rules/` by responsibility boundary, then *"rewrite OBSERVATIONS.md, deleting promoted and expired 🟢 records."* The promotion threshold is stated in the prompt as prose — cross-project generality, repeated verification, a clear applicable scenario — and the garbage collection is a rewrite, so the observation that produced a rule does not survive its own promotion

Scoping model.value: None. One workspace, one owner, one observation file. `rules/WORKSPACE.md` is a routing index over directories rather than a boundary, and nothing in the tree partitions memory by project, user or agent

Agent integration.value: Designed for a coding agent opened on the directory — Claude Code, OpenCode or Cursor — with `AGENTS.md` as the session-start routing table. Scheduled work runs through cron against an OpenCode client; `docs/SKILL_ECOSYSTEM.md` lists separately installable skill repositories so this one stays light

Background processing.value: The heartbeat is the system: a daily observer, a weekly reflector, and further scheduled jobs for a newsletter, a crontab monitor and an AI-news survey. Consolidation is not a background pass over a database — it is an agent rewriting Markdown on a timer

Trust/provenance model.value: Three priority marks assigned by the observing agent at write time, defined by retention rather than by truth: 🔴 is kept permanently and is a promotion candidate, 🟡 is expected to matter for weeks, 🟢 is *"定期垃圾回收"* — garbage-collected periodically. Nothing filters recall on them, and nothing records that a claim was wrong

Notable strengths.value: A promotion ladder with a stated threshold rather than an implicit one; an idempotency rule written into the prompt that performs the write; an instruction in the memory file itself telling a reader not to load it whole; a real embedding index with a lock and a manifest rather than a re-embed on every query; a published system whose author reports running it for a year, offered as a blueprint rather than as a product

Main risks.value: Consolidation deletes its own evidence — the reflector rewrites the observation log without the entries it promoted, and a promoted axiom carries no pointer back to what produced it; the priority marks are retention classes an LLM assigns, so nothing distinguishes a claim that was wrong from one that stopped mattering; every trigger script ships with `/path/to/your/workspace` and `<your-model-id>` placeholders, so nothing in the tree runs as committed; there is no licence file at all, which leaves the whole repository all-rights-reserved by default

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A typed entry in one of three stores — a *decision* (`summary`, `problem`, `why_chosen`, alternatives, tags, scope), a *pipeline* (`name`, `purpose`, ordered steps) or a *constraint* (`rule`, `reason`, `hardness`) — each with an id, a `status`, an `origin`, a `scope`, tags, `related_to` links, and verification and creation timestamps. Entries are human-editable JSON under `.context/` in the project directory

Storage backend.value: Plain JSON files per type under `.context/`, with zero runtime dependencies. `export_snapshot` writes the whole store to a committable `.context-keeper/memory.json.gz` so a team shares memory through git; `import_snapshot` reads it back non-destructively and auto-runs when the store is empty. An optional remote store is reachable through `mirror`, which pulls newest-wins or backfills local to remote. `DECISIONS.md` is a derived read-only projection

Retrieval strategy.value: Two paths, deliberately different. `get_context` ranks by tag and text overlap with a scope boost, recency, status and origin weighting, pulls `related_to` links, and fills a 4,000-token budget, reporting `budget_truncated` when it cannot. `query_entries` applies exact predicates — status, origin, hardness, tags any/all, scope, `superseded_by`, `supersedes`, date bounds, free text — with no ranking at all. An opt-in local embedder adds a calibrated cosine arm blended into the relevance signal

Write strategy.value: `record_entry` over MCP, dispatched by `kind`, with per-kind fields validated server-side before anything is stored: a decision needs `summary` ≥ 5, `problem` ≥ 40 and `why_chosen` ≥ 60 characters, a pipeline `name` ≥ 3 and `purpose` ≥ 40 plus at least one step, a constraint `rule` ≥ 5 and `reason` ≥ 40. A short entry is rejected, not warned about, and `update_entry` re-checks the same floors. At capture the server looks for high-overlap live entries and labels each pair `likely_contradiction` or `likely_restatement` for the caller to resolve

Update/delete model.value: `update_entry` edits in place under the same length floors. Recording an entry that names a predecessor flips the predecessor's status to `superseded`, which demotes it out of default recall while leaving it queryable. `deprecate_entry` requires a reason and can fold a duplicate into a survivor with `merge_into`. `prune_stale` reports entries not verified within a threshold rather than deleting them, and `code_drift` counts commits touching an entry's scope since it was last verified and flags a scope whose file has been deleted as `orphaned_scope`

Scoping model.value: One `scope` string per entry, and one implementation of what it means. `scope_rules.py` decides coverage for every surface: a scope whose last component contains a dot is a file scope matching a path tail exactly; anything else is a directory scope matching whole consecutive components with at least one component after them; `global`, `all`, `*` and empty are domain scopes that cover no path at all. `query_entries` filters on exact equality; the ranking path uses coverage as a boost; the pre-edit hook uses it to decide which constraints to inject

Agent integration.value: An MCP server with fourteen tools, installed as a Claude Code plugin or an `.mcpb` bundle. Seven hooks: `session_start` and `subagent_start` seed context, `scope_guard` runs on PreToolUse before every Edit and Write to inject the constraints covering the target file, `constraint_reinject` re-surfaces rules mid-session, `pre_compact` calls `verify_quality` and `post_compact` produces a compaction report, and `commit_capture_reminder` prompts for capture. With `rules_export` on, constraints are written into the harness's own `.claude/rules/` surface

Background processing.value: No daemon. Hooks fire on session start, subagent start, pre-tool-use, and around compaction. `prune_stale`, `verify_quality`, `code_drift` and `mirror` are tools a person or an agent invokes. Nothing rewrites the store on a schedule

Trust/provenance model.value: `status` gates the project summary and the constraints file, and the write path, though `get_context` excludes only deprecated entries; `origin` records whether a user, an agent or an import wrote it and an unknown value is coerced to `agent`; `hardness` grades a constraint. `get_context` annotates a response with `no_confident_match` and `top_relevance` when the top entry's tag-and-text overlap falls below a 0.20 floor — chosen as the highest value with zero false abstentions on the eval set — while still returning the results. Capture-time conflict labelling separates a restatement from a contradiction

Notable strengths.value: A schema that refuses a thin memory instead of storing it; two read paths with honestly different contracts, one ranked and one exact; one shared implementation of scope semantics with the four-way disagreement that motivated it written into the module docstring; an abstention signal calibrated against a committed eval rather than guessed; zero runtime dependencies, which is load-bearing because the scope hook runs before every edit; paired absence-and-presence assertions in the retrieval tests

Main risks.value: The capture-time conflict check skips every entry whose status is `deprecated` or `superseded`, so a rule that was retired can be recorded again with no warning that it was ever rejected; no append-only record of mutations exists anywhere, so an entry edited in place leaves no trace of what it said before; no validity time, so a constraint true only for a past release cannot say so; the abstention floor annotates but never withholds, so a confabulated answer is still returned and a caller that ignores the flag is unprotected; the mirror resolves conflicts newest-wins with no merge surface

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Whatever the user declares: rows, graph edges and vectors under one MVCC transaction in a single file. The schema, and therefore the memory model, belongs to the system built on top

Storage backend.value: An embedded single-file database in a single process, with relational storage, bounded graph traversal and vector similarity unified under MVCC snapshot isolation

Retrieval strategy.value: PostgreSQL-compatible SQL, pgvector's `<=>` for vector distance, and SQL/PGQ-style `GRAPH_TABLE ... MATCH` for bounded traversal — described as the subset that matters rather than the full standard — all against one snapshot

Write strategy.value: Transactional writes validated against whatever the table declares: a state machine, a DAG constraint, a cascade. Remote changesets arrive through the same validation

Update/delete model.value: MVCC delete markers keyed on a row id and the deleting transaction — the storage meaning of tombstone, not an epistemic one. What deletion means for a memory is the caller's decision

Scoping model.value: None of its own: each agent, device or service runs its own instance and they reconcile through a server, so separation is per-instance rather than a key inside one store

Agent integration.value: A Rust library and CLI, with bidirectional sync between instances over WebSocket through a central server; Python and TypeScript bindings are named as roadmap rather than shipped

Background processing.value: Sync reconciliation applying changesets under a per-table conflict policy and returning applied, skipped and conflicting rows

Trust/provenance model.value: None held. What it offers is enforcement: a table may declare a state machine and the engine validates every update against it, including updates arriving from another instance

Notable strengths.value: A declared lifecycle enforced in the engine holds for every writer rather than for the writers that remembered, and the two relational backends answer the transition question through one shared method; conflict resolution is chosen per table, which is the right granularity when facts and statuses want different merge rules; and a merge that would break an invariant is skipped with the conflict returned and the rest of the batch applied

Main risks.value: It holds no memories of its own, so the six epistemic marks are all the caller's to earn and none of those decisions are made here; the tombstones are MVCC row markers and read as something stronger to anyone grepping for the word; MVCC supplies transaction ordering with no world-validity axis, so an as-of question must be built from user columns; and the language bindings a memory system would likely want are roadmap rather than shipped

Background processing.value: Managed git hooks that background their own invocation, run git with optional locks disabled and a sub-second timeout, and fail open on any error

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A turn: `session_id`, `turn_idx`, `ts`, `role` and a `text` synthesized from the JSONL message content — assistant prose, `[tool:<name>] <description>` for a tool call, and `[result] …` truncated at five hundred characters for a tool result, all concatenated into one field. Above it a session: `id`, `project`, `ai_title`, `cwd`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `turn_count`, `file_path`, `file_mtime`, `indexed_at` and a `source` of `code` or `chat`

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file at `data/continuity.db` in WAL mode: `sessions`, `turns`, a contentless `turns_fts` FTS5 mirror kept current by insert and delete triggers, a `turn_vecs` sqlite-vec table of 384-dimension MiniLM vectors, and an `edges` table of `TEMPORAL` and `SIMILAR_TO` pairs. Nothing is stored that the JSONL transcripts do not already hold

Retrieval strategy.value: Three arms over the same rows. `search_sessions` is FTS5 with a highlighted snippet, ordered by `rank`. `find_similar` is a sqlite-vec KNN over-fetching three times the limit and re-ranking by `0.7 × cosine + 0.2 × linear recency over 365 days + 0.1 × session turn count capped at fifty`, printing all three components on every result. `thread_recall` seeds from FTS5 and walks `TEMPORAL` edges outward in both directions to a hop and turn cap, returning the surrounding conversation grouped by session with the seeds marked

Write strategy.value: Nobody writes memories. `index.py` walks `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` and `chat_index.py` reads an Anthropic data export; both skip a session whose recorded mtime matches the file. The MCP server carries a `reindex` tool holding its own inline copy of the same walk. `embed.py`, `wire_edges.py` and `wire_similar.py` are separate passes a person runs

Update/delete model.value: The transcripts are the source of truth and the index is rebuilt from them: a changed session is deleted from `sessions` and `turns` and re-read whole, and `wire_edges` and `wire_similar` clear their own edge type before rewiring. There is no correction verb, no supersession and no forgetting — and no cleanup of `turn_vecs`, whose rows are keyed on the `turns` autoincrement id that a re-index discards

Scoping model.value: `project` and `source` are stored on every session and offered as optional arguments to `search_sessions` and `recent_sessions` — the project one as a `LIKE '%…%'` substring the caller supplies. Nothing is applied by default, and `find_similar` and `thread_recall` accept neither, so the semantic and graph arms answer across every project on the machine

Agent integration.value: A stdio MCP server exposing eight tools, four CLI scripts, and four Claude Code hooks: a PreCompact checkpoint writer, a SessionStart injector, a Stop-hook checkpointer, and an SSE proxy the user points `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at so it can watch token usage and ring bells at seventy, eighty-five and ninety-five per cent

Background processing.value: None inside the store. The three build passes and both drift checks are commands a person runs; the only always-on component is the optional local proxy. No consolidation, no decay, no summarisation

Trust/provenance model.value: None. A search of the tree for `status`, `confidence`, `verified`, `superseded`, `rejected` or `tombstone` returns one hit, and it is `resp.status` in the HTTP proxy. Recency is a ranking term, not a state. The nearest thing to a provenance distinction is the embedding filter, which skips any turn whose synthesized text starts with `[tool:` or `[result]` — a string-prefix test on generated text, applied to the semantic arm only, while FTS5 indexes tool calls and truncated tool results like anything else

Notable strengths.value: Two read-only consistency checks between a derived index and its source, which is two more than most: `drift_check.py` mirrors the indexer's skip logic exactly to report which sessions are new or stale without writing anything, and `fts_integrity_check` runs FTS5's own check with `fts_rebuild` beside it. `find_similar` prints the three components of its hybrid score on every row, so the ordering is inspectable. The SessionStart hook injects nothing after `/clear`, honouring a deliberate erasure

Main risks.value: No tests at all — no `assert`, no test function, no suite. No redaction of any kind, so every credential pasted into a session is in the FTS index and, above thirty characters, in the vector table. The compaction checkpoint is one file at a fixed path with no session key, and the injector checks its age and never its `Session:` line, so a second session compacting within three hours is handed the first one's state. `edges` is created twice with different schemas and `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, so its shape depends on which script ran first. `turn_vecs` has no delete path while re-indexing changes the ids it points at. Memory unit.value: A memory with a kind, content type, retention tier, scope, project, source, dedupe key, confidence, importance, lifecycle status, an ACL, a provenance document, an observed time, a valid-from and valid-until pair and a supersession link

Storage backend.value: Local SQLite in WAL mode with a full-text index over memories, a separate candidate staging table, and consolidation job and control tables; documents and chunks with embeddings sit beside them

Retrieval strategy.value: BM25 over the memory FTS index with a fallback OR query, gated in SQL on active status, the validity window against the wall clock, project, kind, content type, retention tier, scope, the owner bit and the ACL, then re-scored with importance, confidence and recency

Write strategy.value: Three doors: an explicit remember on MCP, HTTP and CLI that writes canonical memory directly; observations staged as expiring candidates; and consolidation, which promotes a candidate under a versioned policy or an approval boolean

Update/delete model.value: A correction writes a new row carrying `supersedes_id` and marks the target superseded with its content kept; forget marks a row retracted, blanks its content and provenance and removes it from the FTS index

Scoping model.value: A scope column with an owner-only `owner-global` value, a project, and a per-row ACL normalised to the project label when empty, matched in SQL against labels taken from the authenticated credential

Agent integration.value: A Tauri desktop app, an MCP stdio server, a loopback or explicitly secured HTTP API, and a local-owner CLI

Background processing.value: No standing memory worker. Consolidation runs per call from MCP, HTTP or the CLI and records a job row under a control table with a pause switch, and an owner's HTTP call spawns one recovery pass over queued jobs; candidate expiry runs on every candidate operation; device sync exchanges bundles through a compacted journal

Trust/provenance model.value: A lifecycle status filtered on every recall, an ACL validated in SQL, credentials that fix a principal's labels, candidate rate limits and expiries, an automatic-retention gate that policy JSON cannot set, and a posture that starts query-only

Notable strengths.value: The recall statement is the artifact to read. It gates on the active status, on the validity window, on project, kind, content type, retention tier and scope, and on the principal's admin bit before owner-global rows are reachable. Before it matches the access list it checks the list's shape with json_valid, json_type='array' and no element whose type is not text, so a corrupted or wrongly typed ACL matches nothing instead of reaching the empty-means-unrestricted branch. The writer closes that branch from the other side by substituting the project label for an empty list. The product posture matches: a new installation starts query-only, and source authorisation, ingestion, model use, shared-agent access and memory writes are separate decisions. Committed tests assert that another principal, a forgotten row and a superseded row stay out of recall, each beside a case that returns something

Main risks.value: The validity window opens at the write clock: the only product writer binds `valid_from`, `observed_at` and `created_at` to one `now`, and `valid_until` is a working-memory expiry, a 365-day retention ceiling or the supersession time, so nothing records when a fact became true. Review is advisory: the MCP consolidate tool takes an `explicit_approval` boolean from the agent, and the agent's own `remember` tool writes canonical memory without the queue. A rejected candidate blocks only a re-offer by the same principal under the same dedupe key. `confidence` and `importance` rank rather than withhold, and `provenance_json` gates nothing. The surface is broad for a personal store, with one auto-run surface and three unpinned dependency surfaces at this pin

Trust/provenance model.value: Supersession as a view rather than a delete, retrieval inspectability, no model in the retrieval loop, and a CI gate over the documentation's own numbers

Notable strengths.value: The documentation gate is the thing to take away. `scripts/check_doc_claims.py` compares "every advertised count against the one place that owns it" and runs "at the point where the drift is introduced (every push and pull request), not at release time" — so a README number that stops matching the repository fails the build rather than ageing quietly. Its exemption mechanism is better still: a line that states a number meaning something other than the advertised total declares `[not-a-count-claim: <label>]`, and "[t]he declared set is a registry: it is printed on every successful run and pinned by a test naming each member, so an exemption is added deliberately or not at all". An escape hatch that is enumerated, printed and test-pinned is the difference between a gate and a suggestion. The product framing is equally concrete: "[n]o LLM in the retrieval loop, and nothing leaves localhost unless you configure an integration that does", one stdio server with the same fifty-four tools across hosts and per-host differences "stated there, not discovered after install", and a headline that promises accountability rather than intelligence — "[k]eep decisions, fixes and project context between sessions, and inspect what was retrieved"

Main risks.value: The wiki's draft queue looks like a human-review gate and is not one: `wiki_curate` evaluates pending drafts through `evaluate_draft`, described as pure logic, and the compile step publishes "every draft currently in status='approved'" — so a model-synthesised draft, carrying the `synth_prompt` and `synth_model` that produced it, is promoted by an automated evaluation rather than by a person, and `reviewed_at` records when that happened rather than who. Scope is the other gap: a team-scope backfill exists in the schema module and no scope predicate was traced on either recall path, so what separates one project's memories from another's was not established here. `confidence` on a draft is a continuous default of 0.5, so an unset value is indistinguishable from a considered middle. And the surface is large — 274,911 lines, fifty-four tools, a wiki subsystem, a homeostatic fold log, Swift alongside Python — with eleven auto-run surfaces and four build-time execution points at this pin, which is what a multi-host MCP bundle with installers looks like

Update/delete model.value: mem9: LLM-chosen UPDATE overwrites by id, DELETE removes the point; the MCP delete tool and HTTP route take any id. Knowledge: hard delete, an archive status, an invalidate route that stamps invalidated_at, and fix lineage that archives the parent. No tombstone

Trust/provenance model.value: None as a state. Knowledge status is active or archived and search does not read it; a derived deprecated flag from fallback rate hides a document from the session brief only

Storage backend.value: PostgreSQL with pgvector HNSW across 46 tables; a deliberately narrower SQLite core

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Typed cognitive records: goal, epic, task, hypothesis, decision, evidence, conclusion, plus operational runbooks and cognitive triggers. Each carries a state enum and a Traceability record with a caller-supplied author and created and updated times

Storage backend.value: A .ctx directory of indented JSON files beside the project: one working-context file holding every goal, task, hypothesis, decision, evidence item and conclusion; one file per commit, runbook, trigger, packet and run

Retrieval strategy.value: No search. A context packet takes up to three goals by priority and six tasks, then follows id links to hypotheses ordered by confidence, decisions, evidence and conclusions, each capped; runbooks are scored by task, goal and trigger substring match. A goal or task id that matches nothing falls back to the top goals

Write strategy.value: Explicit CLI or MCP verbs, synchronous, under a process and file lock. Hypotheses are born Proposed; decisions and conclusions take any state the caller passes; evidence is always stamped Validated. A heuristic bootstrap reads documents and writes a goal, task, hypotheses and evidence without a model call

Update/delete model.value: Update in place by id, with state changes, merge and supersede verbs. No delete verb for any record. Commits snapshot the whole working context with a diff against the previous commit. Branch merge takes the incoming copy of every entity

Scoping model.value: Physical: one .ctx directory per project. The MCP server is pinned to one repository unless started with an allowed root. Commits carry a branch name that the log filters on; the working context holds one branch at a time

Agent integration.value: CLI, a stdio MCP server that is read-only unless started with --mode write, an ACP-style JSON-RPC agent that is read-only, a local web viewer, and prompt files that teach the agent the loop

Background processing.value: None. Commits are cut by the agent or a person; runs call OpenAI or Anthropic only when invoked

Trust/provenance model.value: State enums are rendered into the packet as labels and used by planning, audit and next-work filters; the packet itself filters no hypothesis, decision, evidence or conclusion by state. Runbooks are filtered to Active

Notable strengths.value: A typed reasoning model with explicit hypothesis, decision and conclusion states; commits that store a full snapshot and an entity diff; a consistency audit that names missing evidence and open hypotheses on closed tasks; atomic temp-file writes under a process and file lock; read-only MCP by default

Main risks.value: Superseded hypotheses reach the packet under their old state label; merge overwrites divergent entities with the incoming copy after reporting them, and its equality test is reference-based on lists; bootstrap_map reads any file path, bypassing the repository guard, in read-only mode; documented states silently become defaults

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Three kinds, one per vault type. A document chunk with its file path and caller metadata; a skill, one markdown file with a name and a description; an episode, one statement with entities, a source, a confidence, a salience, a metadata object, a valid window and a recorded window

Storage backend.value: One directory per vault, registered in a JSON file in the project or the home directory. A semantic vault holds the files and a Chroma collection; a skill vault holds markdown files and a JSON index; an episodic vault holds one SQLite file in WAL mode with episodes, entities, attestations and disputes

Retrieval strategy.value: Semantic: the query is embedded and Chroma returns the nearest chunks by cosine distance, five by default. Skill: list, then read by name. Episodic: SQL filters on entity, source, confidence and both time axes, at most 5,000 rows newest first, then scored in Python by similarity or word overlap, recency of valid_from, salience, or a sum of the three

Write strategy.value: The caller's explicit call through the CLI, HTTP, MCP or Python. A document is written to disk and its chunks upserted; a skill is written as a file and added to the index; an episode is inserted with a new id. No extraction, no deduplication, no model on the write path except the local embedder

Update/delete model.value: Episodes are never deleted: invalidate closes one, supersede closes one and opens a linked successor, revise restates one without moving its valid window. Documents are overwritten in place and deleted with their chunks. The only removal of an episode is purging the whole vault directory

Scoping model.value: The vault is the boundary: separate stores, a restricted flag and an agent allowlist checked by the HTTP routes, the MCP tools and the Python client. Identity is a request header over HTTP and a launch argument for MCP. Nothing scopes rows inside a vault

Agent integration.value: A Typer CLI, a FastAPI app, a stdio MCP server with 17 tools, an in-process Python client and a read-only browser viewer with an HTML export. Nothing is injected into a prompt; the agent calls a tool

Background processing.value: None. No scheduler, no consolidation, no decay job; the recency score is computed at query time

Trust/provenance model.value: A confidence float with a minimum filter, a count of re-assertions kept as dated rows, and a dispute pair that flags both statements and withholds neither. The source field is free text and the MCP server fills it with the agent name when the model leaves it out

Notable strengths.value: Two time axes that move independently and are both queryable; a revision kept distinct from a supersession; closing an episode before its own start is refused; a newer schema version is refused instead of misread; the MCP agent identity is fixed at launch; the viewer is refused off loopback

Main risks.value: Timestamps are unparsed strings compared as text; a revision erases a dispute from past belief states and can duplicate it; overwriting a document leaves the old trailing chunks in the index; no single episode can be removed; the 5,000-row scan is newest first, so relevance never sees older rows; skills written by one agent are returned to another as instructions

Trust/provenance model.value: None stored. Frontmatter is a name and a description, and a captioning failure writes empty sections while the command still reports success

Main risks.value: The delete tool passes an unvalidated model-supplied name to a recursive delete and the server grants every permission by default; a captioning failure is silent and produces a skill indistinguishable from a good one at rest; a demonstration recorded against a hostile screen becomes durable instruction text

Memory unit.value: Three layers in one memory.json: an L0 profile of five string fields, an L1 recent state of three fields, and L2 episodes (content, trigger text, optional source quote, status, weight, evidence ids). Storage backend.value: JSON files in the Electron userData directory: memory.json (whole-file rewrite), rag-data/memory-store.json for vectors (atomic, debounced), chat-social-atoms.json, entity-graph.json and an append-only memory-trace.log

Retrieval strategy.value: L2: the user_memory tool runs hybrid vector plus BM25 with an optional cross-encoder rerank over an allowlist of recallable episodes. Voice calls and proactive messages inject up to four L2 by DMAE activation from keyword and recall hits. L0 and L1 are injected whole every turn. Social atoms: BM25 with a 30-day half-life, top five

Write strategy.value: Background: every sixth turn an LLM judge reads the last eight turns and emits candidates filtered for overclaim; L0 requires explicit and user_explicit. Also a write_memory tool, a reflection pass every 20 turns that rewrites L0 and L1, and compression of similar L2 into summaries

Update/delete model.value: L0 and L1 overwrite in place. L2 changes status (active, aging, archived, superseded, merged) and is never deleted outside a compression rollback; Obsidian edits overwrite L2 content. No tombstone

Scoping model.value: None on the L0/L1/L2 store: one global profile and episode set shared by the desktop app and every channel, QQ groups included. Social atoms carry conversationId and are filtered on it

Agent integration.value: Electron desktop app with Live2D; tools user_memory, read_memory, write_memory and recall_history in the agent harness; a memory panel for L0 and L1 edits; a two-way Obsidian vault sync for L2 content

Background processing.value: A serial LLM queue: judge every 6 turns, one conflict resolution every 5 turns with a 60-second floor, reflection and compression every 20, weight decay every 50; vector reconciliation at startup

Trust/provenance model.value: Social atoms: active versus superseded or resolved, filtered on every read. L2: status filtered on vector recall, not on DMAE injection; a conflict marker is shown as a warning suffix. No human review state

Notable strengths.value: Verbatim evidence-quote check and role gating on social atoms, applied all-or-nothing per batch; L2 recall reads status from the canonical store rather than a copy in the index; a compression transaction with explicit rollback; startup reconciliation between store and vector index with backups; conservative judge prompt with a post-filter on absolute terms

Main risks.value: The write_memory tool and the reflection pass both write L0 past the judge's explicit-user gate; superseded and merged L2 reach call and proactive prompts; decay archives episodes recalled one to ten times and never touches unrecalled ones; channel senders write the desktop user's profile; the judge's turn buffer mixes conversations; memory.json is rewritten non-atomically every turn

Memory unit.value: Trust-classed checkpoint item: open question, decision, belief, uncertainty

Storage backend.value: Per-project JSON checkpoints plus a disposable SQLite FTS5 index

Retrieval strategy.value: Automatic session-start injection; FTS5/BM25 for `recall`, ranked by importance x decay, with contradiction and supersession as tiers applied before the weighting on both read paths — demotion keys and never filters; a forgotten value and a human-confirmed quarantine are judged out before a row is indexed and again on every hit

Scoping model.value: Per-project bucket on every unaddressed read, each latest-read naming a route and an admit rule; cross-project reads by explicit slug, all_projects, a host-declared allowlist, or a ruling layer — an ancestor directory outside every git working tree whose own bucket claims it by name, read-only and never written from below. Background processing.value: A pre-action hook runs a human-armed ruling check before a matching shell action, fail-open under a five-second budget, and logs every firing; a check armed at a ruling layer re-arms in every repository below it on a machine that never synced the layer directly; detached serialize child, retry ledger with self-heal and a serial heal of every healable session under one machine-wide lock, index rebuild

Trust/provenance model.value: Typed provenance on conversational input — client surface and input source, so automation is distinguishable from a person — and nothing at all on a note

Notable strengths.value: An event-sourced conversation store with replay and sequence heads, typed input provenance, a crash-recoverable deletion journal, and a consolidation module whose docstring states its own missing oracle

Main risks.value: The consolidation pass may delete any note on LLM judgement, with a note count as the only mechanical signal, over a store that has no history, no protected notes and no record that a deletion happened
