Memory unit.value: A `Session` — an id, the harness that wrote it, a project, a path, a title, start and update times, and its `Message` list of role, text and time — read from a transcript the agent had already written. The index adds derived fields the parsers never set: `GaveUp`, `Words`, `Touched`, `AgentTitle`, and for a synced session `OrigID`, `From`, `Lifecycle`, `LifecycleNote` and `LifecycleAt`. Beside the sessions, `notes.jsonl` holds remembered facts and promoted notes

Storage backend.value: Its own append-only index over the transcript files already on disk, under `internal/index`, with a digest, an optional embedding rerank and per-source parsers for each supported harness. Nothing is copied into a database the user has to run; the corpus is the history, and the index is a derived artefact that can be rebuilt

Retrieval strategy.value: BM25 over the index with CJK and NFC folding, a freshness decay, and narrowing options for harness, project, session id and time. MCP recall ranks the working directory's project first and then the rest of the machine. A session whose own text reports backing an approach out takes a ranking penalty rather than an exclusion. Notes promoted from a session are lifted above their source in the result order

Write strategy.value: No write path for sessions — the agent's own transcript is the write, and `deja` indexes it. Secrets are stripped during indexing by `internal/redact` before anything is stored. An agent or a person can store a fact with `remember`, and a person can promote a session to a note carrying a lifecycle state

Update/delete model.value: Re-indexing rebuilds from the transcripts. `deja forget` removes sessions and writes their `harness:id` keys to two tombstone files every rebuild filters against, and rewrites `notes.jsonl` to drop their promoted notes. A promoted note's `Lifecycle` — `accepted`, `rejected`, `superseded` or `stale` — is set by a person and synced between machines

Scoping model.value: A default, not a boundary. The session-start and per-prompt hooks draw only from the working directory's project names, widened by `DEJA_RECALL=aggressive`. MCP recall ranks that project first and appends the rest of the machine; CLI search is the whole store unless `--project` is given. Project filters match by substring, an unknown session id answers nothing, and a trust policy can withhold imported memory per surface

Agent integration.value: Hooks into each supported agent — recall arrives at session start, on every prompt, before a file is edited or a command runs, and after a command fails — plus one MCP tool with eight modes, a CLI, and a plugin manifest. `deja install --auto` wires the harnesses it finds

Background processing.value: Indexing and re-indexing; a digest cache per project for the session-start hook; a novelty tracker that sits a served session out for the next ten injections in that agent session and in that project; peer sync between machines

Trust/provenance model.value: A promoted note's `Lifecycle` is a recorded state: a session marked `rejected`, `superseded` or `stale` is never offered as the decision before an edit or a command, while recall returns it labelled *"this was tried and rejected"* and demoted. `GaveUp` is derived from a session's own words; search applies a score penalty and prints a note, and the decision lines refuse it

Notable strengths.value: A corpus that starts full rather than empty, because the transcripts were already written; redaction on the indexing path so what reaches a model has been stripped before it is stored; a vacuity guard written as its own named test with the reasoning in a comment; a recorded state that keeps a reverted decision on record and out of the answer; benchmark runs committed as JSON with a test that fails when the prose drifts from them; code comments that cite the issue each decision came from

Main risks.value: No boundary on the pull path — MCP recall reaches every project on the machine, so a session private to one project can answer a question asked in another; a wrong conclusion nobody marked is retrievable forever with only a freshness decay and a give-up penalty against it; the index is derived from files the tool does not own, so a harness changing its transcript format is a parser problem rather than a migration; the committed benchmark runs record a date and no commit, so nothing ties a figure to the search code at the pin

Memory unit.value: A markdown document at a path with publisher metadata (tags, importance, type, typed rel- relations), each surviving version linked to its predecessor by a previous-hash, and a separate archive state

Update/delete model.value: Correction by publishing a new version. ARCHIVE withholds a document from current reads and an empty-body PUBLISH restores it. A retention metadata key on any write deletes all but the newest N versions; the graph export publishes with a default of 20 and federation checkpoints with 5

Scoping model.value: Capability tokens with path globs and operations; a path no read token covers is public. The memory broker maps each verified identity to one world and refuses any other; the knowledge profile exposes every readable world. The local plugin mints a publish and archive token over the whole store and no read token

Agent integration.value: Plugins for Claude Code, Cowork, Cursor, OpenCode and pi; an MCP server and an OAuth memory broker for hosted clients; a CLI, a TUI and a WATCH change stream

Background processing.value: Knowledge-server compaction of the commit log into checkpoints, catalog rebuild at startup, broker world provisioning, and federation export of graph checkpoints

Trust/provenance model.value: The hash chain and its verdict on VERSIONS, token hashes with expiry, a publish policy with warn, ask and block, a content check that always blocks secrets, the archive state, and user and agent identity keys the writing surface stamps and a caller cannot set

Notable strengths.value: Integrity reported on the history read rather than assumed; a token store that holds only hashes; read authorization applied per row before LOOKUP truncates and per entry before LIST pages, so a protected document neither appears nor displaces a readable one; an archive state that the catalog, listings, fetch and the session primer all honour; a tenant gate that refuses an unclassified tool before provisioning a world

Main risks.value: Retention is publisher metadata: any writer, the agent's own mark_publish included, can delete all but the newest versions, and VerifyChain starts at the oldest surviving version, so a pruned history reports chain-valid true, which the conformance suite asserts; the deletion is recorded only as a server log line. In the file store a head whose body is edited with its frontmatter kept also passes, and FETCH never runs the check. Reads are public on any path no read token covers, which by default is every path on a local soul. There is no validity window and no record of a rejected value

Memory unit.value: An atom — a chunk of conversation with a type, a confidence, a corroboration count, a domain and category, a source chunk, and an expiry with its reason — plus entities and relationships carrying first-seen, last-seen and evidence counts

Storage backend.value: SQLite with a `vec0` virtual table for embeddings and an FTS5 index for the lexical arm, degrading to ANN-only when the SQLite build lacks FTS5

Retrieval strategy.value: Hybrid BM25 and vector search over atoms with the expiry predicate bound, plus an entity-relationship graph walk and spreading activation across domains

Write strategy.value: Conversations are broken into atoms with confidence scoring and domain tagging; entities and relationships are extracted alongside; contradictions between an older and a newer atom are detected and queued rather than applied

Update/delete model.value: An atom is expired with a reason rather than deleted, and reads compare the expiry against today's date. A contradiction never auto-invalidates: it becomes a pending conflict a person resolves or dismisses, with the resolution and its timestamp stored

Scoping model.value: Per-conversation container isolation at the runtime level; the memory database itself carries a domain and category on an atom rather than an enforced scope predicate

Agent integration.value: Messaging connectors, a TUI, containerised per-conversation agents, and a credential proxy that keeps API keys out of the container

Background processing.value: An evolution loop that scores its own responses, generates self-critiques and rewrites the system prompt, plus periodic compression into weekly and monthly digests

Trust/provenance model.value: A confidence and a corroboration count on an atom, an expiry with a stated reason that the read path honours against the clock, and a pending-conflict queue that only a person clears

Notable strengths.value: An expiry compared to the clock rather than tested for presence; a contradiction policy that queues for review and says so at the insert site; a write-once resolution timestamp; and a migration that declines to backfill a value it never observed rather than fabricating one

Main risks.value: The architecture document describes the semantic graph as having bi-temporal validity over a schema carrying one temporal axis — the session date an `as_of` read travels, plus observation stamps and a retirement date — with no column recording when the store came to believe anything; the README's 95% LongMemEval figure is a 50-example run whose own table reports Recall@1 at 94%, and the headline drops the sample size; and the comparison table's ~37K-line self-measurement is five months stale against a tree whose `src` alone is 64,400 lines

Memory unit.value: An event in an append-only ledger under `.edda/`, carrying a family, a level, a payload, digests, its own hash and its parent's; decisions, tasks, verdicts and review artifacts are event kinds

Storage backend.value: SQLite for the event log and its projections, with a content-addressed blob store beside it for anything large

Retrieval strategy.value: Full-text search over the ledger, plus projections the events are folded into

Write strategy.value: Every mutation is an appended event, validated against the current tail before it lands

Update/delete model.value: State changes are new events; blob deletion appends a tombstone record naming the hash, the reason, the last known class and whether it was pinned

Scoping model.value: One `.edda/` workspace per repository; authority is a registered actor with a live session, an RBAC grant and an HMAC-sealed local capability

Agent integration.value: A CLI and MCP surface for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and OpenClaw, plus a bridge crate and a conductor that coordinates parallel agents

Background processing.value: A conductor driving phases and waiting at gates, garbage collection with quota enforcement, and a postmortem crate

Trust/provenance model.value: A chain enforced at append time, capability material held outside the ledger, verdicts bound to a subject, a commit and a freshness window, and a second-provider review that records what it measured

Notable strengths.value: Three decisions are worth the visit. The chain is enforced where it is cheapest to enforce — on append, by reading the tail and refusing an event whose parent does not match — rather than only verified by a later pass, and `validate_event_hash` re-derives the event canonically so a tampered taxonomy is caught alongside a tampered payload; four tests inject the corruption through raw SQL and assert which break is reported. The authority module states its threat model in the header, treats "issue text, manifests, events, environment values, and portable/imported bytes" as untrusted, keeps "[t]he root key, capability record, and bearer … outside ledger events and continuity bundles" so writing memory cannot mint authority, enforces owner-only permissions before any secret byte is read or written, fails closed on Windows "until a reviewed safe owner-only storage abstraction is available", and names what it does not cover: "[a] malicious process already running as that same owner remains outside S6a's boundary". And a verdict binds three ways — to the subject, to the full commit SHA, and to the moment: "a verdict only satisfies a gate if it postdates the gate's `gate_entered_at`. Approving a subject BEFORE its gate opens (a pre-recorded verdict) therefore does not work", which closes the pre-approval an agent would otherwise bank in advance

Main risks.value: The approver is a label. `edda verdict approve|reject` records an `actor` string supplied by the caller, with no authentication on that path and no requirement that the sealed capability be held — so the gate genuinely blocks the conductor until something outside it responds, and what responded is self-asserted. That is why this report claims no human-review mark: the binding and freshness rules are the best half of such a gate and the identity half is absent. The blob tombstones are likewise a record rather than a rule: they are keyed on the content hash and carry the deletion reason, but their only reader is `edda blob tombstones`, an inspection command — nothing consults them when the same bytes are written again. Nothing in the ledger is epistemic: there is no status, confidence or provenance class on a memory, and a decision and the later one that reverses it are two events with no relation between them beyond order. At 213,521 lines of Rust across a dozen crates — an 80,675-line CLI among them — the ledger a reader came for is a tenth of the tree

Storage backend.value: State documents encrypted with AES-256-GCM under `~/.egc/state` with HMAC sidecars, mirrored in plaintext (context, five decisions, five next steps) into the project's existing instruction files and held out of commits by a git clean filter; one plaintext SQLite database at `~/.egc/memory/state.db` for decisions, lessons, working memory, patterns and the session bus; a separate CLI state store at `~/.egc/egc/state.db`

Retrieval strategy.value: `get_state` reads the current branch's document, then `main`, then a flat per-project file, and appends a scrubbed global document; FTS5 BM25 over decisions and over lessons with substring fallbacks; working memory by project and key; hooks inject state sections on detected intents and a prior-session summary at session start

Write strategy.value: `update_state` merges into the branch document under a cross-process lock and mirrors it into instruction files; `store_decision`, `lesson_save` and `working_memory_set` insert rows through a write queue; hooks append a model-mined digest of the transcript and verbatim remember prompts to the state document; team sync merges teammates' documents

Update/delete model.value: State documents are merged and rewritten, and a rule-based consolidation layers old entries by age; lessons are reinforced, decayed weekly after a 30-day grace and archived below 0.2 confidence; decisions are append-only; working memory expires within at most seven days

Scoping model.value: State documents are keyed by the last two path segments of the project and a hashed branch name; working memory by a project path the model may supply; decisions and lessons record the project path and are read without it; the session-start summary falls back to the most recent session of any project

Agent integration.value: Two MCP servers (memory and Guardian) registered by `egc install` into the twenty-nine coding tools the README lists, hooks per tool, a memory protocol written into each tool's instruction files, a session mesh, team sync over git, and a local cost dashboard

Background processing.value: A lesson decay sweep at most daily and a working-memory sweep on reads; transcript mining at session end and before compaction when a provider key is set; rule-based observation compression and pattern detection when invoked; a session bus with heartbeats and file claims

Trust/provenance model.value: A prompt- and command-injection scanner on the memory server's free-text writes and on lesson reads, a generated-data notice and a second scrub on mirrored text, encryption and HMAC tamper warnings on state documents, confidence decay on lessons

Notable strengths.value: Branch-aware project state with a per-commit file for a detached HEAD, encrypted at rest with integrity sidecars; one injection scanner shared with the command guard, applied on lesson writes and again on lesson reads; careful lock, link and quarantine handling on the encrypted files

Main risks.value: Decisions and lessons from every project are returned by search and recall; a state document's identity is the last two path segments of the project, so two checkouts named alike share one document; the transcript miner and team sync write into the state document without the injection scanner; the session-start load hook reads the encrypted file as UTF-8 text

Update/delete model.value: Status transitions rather than deletion: `Superseded`, `Stale` and `Rejected` are epistemic values, `Suppressed` and `Archived` lifecycle ones, and a `memory_transition` table records movement

Scoping model.value: Project id and task id on every canonical record, with scope heads and project sequences

Agent integration.value: An MCP stdio surface with operator, cognition, task and verification handlers, plus Windows IPC, an app, a kernel and a watchdog

Background processing.value: A governor crate of 41,468 lines, a supervision crate, adapter circuit states, and restart windows with runtime checkpoints

Trust/provenance model.value: The epistemic and lifecycle axes, operator disposition of candidates, write receipts re-checked at promotion, a secret report, and an architecture-boundary auditor run against the Cargo manifests

Notable strengths.value: The epistemic vocabulary is the best-shaped in this corpus: nine values covering how a claim came to be believed, on an axis explicitly separate from a four-value lifecycle covering whether it is live — so `Superseded` and `Suppressed` are different facts rather than one overloaded field. A candidate cannot promote itself: the operator path refuses anything that is not an undispositioned candidate, records the disposition with the source write id and memory revision, and a later verification re-reads the claim and fails unless the status, the write id, the `candidate_only` flag, the operator-admission flag and four cognitive-run identifiers all agree — an approval checked against its own receipt. The architecture boundaries are machine-checked: `audit-architecture-boundaries.py` reads the Cargo manifests and a declared policy and reports HARD_VIOLATION, TRACKED_DEBT or AUDIT_SIGNAL, where a debt entry is rejected as malformed unless it carries a positive issue number, a reason and a removal condition — an exception mechanism that cannot be used as a silent suppression

Main risks.value: Pre-alpha, and the README says so first: "Not ready for use." At 1.17 million lines of Rust across nineteen crate groups, with 6,142 test functions, the proportion of this that has been exercised against a running system is not determinable from the tree. The SurrealDB tables are all `SCHEMALESS`, so none of the vocabularies above are constrained at the storage layer — every invariant lives in Rust. The durable-audit surface is named in the architecture and the tables exist (`write_receipt`, `memory_transition`, `canonical_record`), but whether they are append-only across every write path was not verified here, which is why no audit mark is claimed either way. The documentation carries a "mandatory verified-reading protocol" addressed to reading agents; it was treated as data and not followed

Scoping model.value: None. One SQLite file per memory instance; layer and episode are optional filters the model chooses per call

Background processing.value: None in the library. Time-window consolidation and archival run when the host calls consolidate_time_window and maintenance; entity extraction runs inside whichever add call triggers a flush

Trust/provenance model.value: Signatures prove authorship, not truth. A contested marker, a superseded_by pointer and a per-band provenance class are shown to readers; the provenance filter is opt-in and nothing excludes a contested fact or a superseded note

Notable strengths.value: The gates are the thing to take. Three scripts under `scripts/` hold three invariants, each written as an argument rather than a rule: `no-network-at-write.sh` parses the package with Python's AST — "because indentation is the entire distinction and a regexp would be fooled by an import inside a try block at module scope" — to prove no provider SDK is imported at module level; `local-first.sh` holds the install side, an allow-list of exactly three permitted default dependencies ("a new dependency should have to be argued for, not merely fail to match a list of things somebody thought of in 2026") and a full observe-and-recall cycle run with socket creation made to raise, "so a call that would have connected fails loudly instead of passing quietly on a machine that happens to have no route"; and `readme-numbers.sh` recomputes the recall table and corpus size from `benchmarks/results/*.jsonl` rather than quoting them, because "[a] number in a README is a claim with no owner". Each says it is "the ONE copy of this check". Then comes the layer almost nobody builds: `tests/test_gates_are_wired.py` asserts the gates run in `release.yml`, because a tag push does not trigger `ci.yml` at all, so until August 2026 the workflow that shipped the wheel to PyPI ran none of them. That test refuses to parse the YAML, on the ground that PyYAML is not a declared dependency and "a test that quietly depends on somebody else's transitive install is the same class of defect as a gate that runs in one job"

Main risks.value: The bitemporal columns are the gap to read first: `facts` carries `valid_from`/`valid_to` beside `recorded_at`/`superseded_at`, and both shipped writers set `valid_from` and `recorded_at` to the same `now`, while `close_fact` writes one `now` into both `valid_to` and `superseded_at`. Two axes, one clock, and no public API accepts a valid time, so `get_facts_as_of` reads a version chain rather than a belief history — the store cannot answer what it held as of last Tuesday. The bitemporal test suite passes because its helper constructs rows directly, setting `recorded_at=valid_from`, which no shipped path produces. Erasure is the other one: `forget_entity` deletes episodes where the entity is named in the caller-supplied `actors` list, so an episode whose text names the person while its actors list omits them survives, and the next `reflect()` reads the whole episode window and can re-extract the deleted fact. Nothing is keyed on a value and no tombstone concept appears anywhere in the tree, so a re-derived belief returns silently. Smaller: `import_json` writes episodes, facts and entities with no event at all, so an auditor reconciling against `memory_written` finds memories nobody recorded creating; and confidence is a continuous score with no discrete status beside it, so an extraction the model was unsure of is indistinguishable at read time from one it was certain of

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A file in the user's Obsidian vault — markdown or PDF. Its path is its identity, its `mtime` is its age, and its frontmatter is whatever the user wrote

Storage backend.value: The vault itself, untouched; derived state is a SQLite FTS5 table plus an embedding database and its HNSW derivatives, treated as one coordinated persistence family that can be erased and rebuilt

Retrieval strategy.value: FTS5 lexical and embedding arms fused by reciprocal rank fusion, with PDF hits keeping page citations; results carry a path, an excerpt, a score and an age in days

Write strategy.value: Read-only by default; writes are opt-in, with cancellation split between rollback operations that restore committed effects and atomic operations allowed to finish

Update/delete model.value: No memory lifecycle — the user edits their own notes. Erasure applies to derived artifacts through one receipt leaf that believes an unlink only after re-statting the entry absent

Scoping model.value: None in the retrieval sense: one vault, one user, no stored scope key. What is enforced is filesystem confinement — a path is resolved, then classified against reserved and hidden segments at every depth, then refused

Agent integration.value: An MCP server reaching Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, Codex and other clients, with a hybrid search tool, structured Canvas, Dataview and Bases tools, and a stale-notes surface

Background processing.value: A vault watcher behind an activation guard, periodic cache pruning, and embedding sync and replacement staged against full-family erasure

Trust/provenance model.value: None. A note's age is surfaced as `age_days` and a `stale` flag for the model to reason over; nothing is withheld on it, and the recency re-ranking built on the same signal is opt-in and off by default

Notable strengths.value: The path policy is applied to the resolved physical location, so a visible symlink cannot launder a hidden directory into the public surface, and the privacy suite opens with a guard asserting its own fixtures can be built; one erasure receipt leaf replaced the same rule half-applied across six erasers after the project's own re-sweep found the gap; and age is surfaced as a signal rather than folded into ranking

Main risks.value: There is no memory lifecycle at all: writes exist but nothing distinguishes a note an agent wrote from one the user wrote, nothing records a correction, and staleness is computed from `mtime`, so a note a linter reformats is newly young. The repository also ships llms.txt, llms-ctx.txt and an AGENTS.md addressed to reading agents, which is worth knowing when an agent summarises this project from its own documentation

Memory unit.value: Per goal-key level and grid cell: an anchor record of decayed acceptance and rejection counts from the agent's own stop verification, and a frontier record of moving-average information gain, dead-end rate and decayed support

Storage backend.value: One JSON file per scene under results/<exp_name>/scene_ltm/, rewritten whole through a temporary file after every subtask; an in-process episode store beside it, cleared at episode start and end

Background processing.value: None; decay and pruning run synchronously at the end of each subtask

Trust/provenance model.value: None. An acceptance is the agent's own STOP verdict, with no outcome signal, so a wrong stop is recorded as a reliable stopping place; the prompt tells the VLM that hints must not override visual evidence

Main risks.value: Self-confirming: a false stop becomes a positive prior for the next goal; the level fallback is per key, not per cell, so a new goal reads every goal of its modality; a resumed episode replays its subtasks into the store; no test

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A directory. Each one carries a `CONTEXT.md` holding its intent, API surface, constraints, design decisions, known issues, notes to future agents, dependencies, test strategy and a routing table naming its children; beside it a git note under `refs/notes/evogit` per commit records the agent episode that produced it, and a task row records the run

Storage backend.value: The git repository itself — `CONTEXT.md` files as tracked content, `refs/notes/evogit` for per-commit agent metadata, `refs/genesis/archive/T<n>-A<n>-start|final` refs pinning each archived episode's endpoints against gc; a SQLite database (`tasks`, `projects`) for task rows, their review status and their archive metadata; skills as markdown files under `.agents/skills/` in the target repository

Retrieval strategy.value: Structural, not ranked. `build_context/2` assembles the `CONTEXT.md` of every ancestor directory from the repository root to the agent's node, in order; `search_history` runs a regex over commit messages and the `evogit` notes ref; the agent reads files with ordinary tools. No index, no embedding, no scoring — `rg -n -i 'embedding|vector|cosine' apps/evo_git/lib --glob '*.ex'` finds nothing

Write strategy.value: An agent writes `CONTEXT.md` with the ordinary file tools and commits it; the architect agent is told the file is the only place architectural intent can live. `complete_task` then attaches a git note to the final commit with the objective, the result, the agent type, the depth, the parent and the context node path, and — only when the run was started with `--archive` — writes the two archive refs and an episode record that reaches the task row

Update/delete model.value: A `CONTEXT.md` is rewritten in place and the change is a commit; `disable_skill` and `remove_skill_from_all_contexts` edit the frontmatter lists. There is no deletion record for memory: `reject_branch` deletes the branch and nothing else, and the task keeps a `review_status` of `:rejected` keyed on the task rather than on what was proposed

Scoping model.value: The directory position is the scope key. An agent sees the root-to-node chain and no sibling subtree; a skill is callable only where an ancestor names it; each agent gets its own git worktree, and the prompt tells it that siblings are readable but never writable

Agent integration.value: A CLI (`genesis`, `evolve`, `reflect`, `run`), a Phoenix LiveView dashboard with projects, tasks, a review page and a chat entry to a repo-less self-reflective agent, a Tauri desktop shell, a headless daemon release for SSH remote development, and model access through ReqLLM

Background processing.value: None on the memory. Agents run as scheduled episodes; a lease and heartbeat recover stuck tasks and a startup reconciliation moves `:finalizing` to `:failed`; no pass rewrites a `CONTEXT.md`

Trust/provenance model.value: None on a memory. A `CONTEXT.md` has no status, no confidence and no provenance field; the discrete states in the system — a task's `:open`, `:merged`, `:rejected`, `:continued`, `:ignored`, `:no_changes` — belong to the run, not to what was written

Notable strengths.value: A scope key that costs nothing to maintain because it is the file's location; knowledge that lives in the same commit as the code it describes, so a diff moves both together; a routing table that lets a parent delegate without reading a child; skills enabled hierarchically from the same file; 4,655 committed test cases

Main risks.value: `build_context/2` — the function that assembles the memory — has no test, and its one caller degrades to a bare path string on any error, so an agent can run with no context tree and no signal; a rejected branch is deleted and nothing keyed on its content survives; the archive is off by default; each ancestor is truncated to a byte cap with only a log line; there is no validity time and no status on a memory

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A thought — a markdown file whose YAML frontmatter carries a ULID, a parent, a supersession pair in both directions with scopes, an agent id, a bounded confidence float, a source type, a six-value validation status, an intent reference, a creation time, typed relationships, and a metadata block of project, branch, tags and free extra

Storage backend.value: Markdown files with YAML frontmatter in a Jujutsu repository, under `trails/<scope>/thoughts/<namespace>/<ulid>.md`, with the namespace routed from the thought's source type into decisions, observations or preferences, and drafts held separately until promotion

Retrieval strategy.value: Lexical substring AND: the query is lowercased and split on whitespace, and a record is kept only when every token is a substring of its content, id, source type, agent id, project, branch and tags joined. No ranking, stemming, phrase search or vectors. The visibility predicate is applied before the scope filter and the query match

Write strategy.value: `save_thought` refuses obvious secrets and writes a draft stamped with the process's agent id. `propose_truth` runs a trust gate whose verdict sets approved, rejected or error, or leaves the thought proposed when there is no gate result, then commits through a transaction that journals the prior text and refuses if the record changed since review

Update/delete model.value: No edit after a terminal state: approved, rejected and tombstoned records are content-frozen, as is any record with a supersession backlink, so a correction is a new record. Approving a replacement stamps the predecessor in the same transaction, and refuses when the predecessor is ambiguous or already has an approved replacement

Scoping model.value: A scope path plus an agent identity taken from the server process's environment. The default governed view returns approved records only; an authoring view returns the configured agent's own drafts; an operator-only history view selects lifecycle statuses and may include superseded records. A supplied `agent_id` argument filters and never grants

Agent integration.value: An MCP server with its tools classified as read-only, destructive and open-world; a hook pipeline over seven lifecycle events; an HTTP runtime, a reader UI and a CLI; three optional paper-derived protocol packages installed by command

Background processing.value: None on the memory itself. Sync is an explicit fetch-and-rebase that restores the pre-sync state on conflict, and an interrupted write is recovered from its journal on the next entry rather than by a sweep

Trust/provenance model.value: A six-value lifecycle status of which one is visible by default, a bounded confidence float the read path never consults, and an approval block naming the reviewer, the verdict, the reasoning and whether the approval was a model's advisory verdict or a person's

Notable strengths.value: A read scope whose identity comes from the process rather than the request, stated in one line of the module that implements it; a mode that raises rather than narrowing when the caller lacks authority; supersession that retires a record only on an approved successor, so a draft correction cannot blank the current answer; content frozen at every terminal status; an approval compared against the exact text the reviewer saw; and a retrieval baseline document that states the matcher's predicate and says outright that it is not a product claim

Main risks.value: The default reviewer is an LLM one-shot and nothing requires a human pass, so a trail can be entirely model-approved — correctly labelled and still the default; a shared MCP endpoint is one identity boundary, which the project states twice and does not enforce at deployment; `confidence` is stored and never read; the version-control history is the only mutation record, which is provenance rather than an audit log by this atlas's definition; and the published PyPI release is a version behind the governed-read model described here

Scoping model.value: One user_id per server process, read from config, stamped on every write and applied on every reachable read, including both id-addressed fetches; session rows are stamped with a constant and read by an unreachable function that ignores the key

Background processing.value: A watcher over a notes directory, a replay job over the write queue, and a sidecar reconcile at boot

Trust/provenance model.value: A read-time status of current, superseded, expired or not_yet_valid, used to order results and never to exclude them; an operator-authored pointers file that annotates retracted claims; a calibrated hedge string in the QA scaffold

Notable strengths.value: Corrections that keep their history: the superseded record is returned marked, the replacement is pulled into view from the same relevance pool, and an as-of query sees the store before a later correction existed. Memory unit.value: A claim node — normalized claim text, resolved entity refs, a domain set, a five-value memory state, a reinforcement layer, a transaction and event timestamp pair, and a provenance record carrying the evidence span

Update/delete model.value: Revision supersedes rather than overwrites, stamping `valid_to` and `superseded_by`; `forget` computes an exact transitive closure, destroys the subject's content key, redacts the source documents through a Merkle binding that leaves bystanders' receipts verifying, runs a probe battery and issues a signed certificate that states its own scope

Trust/provenance model.value: A five-state `memory_state` beside a separate confidence float, a four-verdict write firewall whose refusals are typed and returned to the caller, and a signer that carries an `adversary_checkable` flag so the certificate reports what its own signature is worth

Notable strengths.value: The write gate is deterministic code on the far side of an RPC boundary; receipts bind claims to byte ranges a stdlib-only reader can re-verify with no engine import; a Merkle binding lets a redaction remove one subject's text while every other party's inclusion proof still verifies; and the tests carry real negative controls on the receipt instrument and on the erasure record

Main risks.value: The default zero-dependency install hand-rolls an unauthenticated HMAC-keystream cipher in the same release whose signing module refuses to hand-roll Ed25519 on principle; there is no scope key anywhere, so this is a single-tenant store; and `quarantined` and `frozen` are declared states with no writer

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A memory row with content, an owning agent, a durability class, a visibility, an archived flag, an optional supersedes link and validity window, an embedding and usage counts — beside an agent identity and a soul of personality, values and procedures

Storage backend.value: Harper over its RocksDB binding, installed and supervised by the CLI, with a BM25 index beside the HNSW vector index

Retrieval strategy.value: Hybrid semantic and lexical, excluding archived, expired and superseded rows by default, with the displayed percentage documented as similarity and not as a probability of being the right answer

Write strategy.value: `memory_store` over MCP, `flair memory add`, the client package or the feed; credential-shaped text is redacted on write, and a server-side conservative-duplicate gate computes a signal and never suppresses the write

Update/delete model.value: In-place update by default, or a supersedes-linked successor that closes the predecessor's validity; archive and restore as a flag; owner delete; operator-only physical purge recording a deletion row for durable memories

Scoping model.value: One read-scope resolver on every memory read path, binding the authenticated agent as the owner key; open within the instance for everything not marked private

Agent integration.value: A stdio MCP adapter written into each detected client, a built-in OAuth MCP endpoint off by default, an HTTP API, and thirteen packages including runtime bridges

Background processing.value: Federation sync, presence, nightly distillation into candidates and their promotion, reflection, maintenance archiving of expired rows, and an out-of-store watcher for lost durable rows

Trust/provenance model.value: Ed25519 per-agent keys for external identity, a server-attested provenance status surfaced on recall and barred from every decision, and a recorded justification required before an auto-promoted memory is shared

Notable strengths.value: The comments record what went wrong and what the code guarantees. The read-scope module exists because the rule used to be scattered: `SemanticSearch` had "its OWN inline grant-resolution + a `visibility === \"office\"` global OR-clause that leaked ANY authenticated agent's read of ANY other agent's memories" — so there is one helper, composed from a record-type registry, with a test that trips on drift. The migration invariant is argued rather than asserted: `not_equal 'private'` is chosen over `equals 'shared'` because the latter would "silently retroactively privatize every legacy row". The dedup gate is labelled NEVER SUPPRESSES A WRITE after an earlier gate silently dropped the second of two distinct findings. The feed and by-id fixes each ship a test that compares the path against the ordinary by-id read rather than restating the rule. And the README says the match percentage "is not a probability that the memory answers your question correctly"

Main risks.value: Within one instance every verified agent reads every other agent's non-private memory, deliberately, and grants gate no read; `private` is the only owner-only exception and the federation push filter the only hard boundary. Only the Fabric branch of `flair init` provisions the least-privilege `flair-agent` Harper user, so on a local install a verified non-admin agent runs as the Harper super user and the resource-level checks are the whole boundary; the memory feed was readable unfiltered that way until 30 September 2026. The owning agent can promote its own continuity candidate naming itself as reviewer. The Ed25519 key proves the caller and signs nothing a memory says, and `attribution` on a usage row is "nothing more than a label". Deletion history covers durable memories only and the purge path removes its own rows, and in-place update is the default edit

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A typed Markdown record with YAML frontmatter in one of eight kinds: Effort, Issue, Finding, Decision, Constraint, Risk, Citation, Blob. Every record but an Effort belongs to one Effort, and typed edges such as derives_from, supersedes and invalidates link records inside it

Storage backend.value: One Markdown file per record under eight directories of a graph root, default .flatbread-proof, tracked in Git with the code; a gitignored write journal holding before and after images and a generation counter; a gitignored cache of rendered read digests

Retrieval strategy.value: Five CLI reads through the Flatbread GraphQL engine: list Efforts by status, records of one Effort filtered by kind, state, status and created_at, one-hop relations, proposed Decisions deriving from open blocker Issues, and get by id with optional walk to the supersession head. No text or vector search; oldest first, 25 records per page

Write strategy.value: Explicit: the agent passes one of 17 typed JSON mutations to flatbread proof write. Zod validates it, a planner checks kinds, Effort boundaries and lifecycle rules, and a journal commits every touched file under a writer lock. A skill gate asks the agent to write only 4/4 durable reasons; the CLI does not enforce it

Update/delete model.value: Lifecycle mutations move Decisions, Issues, Risks and Efforts through fixed transitions; Supersede and Invalidate add edges with materialized reverse links; Retract flags a record, strips its id from other records' relations and drops it from browse reads while keeping the file. No delete verb; bodies are hand-editable outside the journal

Scoping model.value: The Effort id on every record, enforced by the writer on every edge and applied by the records, relations and blocking-decisions reads; get by id, Effort discovery and the GraphQL endpoint span Efforts. One graph root per repository, shared through Git branches

Agent integration.value: A packaged Agent Skill installed by flatbread proof install-skill, plus two companion skills; the agent shells out to the flatbread CLI, which prints one JSON envelope per command and a Markdown digest path. No MCP server and no hooks; an optional 3D explorer and GraphQL endpoint from flatbread start

Background processing.value: None. Journal recovery runs on the next write or live-server start; the live server reindexes after each committed generation; digest pruning runs only when the agent calls proof cache prune

Trust/provenance model.value: Decision state proposed, accepted, rejected or superseded, with acceptance rejecting proposed siblings on the same question Issue and a reopen_history kept on revival; the state is displayed and counted, and no read filters on it. Findings carry no state; invalidation is an edge. The retracted flag is the one property a read excludes on

Notable strengths.value: A typed record model that keeps reasons, evidence and alternatives as linked files reviewed in pull requests; Effort boundaries enforced at write and failed closed at read; a crash-safe multi-file journal with read-your-writes tokens; bounded, paged digests that report when they are incomplete

Main risks.value: The agent accepts and rejects its own Decisions; an invalidated Decision reads as accepted; Retract strips the retracted id from dependents' derives_from, so provenance silently shortens; oldest-first paging puts the newest records of a large Effort on the last page; get, the GraphQL endpoint and the explorer return retracted records

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Two kinds. A `tasks` row in SQLite — slug, project, status, priority, work dir, the harness session id and its resume timestamps, waiting-on, due date, assignee — and a dated bullet in one of five fixed markdown files, written in the format `- YYYY-MM-DD — short quote or paraphrase` by the model, never by the binary. Task briefs, progress notes, project updates and each owner's charter and journal are further markdown files beside them

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file at `~/.flow/flow.db` for task, project, playbook, owner, tag and message-bus state, and a directory tree beside it — `kb/` with five seeded files, `tasks/` and `projects/`, one subdirectory per slug, holding briefs and dated update notes

Retrieval strategy.value: There is no retrieval engine. `flow show task`, `flow show project` and `flow show playbook` print the row, the brief path, the update paths and the five knowledge-base *paths*; the session hook tells the model to Read the brief and updates eagerly and the knowledge-base files lazily, only when the turn needs them. What reaches a context window is whichever files the model chose to open

Write strategy.value: Two paths, both the model's. During a session the skill's scoop rule says to append a durable fact to the matching bucket on hearing it, without asking. At `flow done`, the binary runs a headless close-out sweep through the task's harness — `claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions` or `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` — waits for it to exit, and discards its output; the sweep re-reads the whole transcript and appends what passes three bars. The binary composes the prompt and writes nothing to the knowledge base itself

Update/delete model.value: By convention, not by mechanism. Guardrail four says entries are never edited — 'append-only log; a changed fact is a new dated entry' — and nothing enforces it because nothing but a model and a text editor ever touches the file. Task and project state has an `archived_at` column and the skill states that archiving never deletes briefs or updates from disk

Scoping model.value: Physical and by convention. Tasks and projects have their own directories and a `work_dir`; the knowledge base is one global directory per flow root, listed to every session regardless of task or project

Agent integration.value: A CLI plus a harness abstraction with two implementations, Claude Code and Codex. It installs its own skill (`SKILL.md` plus fourteen reference files, embedded in the binary), a SessionStart hook that emits the bootstrap contract, and spawns sessions into iTerm, Ghostty, Kitty, Warp or Zellij tabs

Background processing.value: Owners — recurring agents with a wake schedule, a tick process and a last-tick status — plus the close-out sweep run by `flow done`, and a message bus with a backoff escalation schedule for pending human messages. Only the sweep is directed at the knowledge base, and it writes there by asking a model to

Trust/provenance model.value: Provenance is the date on the bullet and the file it landed in. There is no status, confidence or source field on a knowledge-base entry, and the binary cannot tell an entry it prompted for from a line the user typed into the file by hand. The close-out sweep that writes entries runs with every tool approval bypassed

Notable strengths.value: `flow stats` mines Claude Code session transcripts for `Read` calls whose path contains `/.flow/kb/` and reports them as knowledge-base lookups — an instrument for the one thing a prompt-directed memory cannot guarantee, which is whether the instruction was followed. The match is a literal on the default root, so a relocated `FLOW_ROOT` or a Codex task reports none

Main risks.value: The shipped artifacts disagree about when the knowledge base is read: the session hook and the skill say lazily and only on demand, while the README, a comment in `show.go` and the close-out sweep's own prompt say the files are loaded into every session — the last is the premise the sweep's strict bar rests on

Memory unit.value: An immutable, timestamped chunk of a transcript turn, carrying its session id and turn uuid as provenance and the agent it came from; never overwritten and never updated

Storage backend.value: A Lance dataset on disk holding the raw passages and their embeddings, optionally synced to a Hugging Face Hub repository the user owns, where recall reads immutable files over `hf://` into a commit-pinned local cache

Retrieval strategy.value: Local embeddings and a local cross-encoder reranker over the chunks, with recency weighting, spanning every indexed agent and naming which one each hit came from

Write strategy.value: Deterministic indexing — parse, chunk, embed — with no model in the ingest path, so the same transcript always indexes the same way and every hit traces to a real line of a real transcript

Update/delete model.value: Nothing is overwritten. A changed fact leaves the old passage in place and adds a newer one, and obsolescence is resolved at read time by recency and by the reader. `funes scrub` exists for one purpose — removing a secret — and rewrites the affected block by deleting its chunk ids and appending the redacted text at the same coordinates

Scoping model.value: A memory is a dataset you own, gated by your Hub token; there is no in-store scope predicate because there is one memory per owner

Agent integration.value: A CLI, hooks that index in the background, and integrations that let Claude Code, Codex, pi and Hermes recall from one memory

Background processing.value: Hooks that index sessions as they end and push in the background, with `funes status` scanning pending rows the same way a push would

Trust/provenance model.value: None, deliberately. Every passage stays and the reader judges; the design document argues that a write-time supersession decision loses information silently when it is wrong

Notable strengths.value: A design document that argues for what it declines rather than listing what it has; deterministic ingest with no model between the transcript and the index; a publication gate that is fail-closed, reconstructs blocks before scanning so a secret split across chunks cannot evade it, and holds back every chunk of an offending block; and a statement that the reader is a separate trust boundary

Main risks.value: Index-time redaction is best-effort and silently absent without the scanner beyond a printed warning, so a local memory can hold credentials; obsolescence is entirely the reader's problem, which is a position rather than an oversight but leaves a wrong passage indefinitely recallable; and every dependency manifest changed on the day of this reading

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file with an optional sqlite-vec table and an entity-triple graph beside the facts, fully offline — "[n]o API keys, no cloud"

Retrieval strategy.value: BM25 and TF-IDF computed in Python, blended with optional sqlite-vec cosine, over facts neither tombstoned nor rejected; pending, deferred and agent-reviewed facts rank at 0.6x. The domain filter is optional and the session hook passes none

Write strategy.value: Mined from Claude Code, Grok, Codex, Ollama and PentAGI sessions straight into the corpus with no person in the path; Gemini harvests stage until promoted at the CLI; an MCP tool writes a fact directly

Update/delete model.value: Duplicates sharing a fact key merge into the oldest row with counts summed and provenance unioned, the losers tombstoned; an opt-in TTL tombstones stale live facts; the audit pass only demotes; no path deletes a fact row

Scoping model.value: None enforced. The domain is a topic label that deduplication ignores; inject and search take it as an optional argument and the session hook passes none

Agent integration.value: A CLI, an MCP server of seven tools including one that writes a fact, and a Claude Code plugin whose hooks inject at session start and, when enabled, per prompt

Background processing.value: Retire, harvest and ingest passes that extract and promote, a decay pass that rescores and can tombstone stale live facts, and a corpus audit that demotes when enforcement is switched on

Trust/provenance model.value: A six-value review state, an outcome a person's reject sets to rejected, a heuristic confidence and contradiction flag at write time, provenance arrays unioned across agents and sessions, and an environment and tty check on the verbs that write a human verdict

Notable strengths.value: Two bounded mechanisms. The enforcement pass states its limits before its purpose: "DEMOTE-ONLY — never tombstones, never DELETEs", touching "ONLY review_state" so the field recording why a fact was believed survives, and reversible because "an operator flips review_state back to 'auto' to undo". Withholding and demotion are separate: a person's reject removes a fact from every retrieval read and keeps the row, while pending, deferred and agent-reviewed facts stay retrievable at 0.6x. The merge of duplicates keeps the oldest row, sums confirmation counts and unions agents, sessions, principals and model families, so the evidence that several runs agreed survives the merge. The verbs that write a human verdict refuse four agent environment variables and a non-tty, and a test pins both refusals

Main risks.value: Rejection is keyed on a row. Session-mined facts take a key from the session stem and the text, so the same claim mined from a later session is a new row and injects at full weight; the MCP tool hashes the text another way again. The withholding predicate reads `outcome`, which the Claude shim fills with raw tool output, and the audit pass treats any non-null outcome as verified, so those facts are never demoted. The domain is a topic label rather than a scope. The audit's contradiction tier groups live rows by fact key, which the partial unique index makes impossible, and its test builds a table without that index. The README's hard gates that exit 2 on force-push ship as an example script in the docs; none of the plugin's hooks blocks a tool call

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Two units over one page graph — a `facts` row of hot memory (one claim with a kind of event, preference, commitment, belief, fact or idea, an entity, a confidence that decays by kind, a visibility of private or world, a validity window, a session and a provenance string) and a `takes` row of graded knowledge (a claim typed fact, take, bet or hunch with a holder, a weight and, for bets, a resolution); a proposal sits between them

Storage backend.value: Postgres or PGLite with pgvector behind two engine implementations; markdown pages on disk whose facts and takes fences are canonical, so a forget or a supersede is a fence rewrite the database reconstructs on rebuild; row-level security on Postgres

Retrieval strategy.value: Hybrid search over pages with lexical, vector and typed graph traversal into cited synthesis with a gap statement; `recall` over active facts by entity, session or time with kind half-lives applied to confidence; a `_meta.brain_hot_memory` injection of the top ten facts into MCP tool responses, cached thirty seconds per session; semantic search over embedded takes

Write strategy.value: `remember` with a required provenance, or an opt-in ambient writeback whose Stop-hook backstop runs a zero-LLM salience gate before a Haiku extractor; every write passes an entity-scoped duplicate search, a cosine 0.95 fast path, an LLM classifier of duplicate, supersede or independent and a 0.92 fallback; the cycle's propose_takes extracts claims from pages into a queue a person drains, and consolidate promotes clusters of three or more facts older than a day into takes

Update/delete model.value: A fact is superseded — the old row gets `expired_at` and `superseded_by`, both stay — or forgotten by striking its fence row and setting `valid_until`; a take is superseded with a strikethrough and `superseded_by`; a bet's resolution is immutable; a source soft-deletes with a 72-hour tombstone, an impact preview and a typed confirmation; a rejected proposal stays rejected and blocks the same claim from the same page content

Scoping model.value: Every read carries the caller's `allowedSources`; visibility `private` hides a fact from remote and MCP readers; mounted brains are read under a four-rule contract whose rule 4 refuses subagents; Postgres enforces the source at the row

Agent integration.value: MCP with three surfaces — seven frozen verbs (`remember`, `recall`, `entity`, `synthesize`, `forget`, `context_pack`, `delta`), a starter set of about twenty operations, or everything — for Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw harnesses; a CLI; cron; an HTTP server; installable harness instruction blocks whose consent is never automated

Background processing.value: Sixty-plus cycle phases with budget metering — extract, propose takes, grade takes into a verdict cache, calibration profiles with a completion fraction, consolidate, drift, anomaly, synthesis — plus a facts queue that extracts off the write path

Trust/provenance model.value: A four-value commitment vocabulary on takes and a per-holder Brier profile with bias tags from resolved bets; a pending, accepted, rejected or superseded status on proposals; confidence with kind half-lives on facts; a judge cache the operator must opt into applying, at 0.95; every take resolution records who or what resolved it

Notable strengths.value: Validity read at query time on facts with history preserved; a human gate between extraction and the knowledge table, with a concurrency-safe accept; BrainBench in the tree with sealed gold, a holdout and executable floors; a destructive guard that previews and tombstones; write outcomes typed as inserted, duplicate or superseded

Main risks.value: Two validity models — read on facts, stored and never read on takes, where `until_date` has no reader and the scorecard's window compares `since_date` at both ends; a rejected proposal is keyed to the page's content hash, so an edited page can re-propose the same claim; `drift_decisions` is a table nothing writes; a 903,931-line tree with two engine implementations to keep in parity; the evaluation numbers that matter are prose in the README and docs rather than committed run artifacts

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A `MemoryRecord` — content, a float32 embedding, `user_id`/`agent_id`, `created_at`/`accessed_at`/`access_count`, `parents` and an `operator` tag, plus a metadata bag. Entities and entity facts are memory records too, tagged by operator, so they inherit scope, cascade delete and search

Storage backend.value: SQLite by default, Postgres behind the same interface; embeddings stored as blobs and compared by exact cosine over the scope's rows, with no ANN index to build or maintain

Retrieval strategy.value: Exact cosine over the tenant's rows, an optional BM25 hybrid arm and an optional local cross-encoder rerank; separately `facts_valid_at(entity, T)` resolves the fact log as of a point in time

Write strategy.value: Embed locally and store — no model call, no network. Fact extraction, conflict resolution and automatic fact detection are each opt-in and each add an LLM call

Update/delete model.value: `delete` by id, `reset` by scope, an MCP `forget` that refuses below a `min_score` cosine floor and names the best candidate instead, and an opt-in conflict resolver returning ADD, UPDATE, DELETE or NONE. No tombstone: a deleted value can be added again, and the journal retains its text

Scoping model.value: `user_id` and `agent_id` columns applied as predicates on every read arm — and both optional, so an unscoped call sees every tenant

Agent integration.value: A Python API, a CLI, a FastAPI server that also exposes the trust firewall over HTTP, a fully local MCP server exposing `remember`/`recall`/`forget`/`reset_memories`, LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters, and a TypeScript SDK with the same reach

Background processing.value: None required. Auto-consolidation is opt-in and its constructor carries a measured warning against enabling it; automatic fact detection runs inline on `add` when an LLM is configured

Trust/provenance model.value: Discrete provenance tiers — system, user, agent, tool, web — that quarantine below a threshold rather than reweight, plus a per-fact `confidence` float used for a detection cutoff

Notable strengths.value: The write path is deterministic, so the journal can replay the store exactly and the record is auditable in a way an LLM-extraction store cannot be; and the project publishes a feature audit that reports one of its own features as harmful

Main risks.value: The journal that makes the store reproducible also makes deletion reversible — a purged memory's text stays in the log and `replay_journal(until_seq=N)` rebuilds it; scope is optional on every call; and the automatic fact path swallows its own failures at DEBUG

the memory firewall, applied on every read arm | genome/firewall.py, genome/memory/facade.py:402-414, :678, :829-833 | provenance is a named discrete tier under a reserved `_provenance` metadata key — `system` 4, `user` 3, `agent` 2, `tool` 1, `web` 0 — and a `TrustPolicy` with `recall_min_trust` set holds everything below the threshold out of `search()`. It is a filter, not a weight: `search_quarantined()` shows what was withheld, so the store can say *I have this on record and will not act on it*. The same test is applied at three arms rather than one — the id lookup checks it because *"knowing an id must not be a way around quarantine"*, and synthesized-parent selection applies *"the SAME quarantine test"*. `supersede_requires_geq` adds the write half: a lower-trust fact cannot UPDATE or DELETE a higher-trust memory *"even when the resolver LLM is fooled into asking for exactly that"*. And the tier cannot be self-assigned: `add()` pops the reserved key out of caller-supplied metadata before the record is built, under a comment naming the attack — *"a caller could pass metadata={\"_provenance\": {\"trust\": 999}} and self-assign authority, defeating quarantine and origin-bound authority"* (`genome/memory/facade.py:369-376`) — so provenance comes only from the validated `provenance=` argument. Off by default (`recall_min_trust=None`), and the tier records where content came from rather than whether anyone checked it — there is no candidate/verified/rejected transition | tests/test_firewall.py asserts an attacker-sourced city is absent from recall; tests/test_round6_fixes.py asserts a victim's secret is absent from an attacker's results

the entity fact log | genome/memory/temporal.py, genome/memory/schema.py | `EntityFact` carries `valid_from` and `valid_until` — when the fact held in the world — while the `MemoryRecord` underneath carries `created_at`, when the store learned it. The two axes are separate columns and the validity axis is queried: `facts_valid_at(entity, T)` returns facts where `valid_from <= T < valid_until`, with the boundary semantics written out as SQL:2011 application-time periods and the successor-at-the-boundary rule stated. `record_fact` invalidates the predecessor by setting `valid_until` rather than overwriting, so a superseded value stays answerable for the period it was in force | tests/test_auto_temporal.py, tests/test_bshr_fixes.py:502 exercises `facts_valid_at` across a scope boundary

the store, both read arms | genome/memory/sqlite_store.py `_select_scope`, `search`, `list_by_scope`; genome/memory/postgres_store.py | `user_id` and `agent_id` are columns on `memories` and `_select_scope` appends `AND user_id = ?` / `AND agent_id = ?` before `search` scores anything, so the key reaches the query rather than sitting in metadata. The temporal reads take the same pair and pass it through `entity_timeline`. The limitation to state with the mark: both arguments default to `None` and a `None` omits its predicate, so an unscoped call reads every tenant's rows — the key is enforced when supplied and nothing requires it | tests/test_bshr_fixes.py:500-502 writes facts as `agent-a` and asserts `entity_timeline`, `current_facts` and `facts_valid_at` all return `[]` when queried as `agent-b`

the journal, wrapping the store | genome/journal.py (`Journal`, `JournalingStore`, `verify_journal_integrity`, `replay_journal`) | an append-only JSONL of store mutations — `add`, `update`, `delete`, `add_edge`, `delete_edge`, `delete_edges_touching` — each line carrying a monotonic `seq` and a `line_hash` chained to its predecessor from a fixed `GENESIS_LINE_HASH`. The line is made durable BEFORE the inner store mutates — written and `os.fsync`'d, because *"flush() only hands the line to the OS page cache"* — and a mutation that raises after its line is durable is cancelled by a second, reversing line, so a replay still reproduces live state. The sequence is assigned under both an in-process lock and an OS advisory lock on a sidecar file, `fcntl.flock` on POSIX and `msvcrt.locking` on Windows, chosen over create-with-`O_EXCL`-and-spin because that variant is broken by any holder slower than the spin count and an advisory lock is released by the kernel. With a key the chain is HMAC-SHA256 rather than SHA-256, and the module states the difference it buys: an unkeyed chain *"can be recomputed by anyone… a determined attacker edits a line and rechains the rest."* Opt-in — passing `journal=` to `Memory` wraps the store; without it nothing is recorded | tests/test_journal.py; `verify_journal` compares a replay against live state, and `verify_journal_integrity` walks the chain

Memory unit.value: A file the agent wrote in a previous run — JSON, JSONL, Markdown, CSV — with no schema the system imposes or reads

Storage backend.value: Three file-backed surfaces — a GitHub Actions cache holding a git repo, an orphan git branch, and a managed issue comment materialised as Markdown — plus an experimental FUSE-mounted GitHub Drive that reuses the cache-memory git layout

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A binding — an external memory reference (provider, external_id) attached to one or more anchors, each anchor an observable fact with a versioned probe and content-hashed transition rules

Storage backend.value: One SQLite database whose append-only half is enforced by sixteen `BEFORE UPDATE`/`BEFORE DELETE` triggers raising `append_only` — journal, bindings, binding_anchors, links, both revocation tables, and a content-addressed `sealed` table that raises `sealed_immutable`. Four tables are mutable and each says so in the schema with its reason: `sighting` and `usage` counters, a per-session `ledger` of verb calls and envelope bytes, and a polling `queue`. Memory content itself stays in an external provider (git files)

Retrieval strategy.value: Not search — surfacing. Observe an anchor, and if its content-addressed fact crosses a declared transition, return the memories bound to it; cobound derives sibling memories from the binding graph

Write strategy.value: Bind a memory reference to anchors at a recorded journal sequence; open, transition, still, revise and close entries accrete on the anchor's append-only journal

Update/delete model.value: An anchor is revised (reprobe/retransition/reterminal/restate) or closed, each with a rationale hash; a memory whose content moved since binding is flagged rewritten and can be reaffirmed. Detaching is a revocation row rather than a delete, and it names the binding rows it observed — so a later re-add of the same anchor is a tag the revocation never saw, and survives. Link revocation works the same way, each row killing exactly one observed edge

Scoping model.value: A memory reference is namespaced by provider and external_id; there is no per-user or per-tenant scope filter — GMR is a single-project grounding layer

Agent integration.value: A Rust runtime and CLI over eight crates, with a `console/` holding the CLI plus Node and Python bindings, `batteries/` for transport, provider, survey and atlas adapters, and `packs/coding` shipping probes and an extractor; memory providers are pluggable behind a `ContentProvider` trait

Background processing.value: Observation runs the probe on a cadence and appends a sighting; a Still is written when nothing moved, a Transition when the fact crosses a rule, an Attempt when the probe fails. A `queue` table with a lease and an epoch high-water mark carries polling deployments, and a caller can demand freshness inline instead: `grounded_within` with `Instructions::fresher_than` errors rather than serving a reading older than the caller asked for

Trust/provenance model.value: A memory's currency is its anchor's discrete state at the sequence it was bound; anchors carry status, terminal statuses, closed and superseded; probes are Closed (reproducible) or Open (declared)

Notable strengths.value: Grounds a memory in the observable fact it depends on and surfaces it when that fact drifts, with a probe-failure taxonomy that never lets an unreachable probe masquerade as a change; append-only enforced by database trigger rather than by convention; a `health` verb that reports which anchors have never answered and which answered without ever moving a memory, so a badly chosen anchor is measurable rather than merely suspected

Main risks.value: It grounds and surfaces but does not decide correctness or store the memory; the value depends on someone writing good anchors, and an Open probe is trusted rather than verified. There is no per-user or per-tenant scope filter anywhere in the runtime or store. And the surface has grown fast — 50,501 lines of Rust across eight crates plus four sibling trees — against a design whose whole argument is that a small number of semantics are held exactly

The consent gate is **blocking and synchronous**: when a (client, tier) is not auto-allowed the MCP server registers a pending prompt, emits it to the frontend and *awaits the user's click*, resolving to allow-with-duration, deny, or timeout. The phrase fallback is HMAC-derived per tier over a time window, compared in constant time, and *\"never logged or returned via MCP\"*, so the client asking for permission cannot read the answer out of the system. Separately, a correction — deterministic or LLM-parsed — produces a diff that is *\"only a PREVIEW — nothing is written until the user reviews and approves it\"*, and temporal decay is designed to route low-confidence nodes into a review deck *\"where the user can confirm or dismiss them deliberately\"* rather than deleting them | tests/ covers the audit trail of the gated tools; the gate's own timeout path is exercised by the headless fallback

Memory unit.value: A `Fact`: one ULID-keyed string of agent-supplied text with created and accessed timestamps, an access count, a decaying weight in [0,1], an optional embedding, a supersession marker, a write-time confidence word, a kind that marks vocabulary aliases, and a pin flag with its timestamp

Storage backend.value: One bbolt file `gray.db` per data directory — a facts sub-bucket per agent, an inverted term index with a recency spine, a session-checkpoint bucket and an audit bucket — beside a persistent chromem-go vector store in `vectors/`

Retrieval strategy.value: Reciprocal-rank fusion of three signals at weights vector 1.0, keyword 1.0, recency 0.5; superseded facts and alias facts are removed before anything is scored; an inverted index answers candidates by default with a full-scan fallback; optional `MinRelevance` cut relative to the top score

Write strategy.value: `Put` blocks on an embedding round trip, one bbolt transaction covering the fact, its term postings and a pending-vector marker, then a chromem upsert; no LLM on the hot path, and no duplicate detection at all

Update/delete model.value: `revise` and `forget` set `SupersededBy`, which excludes a fact from recall immediately and unconditionally while it stays listed, exported and decaying; `UpdateFact` refuses to un-retire a tombstoned fact; a consolidation cycle hard-deletes anything unpinned below weight 0.01

Scoping model.value: A bbolt sub-bucket per `agent_id` plus a reserved `__shared__` namespace that `RecallAll` fuses in — a physical partition, not a query predicate, and the project's own threat model states that any client which can authenticate may read and write any `agent_id`

Memory unit.value: A typed entity and a directed edge. The edge is the memory: `id = r_ + sha(source_id | normalized predicate | target_id)`, carrying the list of source documents it was seen in, a `confidence` that is the length of that list, and an optional `when` validity range

Storage backend.value: `.growmos/` beside the repo — `entities.jsonl`, `relations.jsonl`, `aliases.jsonl`, `mentions.jsonl`, `sources.jsonl`, `profiles/*.json`, `journal.md`, `eval/gold/*.json`. Plain files, hand-editable, no database, and no runtime dependency at all

Retrieval strategy.value: Seeds by alias containment then token overlap against the question, a k-hop induced subgraph around them, serialized as triples sorted by corroboration with each edge's id and source labels attached — the answer schema then requires `cited_edges` and a `not_in_graph` list

Write strategy.value: Three one-line verbs — `remember`, `link`, `journal` — plus an extraction pipeline that hands judgment to whatever agent you already run as a task packet (prompt + JSON shape + the exact `apply` command). No API key required; a headless provider mode exists for cron

Update/delete model.value: `merge` folds one entity into another, rewriting its edges, repointing every alias and deleting the source node and its profile file; `rename` changes a display name; `compact` prunes dangling edges and aliases. Scoping model.value: One `.growmos/` per repository and no scope key on any record. The graph is shared by every agent and person working in that directory, which is the stated design

Agent integration.value: An MCP server, a CLI, and installed hooks: `SessionStart` prints the brief and the pending work, `Stop` returns `{"decision": "block"}` while packets are outstanding. `growmos integrate` writes the config for Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Cursor and Gemini

Background processing.value: None on a schedule. Work is queued by content hash — a changed document flips its source row back to `pending` — and drained by the agent when a hook or a human asks for the next packet

Trust/provenance model.value: `confidence` is the number of distinct source documents an edge was seen in, not a model score. `provisional` marks an entity whose name resolution has not been confirmed, and no read path filters on it

Update/delete model.value: Before each task the scheduler deletes every entry not from an earlier task in the stream; a re-run of a task overwrites its own entry. Nothing lets a later task revise, demote or remove an earlier lesson, and a hand-deleted entry returns on the next resume

Scoping model.value: Physical: a separate directory per run identity, per mode and per domain, so retrieval is by construction rather than by a key or predicate. The domain comes from the benchmark's task id or manifest, never from a model

Agent integration.value: Internal to the method: the improvement stages of Propose–Probe–Compose read it through the context tree; no API, tool or CLI flag exposes the library on its own

Background processing.value: None. Every write happens inline in the task loop; there is no consolidation, deduplication or decay pass

Trust/provenance model.value: None as state. The lesson's confidence is free text no reader parses; the evidence field is a citation the reflector writes about its own edit rows, checked only for being non-empty. Grader verdict strings and answer-key paths are refused at write and at every copy into context

Notable strengths.value: Entries carry executable components rather than prose; a strict prefix rule makes the library each task saw reproducible; content-addressed session caching invalidates when the library changes; grader output is kept out of memory by a tripwire at both ends

Main risks.value: Admission is a non-empty-field check on a model's self-citation; no lesson can be corrected by later evidence; re-running or correcting an upstream task leaves downstream tasks built on its old entry, since a task's reuse identity omits the library it read; the library grows without bound into every editor context; the paper's library ablation and transfer arms have no CLI path
