Memory unit.value: Five units in five stores, separated by lifetime and owner: a `Lesson` (behavioural rule with status, confidence, tags and canary counters), a `Takeaway` (question/answer pair with a feedback verdict), a `Persona` (size-bounded list of inferred facts), an authored `org-context.md`, and the run transcript

Storage backend.value: Plain files under `~/.hats/workspaces/<slug>/`: `memory/lessons.jsonl`, `memory/takeaways.jsonl`, `memory/persona.json`, `org-context.md`, plus a `rag/` chunk index. No database, no server, no runtime dependency

Retrieval strategy.value: Takeaways by BM25, or by cosine when an embedding model is configured; lessons by `confidence * 2 + tagHit * 1.5 + min(textHit, 4) * 0.25` with a deterministic canary slice gating unproven ones. The workspace document index is separate: BM25 and cosine fused by reciprocal rank, each hit labelled with the ranker that found it

Write strategy.value: Post-delivery distillation by a second `light`-tier model call that returns one takeaway, zero or more lessons and at most one persona fact; the agent has no tool that writes memory. Human feedback is the other writer

Update/delete model.value: A rejected takeaway is filtered from retrieval and stays on disk; a corrected one is re-rendered as its correction. `persona.forgetFact` drops one inferred fact, `lessons.setStatus(id, 'disabled')` retires one lesson, and `hats space prune memory` deletes the whole folder. Nothing is keyed on a value, so a re-derived conclusion returns

Scoping model.value: One directory per workspace, which is the whole boundary. `Lesson.scope` (`run | workspace | global`) is stored, used for dedupe identity and printed by `hats memory`, and no read path filters on it

Agent integration.value: A CLI (`hats`), a REPL, a local HTTP panel, MCP client support, and one read-only tool — `recall_memory`. Memory is composed into the system prompt before the first model call

Background processing.value: None over memory. A scheduler runs unattended jobs and a retention sweep ages runs at 30 days and transcripts at 7; no pass re-reads or rewrites the memory stores

Trust/provenance model.value: `LessonStatus` draft/canary/active/disabled with confidence arithmetic and a deterministic canary slice, plus a `FeedbackVerdict` of none/accepted/rejected/corrected on takeaways where `rejected` withholds the record from retrieval

Notable strengths.value: A lesson that tries to widen access is refused when it is written rather than ignored when it is read, by a rule file that names the function enforcing it and a registry that refuses to load a rule naming an enforcement point that does not exist; unproven lessons are staged through a deterministic canary slice, so the runs without them are a control group

Memory unit.value: A memory with content, a user and optional session, agent and turn ids, a validity window, an importance score, supersedes and superseded-by pointers, a promotion chain, an access count, entity references and an embedding

Update/delete model.value: Supersede, and a detach that reverses one supersession edge with an atomic lineage repair; delete removes the row and its index entries

Scoping model.value: A user id bound to the memory system at construction and supplied to every operation, with ownership re-verified before an update or a delete

Agent integration.value: A compression proxy, an MCP server, agent wrappers for a dozen coding tools, Python and TypeScript SDKs, and sync adapters that share one store across Claude Code and Codex

Background processing.value: A learn pass that mines failed sessions into corrections written to a gitignored personal file by default, traffic learning, and cache maturation policies derived from measured re-read behaviour

Trust/provenance model.value: A validity window whose closure marks supersession and is excluded from search by default; importance is a separate score; no vocabulary distinguishes why a memory was closed

Notable strengths.value: Removing a superseded row from the search indexes rather than trusting the status filter, because the indexes cache the field the filter reads; a user id that is a property of the system object rather than a parameter; and a tuning constant derived from a measured distribution over real sessions rather than chosen

Main risks.value: The supersession exclusion has no regression test even though its own comment records that the bug shipped once; the scope key is optional one layer below the enforcing one; and the module named audit measures compression policy rather than recording memory changes

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A Graft node — either a seeded knowledge-base note anchored to a filesystem path, or a file/symbol node projected from a row in Heimdall's own journal

Storage backend.value: Graft, whose C source is vendored and whose binary is compiled from it at install time, plus Heimdall's own authoritative SQLite journal at `~/.heimdall/journal.db` and a `fact_history` archive beside it

Retrieval strategy.value: `graft retrieve` for candidates plus a graph walk, then a per-hit verdict computed by checking the anchor path and its content, with the verdict as the primary sort key and the score only breaking ties

Write strategy.value: A level-triggered reconciler: a hook appends a path hint, a single writer reads that file from disk and makes the graph match it. The hint is never believed and never replayed

Update/delete model.value: A vanished file retracts exactly the nodes its path owns and leaves an `absent` row behind; retracted facts are archived with `invalidated_at` and an optional `superseded_by`, capped at fifty rows per source path and purged outright when the same fact returns

Scoping model.value: A `--scope` substring match against the result's path at query time; no stored scope key

Agent integration.value: An npm CLI, adapters that write hook config for pi, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Windsurf, three agent extensions, and a launchd job

Background processing.value: A single-writer daemon draining the queue, an audit that compares the journal against the filesystem, a read-only `heimdall verify` that reports drift without repairing it, and a detached indexer the install hook spawns

Trust/provenance model.value: Four computed verdicts — STRONG, REBUILT, WEAK, STALE, plus REMOVED and NOPATH — assigned per hit at read time and never persisted

Notable strengths.value: A queued path is a hint that something changed, never a description of what — so a missed, duplicated or wrong hint cannot corrupt the graph

Main risks.value: Installing the package wires detected agent harnesses and spawns a detached indexer, swallowing every error so npm cannot see a failure; and the journal is declared authoritative over a projection that nothing ever reads back

Memory unit.value: A typed entry under a heading in a daily log — `## Topic Name [type]`, where type is `project`, `feedback`, `user` or `reference`, and the type sets compaction priority and whether the entry may expire. A `feedback` entry has a fixed shape: rule, why, how-to-apply

Write strategy.value: The `PreCompact` and `TaskCompleted` hooks run `hipocampus compact`, which turns the transcript into a raw daily log through a secret scanner, then either copies or concatenates below threshold or marks the node `needs-summarization` for the agent's own skill above it

Update/delete model.value: Nothing is deleted. Raw daily logs are *"permanent leaf nodes"* and weekly, monthly and root nodes are *"index supplements — originals are never deleted"*. Scoping model.value: The project directory. Memory lives beside the code it is about, there is no scope key on any entry, and a second project is a second tree

Notable strengths.value: The root node answers *do I know about this?* rather than *what do I know*, which is the question that decides whether a search happens; a tentative node is regenerated from its sources rather than patched, so a summary never drifts by increments; and the one thing the project chose to test is the secret scanner, which is the right thing to have chosen

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A fact: a free-text assertion with tags, an asserted importance capped at 0.3, a source string naming app, context class, instance and session, and an optional channel of sense, act or introspect; beside it decisions with rationale, ideas, entities and typed links

Storage backend.value: Daily JSONL journal files, append-only, per-device hash chains, Ed25519-signed; a SQLite store.db with an FTS5 index, rebuilt from the journal and never authoritative

Retrieval strategy.value: FTS5 over fact content and tags, LIKE over decisions and ideas; facts ranked by effective confidence decayed at query time, or by recency, importance or utility; facts below a minimum confidence, 0.0 by default, are dropped

Write strategy.value: Explicit: hv remember, decide, propose, retract, entity, through the CLI, an MCP server, a Hermes plugin that mirrors the host's memory writes, or a signed module API. Synchronous, no model; identical text corroborates an existing row instead of adding one

Update/delete model.value: No edit and no delete. A peer retract or a contradicts or resolves link adds negative evidence; an owner-signed forget pins the content to -1.0 and an owner-signed unforget lifts it; a decision is superseded or revoked by a link that commands only from the owner or the target's author

Scoping model.value: None on a record. A hive, one HIVE_HOME and its journal, is the boundary, shared by every agent on every admitted device; tags are an optional caller filter and the session digest picks facts by full-text match on the repository name

Agent integration.value: hv CLI for any agent; Claude Code skill and hooks for a session-start digest and save and audit nudges; a FastMCP stdio server; a Hermes memory provider; a loopback HTTP module API with signed requests

Background processing.value: A sync daemon exchanges Merkle chunk hashes with peers over Tailscale every 300 seconds by default; a doctor timer self-heals the node; no consolidation, extraction or rewriting pass

Trust/provenance model.value: Confidence derived from distinct signed identities, discounted on one device, capped at 0.70 for one principal and zero-weighted for introspect-channel claims; admission by an owner key held outside the agent's command; a contested flag that is shown, not filtered

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: An entry in a hash-chained JSONL log: an original claim holding any JSON value, a correction naming the index and hash it replaces with a reason, or a revalidation receipt with outcome, method, evidence and the digest of the version it checked

Storage backend.value: One append-only JSONL file per chain, each line hash-linked to the previous one and optionally zlib-compressed; an opt-in SQLite slot mirror; zero runtime dependencies

Retrieval strategy.value: Case-insensitive substring search over decoded entries in chain order, plus an effective view and a claim index folded from the whole log on every read; no ranking and no scope filter

Write strategy.value: Library calls append, correct and revalidate with no gate; the service facade and the holo append CLI refuse unless handed a single-use authorization bound to the content hash, built from caller-supplied reviewer and reference strings

Update/delete model.value: A correction appends a record and the original stays in raw history; correcting a claim makes every earlier revalidation of it stale. Nothing deletes; prune_suggestions only lists entries older than a threshold

Scoping model.value: None over stored content; a thread id reaches the provenance packet and no read path

Agent integration.value: A Python library and the holo CLI (append, replay with search, index, resume, demo, benchmark continuity); the MCP server exposes one read-only IDX packet check and no memory verb

Background processing.value: None; every read and every append re-verifies the chain from the genesis hash

Trust/provenance model.value: A tamper-evident interior, required correction reasons, revalidation receipts bound to the exact version they checked, and payloads that record truth_claimed false; the head is unanchored and the claim status filters nothing

Notable strengths.value: A check is bound to what it checked. A revalidation stores the digest of the effective version it examined and the index of the correction that version came from, and the claim index reports a claim's status from the latest receipt that still matches — so correcting a claim turns every earlier HELD into STALE without anyone editing those receipts, and the test asserts exactly that sequence. Corrections are appended rather than applied: each names the target's index and hash and must carry a reason, the effective view folds the latest one over the original, and raw history keeps every value the claim has held. Both appends re-validate their target inside the append lock, so a correction whose target changed between read and write is refused. The write facade binds an authorization to the SHA-256 of the exact content and refuses one whose id or hash already appears in the chain, which makes each approval single-use and target-specific. The benchmark scorer is built carefully: the fixture is hashed and "fixes the target before results are observed", the condition schema is closed "so undeclared fields cannot alter the scoring contract", and the pass condition demands full recall of current claims alongside zero resurrections, so the negative half cannot pass on an empty answer

Main risks.value: The published benchmark measures no store. The "CI-verified reference result" is the scorer applied to a twenty-three-line condition file whose recovered, current, uncertain and lineage fields are typed by hand, and the latest-value baseline it is compared against is a dict literal in the test that copies the fixture's own answer key; no code turns a HoloChain into a condition, so the five-for-five row and the two-metric tie describe declared answers. The claim status is computed on every read and consulted by nothing: the continuity checkpoint copies it, and no read withholds a FAILED or STALE claim. The authorization that gates the write facade is built from strings the caller supplies — the CLI takes --reviewer and --approval-reference and builds it itself — and the module says it is "deliberately not proof of the issuer's identity"; the library methods take no authorization at all. Verification walks forward from the genesis hash, so deleting the last entries leaves a chain that verifies. Every append re-reads and re-hashes the whole file under a lock. And the store is 863 lines inside a repository of verifiers, receipts and research experiments that runs to well over a hundred thousand, which is the cost of entry for a reader who came for the store

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A `Fact` — subject, relation, object, a weight, a created time and a last-seen time — in a Python list that is the ground truth, and its term `w · bind(S, R, O)` in one complex vector of dimension `d`, plus the same term bound to the month it was learned in a second vector

Storage backend.value: None. The fact list lives in the object; the traces are rebuilt from it on every query after a write; symbols are derived from a hash of the folded name so no codebook exists; persisting the list is the caller's job

Retrieval strategy.value: Unbind the trace by `bind(S, R)` and snap the residue to the nearest object in the candidate pool by complex cosine, returning the winner, its score and the margin over the runner-up; the inverse query unbinds by `bind(R, O)` over the subject pool with no second index; a dated query unbinds the epochal trace by the month symbol as well

Write strategy.value: `learn` scans the list for the folded key, reinforces an existing fact by 0.25 up to 1.5 and stamps it seen, else appends at weight 1.0; `contradict(s, r, o)` multiplies every other object of that relation by 0.35; `forget_faded` drops facts whose decayed weight is under 0.18; each invalidates the traces

Update/delete model.value: No edit and no delete by name: a contradiction damps, a fade drops, and a fact below the floor still sits in the list until `forget_faded` runs; nothing records what was dropped or damped, and relearning a damped fact reinforces it

Scoping model.value: One object per person or project by convention; no key, no filter, no identity

Agent integration.value: A single module on NumPy, installable with `pip install git+…` since 6 September 2026; no CLI, no server, no MCP; the same author's `membench` harness scores it as a memory arm

Background processing.value: Nothing runs; time enters through an injected clock at query and at `forget_faded`

Trust/provenance model.value: A weight decayed from last confirmation with a 45-day half-life; a margin and a noise floor per answer, with a z-score gate the README recommends at four; no state, no provenance beyond the timestamps

Notable strengths.value: A confidence gate measured in units of the trace's own noise, so silence arrives before the wrong answer does; contradiction as exact linear subtraction that leaves the old belief answerable as history; symbols derived, never assigned, so the vector rebuilds identically anywhere from the fact list; a capacity sweep committed and recomputed exactly by the README, with the project's own three retracted figures named

Main risks.value: No persistence and no scope; capacity collapses past about a quarter of the dimension, and the cleanup pool must hold every candidate; insert is quadratic and every write rebuilds the trace; contradiction is damping so a dominant old belief can outlast a new one under decay; nine commits in five days by one author

Update/delete model.value: Graph edges are reinforced by weight and pruned below a threshold; decayed isolated nodes are deleted with an audit event. Memory records are superseded, tombstoned or archived in place and kept

Notable strengths.value: The model and the approver are separated by a secret rather than by a label. Every mutating MCP tool classifies as review, the approve verb is filtered out of tools/list, and calling it needs a capability HMAC-signed with HUQAN_MCP_OPERATOR_TOKEN from the server's own environment and bound to the approval id and argument hash. A committed contract test asserts both halves: approve absent from discovery, and a wrong secret leaving the row pending. The CLI approve refuses unless stdin is a terminal and the id is typed back. Writes that admission refuses leave an append-only audit event carrying the text and a receipt id

Main risks.value: What HUQAN calls quarantine is a refusal: a quarantined write is not held anywhere a person can release it, only described in an audit event. On the stdio MCP server the workspace is whatever the model names, and the cross-workspace gate runs only for an embedding host. The identity-resolving oversight runtime with separation of duties ships as a library export no binary constructs, so a default approval records no resolved identity. HUQAN_HUMAN_APPROVAL_DISABLED auto-approves every review. Edge pruning deletes without an audit event. The surface is very large for a gate, with seven binaries and an HTTP server

Memory unit.value: Chat: a MemoryNode in one of eight layers (basic info, raw turn, fact, summary, schema, intention and two reserved), with owner, tags, a lifecycle status, a supersession chain and a caller-supplied event time. Working and Coding: a session fact plus reusable experiences, and for Coding a per-function diff chain

Storage backend.value: Chroma by default, or Qdrant or FAISS, for chat nodes; Kuzu or Neo4j for the schema and intention graph in ultra mode; SQLite for history, the operations cache, coding facts, experiences and diff threads. MemHub keeps memories only in the SDK's stores and uses its own SQLite database for grants, sources, queues and call events; its legacy evidence and governed-memory tables are dropped at cutover

Retrieval strategy.value: Vector search over layers filtered by user, agent or session key, status active and latest, with optional BM25 fusion, tag and entity boosts, a local cross-encoder, graph expansion in ultra and evolution-chain expansion of hits. Coding adds lexical search, workspace, branch, agent and session filters and attaches diff chains. MemHub recall searches user local across every agent and re-reads each hit, keeping active ones

Write strategy.value: Synchronous in add(): the raw turn is stored, one model call extracts facts, intentions and basic info, a second compares them with the user's same-source candidates and returns ADD, UPDATE, SUPERSEDE or DELETE ops, which the writer applies; the raw turn is then shadowed. A failed reconcile stores nothing and rolls the raw turn back. Summaries and graph projection run as background tasks

Update/delete model.value: UPDATE rewrites a fact in place; SUPERSEDE marks the old fact superseded and links it; the reconciler's DELETE shadows it. client.update re-embeds by id; client.delete hard-deletes vector and graph rows and restores a deleted chain head's predecessor to active. MemHub's person routes check ownership, then call the SDK's update and delete

Scoping model.value: SDK: an isolation key of user, agent and session, with search requiring user_ids and filtering on them; reconcile candidates are user-wide across agents by design; get, update and delete by id are unscoped, and the OpenClaw tools take a model-supplied userId. Coding: workspace, branch, agent and session filters. MemHub: a broker-built grant envelope checks host, tool and requested scope, then recall searches all of user local with no per-memory scope

Agent integration.value: Python SDK, a stdlib HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 with no authentication and CORS open to any origin, an OpenClaw plugin with six tools and auto-recall and auto-capture hooks, and a Hermes provider whose user and agent come from configuration; MemHub ships an MCP server with recall, write and a diagnostic trace, a recall broker, Claude Code and other host installers, a desktop app and a CLI

Background processing.value: Episode summaries and graph projection scheduled after writes; System 2 schema induction, cross-domain sweeps and forget-marker retirement only when evolve() or sweep() is called in ultra mode; MemHub's durable queue sends imported transcript windows and hand-added memories to SDK add, and in ultra runs evolve once a night per user

Trust/provenance model.value: No epistemic state. SHADOW and SUPERSEDED are lifecycle states that the read filters honour; NEGATED and CONFLICTED have no writer, schema_status is never set, and source_type and confidence rank. MemHub holds no state of its own: recall keeps SDK rows whose status is active

Notable strengths.value: A grant envelope that a model cannot widen, built by the broker and parsed strictly by Core; a coding reconciler that drops any target outside the candidates it offered; a reconcile failure that stores nothing and rolls back the raw turn; a zero-LLM diff chain recording each version of edited code; exact-list negative tests on real stores

Main risks.value: One model setting drives write and read-side model calls; the chat reconciler applies model-chosen target ids without checking they were among the candidates; deleting a correction resurrects the value it replaced; the SDK server has no authentication and open CORS; the OpenClaw tools let the model name any user; MemHub recall applies neither the granted scope nor source revocation; no harness for the published model numbers

Trust/provenance model.value: Fixed labels only: search output is marked untrusted evidence and capture claims unverified; no status field and no review; conflicting content under one capture version hides that version

Main risks.value: hc find, which the agent skill lists before the MCP tools, reads the whole local store without grant, sensitivity or retraction filtering; ordinary notes cannot be corrected or deleted; sensitivity is whatever the writer typed; a remember with kind revoke revokes the writer's own grant

Storage backend.value: A managed record store with pluggable structured stores — vectors, idempotency, extraction state, external mappings and lifecycle tasks — over local adapters or MongoDB, with client adapters for several third-party memory services beside the native in-process provider

Retrieval strategy.value: Hard filtering, then score fusion, then a stable tie-break, then a replayable explanation addressable by snapshot id. Ranking combines exponential recency against a configurable half-life with importance, confidence, an authority score derived from the source type, a verified feature and reinforcement from strength

Write strategy.value: The native path hashes the content and the scope, stamps the record `active` with a pending index state, and on a rewrite links the previous version through a `supersedes` relation rather than editing it. An outbox and a leasing worker carry the record into the vector index, with a dead-letter manager for exhausted lifecycle tasks

Update/delete model.value: A correction writes a new version related to its predecessor by version id; statuses carry a record through superseded, invalidated, deletion_pending and deleted, and the read gate drops the last two unconditionally. Nothing is keyed on the content of a removed record, so the same material can return under a fresh id

Scoping model.value: A structured scope hashed to a `scopeHash` stored on every record, compared for equality as the first test of the retrieval gate, with the same boundary enforced at the provider adapters. Visibility is a second five-value axis — private, session, workspace, tenant, shared — filtered beside it

Agent integration.value: An MCP package, a production harness, a skills and tools surface and a domain-pack model, across seventeen workspace packages

Background processing.value: An indexing outbox with a leasing worker, a lifecycle task queue with retention tasks, provider reconciliation, bounded recovery and a dead-letter manager

Trust/provenance model.value: An eight-value lifecycle status deciding admission, four separate unit-interval scores deciding order, a conflict-free retrieval filter that excludes any record carrying a `contradicts` relation, and a `humanVerified` flag that four call sites read and nothing writes

Notable strengths.value: A scope hash compared before every other test in the read gate, with no path that skips it; a status that withholds rather than ranks, kept apart from the four scores that rank; an index state that never has to borrow a value from the trust state; a retrieval explanation replayable by snapshot id with a committed equality assertion; and an exclusion test measured against a result proven populated in the same case

Main risks.value: `humanVerified` has a retrieval filter, a second filter in the managed store, a ranking feature and a conflict check reading it, and no writer anywhere in the repository — so `verifiedOnly` returns the empty set by construction and the verified score is always zero; `contentHash` is stored on every record and consulted by no write path, leaving the material for a tombstone unused; the memory events are published to an event bus rather than persisted, so there is no durable record of what changed; the scope gate enforces consistency rather than entitlement; and sixteen workspace manifests carry floating version ranges

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A verbatim `records` row in one of five tiers, carrying an embedding, a hypervector, community and centrality, `pinned` and `never_decay`, `last_reviewed` and `labile_until`, `tombstoned_at` and `live`, a JSON provenance list of every capture, recall, hint and rescue that touched it, tags including `entity:` anchors, a `language`, and an `s5_trust_score` float; typed `edges` between rows, `contradicts` and `invariant_anchor` among them

Storage backend.value: SQLite by default with every text field AES-256-GCM-encrypted under the record id as associated data, or the project's own `lilliengine` — a SQL parser, executor, catalog, pager and WAL in Rust that CI runs the suite against — behind one `hippo` table layer; an encrypted capture spool; an in-process exact-cosine matrix and an HNSW index that are caches, never the source of truth

Retrieval strategy.value: An exact-cosine authority over a resident matrix beside an HNSW lane, a warm BM25 lane fused by rank, the community graph and Hebbian edges as rank inputs, anti-hits read off `contradicts` edges, a stale downweight of 0.5 for a hit whose derived `valid_to` has passed and a cap just below its best served corrector; `memory_search` is reciprocal-rank fusion of BM25 and cosine; `memory_temporal_recall` bounds rows by `created_at` and `tombstoned_at` at an `as_of`

Write strategy.value: `memory_capture` stores a turn verbatim and folds a near-duplicate at cosine 0.95 into the existing row as a reinforcement; per-client hooks capture turns through an encrypted spool a daemon drains; `memory_contradict` inserts the corrector as a new row and a `contradicts` edge and never edits the original; sleep cycles cluster, summarise, decay, tombstone, re-score and re-tune

Update/delete model.value: No in-place edit of a memory's text. Supersession keeps both rows and derives `valid_to` at read time. `forget_hint` queues a row and `rescue` cancels it; the nightly erasure step tombstones rows by centrality, idle time and age, sparing `pinned` and `never_decay`, and the optimize step hard-deletes tombstones past a TTL; `blob-quarantine` and `idem-dedup` tombstone with `live = 0`; a hard delete marks the HNSW label deleted and journals it

Scoping model.value: None. One store per person, `episodes_recent` is *"GLOBAL across all projects"*, and `session_id` lives only in provenance and event rows

Agent integration.value: MCP over stdio through a TypeScript wrapper exposing fourteen tools; capture and recall hooks installed per client for fifteen named hosts; a Tauri desktop BrainView; an `iai` CLI with a 33-check `doctor`

Background processing.value: Sleep cycles timed from OS idle with a 48-hour starvation backstop: cluster replay, summaries, dream decay, erasure, an LLM reconsolidation critic, curiosity mining, entity linking, knob tuning; at most one `claude -p` call per REM cycle, capped at 1% of the subscription's daily quota

Trust/provenance model.value: A float. `s5_trust_score` defaults to 0.5, is bound into the structural hypervector as a `CERTAINTY` role, and gates an identity-tier write at 0.9 behind a three-of-five consensus and an injection shield; *stale* is derived from a corrector's record time and spent as a 0.5 multiplier and a rank cap, never as a refusal; `labile_until` opens a window after every retrieval in which reconsolidation may rewrite the row

Notable strengths.value: Supersession that keeps both versions and can serve either on request; a forgetting queue with a visible undo and a tombstone with a TTL before the hard delete; an events table that only grows and encrypts its payloads; seven committed contradiction-benchmark runs whose Markdown records a failing gate beside the passing ones; a doctor row asserting the paid SDK is absent

Main risks.value: The README's *"validated in a single harness against mempalace"* is contradicted by the project's own BENCHMARKS.md, which says the baseline is a published number not re-run, and the harness has no competitor mode; a restated stale fact is folded into the stale row as a reinforcement; the store, the keys and the encrypted spool all sit under one home directory with no scope of any kind; the sleep cycle's LLM critic can rewrite a row inside its labile window unattended

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A text memory row of at most 10,000 bytes with category labels, confidence, a world-time validity interval, a lifecycle revision and a tombstone flag; supersession edges and pending conflict escalations in side tables

Storage backend.value: PostgreSQL with pgvector (1024-dimension bge-m3, partial HNSW over active rows) and a generated tsvector; a Redis object cache and per-agent hot sorted set; forced row-level security on org_id

Retrieval strategy.value: Cosine HNSW search with a full-text fallback when the vector page is short (hybrid RRF and a cross-encoder rerank exist and default off), composite scoring, then the lower-ranked side of any pending conflict dropped

Write strategy.value: Session-end LLM extraction through a Celery worker, an explicit MCP write tool, or the HTTP API; one pipeline runs an injection heuristic, Presidio PII, exact and near dedup, and a temporal conflict stage before one transaction

Update/delete model.value: No edit; a newer same-subject memory with a disjoint interval supersedes the old one; an agent-scoped forget tombstones the row, scrubs content and hash, erases child rows and fences the source session, and a worker proves erasure from the other stores

Scoping model.value: org_id and agent_id predicates on every read and row-level security on org_id; an agent-scoped token is pinned to its agent; a stored visibility field is never applied

Agent integration.value: An OpenAI-compatible proxy that injects a nonce-delimited memory block as the first system message, an MCP server with search, write, feedback and lineage tools, and an HTTP API

Background processing.value: Extraction once per terminated session; an erasure worker that drains forget and purge events; no consolidation, decay pass or conflict resolver

Trust/provenance model.value: Quarantine for instruction-shaped or low-confidence-PII content, status filtering on every read, nonce-framed injection, and an append-only lifecycle outbox; no path releases a quarantined memory or resolves a conflict

Notable strengths.value: Tenant scope is a query predicate and a forced RLS policy at once; forget is revision-fenced, erases every child row and records cache addresses in the same transaction; the populated exclusion tests run against real pgvector in CI

Main risks.value: Conflict escalations and quarantine wait for a review nothing in the tree performs; open-ended contradictions stay active and the read path keeps whichever ranks higher; forget scrubs the hash, so the same value can be written again

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A leaf: a UTF-8 text chunk with a JSON header (timestamp, ingested_at, domain, type, tags, keywords, status) in its own .txt file; beside it, regex-extracted subject-attribute-value facts on a timeline

Storage backend.value: One directory per IHMT_HOME: layer_0 leaf files by domain, layers/N branch JSON, root.json trunk, state/catalog.json and state/facts.json, all written by atomic replace

Retrieval strategy.value: Tree descent from root.json: BM25 over sibling descriptors, a beam of three branches per level, zero-score leaves dropped, catalog HISTORICAL leaves skipped; a confidence and tie test returns AMBIGUOUS and asks for a clue

Write strategy.value: Explicit save_memory over MCP, or CLI ingest; synchronous chunking, fact extraction and consolidation in the call; a leading date becomes the leaf timestamp when the detector picks the temporal chunker

Update/delete model.value: Append-only from the agent. A newer fact demotes the older one to HISTORICAL and annotates its leaf, which stays ACTIVE; only CLI re-ingest of a changed file demotes leaves; no delete or forget verb

Scoping model.value: Physical: one store per IHMT_HOME directory, shared by every agent pointed at it; per-project code indexes are separate stores. No scope key on a leaf

Agent integration.value: Stdio MCP server with eight tools, usage rules appended to CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, a CLI, a Python facade and a read-only loopback GUI; no session-start hook

Background processing.value: None. Consolidation and the trunk rewrite run inside each save; an optional Anthropic summarizer is called there when selected

Trust/provenance model.value: None as a state. Facts carry ACTIVE or HISTORICAL by recency; retrieved leaves carry OUTDATED notices; the provenance label is mcp://claude-code for every agent

Notable strengths.value: Plain readable files that rebuild their own index; deterministic leaf ids; parent written before children point at it; a refusal to guess on near-tied matches; supersession notices travel with the old text

Main risks.value: The fact timeline never reaches leaf ranking, so old and new values tie; under-recall in the beam reads as nothing stored; several agents write one store with no lock on the catalog or the timeline

Memory unit.value: A `knowledge_fact` — subject entity, predicate, object value — carrying `validFrom`/`validUntil` for real-world validity, `recordedAt`/`retractedAt` for knowledge time, a `status` from a six-value set, `supersededBy`, `derivedFrom`, a `confidence`, an optional `userId`, and a `source` object naming the recorder; plus `knowledge_entity`, `knowledge_edge`, `fact_usage` and `memory_outcome` rows

Storage backend.value: SurrealDB, one database per tenant named `co_<companyId>`, with 146 ordered `.surql` migrations as the source of truth for the schema

Retrieval strategy.value: Hybrid search composing a WHERE from named fences — retraction, contest, insight-row arbitration, user scope, scope tags, validity window — plus vector and graph lanes, a multi-hop expander behind a fail-closed edge fence, an entity profile closure, an entity timeline, and a competing-pair list with its own as-of axis

Write strategy.value: REST and a native MCP server ingest facts; conflict-aware ingest sets `competing` on a contradiction rather than overwriting; a supersede sets `validUntil` and `supersededBy` and deliberately leaves `retractedAt` unset; compaction writes skeletons; the dreams pass corroborates and retracts

Update/delete model.value: `POST /facts/:id/retract` stamps `retractedAt` behind an ownership fence that 404s another user's fact and 403s a tenant-global fact for a user-bound token without `brain:admin`; entity forget hard-deletes an entity with its facts, edges and embeddings in one transaction and leaves an HMAC-hashed `forgotten_entity` row as proof of erasure

Scoping model.value: Per-tenant database; a stored `userId` on facts and edges, enforced unconditionally on the search lane and behind `READ_SURFACE_USER_SCOPE` on the timeline, the competing list and entity reads; an ABAC row policy over predicates and sources; PII predicates gated on caller scopes

Agent integration.value: REST under `/v1`, a native MCP server with read and write tools, admin routes under `/v1/admin` behind `brain:admin`, packs, skills and a landing app

Background processing.value: A changefeed drain mirroring data changes into `audit_event` behind a leader lease, a dreams/consolidation pass, compaction, embedding and index maintenance jobs, and an operator-action retention prune

Trust/provenance model.value: Stored status, per-fact confidence, provenance through `source` and `derivedFrom`, an ABAC policy with report-only and enforce modes, and an operator-action log over admin HTTP calls

Notable strengths.value: Two time axes kept genuinely separate, with a committed test pinning that the profile and search agree about the same instant; a fail-closed idiom repeated across search, graph expansion and edges; migration comments that name the failure each migration fixes; a retract path whose ownership fence was added in response to a dated audit finding

Main risks.value: The per-user fence on the timeline and the contradiction list is off by default, so a personal fact yields no timeline event and a personal contradiction is never adjudicated; the GDPR tombstone proves erasure but no write path consults it, so a re-ingest restores the entity; the data-change audit mirror is disabled by default and the always-on log covers admin HTTP calls rather than memory mutations; the memory-decisions review surface is read-only

Trust/provenance model.value: Typed evidence with per-kind weights, a hint-level and spacing multiplier, and an evaluator confidence; a categorical result that constrains the optional numeric score; a misconception status that gates teaching; a learner-facing panel that edits the profile

Notable strengths.value: The evidence model is the most carefully reasoned in this family: eight evidence kinds weighted from `exposure` at 0 to `transfer` at 1, a hint-level multiplier, a spacing multiplier rewarding delay, and a rule that the categorical result constrains the numeric score so "malformed evidence can never invert the learning signal". The misconception gate is real — one correct answer under hints does not clear a misconception, and a later linked failure reactivates it. The L3 indexer excludes the assistant's `thinking` blocks and tool results from the searchable store and proves it with a test. The learner can inspect and edit the profile the agent teaches from

Main risks.value: `patch_learner_profile` writes an absolute `mastery`, a free-text `diagnosis` and an `evidence_ids_append` list that nothing resolves against `events.jsonl`, and `update_learner_profile` submits whole knowledge-state objects including `estimate_confidence` and the retrieval counters; neither appends to the event log, so the append-only record does not cover the profile's write paths. A non-empty `evidence_ids` raises the estimate-confidence ceiling from 0.35 to 0.6 and doubles as the dedup key that makes real evidence be skipped, while the array mixes `event_id` and `evidence_id` values written by two different code paths. The misconception status ladder has four values and the read filter tests only `active`, so `repairing` stops blocking teaching immediately. The web PATCH casts `body.status` to the status type with no enum validation where the tool path uses a schema. `events.jsonl` rotates at 10 MB and the rebuild replays only the current segment

Memory unit.value: A record with a key, an optional explicit `object` carrying the value, a status, a tenant, an owning agent, an event time and a record time, a nonce and receipt material

Storage backend.value: A SQLite row store or a JSON file, plus a hash-chained receipt sidecar, a tombstone chain, an event table, monthly archive segments for captured mechanics, a Merkle transparency log and witness co-signatures

Retrieval strategy.value: Lexical recall over a filtered view, ranked by relevance and accrued value, with optional embedding ranking when an embedder is configured; read guards quarantine instruction-shaped text and demote keyword stuffing

Write strategy.value: `remember()` and `route()`, both passing the echo and objectless guards; `reaffirm=True` and `revert()` are the named bypasses, and `store.last_write` reports a demoted write

Update/delete model.value: Correction supersedes by key and object; `retire()` ends a key with no replacement; `forget()`, `forget_subject()` and `forget_pii()` erase and leave deletion receipts; `apply_retention()` erases by age

Scoping model.value: Tenant and grant-based agent ACLs in the view every read on a bound handle passes through, for a host that opens one in its own code; optional scope, project, user, agent and session filters on recall. The shipped MCP server reads through an operator handle that binds no tenant, takes the agent name from the caller and lets the caller lift the project scope

Agent integration.value: A zero-dependency core module, an MCP server, a Claude Code plugin with five hooks, `install --all` for nine coding agents, framework adapters, and LangGraph and ADK packages

Background processing.value: Consolidation and supersession passes on `sleep()`, optional retention, an optional prompt daemon, archive tiering, an erasure auditor, a witness pool and timestamping

Trust/provenance model.value: A status allowlist on recall, Ed25519-signed receipt chains with the head kept outside the store, a Merkle log with witness co-signature, strict corroboration counting distinct verified keys, GDPR objections that withhold a subject, PII detection, and a `provenance()` whose `limits` field states what the guarantee does not cover

Notable strengths.value: The echo guard is a tombstone keyed on the value, consulted on every keyed write, with a named bypass and a caller-facing verdict. The comment above it cites its own probe, gives comparative stale rates against recency, mem0-v1, a bi-temporal-Graphiti-faithful policy and a verbatim-hash policy, and states its own defeat condition: paraphrase resistance "comes ONLY from the OBJECT being value-preserving", embedding near-duplicate cannot separate a same-value paraphrase (cos mean 0.95) from a different-value correction (0.84) at "~42% false-block at a 0.9 threshold", and "an echo that OBSCURES the value (coreferent 'her old hobby') is NOT caught." It records two shipped bugs in the same place: the guard defaulted off so "the adapters missed it for ten releases", and the documented off-switch was dead. `_serving_class` commits the withheld or served class rather than the raw status to avoid "chain churn proportional to housekeeping, and fourteen chances to miss one". The ACL is tested by a sweep over every public method with its own positive control

Main risks.value: The guard is text- and object-based by design, so an echo that names the value indirectly is not caught. The ledger is the retired rows, so retention and erasure remove values from it. `as_of()` and `believed_at()` apply no status predicate, so a provisional keyed write answers a point-in-time read that `recall` would withhold. The shipped agent surface, the MCP server, is an operator handle: tenant is unbound, `recall` and `get` read everything, the agent name on `recall_as` is supplied by the model, `all_projects=True` lifts the project scope, and `reaffirm=True` on `remember` lifts the guard unless a revert authority is configured. `remember(agent_id="*")` stores `*` unchecked. The README's comparison figures are the project's own measurements at n=30 per system, and none was reproduced here. The "one zero-dependency Python file" framing describes core.py running standalone, not the package

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A fact stored verbatim, with a namespace, a kind, a source, a status, a probability of being true, created and updated times, a last-checked time, an optional lease, a superseded-by pointer, and a cursor into the event log

Storage backend.value: SQLite by default — memories, events and verdicts in three tables — with adapters that put the same lifecycle over another store's rows

Retrieval strategy.value: Relevance judged by the model rather than by embeddings, over a pool already narrowed to live statuses; a caller may supply candidates from its own vector store and they are re-checked before ranking

Write strategy.value: A fact is remembered verbatim and born current — the events already in the log are not evidence against it; each new event is judged against every memory that has not seen it

Update/delete model.value: Nothing is rewritten. A contradicting event moves the status and, when the event states the new value, stores a successor and links the old row to it; a hard lease expires a memory on top of the semantic one

Scoping model.value: A namespace on every memory and event, supplied by the engine to every read and re-checked on caller-supplied candidates

Agent integration.value: A library, a CLI, client wrappers for two provider SDKs, and adapters for a dozen other memory and vector stores

Background processing.value: A sweep for leases, and a lazy mode where recall drains the events a candidate has not been judged against before returning it

Trust/provenance model.value: Seven statuses of which recall returns two, a separate probability field, a dead band that routes a wobbling vote to review, and a per-source ceiling on how far an event may move a memory

Notable strengths.value: An event read as a question or as an instruction to the system is logged and never written, with prompt injection named as the reason; a kill is re-judged with the memory alone in context before it lands; and every judged pair is kept with its raw votes, including the ones that changed nothing

Main risks.value: A fact is born current by design, so re-storing something the log already contradicted is not caught; the verdicts table is append-only by convention rather than by constraint; and the namespace is enforced by the engine, not by the store

Write strategy.value: The assistant edits the open note through anchored `editor_` tools and, when a person has enabled each one, creates, updates, tags, moves and trashes other notes through global tools; an edit that lands while the note changed underneath it is refused; the indexer picks up a saved note from the change feed within about three minutes

Update/delete model.value: A note is updated in place and its previous states go to `revisions` under a ten-minute collapse and a ninety-day expiry; `delete_note` moves to the trash, from which a person restores; a trashed, locked or conflict note has its vectors removed at the next maintenance; a model change clears and rebuilds the whole index

Scoping model.value: One profile is one store; a notebook or a tag is an optional filter a search may pass, never a boundary the assistant is held inside; per-tool enable switches decide what it may reach at all

Agent integration.value: A chat panel in the desktop app tied to the open note; `joplin.ai` for plugins with `chat`, `search`, `getEmbeddings` and `getIndexStatus`; an HTTP JSON-RPC MCP server, off by default, that lists and calls the same global tools; providers OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic and Joplin Cloud, with remote providers behind their own opt-in

Background processing.value: `EmbeddingIndexer` ticks every thirty seconds during the initial scan and every three minutes after, drains the change feed in batches of a hundred, collapses repeated edits to one embedding per note per tick, advances its cursor only after a batch completes, remembers per-session failures, and stops itself where sqlite-vec did not load

Trust/provenance model.value: No state on a note beyond the app's own flags; the assistant's tool results carry a user-facing description; an edit is refused when the note changed during the request; the chat history is not persisted and a note switch inserts a separator; every capability outside editing the current note is off until a person turns it on

Notable strengths.value: Tool exposure as settings with an actionable refusal; an indexer that rides the app's change feed and rebuilds on model change; a scope test written to be non-vacuous and saying so; a token budget that refuses; local and remote classified by host with the LAN counted as remote

Main risks.value: The assistant's memory of a conversation ends with the panel; a trashed note is gone from the index and nothing remembers why; keyword search returns notes the model can read whole through `read_note` while `semantic_search_notes` returns chunks; the MCP server hands every enabled tool to any client that reaches the port; revisions collapse ten minutes of edits into one

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A memory row with three layers (summary, context_summary, content plus details JSON), a free type string, importance and confidence floats, tags, source_type, delivery_mode (on_recall, always, on_trigger) and a working or persistent lifecycle

Storage backend.value: Postgres holds the rows and a neural_memory_edges table; one Qdrant collection holds a dense vector and a Sudachi-tokenized BM25 sparse vector per memory, isolated by payload; an embedded LanceDB backend is a preview alternative

Retrieval strategy.value: recall fuses normalized dense and BM25 scores 60/40, hydrates from Postgres, drops superseded memories, optionally reranks; load_pinned is an unranked SQL scan of always memories; explore walks the Hebbian graph

Write strategy.value: Explicit: the agent calls remember or update_memory over MCP, or REST. The row commits with embedding_status pending before the call returns; embedding and the Qdrant upsert run in a background task with a 30-second retry sweep

Update/delete model.value: update_memory overwrites in place; supersedes edges shadow an older memory out of default recall; forget soft-deletes and removes the Qdrant point, and a daily sweep hard-deletes soft-deleted rows after 30 days. No tombstone keyed on content

Scoping model.value: workspace_id, context_id and user_id on every row and point, all three required on the search path; shared contexts drop the user predicate; agent-bound keys add subtractive per-context and per-type bindings

Agent integration.value: Streamable-HTTP MCP server with 64 tools, a REST API, a Next.js dashboard, and a Claude Code plugin whose hooks fetch tool guardrails stored as memories

Background processing.value: Embedding sweep every 30 seconds, hourly edge decay, a daily hard-delete sweep, and either the opt-in LLM Sleep Maintenance (dedup merge, re-evaluation, consolidation, all undoable) or, when SLEEP_ENABLED is unset, a legacy daily task that hard-deletes unaccessed working memories after 30 days

Trust/provenance model.value: A context-level trust_tier stamped external only by connector provisioning, excluded by an opt-in recall filter and always by the bootstrap lanes; supersede suggestions surfaced, never auto-applied; contradicts edges annotate and hide nothing

Notable strengths.value: Isolation keys required on every search call and asserted by tests; one chokepoint per predicate (pinned, guardrail) shared by readers and every automated deleter; supersede suggestions with an accept verb and a similarity-keyed dismissal; append-only audit enforced in SQL; an eval program with placebo and CI gates

Main risks.value: Default self-host runs the legacy task that hard-deletes working memories untouched for 30 days with no tombstone or audit, over only the 100 newest per user; the pinned lane ignores supersedes edges; any non-viewer member can shadow another member's memory; audit covers agent-bound keys only

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Four kinds, all plain files in the project directory — a single overwritten `lessons.txt`, one `memos/gen_NNNNNN.md` per deep-work generation, a bounded `history` list inside `state.json`, and a set of semantic code hashes in `seen_hashes.json`

Storage backend.value: Files on disk under the project directory, plus `.kaisen_snapshots/` holding up to 25 full project copies, each with a `meta.json` carrying `{created, reason, kind}`

Retrieval strategy.value: None. The prompt builder concatenates the lesson, the latest memo, a keyword-frequency line filtered by a stopword list or a user allowlist, and the last eight history entries into one blob; nothing is queried, ranked or selected by relevance

Write strategy.value: Synchronous and mostly wholesale. `save_lesson` overwrites the file, a memo is written once per generation under its own name, history is appended, and a candidate's semantic hash is added to the visited set before it is scored

Update/delete model.value: A lesson is corrected by overwriting it, with no prior version kept outside the snapshot system. History is a ring truncated to the newest 500 entries. The visited hash set only ever grows

Scoping model.value: Per project by construction — every path is derived from `project.path` — with no scope key inside any record and no cross-project read

Agent integration.value: A local web dashboard, a multi-turn agent tool loop, and KAI, a line-oriented stdio protocol letting an LLM spawn KAISEN as an optimization sidecar

Background processing.value: The evolution engine runs generations continuously, with periodic deep-work and lesson passes driven by the project spec

Trust/provenance model.value: No epistemic state. The nearest thing is a failure vocabulary of ten substrings used to hoist failing outcomes to the top of the history blob under an EXPLICIT FAILURE FEEDBACK banner

Notable strengths.value: Separating failure feedback from ordinary history in the prompt, so a repeated mistake is the first thing the model reads rather than the eighth

Main risks.value: The record explaining why a candidate was skipped ages out of a 500-entry ring while the block itself is permanent and, by an explicit design note, survives a snapshot revert of everything else

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A HyperMemory: a hypervector with amplitude, frequency and phase, a hallucination flag with parent ids, an effective, observed and expiry time beside the creation time, links to other memories and a retention tier

Storage backend.value: A local holographic medium in a .hrm file persisted through chiral hemisphere layers, with sidecar files for links, sightings and reactivations; memories cross between agents over NATS and Nostr

Retrieval strategy.value: Resonance against the medium, cosine over hypervectors with optional beam and temporal factors; rows expired as of the query instant are dropped by default, and dream rows only on request

Write strategy.value: Local remember with exact-repeat reinforcement that never matches a dream row, dream synthesis that flags what it invents, and wire absorption through one absorb_gate chokepoint that sanitises unconditionally and gates promotion on corroboration

Update/delete model.value: Amplitude decay and destructive interference, a validity window set when a fact is written, and hard delete by id through forget; nothing records a rejected value

Scoping model.value: Per-agent ed25519 identity and a pubkey-keyed reputation core for peers; the memory store itself is not partitioned by any key

Agent integration.value: A CLI, an ACP binary, an agent loop with recall, remember and dream tools, a Claude Code plugin and skill, NATS and Nostr transports, and a hive bridge

Background processing.value: Dream consolidation with Kuramoto phase coupling and hallucination bridges, belief-core telemetry, swarm loops and collective sensemaking

Trust/provenance model.value: Ed25519 provenance with domain-separated canonical bytes and a fail-closed replay set, a quarantine staging tier for uncorroborated peer content, a hallucination flag the wire can never set, and a serve guard bounding what an inbound ask may spend

Notable strengths.value: The trust boundary is at the wire, and the modules that hold it are written like a security review. `absorb_gate` is one chokepoint for every wire-to-store path whose sanitisation runs even when the corroboration gate is dormant, and it forces the hallucination flag to the local default. `provenance.rs` signs with domain-separated, length-prefixed canonical bytes and keeps verification pure. `serve_guard` states its invariant, derives the route from local config "and from nothing else", and splits its rate limiter because "[a]n abuse control that a stranger can turn into an outage cheaper than the abuse is not a control". The recall tests carry control arms that state why: "asserting 'the dream is absent' proves nothing unless the dream DOES come back by default"

Main risks.value: The licence is the bespoke SPACE CHILD LICENSE v1.0, whose Peaceful Purpose grant and paid Offensive Military licence make it not open source under the OSI definition, while plugin.json and the npm package.json declare MIT. Dream rows are returned by recall by default and RecallResult carries no flag, so the agent's recall tool hands dreams to the model unlabelled. Belief-core snapshots read every right-hemisphere wavefront, dream syntheses included. Validity bounds are set only when a memory is written. Merge records and the disputed flag have no production writer. The memory core is about a quarter of a tree that also holds a swarm, a hive, mail, QUBO tooling and research surfaces

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A vector with a free-form metadata map — content, memory layer (episodic, semantic, procedural), tags, session and user ids, pin, access count, and underscore flags such as `_is_historical` and `_archived` — plus typed, weighted graph edges carrying created and deleted timestamps

Storage backend.value: In-memory HNSW indexes over memory-mapped arenas, roaring-bitmap inverted indexes, B-trees and BM25 postings, persisted by a batched append-only file with CRC-framed records and periodic snapshots; one index per namespace, default `mcp_memory`

Retrieval strategy.value: Hybrid HNSW and BM25 fusion with metadata filters and decay-weighted scores; graph-scoped search from a root node; adaptive retrieval that expands along edges to a token budget; path finding and subgraph extraction as of an edge timestamp

Write strategy.value: `save_memory` embeds content with a local MiniLM ONNX model and stores metadata; manual links; `evolve_memory` writes a new version, copies incoming edges and flags the old one historical; a document pipeline and an AI gateway proxy index documents

Update/delete model.value: Metadata updates, evolution with `superseded_by` edges, soft deletion of edges with a deleted timestamp, vector deletion, gardener archiving of consolidated memories by flag, and opt-in epistemic resolution that evolves each conflicting memory into one consolidated text

Scoping model.value: Per index; JWT keys list allowed index names; user and session ids are stored in metadata and used by profiling and session tools, not by recall

Agent integration.value: 57 MCP tools (49 in the agent profile), a REST server with a web dashboard and TUI, Go, Python and TypeScript clients, an OpenAI-compatible RAG proxy, and a setup command writing MCP configuration for six coding clients, with a plugin for OpenCode and a skill for Hermes

Background processing.value: The gardener: consolidation of similar memories, episodic-to-semantic summaries, and eleven detectors for contradictions, importance and sentiment shifts, knowledge gaps, preferences, repeated failures and core facts, of which the core-fact detector's selector matches nothing; decay, vacuum and graph refinement; an artifact watcher that recompiles cached knowledge

Trust/provenance model.value: Reflections with an unresolved, resolved or needs_manual_review status, archive and historical flags, pinning, invalidation edges, and an epistemic score computed per query into crystallized, stable, volatile or contested; none is a stored status on the memory that recall reads apart from the two flags

Notable strengths.value: A serious storage engine — CRC-framed AOF with corruption resync, snapshots, mmap arenas and HNSW maintenance; versioned memories that keep their history; a large, documented tool surface

Main risks.value: Historical and archived memories are filtered only by `recall_memory`, and lose that filter when two layers are requested; the same OR-before-AND composition breaks the dashboard's status filter and silences core-fact extraction; a person's reflection resolution changes no memory; no mutation log outlives AOF compaction

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A finding: a unique topic, free-text content, JSON tags carrying a kind label, an inline embedding, optional anchors on a file, symbol, tool or error string, and an optional justification of rationale, evidence, SHA-256 fingerprinted file or tree dependencies, assumptions and a recheck note. Beside it, logged prompts, replies and file touches, and formal premise bundles in a second store

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file per project in WAL mode, .ken/ken.db: cr_findings with cr_justifications, cr_finding_refs and cr_finding_edges, and the session tables cr_sessions, cr_contexts, cr_interactions and cr_session_scores; code vectors in memory-mapped segment files under .ken/vectors/; premises, events and inference checkpoints in .ken/reasoning.sqlite

Retrieval strategy.value: ken_recall routes by argument: anchors match stored keys, a topic walks a graph of shared-file, shared-symbol, shared-tag and cosine edges, a path reads prose-extracted references, a query scans every finding embedding by cosine, and no argument returns the newest. The prompt hook adds findings above cosine 0.48 to a ranked file block; the session-start hook adds the three newest

Write strategy.value: Explicit: the agent calls ken_remember, or a person runs ken remember. One BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction upserts on topic, embeds synchronously, replaces the justification, recomputes references and every edge, and stores anchors. Hooks log prompts, replies and tool touches without a model call

Update/delete model.value: Re-using a topic overwrites content, tags and embedding and drops any justification not resupplied. forget is a hard delete by exact topic with cascades to justification, references and edges. Premise bundles are replaced or retracted by source id, each logged. Logged prompts and replies have no delete path

Scoping model.value: Physical: one .ken directory per project root, shared by every harness installed there. No scope key on a finding. The premise store filters on a context name the caller passes, defaulting to main

Agent integration.value: ken install wires Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and DeepSeek hooks plus a stdio MCP server with twelve tools; hooks POST to a per-project localhost daemon with a bearer token, which injects a resume brief at session start and a ranked block with labelled findings on each prompt; ken tools runs any MCP tool from the shell

Background processing.value: A per-project daemon watches the tree and reindexes changed files, snapshots per-file productivity scores at session end, and lazily embeds code. Nothing rewrites findings; the findings graph is recomputed in full inside each remember and forget

Trust/provenance model.value: Labels only. Every read re-hashes declared dependencies and reports unchanged, stale, unknown or untracked, and a stale or unknown finding is prefixed REVISAR in hook output; kind and justification kind name a hypothesis. No read excludes a finding on any of them. Premise answers are supported, refuted, conflict or unknown, derived per query

Notable strengths.value: Dependency fingerprints re-checked on every read, including tree membership for absence claims and a refusal to record evidence whose hash moved since it was read; whole-conclusion budgeting that offers an expansion rather than a clipped sentence; a premise store with an append-only event log and checkpointed, resumable inference

Main risks.value: A stale finding is injected at session start and on prompts with a label and nothing withheld; anchored memories fire only when the model passes the anchor; the MCP recall floor defaults to zero; findings correct by silent overwrite and hard delete with no history; prompts and replies are retained with no delete path

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: One lesson string with scope, kind, confidence, usefulness score, validity bounds and a provenance snapshot; kinds are preference, convention, command, failure_pattern and fact

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file per project at .kimetsu/brain.db plus a cross-project user brain at ~/.kimetsu/brain.db; an events table is the source of truth, and memories, FTS5, edges, facts and revisions are projections

Retrieval strategy.value: FTS5 BM25, optional BGE-small cosine with an ANN index, 2-hop graph expansion over memory_edges, composite score of relevance, confidence, freshness, scope weight and usefulness, provenance multiplier, MMR, abstention floors and a token budget; an optional cross-encoder rerank

Write strategy.value: Explicit record and add tools, a SessionEnd distiller that asks a configured model for up to 3 lessons, a coding pipeline that proposes memories, and pack import; confidence 0.7 or more is accepted directly, lower confidence waits as a proposal

Update/delete model.value: Correction rewrites text in place and keeps each revision; invalidation, forgetting, supersession and expiry are events that remove the row from every read; compaction can purge invalidated rows from the projection while their events stay. No tombstone

Scoping model.value: Physical: one database per project and one per user, and on the remote server one database per repository behind per-repo bearer tokens. The scope column is a ranking weight, not a filter

Agent integration.value: Claude Code hooks on SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SessionEnd and optionally Bash tool use; an MCP server with memory curation tools; Codex, Cursor, Pi and OpenClaw wiring; a terminal chat; an HTTP MCP remote server

Background processing.value: No resident scheduler; session hooks spawn a detached maintain pass for reinforcement, digest, prune reporting and skill detection. Forgetting is opt-in and off by default; proposals expire after 30 days

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A `fact` element — text, `kind`, `who`, an event time `t`, a three-valued `conf`, topic and entity codes, facet codes for object class, place, event type and duration, and `src` ids pointing at the `line` elements it was extracted from, which stay in the same file as evidence

Storage backend.value: One XML artifact per memory, holding a vocabulary of topic and entity codes, a timeline of sessions, their facts and their raw lines. No database, no index files, no embeddings; the package declares zero runtime dependencies and the posting lists are rebuilt in memory on load

Retrieval strategy.value: Symbolic and lexical only. Each question is compiled three times into a JSON plan — select, where, and a pipe of sort, head, tail and count — and a deterministic scorer keeps the candidate that returns the most rows. The plan runs as prune by time, match by code closure and postings, filter, rank, refine and pack, fused with an IDF-weighted keyword channel over every fact and line. A refine ladder relaxes constraints in a fixed order and abstains rather than return the corpus

Write strategy.value: `remember()` is one LLM call per session that returns facts and retrieval facets, appended to the XML timeline and written back through a staged temporary file that is parsed by the loader before it replaces the original. Synchronous, immediately retrievable, no background pass. A session id already present is refused rather than merged, and the docs rule out concurrent writers

Update/delete model.value: Absent, and it is the design's central bet. The public API is load, remember, recall, answer — no delete, no forget, no edit, no supersession field. A superseded fact stays in the file; the evidence pack is sorted by date and the default reader prompt says the most recent contradicting row wins. A vocabulary merge in the package rewrites stored topic and entity codes, and only the benchmark build scripts call it

Scoping model.value: The artifact is the boundary: `Memory.load` takes one or more XML paths and everything in them is in scope. `who` filters by which speaker said something, which is a content axis rather than an access one, and no tenant, user or project key exists on a fact

Agent integration.value: A Python library and nothing else — no CLI entry point, no MCP server, no HTTP surface. A second, lower-level `research` API exposes the plan objects, a profile protocol, the execution trace and per-stage telemetry for method evaluation

Background processing.value: None. Extraction happens in `remember` and indexing on load; topic and entity consolidation and instance alignment are library functions that only the benchmark build scripts call

Trust/provenance model.value: Every fact carries its source line ids and the raw utterances stay in the file, so an answer's receipts resolve to the words someone actually said. Epistemic status is a `conf` of low, med or high, ordered by a dict named `CONF_ORDER` and spent on a ranking bonus and an optional `conf_min` floor the public API cannot set; no value means a fact should not be believed

Notable strengths.value: The benchmark machinery is built to be checked by a sceptic — dataset revisions and SHA-256s pinned in a manifest, results sealed by digest, a verifier that recomputes the published metric from the sealed bytes without an LLM, and a contamination gate that scans shipped prompt text for terms concentrated in a small fraction of the corpus

Main risks.value: Nothing can be corrected or removed, so a wrong extraction is permanent and an erasure request has no path but a text editor; on the default path a contradiction is settled by the reader model following one prompt line; and the two headline scores come from a benchmark configuration the library does not ship and cannot be checked by a reader, because the sealed rows are named in the manifest, not committed, and the release carries no assets

Retrieval strategy.value: Four sub-retrievers under one query engine — a model-expanded synonym walk of the graph to depth three (skipped in fast mode and always skipped over MCP), a vector retriever over chunk embeddings with graph context to depth three, a BM25 scan of every text node in the graph, and a scan that scores date tokens, temporal words, tag lines and capitalised names — synthesised by Ollama under a prompt that forbids anything not in the context and demands file citations

Write strategy.value: A full build on first run — read the folder recursively, extract frontmatter and wikilink triples in code, then model-extract triples per chunk — and afterwards a watcher: a created note is inserted, a modified note is deleted by document id and re-inserted, a deleted note triggers a full rebuild; every path re-upserts the structural triples

Update/delete model.value: An edited note's chunks and embeddings are replaced under its path; its wikilink and frontmatter triples are upserted with no document id, so a relation the edit removed stays in the graph; a deleted note rebuilds everything, which is the only path that drops a triple; there is no per-fact edit, no supersession and no record of removal

Scoping model.value: One knowledge directory per process and one graph per storage directory, both module constants; `.obsidian/` is skipped; no scope key, no user or agent identity, and the MCP tool answers any client from the whole vault

Agent integration.value: A terminal REPL over Rich that builds, watches and answers; a FastMCP server exposing one tool, `query_graph`, in fast mode with no watcher; Ollama for both models, a cloud-suffixed model id accepted for the build; Obsidian by convention only

Background processing.value: A watchdog observer on the folder with a five-second debounce and an MD5 filter against phantom events, in the REPL only; nothing else runs unattended, and nothing rewrites the graph except the full rebuild a deletion forces

Trust/provenance model.value: None on a fact: no provenance beyond the file path a node carries, no time beyond a frontmatter date copied as text, no confidence, no state; the manifest refuses to load a store built with a different embedding model, which is a guard on the index, not on a claim

Notable strengths.value: Structural triples from wikilinks and frontmatter cost no model call and survive the model's misses; the embedding-model manifest stops a silent mixed-space index; the prompt's rule seven gives the model an out instead of a guess; content hashing keeps editor save storms from rebuilding anything

Main risks.value: A wikilink triple outlives the link that produced it; deletion is a full rebuild of the whole vault; the MCP server never watches the folder, so an agent reads the vault as it was at its first query; the temporal retriever fires on every query and scores any capitalised token; no case asserts that particular material must not be retrieved, and no benchmark scores the anti-hallucination prompt the README names; six unpinned dependencies

Memory unit.value: A keyed Markdown file with YAML frontmatter, one of three kinds by key prefix: knowledge, an incident report with status, timeline and affected windows, or a task with status, owner and deadline; every write is a git commit and every commit a version

Storage backend.value: One git repository of Markdown files under knowledge/, incidents/ and tasks/; a tantivy index rebuilt from the whole history on every start; in-process e5-small vectors with a content-addressed cache file; a token book and a JSONL request log beside the repository

Write strategy.value: Synchronous upsert by key under one global write lock: validate, regex secret scan, commit, reindex the head document, then re-embed; identical content is a no-op; no model touches a write

Update/delete model.value: A rewrite is a new commit and the old version stays searchable under history; closing an incident or task archives it out of the tree and keeps it in default search; deleting knowledge is an admin-only retraction, dated in the index and reported as revived when the key is written again

Scoping model.value: None on reads: one flat key space per server, and a token grants a read, write or admin role, never a subset of entries; agent, session and workspace are attribution trailers, and tags, service and assignee are filters the caller picks

Agent integration.value: A stateless MCP endpoint on the same port replaying 15 tools through the HTTP router, a Bash CLI, a web console, a skill and pointer text installed into Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity, and a PreToolUse hook that adds attribution

Background processing.value: None while serving; a full reindex of history and a vector rebuild on every start and on POST /reindex

Retrieval strategy.value: A cascade: an exact topic-key lookup, then BM25 over the three indexes fused by rank position, then prefix, substring, typo-corrected, any-word and median-floored stages, each only when the one before found nothing.
