Write strategy.value: A save normalises the body, strips private-tagged spans, folds case and whitespace into a hash, then revises the memory holding the same topic key, increments a duplicate count on an identical hash inside a time window, or inserts; the vector is computed after the commit

Update/delete model.value: A topic key or an update revises in place, snapshotting the replaced title and body into a version table capped at twenty per memory. Deletion is soft by default with a hard variant. Consolidation inserts one replacement and records a judged supersedes relation to each source; a judged supersedes verdict hides its target from every listing until the verdict changes or the relation is removed

Scoping model.value: A project and a scope column. The agent's search and context fill the project from the working directory when the caller names none, and read every project when it sets all_projects or when the directory is ambiguous; writes refuse an ambiguous directory. The store API omits a clause it is given no value for

Agent integration.value: One Rust binary: a CLI of twenty-six commands, an MCP server of twenty-three tools with a twenty-tool agent profile, an unauthenticated loopback HTTP API exposing all of them, plugins and lifecycle hooks for five agent clients, a terminal UI, an Obsidian export and an optional self-hosted cloud server

Trust/provenance model.value: A state of active, needs_review or deleted computed per row when it is serialised, so it labels and does not filter. A relation verdict of supersedes withholds its target, and records the actor, kind and model that judged it; every shipped writer supplies agent or system

Two tokenizers read together because no single one both stems and quotes, with the survival rates of each published beside the code. A narrowing builder that writes a clause or writes nothing, never a clause true for every row. One visibility predicate shared by every stage, including the semantic one, with a comment saying the vector stage was the first tempted to restate it. A semantic floor calibrated on held-out answers with its false-answer rate on controls stated. Consolidation that hides rather than deletes, and is reversed by changing one verdict

Main risks.value: The supersedes verdict that hides a memory from every listing is not consulted by the save path: a topic-key save into a hidden memory revises it in place and reports success, and an identical re-save is counted as a duplicate of the hidden row. needs_review is computed after the rows are back and filters nothing. The agent's search reads every project when the working directory is ambiguous or when it sets one argument. A judgement records its actor kind, and no writer records a person; a person's consolidation from the CLI is stamped system. The loopback HTTP API exposes the delete tool with no token. The local outbox is pruned, so outside the optional cloud server nothing records what changed

Notable strengths.value: Privacy is enforced before storage rather than by a filter afterwards, which is the stronger place for it: `stripTags` removes six tag families — `private`, `light-mem-context`, `system_instruction`, `system-instruction`, `persisted-output`, `system-reminder` — and a prompt that is empty once stripped suppresses the observation for that turn entirely. Two of those names matter more than the privacy one: the tool strips its own injected context block and the harness's system reminders back out, so it does not re-ingest what it or the host put into the prompt — the self-reinforcement loop other systems in this corpus discover only after it has happened. And `PrivacyCheckValidator` fixes a conflation with the reasoning written into the code: an absent `user_prompts` row "is NOT a privacy signal — treating it as 'private' silently freezes EVERY observation for the session", so a missing row now ingests with a visible warning while only a row present-but-empty-after-stripping suppresses, each case carrying its issue number

The session store the hooks actually write — observations, summaries, user prompts, vectors — carries no mutation record; the `audit_log` table with its actor type, action and target belongs to the newer server schema, written from the v1 HTTP route layer, whose `legacy_observation_id` and `legacy_table` columns exist precisely to point back at the older store. Memory unit.value: A Qdrant point whose payload carries `memory` beside `original_memory` and `compressed_memory` — the compression lineage kept alongside the stored form — plus `time_stamp`, `float_time_stamp`, `weekday`, `topic_id`, `topic_summary`, `category`, `subcategory`, `memory_class`, `speaker_id`, `speaker_name`, a `consolidated` boolean, and optional `bam_tags`. Storage backend.value: One Qdrant collection behind an `embeddingretriever` factory that has a single implementation. Beside `lightmem` the repository ships two further systems in the same tree — `em2mem` at 51,630 lines and `fluxmem` at 3,386 — with their own READMEs; this report reads the `lightmem` package the paper describes

Retrieval strategy.value: Embed the query, search Qdrant with an optional caller-supplied `filters` dict and a limit, then optionally apply `filter_by_tags` against environment tags. That last filter is permissive by default: `drop_untagged_on_tag_filter=False` lets untagged entries through *"during migration"*, and the default matcher is binary — a score of 1.0 means at least one tag overlaps, not vector similarity

Write strategy.value: `add_memory` runs the ladder: a sensory buffer accumulates messages until a token cap, an LLMLingua-2 pre-compressor and topic segmenter cut it into topic groups, a short-term stage summarises each group, and the result is embedded and inserted into Qdrant with a fresh UUID if the derived id collides. `original_memory` and `compressed_memory` are both retained on the payload, so what was thrown away is recoverable from the row

Update/delete model.value: Two paths, both offline. `construct_update_queue_all_entries` scores each entry against its neighbours and stores an `update_queue` on the payload; `offline_update_all_entries` then applies an action per entry above a score threshold — `delete` hard-deletes the point, `update` rewrites `payload["memory"]` in place with the new text. Neither writes a record of what was removed or what the text used to be, and the online path performs no update at all

Scoping model.value: None. `speaker_id` and `speaker_name` sit on the payload and no read path filters on them; there is no user, session, agent or project key anywhere in the package. The `bam_tags` environment filter is the closest thing, and it keeps untagged entries by default

Agent integration.value: A Python library with a `LightMemory` class, a `from_config` constructor, an MCP directory, a web frontend, tutorial notebooks, and per-benchmark experiment scripts. Backends reach OpenAI, DeepSeek, Ollama and vLLM

Background processing.value: The sleep-time update is the point: consolidation is decoupled from online inference by construction, so the queue construction and the rewrite both run outside the request. A `token_monitor` accounts for what each stage spent

Trust/provenance model.value: None represented. `consolidated` is a processing flag the consolidation scan reads to find work; `memory_class`, `category` and `subcategory` are write-time genres; there is no confidence, no status and no provenance beyond the speaker name and the compression lineage

Notable strengths.value: A three-stage ladder that compresses and segments before anything is stored, so the expensive work happens once on a filtered stream; both the original and the compressed text kept on the row, so a compression decision is auditable after the fact; consolidation moved off the request path by design rather than by scheduling; a token monitor that makes the efficiency claim measurable in the library itself

Main risks.value: The offline update hard-deletes and rewrites in place with no record of either, so a consolidation pass that merges two facts wrongly is unrecoverable and undetectable from the store; no scope key at all, so one Qdrant collection is one undifferentiated memory; the tag filter that exists keeps untagged entries by default, which means it fails open; the whole repository carries one test file of two cases against 98,482 lines of Python, and the paper's headline numbers have their harness committed but no result

Memory unit.value: A SourceDocument: for hook capture, a short Request/Result/Affected paths record per Stop, PreCompact or SessionEnd; for the memory API, one message per row; for the workspace, one file. Claims are regex-extracted from its sentences at refresh

Storage backend.value: Per-project directories under .lint-ai: memory for captured sessions, workspace-memory for indexed project files. Each holds pretty-printed records.json, a binary core, a segment manifest and Tantivy segments

Retrieval strategy.value: Tantivy BM25 over a query augmented with focus terms and entities, per-session segment routing, temporal scoring, optional conversational rerank and spaCy relation facts. Superseded documents are removed from the candidate set before ranking unless the query reads as historical

Write strategy.value: Automatic: lifecycle hooks capture the last user request and assistant result, redacted and capped at 1,500 bytes per field. Explicit: MCP add_memory, HTTP /add, Python Memory.add. Key phrases are extracted in the background

Update/delete model.value: HTTP and Python update, delete, supersede and expire act on rows owned by a user id. The agent's MCP surface has add and get only, and hook-captured records carry no user id, so nothing deletes them. Supersession is also inferred at refresh from claim chains, correction words and timestamps

Scoping model.value: Physical per project for agent memory, with provider as an optional filter. memory_user_id is a keyed filter on the memory API, skipped on search when empty

Agent integration.value: Capture and recall hooks for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, AGY and OpenClaw, event recording only for Muse Code, a Hermes plugin over the HTTP API; per-provider MCP servers with search, list_memories, add_memory, get_memory, a bulletin board and recording controls; a loopback HTTP server; Python bindings

Background processing.value: A key-phrase worker per process, backfilled synchronously at query time for short-lived hook processes; incremental rebuild of claims, relations and a temporal fact table on every refresh

Trust/provenance model.value: A derived SemanticStatus of current, superseded, conflicted or historical per document, recomputed from content at refresh. Only superseded is filtered; conflicted is annotated on MCP search results and absent from hook-injected context

Notable strengths.value: One prepared-query executor reached by CLI, IndexStore, hook and MCP entries, so the supersession filter cannot be skipped by an entry point; history queries invert the filter; captured revision and ancestry status are printed beside each injected memory; an incremental relation store differential-tested against a full rebuild; a test that fails the build on a store bypass

Main risks.value: Inferred supersession suppresses only single-claim documents, so captured session memories are at most marked conflicted and the hook drops that mark; a capture that outlives the 2-second hook budget is abandoned; nothing can correct or delete a hook-captured record; expiry is filtered after ranking; the temporal fact table is rebuilt every refresh and read by nothing

Memory unit.value: One Postgres row per memory: content, type (episodic, semantic, procedural, relational), tags, importance, emotion, source with a confidence derived from it, access counters. A RAM-only concept node mirrors its first 120 characters

Storage backend.value: PostgreSQL over a hardcoded Unix-socket URL, schema re-applied on every boot; an in-process thermal substrate and hot pool that start empty with each process; identity rows mirrored to identity/journal.json

Write strategy.value: HTTP learn, inject, trace, inbox and session routes plus some twenty-five call sites inside the runtime and its scripts, one of them a heartbeat row every 30 seconds; a synchronous insert with no extraction on the write path

Update/delete model.value: No update or delete route. Every recall decays confidence 5 percent and bumps access counts; old, thrice-read episodic rows become semantic; an evening or night dream pass hard-deletes weak agent-tagged rows from the last 24 hours. No tombstone

Scoping model.value: None on the agent paths. A session tag is written by several routes and filtered only by a standalone curriculum script; one database serves every caller

Agent integration.value: FastAPI on 0.0.0.0:8008 with no auth; CSM's OpenCode plugin reads GET /api/agent/context for hormone, circadian and interoception state and ignores its memories; the Python client the README names is not in the tree

Background processing.value: A 10-second pulse loop writes heartbeat rows, ticks the substrate every 100 seconds and dreams every 200 seconds, storing LLM hypotheses as identity memories; a 60-second heartbeat runs an idle REM cycle whose third phase selects from a table no DDL creates

Trust/provenance model.value: None as a filter. source maps to a confidence float that no read path consults; LLM dreams and crystal copies carry the identity tag, which exempts them from the only prune

Memory unit.value: A memory row: one of six kinds (preference, fact, decision, task_state, handoff, note) with a title, up to 8,000 characters of content, tags, an importance from 1 to 3, an author, an archive timestamp, an optional expiry, a uuid shared across databases, and typed links to other rows

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file in WAL mode: memories, an external-content FTS5 index kept by triggers, a history table of full snapshots, a links table, an optional table of float32 embeddings per model, and a meta table holding the database's instance id

Retrieval strategy.value: A session briefing assembled by kind and importance inside a character budget, and a search that runs FTS5 bm25 with prefix terms, AND then OR, optionally fused by reciprocal rank with a brute-force cosine scan

Write strategy.value: The model's explicit tool call, or a person at the CLI or web UI, or a CLI merge of another machine's export. No extraction and no model call; a write is one synchronous transaction and is readable by the next query

Update/delete model.value: An update patches the row and appends a snapshot; forget sets an archive timestamp; supersedes archives the old rows and links them in the same transaction; a merge replaces a row whole with the version carrying the later updated_at; hard delete is one CLI verb that removes rows archived before a date

Scoping model.value: A namespace per project plus a shared global one, applied as an equality filter when supplied and always by the briefing; one user, no principals

Agent integration.value: An MCP server over stdio or Streamable HTTP with eight tools, two resources and two prompts; session-start, pre-compaction and stop hooks for three clients; a CLI with export, import and merge, and a local web UI

Background processing.value: None. Embeddings are caught up 64 at a time inside a search; expired rows are filtered at read time and archived only when a person runs gc

Trust/provenance model.value: None as a state. A row is active or archived, the reason for archiving lives in the history snapshot, and importance is a number the writer picks

Notable strengths.value: History written in the same transaction as every tool, CLI and UI mutation, namespace moves and link edits included, without touching the recency the briefing ranks by; an archive predicate shared by every read arm; hard delete, restore and removal of a supersedes link kept off the tool surface; the author taken from the MCP handshake; and a vector stored only if the row still holds the text it was computed from

Main risks.value: An importance-3 row in the global namespace enters every project's briefing; a merge between machines is whole-row last-writer-wins on wall-clock updated_at, so a namespace move reaches the other machine only when the new name sorts after the old, a later edit on the other machine un-archives a forgotten row, and a purge comes back; a purge deletes the history with the row; with embeddings on, a recall with no namespace sends every namespace's active memories and reindex sends archived ones

Trust/provenance model.value: None. Confidence is a caller-set float that is stored, exported and compared by the contradiction scan but never filters; verified columns have no interactive writer

Notable strengths.value: Row and vector commit atomically; a fuzzy merge that overwrote unrelated learnings was removed and its test rebuilt to fail if it returns; retired observations stay queryable as of a date; import validates every record with the interactive schemas and canonicalises ids; search reports when it downgraded from hybrid to FTS

Main risks.value: An archived learning is re-stored verbatim as a new live row; export then import drops every learning archived with a reason; reflect calls a learning never recalled when nothing records recall; the importance boost has no interactive producer; entity_delete leaves the entity's own vector

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A row with content, a SHA-256 content hash, free JSON metadata that also carries a reinforcement accumulator, an embedding, tags, an importance from 1 to 10, a memory type, and created, updated and last-accessed timestamps

Storage backend.value: SQLite through `sql.js` compiled to WebAssembly, loaded into memory once at start and exported as a whole file on every persist, with no lock and no reload; a `schema_meta` version whose mismatch drops the memories table

Retrieval strategy.value: In-process cosine over `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` embeddings of every row, ranked by similarity alone; type and tag listings ordered by stored importance; a creation-date range

Write strategy.value: `save_memory` with exact-content dedup — a repeat throws naming the existing memory's id — and `update_memory`, which overwrites content, metadata, tags, importance or type in place

Update/delete model.value: Half-life decay per memory type with per-type floors and protected tags, applied lazily on access; hard `delete_memory` by id and `delete_all_memories`; deleted rows survive in the automatic backup snapshots until ten later ones prune them

Scoping model.value: None in the store. One database file shared by every client and project unless `MEMORY_DB_PATH` points elsewhere; the companion skill writes the project name into the content as a prefix and a tag, and nothing filters on either

Agent integration.value: An MCP server launched by an unpinned `npx -y`, with a Claude Code plugin that installs the server and a companion skill telling the model to recall at session start and save after tasks, silently

Background processing.value: No timer. Decay and reinforcement are computed on access; a copy of the database file and a JSON export run on save — the first save in each process, then every 24 hours or at a count that is a multiple of 100 — keeping ten

Trust/provenance model.value: Nothing epistemic. Protected tags exempt a memory from decay; the schema version protects the code from an old file by discarding the file's memories

Notable strengths.value: The forgetting policy is one table: half-lives of 10, 30, 45, 60, 90 and 120 days for ephemeral, task, conversation, general, preference and fact, a floor per type, and a protected-tag set (`core`, `identity`, `pinned`) that exempts a memory entirely. `computeDecay` is exponential on idle days, rounded to the nearest half point and clamped to the floor, and every constant sits in `DECAY_CONFIG` under a name. Reinforcement banks 0.1 per access in an accumulator and moves importance only at 0.5. Dedup throws with the colliding memory's id, so the caller knows what to update

Main risks.value: Every non-protected read writes. `applyDecayAndReinforcement` updates the accumulator and `last_accessed` and exports the whole database file, and `search_memory` runs it for every candidate above the similarity threshold before the limit is applied. Each server process loads the file once and writes its own copy back with no lock, so two sessions on the shared default file overwrite each other's saves. A schema version mismatch in either direction drops the memories table, by design and under test. Decay below the half-point step is discarded, because the access that skipped it resets the idle clock. Nothing is epistemic: no status, provenance, supersession, validity interval or change record, and updates overwrite

Memory unit.value: A fact — subject, predicate, object, a display form, a valid window, a recorded time, supersession columns, a source type, the note path and block anchor it came from, and a confidence — written as a markdown line and replayed into a row

Storage backend.value: A markdown vault as the durable store, with a SQLite index of notes, blocks, links, entities, mentions, edges, facts, fact links, embeddings and an access log, rebuilt from the vault whenever an index sees a changed note

Retrieval strategy.value: Lexical search over blocks, embeddings, and a graph of entity mentions, co-occurrence and current-fact edges, with a rerank stage and a retrievability decay fitted from the vault's own access history; facts are queried by slot, as of a valid date, or as known at a record date

Write strategy.value: lore assert and lore invalidate from the CLI, lore_assert_fact and lore_invalidate_fact over MCP, a capture path that appends timestamped bullets to any vault note, and extraction from frontmatter and field syntax in any note

Update/delete model.value: A new value closes the slot's previous one; an invalidate line closes the current value at a date; nothing deletes a fact, and removing one means removing its markdown line or the note field it was extracted from

Scoping model.value: None — the vault is the boundary; search takes optional folder and tag facets chosen by the caller, and no fact carries a scope key

Agent integration.value: A lore CLI, an MCP server with fifteen tools, a file watcher, and a session-resume delta computed from record time

Background processing.value: A dream pass that consolidates, proposes links, writes a digest and a review-queue note, and fits the vault's forgetting-curve shape from its own retrieved-then-used history

Trust/provenance model.value: Provenance on every fact through the note path and block anchor it came from, a stated, extracted or inferred source type honoured from a line only under lore/journal, and a confidence; supersession closes rather than overwrites

Notable strengths.value: The authoritative artifact is the user's markdown, and the index is a replay that can be wiped. Assertions and closures are appended to a dated journal before any row changes, and a rebuild reproduces the same fact state, which a test pins. The code refuses inputs it cannot make meaningful and says why: a subject that normalises to an empty key, a close before its start. Totals are returned rather than requested: a capped fact query or aggregate reports how many matched, because the bug each replaces was a caller not asking. Commit messages carry the reproduction for each fix, with the measured output before and after

Main risks.value: There is no scope of any kind, so two agents sharing a vault share every fact in it. The record-time axis has gaps. valid_until is one column rewritten by each close, so asOf combined with an earlier asKnownAt answers from a close learned afterwards. An invalidate records no transaction time. An extracted fact's recorded_at is its note's modification time, and a recorded_at attribute in any note is believed. By reading, an invalidate on a slot held only by an extracted fact is lost at the next replay, because extraction inserts after the journal's closes are applied. source_type withholds nothing from retrieval. The only adjudication surface is an MCP tool description addressed to the model

Memory unit.value: One version of one file, addressed by the SHA-256 of its content, with a git blob sha1 beside it and an event recording when and how the agent came to see it

Storage backend.value: A content-addressed blob store on disk plus per-writer append-only JSONL event logs, and per-session working-set manifests under a context root

Retrieval strategy.value: Rank and re-emit rather than search: `restore_context` replays the ranked working set from current disk state under a token budget, packs rank stable hot files across sessions, and receipts resolve exact versions

Write strategy.value: Hook-fed. A PreCompact sweep parses the session transcript and archives every file the session touched — native Read/Edit/Write included, not only MCP reads — and blob writes are content-addressed, idempotent, temp-file-then-rename

Background processing.value: None scheduled. The sweep runs on the compaction path and is benchmarked to sit there — one 14 MB transcript in 361 ms

Trust/provenance model.value: No epistemic state on content. What the system tracks instead is whether the model has actually seen the current version of a file, and it refuses an edit when it has not

Notable strengths.value: A benchmark that publishes the project's own negative result on the realistic workload, with losslessness as a mandatory second metric proved by byte-for-byte reconstruction after every operation

Main risks.value: The compression premise does not pay on real sessions by the project's own measurement, and the value that remains — restore, coordination, receipts — is the part the benchmark does not score

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Two shapes in one database. A wiki `Page` — slug, title, an optional kind and summary, a Markdown body whose `[[slug]]` links become edges, the paths of the sources supporting it, an ordered `provenance` list, created and updated. And a `memory_event` — a 64-character fingerprint, an event type, a context, `occurred_at`, `recorded_at`, an optional validity interval, a `pinned` flag and a logical byte count — with `memory_fragments` typed `observed`, `decision`, `constraint`, `learned`, `unresolved` or `outcome`, `memory_changes` holding a subject with its before and after values and a reason, `memory_evidence` holding a reference and an excerpt, and `memory_relations` typed `supersedes`, `contradicts`, `resolves`, `supports` or `related`

Storage backend.value: SQLite with a versioned migration chain, one database per scope: `.lwc/wiki.db` under the project root and a separate store under the home directory. There is no scope column — `Scope::Project` and `Scope::Global` resolve to different files and `Scope::All` opens both read-only. An FTS5 contentless index sits over the memory events, and changesets and checkpoints sit over the wiki

Retrieval strategy.value: Two arms. The wiki search is weighted lexical with graph awareness — title thirty-two, path sixteen, generic eight, a graph-match and a graph-hub term — and decorates each result with the page's provenance. Memory recall is FTS5 `bm25` with column weights, bounded by a configured age window and optional `since`/`until` on event time, with every candidate resolved forward through the `supersedes` chain and re-ranked by a feedback score clamped to plus or minus three

Write strategy.value: An agent drives it as a CLI or over MCP. A page cites its sources with a repeated `--source` and declares `--provenance` otherwise; a citation adds `source-grounded` automatically. A memory event is a capsule of JSON — `remember` — deduplicated by a 64-character fingerprint and idempotent under a `request_id`, where a replayed request with a changed payload conflicts instead of mutating. A semantic wiki relation is refused unless its type is one of six, its provenance one of four, its reason non-empty and its confidence a finite number in zero-to-one

Update/delete model.value: Supersession rather than deletion at the memory layer: a new event points a `supersedes` edge at the old one, recall returns the successor, and the old event stays reachable behind an explicit flag. Retention does delete — an age pass evicts events past the configured window and a byte-budget pass evicts the oldest, both skipping anything pinned or carrying an unresolved fragment, with the counts kept in a `memory_state` row. The wiki layer has changesets with restore and rollback

Scoping model.value: Physical rather than keyed. A project store and a global store are separate SQLite files chosen by a `Scope` enum, and `Scope::All` reads both and labels each result with the store it came from. No record carries a scope key and no query filters on one, so this partitions the way a per-project configuration directory does rather than the way a tenant column does

Agent integration.value: A CLI on npm as `@i-xor/lwc` and on crates.io as `lwc`, an MCP server, and a published skill; documented for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Kiro, Hermes, Antigravity, Copilot in VS Code, Copilot CLI, Copilot for JetBrains and pi. READMEs in seven languages

Background processing.value: A hint engine runs inside every `remember`: it returns up to three prompts to the agent — a `contradicts` or `supersedes` edge needing review, five or more events sharing an exact type and context, an unresolved fragment older than fourteen days, and storage past eighty per cent of the byte budget — each suppressed by a seven-day cooldown row that a prune pass clears when it expires. Beside it, age and capacity eviction, ingest jobs with a status ladder, checkpoints, and a git-backed sync

Trust/provenance model.value: Three separate vocabularies. The wiki has a four-value ordered provenance — `source-grounded`, `user-provided`, `agent-observed`, `hypothesis` — rejected at the boundary if unrecognised, decorated onto every search result, and filtered on nowhere. Memory events have `latest_known` versus `superseded`, resolved from the relation graph on every recall and used to drop the replaced event, beside an `unresolved_conflict` flag and a `live_verified` field pinned to `false`. And `memory_feedback` records a `useful` or `not-useful` signal with a mandatory reason, aggregated into an integer clamped to plus or minus three that adjusts rank by five per cent and never excludes anything

Notable strengths.value: A recall that walks the supersession chain and hands back the replacement, with the history one flag away and each result labelled; a provenance vocabulary that names a hypothesis as a hypothesis and refuses an unrecognised value; retention that protects pinned events and anything still marked unresolved, so the open questions are the last thing forgotten; benchmark adapters that pin the upstream by commit and the dataset by content hash and stamp a limited run `partial=true`; an operations log written through one helper from fifty-four sites; a mandatory reason on a wiki relation and on a feedback signal alike

Main risks.value: The wiki's provenance ladder is stored, ordered, validated and attached to every result, and no read path acts on it, so a hypothesis ranks like a cited fact; `valid_from` and `valid_until` are written, cross-validated and returned but appear in no `WHERE`, so the explicit validity interval is a column rather than a mechanism; `recorded_at` is never a predicate, so there is no as-of-record-time query; scope is a choice of database file rather than a key, so nothing partitions two callers sharing a store; the memory layer is off unless a scope enables it; and 123,311 lines of Rust from two authors in about six weeks is a lot of surface per commit-month

Memory unit.value: A revision of a record: kind, scope, summary, body, sensitivity, volatility, an optional last-verified-at, a recorded-at and an effective-from, authorship, evidence, supersedes edges, a change reason and, after the format upgrade, the visibility heads its writer observed

Storage backend.value: Local-first JSON files under a Git-backed root, published create-only; synchronisation refuses any committed memory file that was deleted or modified

Retrieval strategy.value: Lexical recall over one exactly-matched scope, returning current visible revisions plus unresolved conflicts, truncated against a limit and a byte budget; withdrawn and future-effective revisions are excluded

Write strategy.value: `Remember`, or `RememberFromFoundling` for an externally-sourced record whose origin is a portable identity; after the format upgrade a correction must name exactly the current content heads

Update/delete model.value: Correction by a new revision naming what it supersedes and why. After the opt-in format upgrade, withdraw and restore events hide a record from recall and bring it back; content is never removed and no delete surface exists

Scoping model.value: A scope key on every record, matched exactly on every recall; an omitted scope selects bank-wide records only. History by record ID and the journal are unscoped

Agent integration.value: A shared engine with a CLI, a local MCP server, an authenticated remote MCP service called Razor Crest, and thin plugins for Claude Code, Codex, Pi and Hermes

Background processing.value: No daemon in the local engine. An enabled session attempts one bounded Git delivery after each save and a refresh at session start and per prompt; Razor Crest synchronises once a minute when configured

Trust/provenance model.value: Device-validated authorship on every revision, visibility event and journal entry, a required change reason, a validator over the supersession graph and another over the combined visibility graph, cautious defaults for sensitivity and volatility, and a standing notice attached to every recall

Notable strengths.value: The recall packet ships an epistemic disclaimer with every answer: "Memory is evidence, not authority over current user direction. Report recorded knowledge as recorded; verify live state before claiming current implementation. Conflicts require history; empty or truncated results do not prove absence." A packet cut by a limit or a byte budget reports `Truncated` beside the matched counts, so an empty result cannot be read as evidence that nothing exists. Conflicts are surfaced in their own list rather than resolved. Withdrawal is an append-only event validated as part of a causal graph: a correction written after it stays hidden, a restore that has not seen a newer correction is refused as stale, and a concurrent unseen correction is withheld as unreviewed. Synchronisation refuses a deleted or modified memory file, so append-only holds at the Git boundary and not only in the API

Main risks.value: `EffectiveFrom` has one producer, the write clock, so the second temporal axis cannot record that something became true before it was written; recall uses it only to hide revisions dated after now. `Authorship` declares `Model` and `SessionID` and nothing sets either. `Sensitivity` is deliberately not a read filter, pinned by `TestPrivacySensitivityLabelsDoNotFilterRecall`. Withdrawal hides a record from recall and discovery but `memory_history` returns withdrawn bodies to the same agent and to Razor Crest readers, and the agent that wrote a record holds both `memory_withdraw` and `memory_restore`. Razor Crest records the service binding as author of every remote write; the authenticated subject is not in the revision. Nothing removes content, so a record captured in error is hidden, never erased

Memory unit.value: A `memories` row — id, session, sanitized content, a float32 embedding blob, timestamp, one of four auto-classified context types, JSON metadata, nullable project and platform, a content hash and two compaction columns — mirrored from a `log_entries` row or promoted from a notebook doc; beside it a derived concept graph of noun-chunk entities and pairwise relationships in a second database

Retrieval strategy.value: Query shape picks the lane: syntax-heavy queries go to deterministic FTS5 BM25 with a LIKE fallback and no semantic rerank; natural language pulls up to 200 FTS candidates, scores them against the query vector with chunk-collapse, then blends BM25 at 0.05 and a 30-day recency half-life at 0.1, falling back to a bounded 10,000-row embedding scan with an explicit truncation flag

Write strategy.value: Only `marm_log_entry` puts agent text into semantic memory, dual-writing a log row and a memory row through a single-worker async queue; embedding is computed on the request, chunk embeddings after it. Exact-hash and semantic-merge consolidation exist but are off unless `CONSOLIDATION_ENABLED=1`

Update/delete model.value: Hard delete only: deleting a log entry or session also deletes its mirrored memory rows by `metadata.log_entry_id`; the Console deletes memory rows directly, restoring compaction sources and pruning the summary's source list. Compaction supersedes by setting `compaction_role='source'`, which every read query excludes. Concept entities have a real correction path — merge to an alias, dismiss a pair, or remove with a durable name suppression

Scoping model.value: `session_name` filtered by default and `project`/`platform` filtered when the caller names them, on all four read queries. The write side is process-global: `MARM_PROJECT` is the server's working-directory name resolved once at import, and no agent-facing tool can override it

Agent integration.value: One FastAPI app exposing 14 MCP tools over HTTP via fastapi-mcp and the same 14 over STDIO via FastMCP, plus a runtime CLI, a bundled React Console with an embedded PTY, a Docker image, and a skill installer for detected agent harnesses

Background processing.value: A single-worker write queue; a durable concept-index outbox drained about 30 seconds after a write; a code-graph auto-index poller with a filesystem watcher and a git content signature; a delayed compaction scan per session; both index workers coordinated across transports by leased rows in the memory database

Trust/provenance model.value: None at the memory layer — no trust field, no confidence, no provenance beyond `metadata.source`. Prompt-injection defence is a paragraph in the injected protocol asking the model to treat retrieved memories as context rather than instructions, plus an HTML-escaping sanitizer applied to every stored memory

Notable strengths.value: A value-keyed entity suppression that a full graph rebuild cannot undo, a deliberate exact-lexical lane for config keys and file paths that never gets semantically reranked, cross-process serialization by leased database row rather than in-process lock, a durable outbox that commits the indexing task with the memory, and a README that publishes its own negative results

Main risks.value: Every stored memory is HTML-escaped with no inverse anywhere, so code and config come back as `<` and `&`; the write-side project scope is the server's own working directory, so a shared HTTP server tags every agent's memories with one project the recall filter then splits on; concept extraction turns every noun chunk into an entity and every pair of the first 25 into an edge; and the `causes` predicate is unreachable for the verb *cause* because `uses` matches it first

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Two units: a dated observation group derived from raw messages, and a knowledge record — text about a node, with a scope, a stamped ceiling, a capture time and an optional validity time

Storage backend.value: Mastra storage adapters. The knowledge domain adds nodes, records, mentions, an activity log and a semantic outbox, with the record bound and the description bound part of the storage contract every adapter enforces

Retrieval strategy.value: Sequential active observations plus a recent raw tail for the context path; for the graph, scope-filtered listings by node, mention and relation, with a semantic index maintained through an outbox

Write strategy.value: Processor observes at token thresholds; reflector compacts observations

Update/delete model.value: Range replacement and buffered activation for observations. Knowledge records are immutable — an edit is a remove plus an append — and removal is a soft delete stamping `deletedAt` and `deletedBy`; the curator has no tool to restore or physically erase one

Scoping model.value: `org` < `resource` < `thread`, applied as a filter on every graph read, plus a per-record `maxScope` ceiling re-checked on append and rescope and raisable only through a dedicated call

Agent integration.value: Deep Mastra input/output processor integration

Background processing.value: Early async observation and reflection buffers with activation, plus a subconscious of observation agents (capture, remind) and reflection agents (curate, learn) over a worklist whose cursor advances only on completion

Trust/provenance model.value: None as a field. A knowledge record carries free-form `metadata` holding the capture agent's stated reason, and no status, confidence or verification anywhere

Notable strengths.value: A ceiling that caps how widely a record may ever be shared, re-checked on every rescope; an activity log of every mutation on the storage base class; a rescope that re-enqueues the semantic index for both the old and the new scope, so the vector view follows the permission change

Main risks.value: Distributed locking and progressive summary drift, and a soft delete that nothing consults on the capture path — a curator removes a superseded record and the next observation of the same fact writes a new one

Storage backend.value: SQLite through Drizzle with a hand-maintained `memories_fts` FTS5 table beside it; a markdown export exists and nothing outside the tests calls it

Retrieval strategy.value: FTS5 with the query's terms joined by `OR`, ordered by rank, ten results by default, with an optional exact-match filter on category

Write strategy.value: A regex extractor over user messages only — nine patterns, no model — plus a direct `remember` on the store; a repeat of identical content updates the existing row rather than inserting

Update/delete model.value: `forget(id)` deletes the FTS row and then the record; there is no update path for content, no supersession and no record of what was removed

Scoping model.value: None. The table has no user, agent, session, project or tenant column, and no read path filters on one

Agent integration.value: A kernel memory store reached over IPC, a gateway extractor on the message path, and a `memory_search` tool

Background processing.value: None for memory. Extraction runs inline on the message path

Trust/provenance model.value: None. `category` names a kind rather than a status, there is no confidence field, and a pattern hit is stored with the same standing as a deliberate `remember`

Notable strengths.value: Capture costs no model call and is deterministic; the FTS projection is maintained on both write and delete; and the memory tests run about two lines of test per line of implementation

Main risks.value: Two of the nine capture patterns match ordinary conversational filler and there is no confidence, review or trust state to mark the result, so a false capture is durable and indistinguishable from a real one; `exportToFiles` has no caller outside the test suite

Memory unit.value: Not defined here. The SDKs address memories, user and customer contexts, conversations and profiles on the Synap service

Storage backend.value: Delegated to the hosted Synap service; this repository is clients, connectors, MCP servers and integrations synced out of a private monorepo

Retrieval strategy.value: Delegated. The SDK offers `fetch` against user, customer and conversation contexts, and an `as_tool` surface that hands the agent a retrieval tool

Write strategy.value: `memories.create`, `create_from_file`, `conversation.record_message` and `ingest_transcript`, all posted to the service

Update/delete model.value: Not exercised in the client surface read here

Scoping model.value: A B2C/B2B identifier contract validated client-side: on a B2C instance `user_id` is the whole identity and a `customer_id` is refused before the call is made; the isolation mode comes from `GET /api/v1/auth/whoami`, and an unknown mode deliberately refuses nothing

Agent integration.value: Python and TypeScript SDKs on PyPI and npm, plus MCP servers, connectors and a generated table of framework integrations

Background processing.value: None client-side

Trust/provenance model.value: The identifier contract and its call-site guard; the server is described as authoritative and rejecting independently

Notable strengths.value: `scoping.py` is a model of documenting why a guard exists: it names the failure it prevents — a `customer_id` sent to a B2C instance filed the write under the customer while the read asked for the user, both returning success — and quantifies it, "[o]ne client ran 4,634 consecutive empty fetches across seven days without a single error to look at", before stating the principle: "[a]n SDK that stays silent about a misuse it can see is not being permissive, it is hiding the bug." Its unknown-mode branch fails open on purpose, with the reasoning written down. And the Python suite enforces coverage structurally: `test_every_public_method_taking_a_customer_id_checks_it` parses the package's own AST, enumerates every public method taking a `customer_id`, and asserts each calls the check, with a justified exemption list and a `test_the_guard_is_not_vacuous` control so the rule cannot "pass for the wrong reason"

Main risks.value: The TypeScript SDK ships the same `checkCustomerId` and applies it at five call sites — context fetch, two conversation paths, two memory-create paths — and has no equivalent coverage test. The surfaces it misses include the two closest to the original failure: `user/interface.ts` `get_profile` reads `customer_id` or `customerId` from its options and forwards it as a query parameter without checking, and `tool/as-tool.ts` builds three request bodies carrying `customer_id` with no check anywhere in the file, while the Python SDK guards both. A JavaScript caller can therefore still produce the silent empty read the module was written to prevent. The store itself is hosted and closed: no memory mechanism — schema, ranking, consolidation, forgetting — is inspectable from this repository, and the README states it is generated and synced out of a private monorepo

Memory unit.value: A context entry: text or text plus images, a source of user or agent, JSON metadata, a tag set, an LLM summary, chunk embeddings and optional per-heading node summaries

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A `Memory` — content, a `content_hash` that is its identity, a tag list, an optional `memory_type` validated against an ontology and canonicalised so `Decision` and `decision` are one type on disk, a free metadata dict, an optional embedding, and `created_at`/`updated_at` in both float and ISO form beside a legacy `timestamp`. Quarantine, belief membership and archival status all live in that metadata dict rather than in typed columns

Storage backend.value: A backend chosen at runtime: SQLite-vec, Cloudflare, Milvus, or a hybrid that combines them, behind a `MemoryStorage` base with a migration runner and shared mixins. A separate graph store backs relationship inference. Forgetting archives to a filesystem tree under `~/.mcp_memory_archive` rather than deleting

Retrieval strategy.value: Semantic search over the backend's vector index with tag and time filters, plus a scoring package and a reasoning layer. `search_by_tag` is the tag path. Twenty-eight MCP tools front it. No scope key is applied by the server: a `proj:` or `user:` tag is a convention a caller may filter on, not a predicate the read path enforces

Write strategy.value: `store_memory` over MCP hashes the content, validates the `memory_type` against the ontology — warning and defaulting to `observation` when it does not match — checks tag namespaces and logs the invalid ones without rejecting, then writes. A contradiction check may follow and quarantine the new memory, which the write response reports as *"⚠️ Memory quarantined: contradicts an active belief"*

Update/delete model.value: Deletion by content hash and by tag. Consolidation is the interesting path: a decay score, a compression pass, and a forgetting pass that archives rather than deletes, writing to a daily archive tree outside the store. Quarantine marks a contradicting memory with metadata and a `quarantined` tag; `unquarantine_memory` clears both

Scoping model.value: None enforced. `TagTaxonomy` defines six namespaces — `sys:`, `q:`, `proj:`, `topic:`, `t:`, `user:` — and validates them at write time by logging the tags that do not match, with legacy unnamespaced tags explicitly still supported. Nothing on the read path filters on a namespace, so `proj:` and `user:` are a convention rather than a boundary

Agent integration.value: Twenty-eight MCP tools, a REST API, a web surface with OAuth, a CLI, ingestion and harvest paths, a sync package, health checks and a backup module. Distributed for several agent harnesses with a discovery mechanism

Background processing.value: A consolidation scheduler running associations, clustering, compression, decay, forgetting, insights, belief derivation, contradiction detection and relationship inference, with a run tracker and a health module. each concern is its own module rather than one consolidation pass

Trust/provenance model.value: Two layers with different answers. A belief carries a typed, indexed `status` of `candidate`, `active`, `superseded` or `disputed` in its own table, promoted only when confidence clears a floor and the supporting count clears a provenance floor, demoted when confidence falls back, and read with `WHERE status = ? AND confidence >= ?` — so a candidate, superseded or disputed belief is excluded. A memory carries no status: the contradiction detector quarantines one that disagrees with an active belief by writing a metadata flag and a tag, with a threshold defaulting to three, and no retrieval path consults either, so a quarantined memory continues to be returned by search

Notable strengths.value: A belief ladder with two floors to promote and one to demote, filtered in SQL rather than scored; a consolidation package that models associations, decay, compression, forgetting, belief and contradiction as separate concerns with their own modules and a run tracker; forgetting that archives to a dated tree instead of deleting; a memory-type ontology that canonicalises spellings so a filter matches either; committed LoCoMo and LongMemEval harnesses with no score asserted without them; a retrieval test that asserts a non-empty result and a present control before asserting what is absent

Main risks.value: The memory row skips the pattern the belief table demonstrates — the quarantine writes a flag no read path consults, so the mechanism that detects a contradiction does not stop the contradicting memory being retrieved; every epistemic attribute lives in an untyped metadata dict rather than a column, so nothing at the storage layer can enforce or index it; no scope key is applied, so a multi-project or multi-user deployment separates memories only by a tag a caller must remember to filter on; `storage/base.py` carries an MIT licence header while the repository ships Apache-2.0

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: An OKF v0.2 record — a markdown document with YAML frontmatter (type, key, namespace, tags, status, verified, stale_after, sources, generated) — stored as an okf_payload TEXT column and mirrored to a .md file

Storage backend.value: One per-project SQLite database (WAL) with an FTS5 mirror; the OKF markdown files on disk are a human-browseable copy written after the DB commit, never read back

Retrieval strategy.value: FTS5 prefix search ordered by rank, or updated_at DESC with no query; tags filtered in Python after the fetch; exact key+namespace lookup; no vector or semantic search

Write strategy.value: memory_store upserts by (key, namespace) via ON CONFLICT, overwriting content in place with no version history; each store and delete adds a dated line to log.md; a system/last_memory checkpoint carries continuity across sessions

Update/delete model.value: Update is an in-place upsert; delete is a hard DELETE plus os.remove of the .md; deprecation is a status string that nothing reads, and re-storing deleted content is always accepted

Scoping model.value: namespace is a key on every row and a predicate on retrieve and delete, but an optional argument on search, which spans every namespace when it is omitted; project_root selects one SQLite file per project, a physical partition with no project key on a row

Agent integration.value: A FastMCP server exposing six tools (store, retrieve, search, delete, get_last, update_last); each call takes a project_root to locate the per-project store; stdlib sqlite3, no external services

Background processing.value: None — every operation is synchronous within the tool call; no daemon, extraction, consolidation or decay

Trust/provenance model.value: OKF status (draft/stable/deprecated, silently coerced to stable), a verified actor-event list, and stale_after are all serialized into frontmatter and read by no retrieval or gating path

Notable strengths.value: A small, self-contained, dependency-light MCP memory server whose store is human-readable OKF markdown mirrored to disk, with a dated change log beside it

Main risks.value: The OKF trust and lifecycle model is write-only — verified, status and stale_after are stored faithfully and consulted nowhere; the conformance validator is never called on the write path; and an unqualified search reads every namespace

Memory unit.value: A concept node with name, one of six kinds, summary, why, file_refs, parent_id and created_by_task, plus a 384-dimension embedding; typed edges in five relations between nodes

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file per working directory through libsql, .megamemory/knowledge.db or MEGAMEMORY_DB_PATH, in WAL mode; embeddings are float32 blobs on the node row

Retrieval strategy.value: understand embeds the query in process with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 and scores every active node by cosine, top_k default 10, no threshold; get_concept by exact id; list_roots for the top level. Each hit carries children, edges both ways and the parent

Write strategy.value: Explicit MCP tools the agent calls after a task: create_concept, update_concept, link. The id is a slug of the name under the parent id. Installed instructions tell the agent to query before work and record after

Update/delete model.value: update_concept overwrites fields in place and keeps no prior value; remove_concept sets removed_at and a reason and hard-deletes the node's edges; no tool removes a single edge; conflict resolution hard-deletes the losing copy

Scoping model.value: Physical: one database per project directory. No scope key on any row and no predicate on any read

Agent integration.value: A stdio MCP server with nine tools; an installer writing MCP config and workflow instructions for opencode, Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity; bootstrap and save slash commands; a read-only web explorer with a time slider

Background processing.value: None. A two-way merge command for knowledge.db files that diverged on branches keeps conflicting concepts as suffixed copies until resolved

Trust/provenance model.value: None. Every active node is returned as fact; unresolved merge copies are searched like any other node, and the agent resolves conflicts itself

Notable strengths.value: Small and legible; soft delete with a stored reason, filtered on every agent read; a per-call timeline table; a merge that raises removal conflicts instead of dropping them; no API key and no network after the model download

Main risks.value: Removing a concept makes its name unusable under that parent, refused with a raw UNIQUE error; MCP resolve_conflict turns foreign keys off inside a transaction, where SQLite ignores the pragma; a default merge discards the timeline; the explorer binds every interface with open CORS

Memory unit.value: A topic — one markdown file, one question — whose body is an ordered list of links, newest first. A link is one ruling: date, status, kind, an optional reverses with a reason_for_change, a ruling and a rationale each carrying their own authority, alternatives with what was rejected and why, evidence, revisit_if, an optional checkable invariant, typed edges, and recorded_by and recorded_at. A topic may name some of its own links as standing. Beside topics sit concept records naming what the code already contains

Storage backend.value: Markdown under a git repository that is the store — topics/area/slug.md, and inbox/ for proposals — projected into a SQLite index with FTS5 and whole-record embeddings; a separate SQLite code index of chunked source; a per-session JSON edit ledger and a hook log rotated across a bounded number of files under MEMCONTINUUM_HOME

Retrieval strategy.value: for-path maps a file being edited to every topic whose code_refs cover it and returns the whole chain, every link regardless of status, with a note when a bound file or symbol differs from its captured baseline; it opens the index read-only and refuses one that needs migrating; on a miss the hook runs a labelled search on the path's words. A session-start digest delivers active owner-level links that topics name as standing. search is FTS5, vector or hybrid with a default status of active and inbox records excluded; an opt-in channel searches on the user's prompt; why walks path to concept to governing topics; context-pack prints the standing digest and the bound chains as one capped, fingerprinted block for a reviewer's brief

Write strategy.value: A person or an agent appends a link to a topic file and commits. Nothing extracts: there is no summariser and no consolidation pass. Three commands edit topic frontmatter by line insertion, print the diff and commit nothing: bind adds a code_ref with a hashed baseline, mark-standing changes standing with its audit row, anchor-backfill adds baselines to older refs. current is hand-set to the newest active link and the guard refuses it moving while the newest active link has not

Update/delete model.value: There is no update. A change of mind is a new link with reverses and a reason_for_change; the predecessor keeps its text and gains status superseded with superseded_by. Three lifecycle fields may each move forward once and only alone; every other field and the link's raw bytes are frozen against the last commit, and a removed link or a deleted record file is an error. standing, current, link order and anchor baselines are guarded; code_refs, title, tags and type are not

Scoping model.value: One store per repository: each is wired on its own with its own store root and project name, so several repositories run side by side and none reads another's rulings, and no two can share one. One decision database per project, enforced rather than assumed: records is keyed by path alone, so opening the same file under a second project is refused with the reason in the error. A project column sits on every record and most queries carry it; the chain read keys on the topic path. The code index is the multi-project store, keyed by path, project and code root

Agent integration.value: Claude Code hooks — a pre-edit lookup on Edit and Write with a search fallback, a post-edit ledger, session-start and user-prompt nudges with the standing digest and an opt-in prompt search, a code-index refresh at session start and turn end, a precompact persist, a session-end stamp — plus two skills, a rendered rules file that tells briefs to open with a context pack, a store-side git pre-commit and post-commit, an installer, an updater, and a per-machine registry of which repositories have a store

Background processing.value: None on the decisions. A post-commit hook reindexes, re-runs the commit checks and can write a verified git bundle backup; a background worker fills missing embeddings; a watchdog bounds each hook at two seconds, and the nudges are triggered by the edit ledger rather than by a timer

Trust/provenance model.value: Five authorities — owner-verbatim, owner-ratified, reviewer-finding, code-derived, agent-inference — carried per field, and five statuses. Together they select one of three citation tiers; the tier decides whether a violated invariant fails a manually run drift check, is reported, or is skipped, and only active owner-level links reach the standing digest. Cited commits and file:line references are checked against the code root at lint time. A changed-since-capture note on a bound reference is shown beside the chain and never changes a status or an authority

Notable strengths.value: An append-only guarantee enforced by a linter and a git hook rather than asserted, freezing new fields by default and raw bytes as well as parsed values, and extended to the standing list by pairing every change with a frozen audit row; an authority vocabulary where only the owner's own or ratified words may block work or ride in every session; a retrieval timeout and a search miss that each say what was not established; a public retrieval benchmark with a negative control

Memory unit.value: A document holding a captured conversation, owned through the machine it arrived from; a separate knowledge layer holds entity and relation rows carrying a direct user id

Storage backend.value: Postgres with pgvector, documents keyed to machines and machines to users, plus a separate embedding table and an access log

Retrieval strategy.value: Hybrid keyword and pgvector cosine, fused by reciprocal rank fusion with the constant cited to the original paper; the semantic branch returns empty on any failure so a slow embedding server degrades the endpoint to keyword rather than failing it

Write strategy.value: Collectors on each machine parse tool-native conversation formats and ship them to the server; redacted thinking blocks are recorded by size rather than content

Update/delete model.value: No supersession, no tombstone and no soft-delete column. Removing a document, a user or a device cascades to the access-log rows that reference it

Scoping model.value: Ownership runs through devices: every scoped read resolves the caller's machine ids once through a shared helper and filters on `machine_id`, with an empty list matching nothing and admin or owner bypassing the filter entirely

Agent integration.value: An MCP server mounted on the API, a web interface, and collectors for several coding tools across CLI, desktop and mobile

Background processing.value: Session compaction, title healing, orphaned-subagent repair and workspace extraction, each with its own test file

Trust/provenance model.value: None. Nothing carries a status, a confidence or a validity window; a memory is a record of what was said rather than a claim the system holds a position on

Notable strengths.value: The scope is resolved once and passed, so the keyword and semantic branches cannot disagree about the caller; the admin bypass is a return value decided in one function rather than a condition repeated at each call site; the empty-device case is documented as 'sees nothing' before anything depends on it; and the timeouts and constants carry the reasoning behind their values, including why a shorter embedding ceiling would produce false unavailability

Memory unit.value: One Markdown page with OKF v0.2 front matter under docs/global/{type}/{slug}.md or docs/projects/{folder}/{type}/{slug}.md; five built-in types, five catalogue knowledge types and project-declared custom types, each page carrying a status

Storage backend.value: The filesystem is the source of truth; SQLite FTS5 in `mem.db` is a disposable index rebuilt from the pages, and generated `index.md` files per directory serve as a second, index-free search surface

Retrieval strategy.value: Weighted BM25 over FTS5 with alphanumeric tokens, scaffolding phrases and stop words removed, matched with AND and retried with OR on zero rows; filtered to active pages inside their validity window, and to one project when project scope is requested

Write strategy.value: `memex_write(type, title, body, scope, description, tags, importance, links, parent, supersedes, depends_on, project_id, project_label)` — no slug field, so every call derives a new one; consolidation writes knowledge types as pending

Update/delete model.value: `forget` is `hard`, `soft` or `decay` from the model and also `archive` from the CLI; `approve`, `merge` and `import` are CLI-only. No tool on the model's surface changes an existing page's content: a repeated title becomes `title-2`

Scoping model.value: A `global` or `project` scope on every page, the project id a hash of the Git remote. Project recall filters on it; global recall, the default and the one the per-turn hooks use, returns every project's pages

Agent integration.value: Five MCP tools; per-turn injection hooks for pi and Claude Code, transcript capture for pi, Claude Code and Codex, and a CI workflow for Copilot

Background processing.value: An optional polling watcher re-indexing hand-edited pages; at capture, an episode summary from a spawned harness CLI and an opt-in consolidation; decay and consolidation otherwise explicit commands

Trust/provenance model.value: A four-value page status filtered on every recall path, a pending queue for consolidated knowledge, provenance from a page back to its transcript, reserved provenance fields a caller may not set, and `memex verify` as a CI gate

Notable strengths.value: The index is disposable and the code means it: `rebuild_index` deletes rows for missing pages, re-syncs links, and rewrites the front-matter hash of a page edited outside the tool, so hand-editing a memory is a supported operation. Model-distilled knowledge waits: consolidation writes entity, preference, procedure, catalogue and custom pages as `pending`, every recall path hides them, and the approve verb is a CLI command absent from the MCP surface. And `memex verify` turns "the agent should have used memory" into an exit code — `--require-recall` and `--require-write` fail a build when nothing was read or written since a cutoff, beside parse, index-freshness, link and OKF checks

Main risks.value: No tool on the model's surface can update a memory. `WriteInput` has no slug field, `Memex.write` builds a `WikiNode` with an empty slug, and `WikiStore.write` derives a fresh collision-suffixed one, so the same title written twice is two active pages; the consolidator's `updating = bool(node.slug) and self._store.exists(node.slug)` tests that empty slug, so `nodes_updated` is always empty. The `memex_write` description says the opposite — "Writing an existing slug updates it, preserving creation history and access counts" — and the tool is annotated `idempotent_hint=True`. `supersedes` on a write is a link edge only; the replaced page stays active. The per-turn hooks recall in global scope, so pages from every project are injected. And `memex import` drops `status`, so an imported or round-tripped page lands active whatever it was

Storage backend.value: A git repository of HTML under MEMHTML_ROOT in PARA directories; a rebuildable SQLite index.db projected from HEAD and the working tree; a state.db access plane exported to a committed append-only JSONL sidecar

Update/delete model.value: A correction archives the loser with superseded-by and gives the winner a supersedes link in one commit; eviction and compression are a git mv into archive/YEAR; nothing deletes a memory file

Scoping model.value: Caller-supplied type, workspace, tag, entity, facet and date axes in one filter; workspace is stored per memory from its projects/ directory and applied only when a caller names it

Agent integration.value: Two binaries, an MCP server over stdio with fifteen tools and three resources, and installers for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode that record a SHA-256 receipt per owned file or fragment

Background processing.value: A seventeen-phase sleep run on a dated sleep branch, each committing phase its own commit; sleep merge fast-forwards main after a discrimination gate over a generated fixture corpus

Trust/provenance model.value: Two-state lifecycle status taken from the path, supersession links in both directions, an as-of lens, tasks that propose rather than assert, and a merge step a person runs from the CLI

Notable strengths.value: The single scope filter: "[p]er-arm filters would let a scope apply to three arms and not the fourth, which surfaces as a scoped query returning a result from outside the scope. No type catches that leak", with a stated rule that anything narrowing one arm's candidates belongs in that arm and "must never enter this filter". The empty result that answers: when a named scope matches nothing, archivedMatches counts the archived rows the same scope matches, so an agent "can tell 'never existed' from 'archived'" and follow supersededBy to the replacement. And adversarial controls derived from the system's own anti-merge predicates, each validated against its own family rather than the disjunction

Main risks.value: Unmerged curation is not withheld from search. A successful sleep run leaves HEAD on its branch, every write door re-indexes HEAD, the runbook's cron re-indexes every ten minutes and a deep run re-indexes mid-run, so the agent can retrieve what a person has not yet reviewed, and an agent write in that window lands on the sleep branch. The merge gate measures a generated fixture corpus and does not read the branch it guards. The mutation record is git history. Scope narrows only what a caller names, and the session-start hook recalls across every workspace. Write-time dedup and conflict checks read active rows only, so a corrected claim can be written again unchallenged

Memory unit.value: A `Memory` — content, an optional summary, a namespace, a tier of `working`, `episodic`, `semantic` or `procedural`, a derivation `level` of explicit or deduced, free tags, a JSON metadata map, an importance in [0,1], access counters, an optional expiry, an optional `superseded_by` pointer, a `valid_from`/`valid_to` interval, an optional corroboration confidence and an optional LLM-assessed importance

Storage backend.value: One Go binary over SQLite with a vector extension, or Postgres; both implement the same `Store` interface and are exercised by one shared conformance suite. A row with no vector is kept keyword-searchable rather than rejected

Retrieval strategy.value: Vector and keyword legs per namespace in parallel, an absolute semantic floor before fusion, fusion within then across namespaces with first-seen order breaking ties, then a composite of relevance times a quality modifier, a durable-tier reserve, a turn-echo guard, dedup and an optional reranker

Write strategy.value: A ten-step pipeline: validate and resolve the tier, route the namespace, stamp provenance, scrub secrets, sanitize, gate low-signal captures, exact-dedup before embedding, embed, near-duplicate dedup, then store and hand off to background jobs. Some writes are accepted but not stored, and the response says so

Update/delete model.value: `memory_forget` deletes by id after reading the row for the activity log; supersession points a predecessor at its replacement and stamps its `valid_to`; an optional tombstone TTL, off by default, hard-deletes superseded rows. Re-writing a superseded value creates a fresh live row, because the exact-dedup lookup reads live rows only

Scoping model.value: Namespaces with a cascade — primary, ancestors nearest-first, home, links — where every cascade leg is restricted to durable tiers. Recall, briefing and answer take no namespace argument; memory_list, memory_get, memory_history, memory_update and memory_forget take one from the model and accept any valid namespace, and API keys carry no namespace grant

Agent integration.value: Nine MCP tools including `memory_answer`, `memory_briefing` and `memory_history`, a REST API generated from an OpenAPI document, a CLI, a UI, and plugins for several agent harnesses

Background processing.value: An hourly sweeper purging expired rows, capping short-term tiers, demoting stale durables, optionally purging old tombstones and pruning the activity log; separate jobs for promotion, repair, chunk backfill, periodic dedup and LLM importance assessment

Trust/provenance model.value: A corroboration `confidence` that grows logistically on re-observation and decays without reinforcement, nil meaning untracked and treated as fully trusted; a derivation `level` of explicit or deduced; an `assessed_importance` cleared whenever a caller sets importance explicitly, so it can only ever refine a guess

Notable strengths.value: A ranking composite that multiplies relevance by a quality modifier instead of adding a flat recency or importance bonus, with the unused weights left at zero and the documentation saying so; a write path that degrades to keyword-only rather than failing when the embedder is slow or absent; a store interface whose comments state the contracts the backends are held to, and one conformance suite that runs them

Main risks.value: Five MCP tools accept a model-supplied namespace and resolve any valid one, at every tier, with no grant on the key, so the tier-bounded cascade is not the only cross-namespace read; the activity log is pruned hourly to 720 hours and 100,000 rows by default; the benchmark table's source JSON is gitignored and was never committed, and the README's reading of that table says hybrid never trails a single leg on the session sets where the table shows it trailing keyword

Memory unit.value: Two kinds — an entry file (markdown with YAML frontmatter, one of six types) living in whichever host tool's memory directory owns it, and an item in the session working set keyed on its normalized text

Update/delete model.value: Union-merge with newest-wins per identity, and two tombstone classes — `hidden` monotonic for decisions, `done_at` temporal for next actions. Both are honored on merge and both have shipped writers — `memoir forget` and `memoir_forget` for the absolute one, `memoir_complete_next` for the temporal one

Memory unit.value: A lesson — a free-text label with a working directory, a creation time, the author's kind and name, the session it came from, an approval flag and a lifecycle status. Beside it sit the bulky evidence surfaces it was distilled from: command runs with their output and error fingerprint, session transcripts, and agent turns

Storage backend.value: One local SQLite database with an FTS5 index over commands and an embeddings table, plus numbered `PRAGMA user_version` migrations that add columns with constant defaults so a populated database is never rewritten

Retrieval strategy.value: Full-text search over captured commands with prefix-expanded terms, a scorer with named reasons, and an optional embedding path

Write strategy.value: `mw mark` and `mw remember` record a lesson as human; the MCP surface records one as agent with the client's name. Every note-writing surface routes through one function, which applies the capture gate before the database is opened

Update/delete model.value: Approval is a one-way flag a person sets. A lifecycle status retires a memory without removing it — expired by the sweep, stale by judgement, superseded in favour of a named replacement — while rejection from the review queue deletes the row outright. Bulk evidence is compacted rather than deleted, by a rulebook that names which rule fired

Scoping model.value: A project and a machine on the session. Both are narrowing arguments: the query is `(?1 IS NULL OR project = ?1)`, so a caller that passes nothing gets no predicate

Agent integration.value: A Rust CLI on crates.io, a Tauri desktop dashboard, a terminal UI, shell hooks that capture commands, an MCP surface for coding agents, and a sync path to MemPalace

Background processing.value: None over memory. An expiry sweep and a compaction pass are commands

Trust/provenance model.value: Provenance on every lesson — the author's kind, the author's name and the originating session — an approval gate that defaults to on for agent writes, a four-value lifecycle filtered in the same query, and a loader that refuses a schema in which review filtering could not be enforced

Notable strengths.value: The review gate is decided at write time and enforced at read time, and the seam between them is defended: a schema carrying the lifecycle column without the approval column is rejected as unsupported rather than quietly falling back to a weaker filter, because "no released migration creates it". Provenance is structural — one function records a human and a different one records an agent with its client name — so the queue can be exactly the agent-written unapproved rows. The compaction policy is a pure rulebook with its thresholds passed in, its rules in evaluation order, and a named reason attached to every decision, opening with the rule that matters most for a debugging memory: "Failures outrank successes. A failed command or an errored run is exactly what future-you will search for, so it is never auto-compacted." And the migration comments say what each one does to an existing database, noting that `ADD COLUMN` with a constant default never rewrites rows

Main risks.value: The scope keys do not bind. Project and machine sit behind `(?1 IS NULL OR column = ?1)`, so a caller that supplies nothing reads across every project on the machine — the boundary is the caller's habit rather than the store's rule. Nothing records mutations: fifteen tables and none of them a history, so an approval, a supersession and a rejection leave the same trace, which is none, and the rejected row is gone rather than tombstoned. Because rejection deletes and nothing is keyed on the lesson's content, an agent that proposed a lesson a person threw out can propose it again with nothing in the store positioned to notice. And the review gate is a setting: it defaults to on and is documented in the safe direction, but a single line in `config.toml` or one environment variable makes every agent lesson retrievable the moment it is written
