project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: One markdown file with YAML frontmatter. A `claim` typed `fact`, `decision` or `procedure`, or an `observation` with a hard expiry. The frontmatter is the schema spine: `id` (a ULID), `kind`, `type`, `state`, `created`, `source` and `source_kind`, `tags`, `scope`, `check_by`, `stale`, `last_verified`, `verified_with`, `pinned`, `anchors`, `probe`, the six typed edge lists, `expires`, `valid_from`, `valid_to`, and an `ext` bag whose conventions are documented in the type definition

Storage backend.value: The markdown files under `.memspec/` are canonical — *"lose the index, lose speed — not data"* — with `memory/`, `observations/` and `archive/` directories and git as the history. A derived SQLite FTS5 cache sits beside them, rebuilt when any source file's mtime is newer, and dropped and recreated when its schema predates the running version. A project store and a global `~/.memspec/` merge at read time, project first, and a repository with no store of its own can point at external stores through a `.memspec.yaml`

Retrieval strategy.value: FTS5 with BM25 weighted title ten, tags five, body one, over a porter-stemmed index, with a four-step fallback — exact-AND, prefix-AND, exact-OR, prefix-OR — so a multi-term natural-language query does not return nothing because one term is absent. There is no second retrieval mode: v0.11 deleted `src/lib/embeddings.ts` and its config surface outright, and at the previous pin nothing under `src/` imported that module either, so the hybrid engine was a scaffolding prompt and a config key rather than a code path. Optional graph expansion follows the typed edges one or more hops, tagging each neighbour with the `expanded_via` that surfaced it. Filters: type, active scope, and an as-of validity instant

Write strategy.value: `remember` for a claim, `observe` for a point-in-time note, both CLI and MCP. A write refuses when an active record of the same type already carries the same title, naming the survivor rather than accepting a duplicate. `anchor` records the git blob SHAs a claim depends on, `probe` records a shell command and the sha256 of its output, `relate` and `unrelate` manage typed edges. `normalize` → `distill` → `reduce` turns raw harness transcripts into weekly digests without the transcripts leaving the machine

Update/delete model.value: Nothing is edited in place to correct it: `supersede` writes a new record, links the pair in both directions, and preserves the reason on both. Passing `check_by` sets a `stale` flag at read time and never deletes. `sweep` is the only removal path, runs at a terminal only, and either prompts a person per item or reads an answers file of `<id> <y|n>` lines in which an unlisted id means keep. Retired and superseded records move to `archive/` and out of the search index, reachable through the lineage chain or `--include-superseded`

Scoping model.value: Two mechanisms with different jobs. `claims:` routes writes between stores by working directory, holding unclaimed content local so nothing crosses a sync boundary by default. `scopes:` partitions one store on the read path via a `scope` field with three states — absent, `universal`, or a name — applied inside the FTS SQL and as a hard wall on graph expansion. An unknown scope name is an error, not an empty result

Agent integration.value: A fourteen-tool MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex, carrying no removal verb; a CLI with twenty-three commands; three Claude Code hooks — a session-start context injector that no-ops gracefully when no store is found, a claims check, and a consolidation pass. Generated agent addon text rather than a rewritten instruction file

Background processing.value: No daemon. A `dream` pass reads the last N days of writes and git log and asks a model for stale memories, supersede candidates, verify candidates, missing relations and rules worth promoting — output is review material, never applied. `reconcile` scans anchored claims for drift including uncommitted edits. A local `usage.jsonl` records retrieval hits and feeds a boot-context recency boost; v0.11 adds `outcomes.jsonl` beside it — append-only, gitignored, `useful | dead_end | corrected` recorded after a memory was used — which never mutates the record and is read only to compute the cold and promotion-candidate sections of `status`

Trust/provenance model.value: A discrete lifecycle — `active`, `superseded`, `retired` — that decides what search can see, plus a `verified_with` witness ladder of `anchor`, `probe`, `operator`, `evidence`, `assertion` that annotates and never filters, and a `stale` flag that warns and never withholds. Confidence as a number was removed in v0.3 and replaced by the witness; the type definition says so. A source tier of `operator`, `agent` or `import` protects operator records from being superseded or edited without an explicit override. The override is clamped off for `unrelate` on the MCP channel in code; for `supersede` it is a tool parameter the caller sets, so that half of the protection is a convention rather than a boundary

Notable strengths.value: Anchoring a claim to the git blob SHAs of the files it is about, so drift is detected against the code rather than against the calendar; a scope predicate inside the query rather than over the page, with the starvation case as a test whose comment records the mutation check; refusing to traverse through an out-of-scope record because a traversable-but-unreturnable one leaks the foreign graph's shape; an unknown scope name that throws rather than under-retrieving silently; removal reserved to the terminal and absent from the tool surface; a write refused outright when `scopes_require` is set and no scope resolves, rather than landing visible from everywhere; a ranking normalization added in v0.11 with a comment saying which weight it still ignores and why; a benchmark page that pins its datasets by sha256, reports a saturated result as *"continuity, not bragging rights"*, and notes that an upstream file's hash changed since the earlier runs

Main risks.value: The generated config still advertises `min_confidence: 0.7`, threaded through `search.ts` and the store into the FTS options where `fts.ts` declares the field and never reads it — a leftover from the confidence field v0.3 removed. The `ranking` block beside it is half-fixed: v0.11 normalizes relevance per result set so the relevance and recency ratios now actually move the order, and the `confidence` weight is ignored with a comment saying so. `memspec_supersede` hands the agent the `override_operator` flag that `memspec_unrelate` refuses it. Duplicate refusal keys on an exact title match within a type, so the same claim in different words is accepted. `verified_with` orders five witnesses by strength and no read path uses the order. The benchmark samples twenty questions per dataset. Three release tarballs are committed in the tree. And the whole design assumes a person who runs `reconcile`, answers `sweep` and reads the dream output — the mechanisms that keep memory honest here are all operator-driven

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A Thought — a semantically typed record (one of 30 thought types across 8 roles) with content, confidence, importance, tags, concepts, typed relations, an index, a prev_hash and a SHA-256 hash; embeddings live in a separate vector sidecar

Storage backend.value: One append-only, hash-chained log per chain through a swappable StorageAdapter (only the length-prefixed bincode binary backend ships; JSONL is legacy read-only); vectors in sidecar files; a separate git-like skill registry

Retrieval strategy.value: Multi-signal — BM25 lexical, cosine over local fastembed vectors, and personalized PageRank over the concept/relation graph, plus type/tag/time/confidence filters and chain traversal

Write strategy.value: Append a Thought; prev_hash links it to the last and its SHA-256 is computed over a canonical encoding; near-duplicate detection can auto-attach a Supersedes relation on append

Update/delete model.value: No update, no delete, no hard forget — correction is an appended thought carrying a Supersedes/Corrects/Invalidates relation to a prior id; superseded ids are excluded from default reads and readable only with include_invalidated

Scoping model.value: A MemoryScope (user/session/agent) stored as a tag and filterable on read only when the caller opts in; not enforced by requester identity

Agent integration.value: A standalone daemon exposing an MCP tool surface (and REST + a web dashboard) over HTTP/HTTPS with optional bearer auth; harness config generators for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, Gemini and others

Background processing.value: Append-time near-duplicate auto-supersession and vector-sidecar sync; integrity verification runs on open

Trust/provenance model.value: confidence is an optional float and there is no discrete status field; the trust guarantee is integrity — every record is chained and re-hashed on load, and a tampered chain refuses to open

Notable strengths.value: A genuinely append-only, sequenced, SHA-256 hash-chained thought log that is integrity-verified on open and refuses to load if tampered, with validity-time on relations and a signed, immutable, git-like skill registry

Main risks.value: Tamper-evidence is detection not prevention, two record fields are excluded from the hash, thought signatures are stored but never verified (only skill signatures are), and scope is an opt-in tag rather than an enforced boundary

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: One Markdown document per agent per run, replaced whole, with every superseded version appended to a sibling history file

Storage backend.value: Two files on disk under the run directory; the twelve-table SQLite database holds world state and no memory

Retrieval strategy.value: None. `read_memory_doc` returns the whole document; there is no query, no ranking, and no index

Write strategy.value: `write_memory_doc` overwrites the document synchronously, capped at 256 KiB, deduplicated by an idempotency key of agent, step and tool-call id

Update/delete model.value: Overwrite is the only update. No delete tool, no TTL, no supersession record; the previous text survives only in the history file the agent cannot read

Scoping model.value: Run and agent id, applied by deriving the file path; the tools expose no scope argument

Agent integration.value: 26 HTTP tools over an OpenAI-shaped `/act` endpoint, a Python SDK, a ReAct baseline, a rule-based baseline, and a browser playground for human participants

Background processing.value: None on the memory path. The simulator ticks hourly and activates the agent every twelve hours

Trust/provenance model.value: None. The document is whatever the model last wrote; no provenance, no confidence, no status field, no verification

Notable strengths.value: Memory failure is scored as money rather than as recall; the version history makes a wrong belief traceable to the turn that wrote it

Main risks.value: One turn's warning before the context is cut, no re-injection afterwards, and a memory the agent must remember to read

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A capture frame — an app name, a window name, a timestamp and extracted text in exactly one of two columns, OCR or accessibility tree — rolled up by an ETL into sessions, a timeline, day tasks and worklogs

Storage backend.value: One SQLCipher-encrypted SQLite database on the machine, keyed with a raw 256-bit key rather than a passphrase, written by the tray's in-process capture engine and read by the daemon's ETL

Retrieval strategy.value: Timeline and session queries over the rolled-up tables, a dashboard, and an MCP server that reads the database through a WebAssembly SQLite build

Write strategy.value: A capture engine in the tray writes one row per frame; an ignore list drops a frame before the write when its app name matches exactly or its focused URL matches a domain

Update/delete model.value: A retention pass deletes capture frames below the ETL watermark and older than the cutoff, so nothing is pruned before it has been processed. Adding an app to the ignore list is forward-only and leaves existing history untouched, which the setting says in capitals

Scoping model.value: None. One user, one machine, one database; the ignore list is a write-time filter rather than a read predicate

Agent integration.value: A Tauri tray application with in-process capture, a Rust daemon, a dashboard, an OAuth crate for tracker integrations, and an MCP server package

Background processing.value: Continuous screen capture with OCR and accessibility-tree extraction, an ETL that builds sessions and detects gaps, a retention prune, and a daily worklog draft

Trust/provenance model.value: None on a frame. Extracted text is OCR or accessibility output with no confidence, no provenance beyond which of the two columns holds it, and no status

Notable strengths.value: An ignore list enforced before the write with its semantics and its forward-only limit documented, and unit-tested in both polarities including the suffix trap a naive domain match would fail; a retention prune gated on the ETL watermark so nothing is deleted unprocessed; a raw-key SQLCipher setup with the reason for skipping key derivation stated correctly; and a cross-user collision in the export path found, explained and fixed

Main risks.value: Two plaintext copies of the capture database persist with nothing in the tree deleting either — the timestamped backup the encryption migration leaves beside it, and the temp-directory snapshot the MCP reader exports on every read because its WebAssembly SQLite cannot open an encrypted file; the export passes the database key through a child process's environment; and the ignore list matches an app name exactly, so a renamed or differently-titled window of the same application is captured

Memory unit.value: A triple of timestamp, atom and embedding — the atom's representation left to the agent, so several formats coexist in one AtomSpace

Notable strengths.value: The reinforcement signal is a deliberate tool call rather than an inference from retrieval telemetry, and recall refuses to collapse two priors into one score

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A typed Wiki entity (decision, convention, pattern, component, fact, risk, spec and others) embedded in Markdown with an id, lifecycle, revision, relations, sources, provenance and code groundings; beside it free-text project notes in a JSONL log, Inbox proposals and Relay handoffs

Storage backend.value: Canonical Markdown and JSONL under .mex in the repository, shared by Git commit and push; per-checkout rebuildable SQLite indexes wiki.db (FTS5) and graph.db; drafts and identity under the ignored .mex/local

Retrieval strategy.value: Agents read ROUTER.md and follow its routing table to whole context files; on demand, mex wiki query runs FTS5 per field with archived excluded and lifecycle and grounding health as tiebreakers, wiki related walks relations, for-code joins groundings to code nodes, timeline filters the note log by substring, file, type and date

Write strategy.value: Mostly direct Markdown edits by the agent under the GROW checklist; structured writes through wiki apply with a plan and an explicit apply flag; model synthesis proposes operation plans gated on its own confidence; Inbox approval materialises a proposal into a Wiki operation; mex log appends notes

Update/delete model.value: Wiki operations update, set properties, supersede (old entity marked deprecated plus a supersedes relation) and archive (status only, body kept); there is no delete operation, so removal is a hand edit; notes are append-only

Scoping model.value: Physical: one .mex scaffold per repository and branch; no scope key on an entity and no scope predicate on a read. Relays carry recipients, used by an opt-in mine perspective and by the acknowledge check

Agent integration.value: CLI mex-agent with instruction anchors for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot and OpenCode, Inbox and Relay skills, a loopback Hub web UI with session and CSRF protection, a post-commit drift hook, and an unpublished source-only MCP server

Background processing.value: None scheduled for memory. mex check scores drift of paths, commands, dependencies, staleness and groundings; mex sync hands the drift brief to an interactive agent session; mex watch installs a post-commit drift check

Trust/provenance model.value: Lifecycle in_flight, promoted, deprecated, archived; only archived is filtered and the rest rank. Grounding health fresh, changed, missing, ambiguous, unverified is derived per checkout and only lowers rank. Synthesis maps model confidence to promoted or in_flight

Notable strengths.value: Code groundings with a MinHash identity fingerprint and a body hash, so a claim can be flagged when its code changes; a crash-safe two-phase operation ledger that never logs bodies; precondition hashes and re-planning on apply; lifecycle and grounding health kept on separate axes; bounded, truncation-reporting reads everywhere

Main risks.value: The default write path, direct file edits, bypasses the operation layer and its ledger; the router file reads that agents actually use apply no lifecycle filter; deprecated entities are returned by default; the Inbox approve verb is on the same CLI the agent runs; model confidence alone chooses promoted

Memory unit.value: An episodic Memory object with text, emotion label, importance 1 to 10, stability, a PAD emotion vector, flags for flashbulb, anchor and cherished, and a 160-character supersession note; plus lessons, reminders, facts, tasks and solutions

Write strategy.value: The chat model writes remember tags in its reply; the server parses them after the reply is sent and stores each one, merging into any memory at Jaccard word overlap 0.55 by replacing its text

Update/delete model.value: An updates attribute marks the matched old memory superseded, labelled and down-ranked but still served; delete removes the row; a swiped reply forgets the memories it created; every 40 turns an LLM pass may delete up to 20 recent memories

Scoping model.value: One directory per character; no scope key on a record and no predicate on a read

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: An explicit relationship between stable entities — `project → uses → Neo4j` — carrying layer memberships, a spike classification, a weight, store validity and optional world-validity bounds

Storage backend.value: Neo4j, reached over Cypher, with a vocabulary of classes and properties kept global by construction

Retrieval strategy.value: Lexical and label matching fused with semantic similarity and a bounded structural context, ranked by spike tier then weight then score

Write strategy.value: MCP tools only, and only what the agent deliberately decides to keep: "Mindreader never listens to conversations or extracts facts on its own"

Update/delete model.value: Corrections coexist rather than overwrite; withdrawal and duplicate merge soft-retire by setting `validTo` and pointing at the survivor

Scoping model.value: Layer memberships stored on nodes and edges, checked on subject, relationship and object in Cypher; an empty request scope sees the global layer only

Agent integration.value: An MCP server shipped as a Rust binary, a crate, an npm package, a Docker image and a bundled agent skill

Background processing.value: None on the memory itself; merge and retirement are explicit operations with expected-row-count assertions

Trust/provenance model.value: Provenance through Episode nodes per mutation, a spike classification of how well-founded a fact is, and supersession and contradiction edges kept out of search

Notable strengths.value: Three things. The scope default is the first: "Empty `scope` is global-only", so asking for no scope returns the global layer rather than the entire graph — the inverse of the usual arrangement, where an omitted scope argument quietly means everything, and the failure it prevents is the one that produces a confident answer from the wrong project. The second is that the visibility predicate is applied to all three elements of an assertion and to the anchor beside it, so a hidden endpoint cannot be reached through a visible edge. The third is `assert!(!SEARCHABLE_RELATIONSHIPS.contains(&"SUPERSEDES"))` and the same for `CONTRADICTS`: the edges that record a correction are barred from ordinary search by a committed test, so the bookkeeping that says one fact replaced another can never itself come back as content. Behind all of it is a thesis stated plainly — "Mindreader gives AI agents a memory they must curate, not a history they can search", with nothing captured secretly and nothing silently overwritten

Main risks.value: `SpikeRank` is a ranking input rather than a status that withholds, and the doc comment says so: "Epistemic fact classification used in retrieval ranking (Knowledge highest)." A `Signal` — the lowest tier, a lone unconfirmed observation — is ranked below a `Knowledge` fact and returned all the same, so the epistemic vocabulary sorts the answer rather than gating it, which is the same shape the atlas found in OKF Agent Memory one report earlier. The point-in-time path has a quieter consequence: because a fact enters an `$effectiveAt` answer only when `effectiveQualified` is true, and qualification is the agent's choice at write time, an as-of query over a corpus where nobody set those bounds returns nothing rather than the current state — correct, and surprising, and worth knowing before relying on it. The layer check is a visibility filter rather than an authorization boundary: it is applied in Cypher against a caller-supplied union, with no identity behind the request, so it separates contexts and does not defend against one. And the durable store is a Neo4j server, which is a heavier dependency than the single-file stores this family usually ships

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: An `insight` row — content, category, an importance of 1 to 5, tags, entities, a source label, an access count, `created_at` beside a trigger-set `stored_at`, `last_accessed_at`, a computed `effective_importance` and a nullable `deleted_at` — linked by typed edges restricted by a CHECK constraint to `temporal`, `semantic`, `causal` and `entity`

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file per named store under `~/.mnemon/data/<name>`, holding insights, edges and the oplog, with an `active` file naming which store the CLI opens. Optional embeddings are a BLOB column filled by a local Ollama model; there is no vector database and no server

Retrieval strategy.value: Intent-adaptive beam search over the four graphs, following MAGMA: the query is classified as why, when, entity or general, each intent selecting its own beam width, depth and visited budget; anchors come from keyword search and, when embeddings exist, cosine similarity; candidates expand by BFS with structural and semantic weights of 1.0 and 0.4. A plain keyword path remains for `search`

Write strategy.value: `remember` is one CLI call inside one SQLite transaction: diff the new content against existing insights, soft-delete the one it replaces when similarity crosses the bar, insert, embed if a local model is configured, build temporal, semantic, causal and entity edges, recompute this insight's effective importance, auto-prune if over capacity, append the oplog row. Synchronous, immediately recallable, no background worker

Update/delete model.value: Soft delete throughout — `deleted_at` set, edges removed, every read path filtering `deleted_at IS NULL`. An update is a replacement: the superseded row is soft-deleted and the oplog records `replaced by <new id>`. Nothing is keyed on the value, so the same sentence remembered again after a forget is a new live insight

Scoping model.value: Physical, not predicated. Named stores are separate SQLite files selected by the `active` file; a store has no user, project or tenant column and no read path carries a scope predicate

Agent integration.value: A CLI first — `remember`, `link`, `recall`, `forget`, `gc`, `show`, `log`, `receipt` — with structured JSON output, plus `mnemon setup --target <host>` which installs a skill file, hooks and prompts into OpenClaw, Cursor, NanoClaw, Zcode, Qoderwork and others. The host's own LLM is the supervisor: importance, links and forget decisions arrive as arguments the agent chose

Background processing.value: None in the memory path. Decay is a formula evaluated when something recomputes it, auto-prune fires inline on a write over capacity, and the corpus-wide recompute happens only when `gc` is invoked

Trust/provenance model.value: Provenance is a `source` string and the oplog; there is no epistemic state. Importance is an integer the supervising LLM assigns, and it drives ranking, an immunity rule and pruning order — nothing distinguishes a memory held on record from one believed

Notable strengths.value: The deviations from the paper it implements are written down in a table — entity extraction, causal reasoning, node types, storage, embeddings and deployment, each with the paper's choice beside the implementation's — which is the rarest form of honesty in a system that cites research

Main risks.value: Auto-prune orders by the stored `effective_importance` column, and the only thing that recomputes that column across the corpus is the agent-invoked `gc`; on a store where nothing runs `gc`, the decay the design is built around never reaches the automatic deletion path, which then drops rows by their scores as of the day they were written

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A markdown file with YAML frontmatter carrying a title, tags, a lifecycle of temporary or permanent, an optional role and importance, an alwaysLoad flag, a project id, and typed relationships to other notes

Storage backend.value: Plain markdown in two kinds of git-backed vault: a project vault in the repository's .mnemonic directory, committed with the code, and a main vault for global notes; embeddings and projections are gitignored; no database and no always-on service

Retrieval strategy.value: Reciprocal rank fusion over semantic, lexical, graph-spreading, exact-identifier and full-text channels, plus bounded priors for project, role, recency and canonical notes; brief output shows a summary and the best-matching passage

Write strategy.value: remember, update, relate, consolidate, move_memory and forget, each producing a git commit in the vault it touched, with an optional push

Update/delete model.value: forget deletes the file and strips inbound edges; consolidate merges notes in supersedes or delete mode and prune-superseded deletes notes marked superseded. A supersedes edge is stored on the superseded note, refreshes its updatedAt, and does not lower its recall rank

Scoping model.value: A project derived from the git remote of the caller-supplied cwd. With scope omitted, weak semantic matches from unassociated global notes are held back; an explicit scope of project, global or all is honoured as given, and the main vault is always searched

Agent integration.value: A local Node MCP server with a full and a core toolset, server instructions sent at initialize, and read-only document sources that index another repository's markdown alongside the notes

Background processing.value: No daemon. Embeddings are backfilled lazily during recall; document sources are re-indexed by sync when the indexed commit or the extractor, chunker or embedding identity changes

Trust/provenance model.value: A signal strength and a high, medium or low confidence computed from frontmatter role, lifecycle, recency and relationship count for display on each result; recall diagnostics that disclose suppression and widening

Notable strengths.value: The recall tells you what it did not return. Alongside the ranked matches it reports suppressedGlobalCount, the weak global matches held back, and widenedScope, set when the gate lifted after the admitted pool came back empty, with the response text saying "weak global matches suppressed" in words. Both are asserted end to end, in both directions. A caller can tell nothing matched from something matched and was held back. Every weight, prior and threshold in the ranking and in the displayed confidence is a named constant, and compact evidence decomposes a final score into its channel ranks and priors. The notes stay plain markdown with YAML frontmatter, so uninstalling loses nothing

Main risks.value: The scope argument runs opposite to the usual expectation: gateActive = scope === undefined && project !== undefined, under the comment "Explicit scopes run fully ungated." Omitting scope is the stricter path, the model chooses the scope and the cwd, and the main vault is in every search order, so this is a relevance heuristic and not a boundary. Supersession does not lower recall rank: writing the edge stamps the superseded note with a fresh updatedAt, the decay half-life it gets feeds only a prune suggestion in project_memory_summary, and the evidence line on a superseded note reads "supersedes 1 note", the inverse of its structured superseded flag. Nothing is epistemic: lifecycle is a retention genre, importance is a ranking prior, and confidence is computed after selection. The write record is git, which forget and delete-mode consolidation rewrite the working tree past. Screening flags a devcontainer, Copilot instructions and an OpenCode bundle as auto-run surfaces

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A memory with content, digest, a five-value status, a strength bounded at 1, occurred and recorded times, an optional validity window, an optional claim key, caller attributes, and a provenance that is a discriminated union

Storage backend.value: Postgres with pgvector, behind store interfaces a shared conformance kit tests; an outbox table carries background work, and a memory_events table records each status change

Retrieval strategy.value: Similarity × decay × tag match × freshness × strength over vector and lexical candidates, gated by status, validity and decay, with contested companions pulled in, an association frame, a digest band, and a stored record of each recall

Write strategy.value: Observations in, LLM extraction to memories; creation is idempotent on observation, extractor version and content hash; an optional claim key marks a conflicting pair contested

Update/delete model.value: Compare-and-set status transitions with an event per change; forget then purge, which overwrites content with a fixed string and keeps the row; a separate erase-tenant routine deletes every table's rows for one tenant

Scoping model.value: A required tenantId on every call, applied as a predicate on every read; an optional subjectId organises memories within a tenant. Both are opaque caller strings and nothing authenticates them

Agent integration.value: A library to sit beneath LangGraph, Mastra or a hand-written agent; adapters for OpenAI, Anthropic, a local embedding model and BullMQ; no tool surface of its own

Background processing.value: Embedding, extraction, consolidation and reflection through an outbox drained by tick(), a decay archive sweep, and an event retention purge the operator runs

Trust/provenance model.value: Provenance as a typed union checked at the store's write entry, a contested status that stays in recall with its companion, an event per status change with a caller-declared actor, and a strength ceiling

Notable strengths.value: Provenance is the tag of a discriminated union, `stated | inferred | consolidated | reflected | imported`, and each arm names its own evidence: `stated` a source observation and a time, `inferred` a model, a prompt version, basis ids and a confidence. The store checks the arm at its write entry and Postgres checks the kind and the source observation. A contested memory is surfaced with its counterpart rather than resolved at write time. Every multiplier in the ranking formula is bounded and the bound exported, `MAX_STRENGTH = 1` among them. Status transitions are compare-and-set, and each writes a `memory_events` row with the digest at the time

Main risks.value: The tenant is an opaque caller string with no existence check and no authentication, so the isolation the read path enforces is only as good as the application's choice of string. `inferred` provenance records the model the caller configured, `unknown` when none, not the model the provider ran. The event log is pruned by a per-tenant retention setting and erased with the tenant, so it is not an audit log. Forget is record-keyed: the same content in a new observation is extracted as a new active memory. Background consolidation and reflection run under the seed memory's subject, so a subjectless seed gathers neighbours from the whole tenant. A forgotten, unpurged memory's digest stays in earlier recall records

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A fact with a category, importance and memory type as a revision in a lineage in Qdrant — a revision state, a validation state and count, a fact hash, a source kind and fingerprint, evidence root ids — optionally pointing at a larger artifact held separately

Storage backend.value: Qdrant for vectors and for the `_mnemory_operations` journal, S3 or MinIO for artifacts, stateless HTTP in front of both

Retrieval strategy.value: Multi-query semantic search with temporal awareness, a score threshold, an active-revision condition in the query, and a recall penalty applied to raw and superseded layers rather than an exclusion; a validation-aware slow decay when enabled

Write strategy.value: One LLM call extracts facts, classifies metadata and deduplicates against existing memories, resolving contradictions in the same pass; the dedup outcome is an ADD, a CONFIRM against an independent evidence root, an UPDATE that creates a successor revision, or a SKIP, and each is an operation in the journal

Update/delete model.value: A revision model: an update is a successor revision with the predecessor marked `superseded`, a delete is a `retract` that keeps the content under a retracted state, consolidation marks its inputs `source`; every transition writes an operation record with actor, reason and fingerprints, guarded by `If-Match` preconditions; a privacy delete erases a lineage and its records; no record of a rejected value, and a retracted fact can be re-added

Scoping model.value: `user_id` as a `must` condition on every Qdrant query, with a separate owner scope for shared memories, and a per-user lease that serializes trusted semantic decisions

Agent integration.value: An MCP server with sixteen tools plus a REST API with an OpenAPI spec, native plugins for ten-plus clients, a built-in management UI, and two signed-request routes for trusted user events and evidence that ordinary API keys cannot use

Background processing.value: A three-phase consistency check runnable on a schedule with auto-fix, journaled per action and recoverable after a partial apply; consolidation into layers; TTL expiry; slow decay with a longer half-life for confirmed memories

Trust/provenance model.value: `revision_state` — active, superseded, source, retracted, aborted — filtered to active on every read; `validation_state` unverified or confirmed with a bounded count of independent evidence roots, used to extend TTL and slow decay and never as a filter; an importance score; a source kind on every revision

Notable strengths.value: The consistency check screens for injection with a regex before any LLM reads the memory and re-screens what was already stored; every mutation since September 2026 leaves an operation record and a lineage history a client can read; a retracted memory keeps its content; fsck actions are checkpointed and resumable

Main risks.value: A superseded memory is penalised in ranking rather than excluded, so a corrected fact can still be returned; a retracted fact carries no bar on re-assertion; the journal is a per-operation checkpoint updated in place, not appended rows, and a privacy erase removes it; provenance and confirmation reach only the two signed routes, so an ordinary API-key write starts unverified and stays so; fsck's own accuracy is unmeasured

Memory unit.value: One node: a caller-chosen string id, any JSON content, five optional provenance strings and an optional event_time. Immutable and content-addressed, so an update is a new object under the same id

Storage backend.value: One redb file per store directory, .mnem/store.redb, holding objects, refs, staging, staged deletions and a derived change index; HEAD and config are text files beside it

Write strategy.value: Explicit. Every MCP remember, revise, remember_many or forget is a stage and a commit: a new state snapshot and a commit object, synchronous, the branch moved by compare-and-swap

Update/delete model.value: Update writes a new node object under the same id. forget stages a deletion that the next commit applies, and every past state keeps the node. No hard delete, no garbage collection, no tombstone on a value

Scoping model.value: Physical: one .mnem store per directory, chosen by path or MNEM_STORE. Branches are named pointers, not row keys. The LangGraph adapter encodes namespaces as a colon-joined id prefix with no validation

Agent integration.value: MCP server with ten core tools and three harness tools behind a flag, a LangGraph BaseStore, an OpenAI Agents SDK Session, a Python SDK and the mnem CLI. No automatic injection

Background processing.value: None. No model calls, no network, no compaction; the change index is rebuilt only on import or on request

Trust/provenance model.value: None. Every node in HEAD's state is equally current. A semantic-merge seam can return a Contradiction verdict that nothing persists and a blanket strategy overrides

Notable strengths.value: Append-only content-addressed history with the exact state at any commit; blame through merges to the introducing commit and its provenance; bisect over a first-parent chain; deterministic three-way merge that returns conflicts instead of guessing; import re-hashes every object

Trust/provenance model.value: A three-condition baseline gate no configuration can relax, shadow evaluation before activation, canaries, a safety probe, and an objective delta that must not be negative

Notable strengths.value: The gate is the thing, and what makes it worth reading is that it is defined as a floor rather than as a policy. `EvalReport::is_committable()` is three conjoined conditions — every canary passed, the safety probe passed, and the objective delta at or above zero — and the README's claim about it is the unusual part: "setting every configurable gate threshold to its weakest value *still* cannot bypass the baseline." That is not left as prose. `fully_relaxed_gates_still_reject_baseline_failure_through_pipeline` runs the whole compile pipeline with the gates relaxed and asserts the rejection anyway, beside unit tests that trip each of the three conditions in isolation with a message naming which invariant broke. Most systems this atlas reads have an escape hatch that a configuration can widen until it admits anything; this one has a floor underneath the configuration, and a test standing on it. The bitemporal design is the second piece: two intervals per node with `is_live_at` requiring both, justified by a concrete failure — "[a] flat 'current' graph would lose that lineage the moment the worker fires" — and tied to a replay invariant the view layer also enforces

Main risks.value: The procedural loop is the product and its honesty depends on the evaluation behind the gate: canaries, a safety probe and an objective delta are only as good as the cases and the objective somebody wrote, and nothing in the repository pins those to a corpus the way the gate itself is pinned by a test. Erasure is crypto-shredding through a keyring, which makes a payload unrecoverable and leaves the graph's structure — nodes, edges, intervals, evolution counts — in place, and nothing is keyed on a shredded value, so the same content can be written again with no record that it was once erased. There is no person anywhere in the loop: `is_committable` is a mechanical floor rather than an approval, and a policy artifact that clears it activates without anyone reading it. And the repository is early — the README notes that the documented install line "starts working at v0.1.1" because "v0.1.0 predates it and carries no binaries", which is a candid disclosure and also a statement about maturity

Memory unit.value: An entity node with properties and normalised aliases, a Note node linked to what it is about, hand-written fact edges, and rule-derived edges that carry the rule, the score and the property values that produced them

Storage backend.value: A directory on disk: an append-only WAL over mmapped snapshot sections, with an overlay-over-base column, topology and edge-property view; roles and commit times in sidecar files

Retrieval strategy.value: Cypher-shaped queries, vector, full-text and hybrid search, traversal and shortest path through a view that can carry a node mask, and a recall digest over the full-text index

Write strategy.value: `remember` with entities and facts in one commit, `upsert_entity`, `ingest_json` and Cypher writes; a rule declared once derives matching edges on every later write and retracts them when it stops matching

Update/delete model.value: Derived edges are retracted by the rule engine in the commit that invalidates them; deleting a rule removes exactly the edges it owns; `forget` tombstones a node, removes a property or retracts a hand-written fact, and refuses a rule-derived edge

Scoping model.value: A role bound to the bearer token on the HTTP surface, resolving to a node mask a caller-supplied mask can only intersect; a read-only scoped handle in the Python binding; on the stdio MCP surface `role` is an argument

Agent integration.value: Twenty-three MCP tools over stdio by default, twenty-five with --all-tools; an HTTP server with role-bound tokens; Rust, Python and npm distributions; an installer writing a skill, an MCP entry and session-start and per-prompt hooks

Background processing.value: None; no model call anywhere in the tree, and vectors are supplied by the caller

Trust/provenance model.value: Per-edge provenance answering why two nodes are related, a `what_if` that computes without writing, history reads bounded by a reported horizon, and a provisional mark on stub entities that a describing write clears

Notable strengths.value: A hidden key returns the same 404 as an absent key, under a comment naming the reason — "[h]idden keys must respond identically to absent keys (no oracle)" — and the history handler filters edge-added and edge-removed entries whose other endpoint is hidden, because "[a] role token must not learn about hidden nodes via edge history events". Three failure modes resolve to deny: an empty role sees nothing, an unknown role is an error rather than a grant, and a corrupt `roles.json` poisons every role until it is fixed. The sidecar's version numbering is a security decision: a file using `visible_where` or `namespaces` is deliberately not loadable by an older binary, because such a binary "would resolve a narrowed role to its full label set". The scoped handle carries the same contract into the engine, refuses the whole-store reads it cannot narrow, and is pinned by a test file that fails when a method has no leak row. Making a relationship a schema rule that retracts its own edges is the right shape for derived memory: the edge carries the rule and the values that produced it, so `explain_association` answers with evidence rather than an assertion

Main risks.value: The enforcement and the advertised surface are not the same surface. The MCP server is JSON-RPC over stdio with no identity — `dispatch_call` takes no role — so `query`'s `role` is an argument, one of "[t]wo ways to ask the same restricted question", and `forget` has no role check by the project's own statement. The session brief and the per-prompt recall digest read the whole store, and so do `analyze` and `suggest_rules`. The identity preset's `SAME_AS` rules carry no namespace, so same-named entities in different namespaces link. The core's history reads bypass masking — "[a]pply masking at the caller level" — which the HTTP layer and the scoped handle do. History is bounded: a truncating snapshot ends it, and Python's `snapshot()` truncates. Nothing here is epistemic — an edge has a score and a rule, not a status or a validity window — and the project is pre-1.0 alpha

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A document row: title, content, tags, free JSON metadata, collection (memory for agent notes, sessions for harvested transcripts or their summaries, code for indexed source) and an optional supersedes_id pointer. No status, author, confidence or validity time

Storage backend.value: PostgreSQL 17 with pgvector: documents, chunks with a trigger-maintained tsvector, and 768-dimension embeddings under HNSW. Session summaries are also mirrored to markdown files under the summaries directory

Retrieval strategy.value: memory_query runs BM25 and pgvector legs in parallel, fuses them with dynamic RRF, deduplicates, boosts code and recent documents, optionally reranks; memory_search and memory_vsearch run one leg each; memory_wake_up lists the newest memory and sessions documents

Write strategy.value: Explicit: memory_write over MCP or POST /api/v1/write, chunked and committed in one transaction, embedded later by a queue. Automatic: a harvester every 120 seconds summarises finished OpenCode, Claude Code and Pi sessions through an LLM, or stores the raw transcript when no summariser is configured or it fails

Update/delete model.value: An upsert on source_path replaces content; supersedes records a pointer and hides nothing. memory_delete and DELETE /api/v1/documents/:id hard-delete a row and cascade to chunks and embeddings. A deleted session summary is regenerated on the next harvest while the transcript remains on disk. No tombstone

Scoping model.value: A workspace_hash on every document, chunk and embedding, applied as a predicate by every named-workspace read, the OR fallback included. memory_ticket and GET /api/v1/sessions/by-ticket take no workspace and return session snippets from every workspace. The search tools also accept the value all as an explicit caller choice. Writes require a registered workspace

Agent integration.value: Nineteen MCP tools over streamable HTTP and SSE, a REST API, and a CLI; init writes MCP client configuration for Claude Code, OpenCode and Codex. No session hook injects memory; the agent calls memory_wake_up and the search tools itself

Background processing.value: Session harvest every 120 seconds, LLM summarisation (single shot below 4,000 characters, map-reduce above), an embedding queue that rescans pending chunks every five minutes, a file watcher that re-indexes code, telemetry cleanup. An LLM consolidator that merges and deletes memory documents is written and never constructed

Trust/provenance model.value: None. Every document is retrievable on equal terms; a superseded note ranks by relevance and recency like any other

Notable strengths.value: Transactional write of a document and its chunks; parallel lexical and vector legs that degrade to one when the other fails; a refusal to bind beyond loopback without authentication; memory_search's OR relaxation skipped when a time filter is set, with the reason written down; committed cross-workspace isolation tests with positive controls; committed benchmark result files

Main risks.value: The hybrid search's OR fallback drops the time-range and tag predicates the first leg applied; memory_ticket returns session snippets from every workspace and has no argument to scope it; deleting a harvested summary does not stick; the Claude Code and Pi harvesters have no active-session check, and presence dedup freezes the first summary; the README's headline precision trio mixes workspaces

Memory unit.value: Five tiers plus an operator vault; the tier this report reads is a ground-truth fact — statement, source, scope, asserted and revoked timestamps, fact state, a source-count map, confidence, episode backlinks, maturity and a confirmed count. Beside it, a structured operator profile whose claims are extracted from conversation

Storage backend.value: SQLite indexes beside a write-ahead log with a single-writer invariant, O_APPEND, fdatasync per flush, mode 0600 and segment rotation at 16 MiB or 24 hours

Retrieval strategy.value: Three lanes per prompt: verified, unrevoked ground truth matched by substring and prepended; region-routed episodic recall fused across semantic and episodic lanes; and pending contradictions touching the topic

Write strategy.value: Operator-attested sources write verified facts; imports, crons and transcript feeds write candidates or raw rows that corroboration by distinct sources promotes; the opt-in consolidation sweep writes mature episodic clusters as candidates

Update/delete model.value: Revocation sets revoked_at; a polarity contradiction flags the lower-credibility side and a value divergence is recorded for the operator; topic forget deletes across the episodic, profile and graph tiers, revokes matching facts, and installs a never-recreate sentinel

Scoping model.value: A scope column on ground truth that keys corroboration and contradiction peers; no scope predicate on any recall read

Agent integration.value: A local daemon with chat, channel bridges, a GUI, a plugin SDK with a WASM sandbox, sub-agent personas and origin-bound consent before any outbound provider route

Background processing.value: Decay, opt-in consolidation and synthesis sweeps, an opt-in daily contradiction resolver, drift detection, a compaction guard and an evaluation harness

Trust/provenance model.value: A decay-immune ground-truth table with a six-value fact state gating every model-facing read, corroboration-based promotion, polarity-only automatic demotion, and a forget sentinel that profile extraction and peer gossip consult

Notable strengths.value: The ground-truth module is built against a failure it names in its own header: "[s]liding 'if importance ≥ 0.95 treat as fact' is the failure mode this module exists to prevent." Facts get a separate table with "no Hebbian decay, no FORGET_FLOOR sweep, no consolidation pass", a six-value state that every model-facing read filters, and placement ahead of every episodic row. Who wrote a fact decides where it starts — an operator assertion is verified, an import or cron output a candidate, extracted bulk text raw — and only agreement between distinct sources lifts the rest. The contradiction detector splits a statement at the first copula, excludes a superset ("'nas at X' vs 'nas at X primary' is NOT flagged"), and hides a fact automatically only for a polarity flip, leaving "a legitimately multi-valued attribute (two meetings, two servers)" to the operator. A forgotten topic leaves a lowercased sentinel that profile extraction checks twice, once before the apply transaction and once inside it, and consent to a remote provider is a marker file an operator can audit with `ls`

Main risks.value: The importance threshold the header rejects reaches the table anyway: the opt-in consolidation sweep writes any cluster spanning seven days with mean importance of at least 0.5 into ground truth, as a candidate, so the fact state rather than the separate table keeps it out of recall. The profile approval gate, default-on in configuration and announced by the init wizard, is never constructed outside tests: every production profile run passes no gate context and applies directly. The forget sentinel is not consulted by `groundtruth::insert`, document claims, bulk-text import or episodic ingest. The opt-in contradiction resolver supersedes the older fact by assertion time and closes genuine conflicts as `human_review`, which drops them from the pending-contradiction recall lane while both facts stay verified. `scope` keys corroboration but filters no recall read, and ground-truth mutations write no log frame: the WAL codes for them are emitted only by tests

Retrieval strategy.value: BM25 and embeddings with a context selector and compressors, graph-aware; decisions by FTS5, a local embedding scan, or both fused by reciprocal rank, ACTIVE only unless a status is asked for

Update/delete model.value: The index is rebuilt; a synapse namespace can be cleared and weak edges decay away; a decision is amended in place, marked STALE by the post-commit scan, invalidated or restored; the decision delete method has no caller

Scoping model.value: Per project directory, chosen on every MCP call by a path the caller supplies; synapse weights partitioned by git-branch namespace, with personal and shared merged into every read

Agent integration.value: An MCP server, Claude Code hooks, a Hermes plugin, editor extensions, a CLI, a daemon and a dashboard

Background processing.value: A post-commit decision scan, synapse decay and team-memory import at session start, a daemon with backpressure, a CI tuner and benchmark workflows

Trust/provenance model.value: A status on every decision that search filters on, a stale-decision warning before an edit, two hash-chained audit trails with strict verifiers, role-gated MCP tools, and a test suite that gates the project's own published numbers

Notable strengths.value: Staleness is computed from the repository rather than from time. Recording a decision fingerprints the git blob of every file it names; the post-commit scan marks it STALE when a commit changes one of those files, unless that commit holds exactly the fingerprinted blobs, so the commit that carries a decision does not retire it and the next edit does. Search withholds STALE and INVALIDATED decisions, and the PreToolUse guard shows them, with the reason recorded on each, before the agent edits a file they govern. The audit verifier fails on an unreadable line, a hashless record after the chain starts and a broken link, and a committed test pins the one tampering it cannot see. And tests/test_site_claims.py gates the project's own marketing: every N× ratio on a high-traffic page must appear in site/claims.json with a source and a reproduction command, private names may not appear under site/, and the guards carry negative controls built from the copy that shipped

Main risks.value: _emit_audit wraps the append in a bare except Exception: pass, so a build or ingest whose audit write fails leaves a gap nothing counts, and records cut from the end of the log verify clean because the hash carries no key. The chain records a decision change only as the name of the MCP tool that made it: an amend overwrites the rationale, a status change is an UPDATE, and invalidation is published only to the in-process event bus. The maintenance view called stale returns ACTIVE decisions untouched for 90 days and never a decision whose status is STALE. dependency_constraints and author have no writer, so cascade invalidation never fires. The project boundary is a path the MCP caller supplies, the default declared identity takes its role from the call, and the edit guard tells the agent itself to run restore

Update/delete model.value: Nothing is destroyed. Forget, merge-source, TTL expiry and prune all copy the row into an archive table carrying the reason and the time, then delete it from the working set; a restore moves it back

Scoping model.value: A workspace string on each memory, matched as an exact or prefix filter when a caller passes one; no default and no requirement

Agent integration.value: An MCP server with twenty-four tools, published to PyPI and npm, with a client setup command that merges configuration for Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, VS Code and Codex

Background processing.value: Consolidation, synthesis of recurring memories into learnings, drift detection against the notes a memory references, a promotion queue in four buckets, and a status reconciliation driven by usage

Trust/provenance model.value: No epistemic state. Drift and ignored triggers are recorded and feed a worklist; note status moves between active and dormant on usage and is superseded at ranking time by a continuous hotness blend

Notable strengths.value: Four delete paths that converge on one archive helper whose target table has no index and no embedding; expiry enforced by relocating the row at read time rather than by a clause every caller must remember; and a redaction pass applied to unattended writes and deliberately not to deliberate ones

Memory unit.value: A `node` — kind, project, event timestamp, source, title, body, a `signal` float and a JSON `meta` blob — with an id of `sha256(projectId + kind + naturalKey)`; eight kinds declared and seven collected, with `shell_command` carrying exit codes from a shell hook and from Claude Code tool calls

Storage backend.value: One `better-sqlite3` file per repository: `nodes` plus an external-content FTS5 index, a `sqlite-vec` vec0 table partitioned by project, a `node_files` path index, a `node_links` edge table and a `file_edges` import graph replaced wholesale on every sync; two machine-wide JSONL logs feed it, one for shell commands and one for agent tool calls

Retrieval strategy.value: Three read paths. A query fuses BM25 over FTS5 with cosine over sqlite-vec, ranks by `relevance x signal^e x recency^e` with the two priors sharing one overturn budget, and packs to a token budget. A Claude Code hook looks up past failures of the command that just failed by an execution hash, and a session-start hook prints a digest of recent failures; neither uses the ranker, an embedding or a model. `precheck` matches staged file basenames against unresolved failures

Write strategy.value: Collectors per source, cursor-resumed, all through `upsertNodes`. Opt-in shell hooks append command, cwd and exit code to a JSONL; opt-in Claude Code hooks append each Bash call and edited path to a second one, redacted before the write. Redaction covers shell, agent, conversation and session text in full and code diffs on a high-confidence profile; docs, git commits and GitHub threads are stored as read

Update/delete model.value: Three granules. `forget` deletes every node matching a value and writes a standing deny list consulted at every future write, with a hash-only tombstone per node and an audit row; `--prune-source` wipes one source across the live project id and its prior identities and writes an audit row with no tombstones; `sync --rebuild` clears the project unrecorded. `mark-stale` down-weights without deleting, prompted by a local model that judges whether a newer node contradicts an older one. A deny-list entry cannot be removed

Scoping model.value: `project_id` on every node and a predicate on every read: both retrieval arms, the vec0 partition, ambient recall, the session digest, precheck and the MCP listings. One database file per repository, so inside a file the key separates the repository's current identity from prior ones; a cross-project query opens each registered database and tags every hit with its origin

Agent integration.value: A CLI, a six-tool stdio MCP server (search, sync, status, list-recent, list and resolve stale suggestions), three Claude Code hooks installed by `agent install` (capture, recall after a Bash call, a session-start digest), a VS Code extension with search, recent-memory and stale-review views, and opt-in git pre-commit and post-commit hooks

Background processing.value: No scheduler. Collectors run inside `nexusmem sync`, started by hand, by the MCP `sync_project` tool, by a git post-commit hook, or detached by the Claude Code SessionStart hook. `sync` also spends at most three local-model judgments per run on contradiction checking, on by default

Trust/provenance model.value: Three fields and no gate. `trust_state` is `candidate` until a person runs `nexusmem review`, then `verified` or `rejected`; a rejected node is multiplied by 0.3 in ranking and still returned, which is why the mark is withheld. `provenance` is a four-tier ordering set per collector that scales recency decay. An agent command's `outcome` is `unknown` when a pipe hid its exit status, fixed at capture. Ambient recall derives resolved, stale, superseded and uncertain at read time from links and revert commits, and changes its wording rather than what it returns

Notable strengths.value: A value-keyed deny list whose test proves the resurrection case; exit codes for the commands an agent ran, which git cannot supply; recall keyed on an execution hash that survives `cd` and exit-echo wrappers and is silent on no match; a fix that failed again is reported as one that did not hold; a ranker that bounds how far query-independent priors may overturn the query; an ambient-memory experiment whose null results are recorded beside its design

Memory unit.value: A row in `memories` — a type of rule, skill, fact or anti_pattern, a title, a content body, JSON tags that double as trigger terms, a checkout path and a remote-hash scope, a `source` that says whether the queue may see it, an `origin` that says which signal produced it, structured JSON evidence naming the task and event, a dedupe key stored in `file_path`, and the lifecycle flags confirmed, confirmed_by, activated_at, archived, superseded_by, paused, quarantined, use_count and last_used_at

Retrieval strategy.value: No search at retrieval time — every confirmed, unarchived, unquarantined, unpaused row in the task's scope plus the globals is loaded, a rule with tags is kept only when one tag or a vocabulary alias appears as a whole word in the task's title, description, acceptance criteria and planned file paths, a vendor-term screen holds the rest, and `rank_and_select` orders by importance tier, a fourteen-day recency decay and normalised use count under a ceiling of 25; `nh recall` is substring matching over confirmed rows

Write strategy.value: No hot-path extraction — proposals come from a reviewer FAIL round's blocking findings distilled by a utility model, from supervisor corrections, escalations, repeated review failures and tamper trips clustered on a deterministic gist and proposed only at two or more occurrences, from mined transcripts and operator replies, and from the curator; every write passes one chokepoint that refuses an unqueueable source, dedupes on the key, drops personal data and stamps provenance and quarantine

Update/delete model.value: A human's reject deletes an unconfirmed proposal from the outcome, review or reply path together with its dedupe key, archives one from a batch-driven origin, and pauses a confirmed row; `nh rules remove`, `nh skills remove` and their API routes hard-delete any row an id prefix resolves, with no audit row; archive is the verb for the 45-day sweep of unconfirmed proposals, the 90-day retirement of auto-activated rows, a supersede on confirm with a `superseded_by` pointer, a failed activation screen and the UI's Delete; pause withholds without archiving; restore reverses any of them; a human confirm overwrites an auto confirm

Scoping model.value: Per repository by remote hash with checkout-path fallback and explicit globals, applied on the injection query, the sessions recall query and the CLI; per channel by construction — the reviewer never receives an auto-confirmed review-origin rule and the team brain never enters the coder's local table

Agent integration.value: Injected as an importance-tiered block after the rules block of the coder's and supervisor's prompts and as a filtered copy for the reviewer, up to 8,000 characters of critical rules and 4,000 of relevant ones; `nh recall` is named in the coder's instructions as a Bash command; a FastAPI surface and a React pane in Settings; no MCP tool for memory

Background processing.value: `HarvestJob` every twelve hours clusters corrections and failure signals into proposals and, with `learning.auto_manage` on by default, activates up to ten screened proposals per rolling day; `RetirementSweepJob` daily archives unconfirmed proposals older than 45 days and auto-activated rows unused for 90; a terminal-state finalizer fills the ledger's outcome column; nothing rewrites content

Trust/provenance model.value: Five discrete flags on the row; a write-time quarantine that fails closed on a matcher error and a read-time term screen that fails open, stated as such; provenance JSON on every insert; a personal-data gate that drops rather than redacts; auto-activation gated on dedupe, PII, provenance and terms with a daily cap and a kill switch; a ledger labelled correlational, not causal, in the migration and in the CLI

Notable strengths.value: One injection chokepoint enforced by an AST test with its own known-positive control; a queue lifecycle whose every verb is reversible and audited; a reviewer channel that cannot consume its own verdicts; measured flood numbers written into the code that fixed them; a dedupe key that survives rejection so a batch producer cannot re-propose a refused lesson

Main risks.value: Auto-activation is on by default and the ten-a-day cap is the only ceiling on a store the operator has not read; the sessions source is a second SQL route into the prompt that each new flag has to be added to by hand; the vendor-term screen ships with eight names outside the operator's private supplement; a `memory_uses` ledger row per injection on every attempt; 21,785 lines of orchestrator around the chokepoint; four remove commands hard-delete any row by id prefix, bypassing the lifecycle and the audit trail

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A row in a collection, in whichever engine the collection uses — key-value, document, columnar, graph, vector, text, array, spatial or CRDT; a bitemporal collection adds required system-time and valid-time columns

Storage backend.value: Its own storage stack: a write-ahead log, columnar segments, CSR graph indexes, HNSW vectors, an FTS index, with Raft replication for the clustered deployment

Retrieval strategy.value: SQL and a RESP protocol surface over one planner, with vector, full-text, graph and spatial operators in the same process, and `AS OF SYSTEM TIME` for point-in-time or all-versions reads

Write strategy.value: Statements through the planner, with row-level write policies admitting or rejecting each row image before dispatch

Update/delete model.value: MVCC versions addressable by system time; a bitemporal collection closes a row's `_ts_valid_until` rather than losing the prior interval

Scoping model.value: Tenant, database, collection and row: row-level policies compiled to predicates and injected into the physical plan, plus scope grants with expiry, grace periods and conditions, an API-key and JWT/OIDC identity layer, and namespace authorization

Agent integration.value: Embedded in-process on device or run as a server; RESP and SQL surfaces, a client crate, a bridge, and a Docker image

Background processing.value: Raft consensus, WAL catch-up, compaction, catalog recovery checks that verify the in-memory policy store against the catalog, and a CDC event plane

Trust/provenance model.value: An immutable hash-chained audit log for authentication, authorization denials, privilege and tenant changes, snapshots and DDL; row-level policies; scope grants with conditions; redaction; rate limits; emergency and escalation paths

Notable strengths.value: The RLS walker is exhaustive over every engine's own op enum with no wildcard in any of the nine dispatch modules, so adding a plan variant fails to compile rather than silently escaping the filter — the property most access-control layers in this corpus assert in prose and cannot enforce. Each variant resolves to one of four named outcomes and "[a] write is never a silent no-op"; a write check left un-run is detectable as `PendingInjection` rather than defaulting to allow, and a second pass refuses undecided writes. The one wildcard in the subsystem rejects. The end-to-end test requires an excluded row to read as absent rather than as an error, because the distinction is itself a probe

Main risks.value: The memory framing is not backed by code: the README offers "[s]emantic, relational, episodic, and time-series memory in one engine", and the string `episodic` does not appear anywhere in the engine's Rust — the four kinds are the vector, graph, time-series and document engines under memory names. `nodedb-mem`, the only crate whose name suggests agent memory, is RAM arena and budget management. There is no memory-specific schema, no decay, consolidation, importance or provenance model, and no agent-facing memory API; a caller gets a database and supplies those itself. The licence is BUSL-1.1 with a change date of 1 May 2030, so the current release is not open source. The audit log covers security and DDL events rather than row-level data mutations, which go to the WAL — a durability log, not a queryable mutation record

Memory unit.value: A capture, promoted to a candidate, promoted to a wiki article with topics, revisions and scopes

Storage backend.value: Postgres through Prisma, with an optional hybrid embedding tier behind consent state

Update/delete model.value: Revocation writes a tombstone keyed on an HMAC subject hash and enqueues a durable cleanup job

Scoping model.value: privateScopeTag on the principal and on every row, plus a RestrictedScope table and restricted tags

Notable strengths.value: The tombstone is checked across every retained HMAC key version, so rotating the key cannot resurrect a revocation

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A JSON node (title, body, tags, kind, source label, recorded, observed and valid times, status) joined by typed directed links; JSON sources, source-matched claims and rejection tombstones are further node kinds

Storage backend.value: Two copies of one AES-256-GCM sealed, hash-chained event journal on different filesystems, appended under flock and reconciled on every read; the key in a separate owner-only file; state rebuilt in process memory by full replay

Retrieval strategy.value: Substring and word-overlap scoring over title, tags and body with an optional validity as-of filter; a character-budgeted context packer; a three-hop neighbourhood walk; an evidence query that re-verifies each claim against its source; project briefings by tag

Write strategy.value: Explicit MCP calls only, with no model on any path; a claim is created only from a JSON pointer into a stored source and is refused when its value was rejected

Update/delete model.value: Revise replaces a node and stales its derived_from descendants; invalidate stales a node and its descendants; archive hides a node; nothing leaves the journal; rejection writes an immutable value-keyed tombstone

Scoping model.value: None on the note tools; a scope string on evidence and a project tag on briefings, each matched exactly and described in the code as a filter, not an access control

Agent integration.value: A 22-tool stdio MCP server on the MCP Python SDK and a CLI for init, status and serving; POSIX only, since the vault imports fcntl

Background processing.value: None; Git drift is checked live on each status or evidence read and becomes a stale mark only when memory_git_scan is called with invalidate_stale

Trust/provenance model.value: A current or stale status cascaded along derived_from links and withheld by the context, briefing and evidence reads; claims are labelled source-matched and unreviewed, two values for one key are both withheld, and no path approves a claim

Notable strengths.value: An authenticated, hash-chained journal mirrored across filesystems that refuses to reconcile diverged copies; a value-keyed rejection tombstone nothing can lift; claims re-verified against their source bytes and live Git blobs on every read

Main risks.value: Every call decrypts and replays the whole journal under an exclusive lock, up to 51 times for one search; scope and project are filters the unscoped note tools bypass; memory_add writes any kind, a tombstone included; a corrupt copy is replaced silently and status reports the mirrors valid as a constant

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A graph node or edge with properties and an optional vector, under a Neo4j-compatible model

Storage backend.value: Badger with MVCC snapshot isolation, an HNSW vector index and prefixed key spaces per index type

Retrieval strategy.value: Cypher — including temporal procedures that take a validity instant and an MVCC commit version independently — plus hybrid graph and vector search, with knowledge-policy scoring applied as a visibility filter

Write strategy.value: Transactional, anchored to an MVCC version, with declarable constraints including a TEMPORAL kind

Update/delete model.value: MVCC versions with a retained floor; pruning keeps the head and fails historical reads below it

Scoping model.value: A namespace component in every storage key prefix, plus multi-database separation

Agent integration.value: Bolt and Cypher for Neo4j clients, gRPC, GraphQL, a Qdrant-compatible endpoint and MCP

Background processing.value: Access accumulation and flushing, decay driven by temporal access patterns, retention and replication

Trust/provenance model.value: A confidence property filtered through a per-property Kalman filter that dampens single-measurement spikes

Notable strengths.value: Validity can be declared and enforced as a constraint, and a single query can fix both clocks — what was recorded then about what was true then

Main risks.value: The hybrid and vector search arm is current-state only by design, so the two clocks are reachable from Cypher and not from the search path a memory client is most likely to use

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A shard: event time, event type, title, content, tags, a utility prior, an access count, a unique content hash, a domain key, a sensitivity, an embedding, a source URI, the writing host, `learned_utc`, `valid_until` and `last_verified`

Storage backend.value: Local SQLite across up to nine grid databases, with private and secret bodies AES-256-GCM encrypted before they reach the file; a separate dedup index maps content hashes to grid databases, and history.db holds the event log

Retrieval strategy.value: Keyword, embedding, title and optional distilled lanes fused by reciprocal rank and blended with the utility prior; filterable by tag scope, by what the node had learned by a date, and by an event window

Write strategy.value: `nougen brain scan` harvests traces from Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Codex and others and stamps them at import time; capture redacts, hashes, embeds and encrypts in that order; the MCP, HTTP, tube and sync paths may supply the original event time

Update/delete model.value: The dedup index refuses identical content; `mark_shard` moves the utility prior; the network node's MCP amends by appending dated text, retracts by title prefix, tag and zero utility, or deletes the row and leaves its hash in the dedup index

Scoping model.value: A `domain_key` derived from the working path on write. On read an implicit domain only boosts, an explicit one falls back to every domain when it matches nothing, and agent, user, machine and project tag filters are optional arguments. The network node gives each authenticated tenant its own vault directory

Agent integration.value: A CLI, a local MCP server, a network node serving HTTP and MCP behind tenant tokens, hooks, a Tauri desktop app and a Docker image

Background processing.value: Scanning, federation between nodes, a dream pass that consolidates and decays utility, and opt-in write-time consolidation tags

Trust/provenance model.value: Credential redaction before hashing and embedding, encryption by sensitivity, a command denylist, and an execution sandbox that refuses the single-command MCP tool by default and runs the batch tool's code as trusted

Notable strengths.value: Two safety mechanisms carry disclaimers written by the person who built them. The command gate: "This is a defense-in-depth speed-bump, NOT a security boundary. It is a best-effort denylist meant to catch obvious destructive commands and slow down accidents; it can be trivially bypassed by obfuscation (encoding, indirection, aliases, etc.) and must never be relied upon as the sole protection against malicious input." The sandbox: "this is process-level isolation (no parent env, no shell), NOT a full security sandbox". The capture ordering is the other decision to copy: credential-shaped text is redacted before hashing, embedding, indexing or encryption, "so neither SQLite nor an embedding blob preserves a recoverable copy of a leaked credential". Encryption states its edge too: "[t]itles and tags stay plaintext: they are the only handle recall has on an encrypted shard, so keep identifying detail out of them". Federation keeps that edge: `/sync/pull` ships encrypted bodies as ciphertext

Main risks.value: The licence is source-available and not open source: commercial use needs a subscription or written permission, and redistribution for a fee, competing hosted services and use to train, develop or improve competing AI memory or retrieval products are prohibited. The MCP tool `batch_execute_sandboxed` runs agent-supplied code with `trusted=True`, so the opt-in that refuses the single-command tool does not apply to it and only the denylist stands. The brain scan, the product's central import, discards the timestamps its parsers read, so the event axis says nothing about scanned history. `domain_key` organises rather than isolates. `shard_forget` leaves the hash in the dedup index, so identical content is refused afterwards with `durable: true` for a row that is gone. The node's `temporal_query` answers `as_of` on event time

Scoping model.value: A scope column set from the normalized git remote, with the empty string as global; a project read also returns global rows.
