Memory unit.value: A project-memory record with a summary, a revision, a scope, a retention class, a safety evaluation and an admission block; plus memory blocks by label and tier for prompt assembly

Storage backend.value: JSON files under an OMH home — `candidates/`, `records/`, `reviews/`, `scopes/`, `operations/`, `tombstones/` — written atomically under a store-wide file lock, with an index rebuilt from the directories

Retrieval strategy.value: Scoped lookup over the record index with ranking, plus a separate rejected-decision recall surface that is deliberately not prompt-eligible

Write strategy.value: Capture produces a candidate; approval promotes it to a record. Batch staging, review and apply are three distinct CLI commands, and the apply requires an explicit `--apply`

Update/delete model.value: Revisions with a staleness check that fails closed on a changed card; forgets and scope changes write a tombstone keyed on the item and are verified afterwards against the expected end state; lifecycle demotion, retirement and reapproval have their own executor

Scoping model.value: Records carry a scope, stored one directory per scope with a principal ref; the scope selects which scope file is read rather than being applied as a predicate to a shared query

Agent integration.value: An operating layer installed alongside NousResearch's Hermes Agent — `omh` CLI, skills, roles and a plugin bundle, keeping Hermes in place rather than replacing it

Background processing.value: Operation recovery on startup for interrupted writes, evidence pruning on a retention window, lifecycle scans for stale and expired records, and sync-fidelity validation of applied batches

Trust/provenance model.value: An admission state on every record that gates prompt assembly and replay; a safety evaluation re-run at approval time, not only at capture; credential-like reviewer metadata refused; blocked candidates refusable only by rejection or recapture

Notable strengths.value: The approval is a property of the record rather than an event in a log — `approved_manual` and `approved_auto_safe` are distinct stored values, so a record admitted without a person is permanently marked as such instead of being indistinguishable afterwards. The single-candidate approval does its read, its staleness check and its write under one hold of the store lock, with a comment naming the interleaving that made the guard advisory before. Safety is re-evaluated against the current policy at approval time, so a candidate captured under a looser policy cannot be admitted under it. The rejected-decision surface keeps refusals retrievable while marking them not renderable as instruction. Operations carry a state machine with recovery counts, so an interrupted write is resumable rather than ambiguous

Main risks.value: The governance is not uniform across write paths. `approve_project_memory_candidate` — the ordinary way a record is admitted — writes no operation record, while the batch, lifecycle, migration and principal-assignment paths all do. The per-candidate review file is keyed `review_{candidate_id}` and written with `atomic_write_json`, so a re-approval overwrites the previous decision rather than appending to it, and a candidate's decision history is not kept. `prune_expired_memory_evidence` deletes operations and tombstones older than thirty days by default, so the evidence behind an old admission expires while the record it admitted does not. Tombstones are keyed on the record id and revision, not on the value, so they mark that something was forgotten rather than preventing the same content being re-captured and re-approved. In `auto-safe` mode a candidate passing the safety evaluation is admitted with no person involved

Memory unit.value: A concept: one markdown file with YAML frontmatter carrying type, title, description, tags, a `generated` provenance stamp, `verified` entries, `status`, `governance`, `code_refs`, `stale_after`, sources and an optional attestation

Storage backend.value: Plain markdown under `knowledge/` in the repository, parsed by a zero-dependency Go library; no database and no vector store

Retrieval strategy.value: In-memory BM25 over the bundle, plus a code-path leg matching `code_refs`, ranked with a governance multiplier

Write strategy.value: `okf create` and `okf update` from the CLI, or `okf_create` and `okf_update` over MCP; both round-trip the frontmatter through the parser rather than editing text

Update/delete model.value: An update rewrites the file and appends a log entry; there is no delete in the library, so erasure is a file removal outside the tool

Scoping model.value: The bundle directory is the boundary; there is no scope key on a concept and no scope predicate on a search

Agent integration.value: A single Go binary serving a CLI and an MCP server with six tools, plus `okf agents link`, which symlinks `CLAUDE.md` and other tool instruction files at a single source of truth

Background processing.value: None; validation, linting and search are invoked, and CI runs the validator over the repository's own bundle

Trust/provenance model.value: `generated` records which agent wrote a concept and when, `verified` and `attestation` record checking, and a validator gates the bundle's structure in CI

Notable strengths.value: The write path is built as though the thing writing it is not trustworthy, which for agent-written memory is the correct assumption. `mutate_security_test.go` covers path traversal on save and on parent-index update, reserved root and subdirectory filenames, symlinks pointing at reserved or non-markdown targets, external symlinks on load, YAML quoting, and newline sanitisation on both log entries and relations — and `TestSaveConceptRejectsFrontmatterInjection` is the one that matters most here, because a concept body reaches other agents as instructions: `okf agents link` symlinks `CLAUDE.md` and its equivalents at the bundle, so a frontmatter key smuggled through a description would be read as configuration by every tool in the repository. The second thing worth taking is the log: a dated, in-band change record that the MCP path cannot disable, which is a stronger claim than the `git log` the README offers, since a commit records what a human chose to stage and this records what the tool actually wrote

Main risks.value: Three frontmatter fields read like epistemic state and only one of them reaches retrieval. `status` is parsed, validated against `draft|stable|deprecated`, and serialized back, and no read path consults it: `okf search` ranks a deprecated concept exactly as it ranks a stable one. `stale_after` is the same shape — the validator emits a warning once the date has passed, and search is unaffected, so a concept the tool itself calls stale is still handed to an agent at full weight. `governance` is the one search does read, and it multiplies the score, so the effect of the trust vocabulary on retrieval is to promote rather than to withhold. The `hold` level compounds this: `EffectiveGovernance` documents it as "execution freeze / manual signoff required", but the freeze exists only as a line of bootstrap prompt text — `IF governance == "hold" => STOP("Subsystem frozen by governance. Request explicit human confirmation.")` — so the code ranks the concept higher and asks the model to stop, which is an instruction rather than a gate. Smaller: `okf update --help` offers `'active'` as an example status, and the validator rejects it, while `stable`, the value that is valid, goes unmentioned

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A JSON record of string fields in one SQLite row under `mem:<namespace>:<ulid>`, in one of five namespaces — episodic, project, knowledge, preference, skill — with a 384-dimension vector in a side table, a lifecycle state, a trust value, a surface score, licence and provenance labels, and on episodic rows effort, outcome, breakthrough, lesson and a JSON graveyard of abandoned approaches

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file: a memories table whose state, trust, project and timestamp columns are generated from the record, a vectors table loaded into an in-process matrix and searched exactly, a kv table for suppressed topics and their reasons, pending resolutions, 30-day recall logs and counters, an audit table, and a durable enrichment queue

Retrieval strategy.value: A word-boundary keyword scan of the graveyard, kept to the caller's project by default, before embedding, up to three warnings ahead of the results; then exact KNN per namespace over keys pre-filtered in SQL by state, project and trust, suppressed topics dropped by word match, scored as similarity × surface × recency × experience × a date boost × a trust weight, superseded memories folded into their winner, extracted facts folded into their source, a floor on raw similarity

Write strategy.value: remember embeds, refuses a near-duplicate at cosine 0.92 in the same project, warns on a negation-pattern contradiction, stores as accepted, and queues Claude fact extraction that writes facts and preferences at surface 0.5 as candidates carrying enriched_from and as_of; force skips all three checks; a Claude Code session-end hook writes a redacted session record

Update/delete model.value: A four-state lifecycle — active, deprioritised (x0.2, with a reason and reinstate hints), archived (x0, excluded in SQL, with a reason), deleted (row removed, its text scrubbed from the audit log) — that extracted facts follow; a contradiction resolved as supersedes, both valid, both wrong, false positive or reopened, recorded on both links with its history; forget previews before it deletes

Scoping model.value: project on every row, applied in SQL to every searched namespace and re-checked in Rust, on the briefing's reads, and to the graveyard and the pre-tool-use hook under the default GRAVEYARD_SCOPE=project; an unscoped recall and warn_if_abandoned read every project's dead ends

Agent integration.value: One binary: 48 MCP tools over streamable HTTP with bearer or OAuth 2.1 auth and a 96-line instruction block, MCP elicitation for the two gated calls, a desktop tray app whose settings panel is served to its own window over omnimem://, a CLI for trust, contradictions and the audit log, an RSS thread, and Claude Code hooks for session start, pre-tool-use and session end

Background processing.value: An enrichment worker polling the queue table; RSS ingestion on a schedule; a maintenance pass every tenth briefing per project — audit pruning, dedup, a negation scan that links and, when the model confirms, disputes, article expiry; a daily skill scan that proposes drafts; a release check against the Forgejo API unless UPDATE_CHECK is off

Trust/provenance model.value: A trust value per memory, set by person, model-confirmed contradiction or resolution and acted on by every recall and the briefing; a lifecycle state with a stored reason; provenance says who is speaking and is never filtered on; an audit log of state changes, deletes and suppressions, pruned after 90 days by default

Notable strengths.value: A graveyard matched on word boundaries before any embedding and enforced at the point of action by a hook that denies a mutating tool call and returns the way out; an extracted fact that stays a candidate until a person confirms it; an agent's skill write and contradiction verdict turned into a question the client puts to the person; a negative-recall suite whose excluded rows are asserted near-duplicates of the query

Main risks.value: Audit rows older than 90 days are deleted at startup and on every maintenance pass by default; the briefing and the graveyard ignore suppressed topics; the graveyard ignores trust and state, so a rejected or archived memory's dead end still denies a tool call; the human gates rest on a CLI any shell can run and on a client that does not auto-accept; force bypasses three checks

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: One merged record per composite key, shaped by a caller-supplied Pydantic schema, with the raw pre-merge extractions of each contributing document kept beside it when the ledger is on

Storage backend.value: Files: the merged store, a FAISS index with an `index.meta.json` companion, and an optional source ledger holding the current version of each source's raw results

Retrieval strategy.value: Vector search over the merged records, with O(1) secondary lookups by custom key and an optional restriction to named source ids or tags

Write strategy.value: `add(items, source_id=...)` extracts and merges into the existing record for a key, through either a deterministic merger or an LLM one

Update/delete model.value: `remove_source()` re-merges the surviving sources for every affected key; `upsert_source()` replaces a document in one step; `edit()` removes one wrong fact from a record with key-invariance validation and a dry run

Scoping model.value: None enforced — `source_ids` and `tags` are optional search filters the caller supplies, with union semantics across a key's contributing sources

Agent integration.value: A Python library, published to PyPI, with a documentation site; no server and no agent protocol surface

Background processing.value: None; consolidation happens on the write that triggers it

Trust/provenance model.value: Provenance through the source ledger, an embedder signature that refuses vectors from a different embedding space, and key-invariance validation on a semantic edit

Notable strengths.value: The source ledger earns its overhead by naming the problem it exists for: "because merges are destructive, the only way to remove a source's contributions precisely is to re-merge the surviving sources' raw results for the affected keys." That sentence is the whole design. Most stores that consolidate on write cannot answer what a particular document contributed, and so cannot take it back — they can only delete every key it touched. OntoMem keeps each source's raw pre-merge extraction, which lets `remove_source(strategy="exact")` recompute the affected keys from the survivors and delete only those nothing else contributed to. The coarse alternative is kept and named rather than hidden: `strategy="touched"` deletes every key the source touched, which is what a system without the ledger is forced to do. The overhead is stated as a number ("~1.5-2x storage") and bounded on purpose, since only the current version per source is retained. Two smaller pieces are worth taking: the FAISS index records an embedder signature in an `index.meta.json` companion and refuses vectors from a different embedding space, which turns a silent similarity-nonsense bug into a load-time refusal; and `edit()` validates key-invariance before applying a semantic edit, so removing a wrong fact cannot quietly move the record to a different key

Main risks.value: Nothing here carries epistemic state. A merged record has no status, no validity interval, no recorded-at, no confidence and no supersession link, so a claim that stopped being true and one nobody has checked are indistinguishable from one that was verified this morning — the merge produces a single current value per key and the history of how it got there lives only in the ledger's current-version-per-source snapshot, which is not an append-only record of what changed. Scoping is a caller-supplied search filter (`source_ids`, `tags`) with union semantics, so a key contributed to by several documents matches when any one of them fits; there is no stored key applied on the caller's behalf, and nothing separates one tenant's records from another's. Deletion has no memory: `remove_source` reverses a document's contribution and leaves nothing keyed on what was removed, so re-adding the same document restores the same claims with no sign the store was once asked to drop them. And the surface is a library — 5,774 lines across 36 files, no server, no agent protocol — so everything above is the caller's to wire

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A `MemoryCard` — an entity name, up to six aliases, a category of personne, organisation, projet or autre, a bounded `facts` string of at most 600 characters that compacts rather than grows, a `factsLog` of up to three replaced sentences, a `source: "auto"` when the extraction wrote it, `reviewedAt`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt` — plus one always-injected `profile` of at most 1,200 characters

Storage backend.value: The `memoire` field of the settings object — in the desktop app's per-account libSQL file, encrypted at rest in packaged builds through an Electron `safeStorage` key and stripped from the plaintext `localStorage` mirror whenever that database exists; in an account-keyed `localStorage` entry alone in the browser preview; per-card e5 vectors and text hashes in a `memory_embeddings` table on the desktop; cards and profile ride the end-to-end encrypted user-data sync without `factsLog` or `reviewedAt`

Retrieval strategy.value: At send time a deterministic client-side cascade on real values — the typed text mentions the entity or an alias, the entity is in the conversation's vault, or a distinctive token appears — then one hop along cards whose facts name a certainly-mentioned entity, filled by score then recency under a 4,000-character budget; on demand, `memory_search` scores cards by content-word hits and tops up from an on-device multilingual-e5-small index above cosine 0.88

Write strategy.value: Deferred: an idle timer of 120 seconds after a turn, a flush on blur or switching conversations, and a startup sweep over at most three recent conversations run one extraction call with the conversation's own model at temperature 0 over the replayed wire of turns whose redaction completed, off by default; an explicit « retiens que… » runs regardless, re-reads a few earlier turns, includes the assistant's, sweeps up to four calls with an exclusion list and reports its count; every entity must anchor verbatim in the real text or is dropped

Update/delete model.value: An attribute fact replaces its competing sentence and the loser enters `factsLog`; a restatement keeps the richer version and logs nothing; saturation evicts whole sentences oldest first; a card updates in place; delete is immediate with a six-second undo and syncs as a tombstone keyed on the card id; there is no supersession record, no TTL and no value-keyed rejection

Scoping model.value: One store per signed-in account, selected by a per-account database file or storage key at load; no scope key on a card; a per-conversation switch cuts both the injection and the tool; an organisation's remote flag hides the Mémoire screen and leaves injection, search and extraction running

Agent integration.value: A block titled « Mémoire de l'utilisateur » inside the system content of every send, built before the user-message pass so its entities are forced into the vault, then pseudonymised through the same engine as the message; a `memory_search` tool offered to the model only when the store is non-empty and the conversation allows it, whose query is un-redacted and whose result is re-redacted; a « Mémoire utilisée » caption under each message naming the cards that rode it, by id

Background processing.value: No consolidation pass; `autoCleanMemory` runs on every store change as an idempotent fixpoint — migrating auto-written self-preferences into the profile, merging same-key cards and identical notes, recompacting a card that repeats itself — and the desktop re-embeds changed cards 800 ms after an edit

Trust/provenance model.value: Provenance is one flag; the vault is the anti-hallucination filter, since an extracted entity must resolve to text the user or the assistant actually wrote; a pseudonym the vault cannot map back is refused; secret shapes are dropped; a real failure is shown as « réessayez » instead of a count of zero; no state ever keeps a card out of a prompt

Notable strengths.value: Egress-neutral extraction by design, replaying only redacted turns through the send-time substitution; injection selected on real values and forced into the redaction vault so a remembered name cannot leak under the regex engine; attribute replacement with a restorable history; measured thresholds with the measurements written beside them; a scenario suite that runs the product's own pipeline over a growing memory

Main risks.value: Cards live in the clear on the machine and in plaintext `localStorage` wherever there is no host database; the inbox is the only review and nothing waits for it, which is why no review mark is carried; a card's only time is its last update, injected as a date the model is asked to reason from; the restorable history and the review state stay on the device that wrote them; French-keyed attribute and glue lists

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Two: a provider memory written through memory_add (a Hindsight bank item, a mem0 memory with infer false, a Cognee dataset entry), and a session-store row, one per content block of a proxied message, chained by fingerprint and kept verbatim

Storage backend.value: Provider memory is delegated to one active Hindsight, mem0 or Cognee server, Hindsight pinned by image digest. The session store is one SQLite file per session in WAL mode with FTS5 over messages and lines, float32 vectors, and a shared blobs directory of full tool results

Retrieval strategy.value: Provider recall is the provider's, reached by bank. The session store runs FTS5 BM25 fused by reciprocal rank with brute-force cosine over embedded heads, or a regex scan, over up to 20 sessions registered to the same repository, plus one read-only SELECT under a SQLite authorizer

Write strategy.value: SessionStart and prompt hooks recall; the Stop hook retains up to 12,000 characters of new transcript text per turn into the project bank, async on Hindsight. The proxy writes every message of every request it handles into the session store before forwarding; agents call memory_add directly

Update/delete model.value: No update verb. memory_forget deletes a mem0 memory by id or drops a whole Hindsight bank, and is refused on Cognee; the skill tells agents to correct by adding a new memory. The indexer deletes documents whose source file disappeared. Session files expire after 30 days; blobs never do

Scoping model.value: A bank string resolved from the workspace's git root through index.yml, then two JSON mappings, then coding-agent:: plus the repository name. Hooks pass it; the memory_* tools take any bank the model names. Session reads default to sessions registered under the same repository and accept any explicit session id

Agent integration.value: A stdio MCP server with 19 tools, session hooks for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, plugins for OpenCode 1 and 2, a LiteLLM pre-call hook as context proxy, an indexer container, a setup wizard and a shipped skill

Background processing.value: The indexer polls git repositories and watches vaults and note trees, retaining changed documents and deleting vanished ones; it turns Hindsight auto-consolidation off on banks it prepares. project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Two units. An `episode` is a raw message turn — role, content, metadata, sequence number, embedding, an enrichment status bitmask and a soft-delete flag. A `fact` is what an LLM extracted from it: a subject, predicate and object with types and optional entity ids, a confidence float, the source episode, `valid_from`/`valid_to`/`invalid_at`, a `superseded_by_fact_id` and its own embedding

Storage backend.value: PostgreSQL with pgvector (768-dimension columns under HNSW cosine indexes), pg_trgm and btree_gist, 62 Alembic revisions; Redis for the ARQ job queues and cache; a pluggable graph backend defaulting to FalkorDB with one graph per organisation and project, with SurrealDB and a deprecated Postgres-native backend beside it

Retrieval strategy.value: Five legs run in sequence — vector over episodes, vector over facts, BM25 over episodes, BM25 over facts, and a breadth-first graph walk — fused by reciprocal rank at k=60 with episodes and facts fused separately and entities bypassing fusion, then an optional cross-encoder rerank. Any leg failing aborts the whole search rather than returning a partial result, and there is no relevance threshold anywhere on the path

Write strategy.value: `POST /v1/projects/{id}/memory` stores the turn inline — archived-project check, idempotency key, session resolution, an atomic content-hash claim, fail-closed PII redaction, sequence numbers under a session row lock, batch insert, commit — then enqueues three background jobs per episode: one LLM call producing classification, entities, fact triples, structured extractions and contradiction invalidations in a single response, applied in independent savepoints, plus embedding and entity linking

Update/delete model.value: A fact is never edited. Re-asserting the same normalized triple with new content, or an LLM-detected contradiction, closes the predecessor's window with `valid_to = now`; retraction sets `invalid_at`; each is recorded in `fact_invalidation_events` as superseded, llm_invalidated or retracted, and the fourth permitted kind, time_expired, has no writer. The retracted set is consulted before every insert. The project wipe soft-deletes episodes and stamps `invalid_at` on every fact, so each wiped triple becomes a tombstone and the facts stay readable through an earlier `as_of`

Scoping model.value: An organisation and a project column on every record and a membership dependency on every project-scoped route; the four search legs filter on the project and the graph leg opens a per-organisation-and-project graph; row-level security on the organisation binds only a role that does not own the tables

Agent integration.value: A FastAPI service with thirty-one router modules, an ARQ worker with fifteen task types and a cron schedule, a Streamlit chat client, Docker Compose and Helm charts, OpenBao for secrets and a Grafana stack. The MCP server the README advertises is not in this repository

Background processing.value: Enrichment with contradiction invalidation, embedding, entity linking, blob text extraction, audit writes, entity merging, community summarisation, observation computation, webhook delivery, user summaries, orphan-blob cleanup, and cron jobs that reconcile stalled enrichment and expire graph edges

Trust/provenance model.value: A confidence float on a fact, thresholded at 0.3 once at extraction time and offered as a sort key on the fact listings; no status, no state, and no retrieval leg ranks or filters on it

Notable strengths.value: One effective-at test applied on every fact search and listing, with an as-of instant threaded from the route to the graph backends; a retraction gate keyed on the normalized triple and consulted on both insert paths; a negative test that forces the ranking to fail if the filter does; a cross-tenant search test with a positive control

Main risks.value: The project wipe stamps the retraction column on every fact, so wiped facts stay readable through an earlier as_of and every wiped triple is refused if it is said again; the effective-at test is restated inline at most read sites rather than shared; the search SQL carries the project key and not the organisation key, and row-level security binds only a role that does not own the tables, which the tag-deploy workflow's single database URL does not arrange; a superseded triple is inserted again by design; no GitHub Actions job runs the cross-tenant suite; `episodes.token_count` is returned to clients and written by nothing; the context formatter's community section is always handed an empty list

Memory unit.value: A Markdown document the agent writes and maintains: an operator.md of standing instructions and a catalog.md per partition, codebase index files with description and read_if frontmatter, and freeform specs, guides and plans

Storage backend.value: Three directories: a private project partition in .operator/ added to the user's global git excludes, a shared partition in .operator-shared/ committed with the repository, and a user partition in the home directory

Retrieval strategy.value: None in code. Each session receives the fixed guidance, all three instruction files, the root catalogs, the main index bodies and a listing of every index file; the agent opens anything else with its own file tools when a Read If line matches

Write strategy.value: The model edits the Markdown with the harness's ordinary file tools, steered by a fixed preamble; the helper CLI only seeds missing core files from templates

Update/delete model.value: Rewrite in place and delete obsolete documents, per the preamble's instruction to state what is true now; the shared partition keeps git history, the private partition keeps none

Scoping model.value: Physical partitions by directory, merged at injection with private over user over shared for instructions; no key on a document and no predicate on a read

Agent integration.value: Adapters for Claude Code (an in-process mod on prompt.compose and agent.spawn), Codex (SessionStart and SubagentStart command hooks), OpenCode V1 and V2, Pi, DeepSeek Harness, and a Kiro hook installed by the helper

Background processing.value: None; the preamble is rendered once per session or per process and nothing rewrites the store

Trust/provenance model.value: Every injected document is presented to the model as instruction or system truth; any partition failing to load suppresses all memory and leaves a repair diagnostic

Notable strengths.value: A deterministic, byte-stable session preamble across six harnesses with an all-or-nothing load rule, a progressive-disclosure index and catalog, and a store a person can open and edit

Main risks.value: Write quality rests entirely on the model following prompt rules; nothing bounds the injected size; corrections leave no residue; a cloned repository's shared operator.md enters the system prompt

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A markdown entry with a machine id — a DECISIONS heading, a numbered LESSONS item, a PROJECT_STATE bullet — stamped with id, created, touched and an optional pinned tag in a one-line HTML comment; and an ask, which is a line of events rather than a record

Storage backend.value: Plain files in the project folder under orbital: four budgeted Layer-1 files, their read-on-demand archives, and ASKS.md

Retrieval strategy.value: Whole-file injection each turn, capped per file by a budget derived from the active model's context window; over the cap the newest entries within budget are shown plus the oldest three, with a note saying what was omitted

Write strategy.value: The agent's write and edit tools, routed through a per-file chokepoint that stamps ids, re-applies the format contract and enforces the append-only rule on the asks log

Update/delete model.value: Nothing is deleted. An oversize durable file demotes its coldest entries to an archive and leaves an addressable pointer in their place; PROJECT_STATE moves only lines older than a fourteen-day probation window and stays over budget rather than cutting recent work; INDEX alone is tail-trimmed, because it is regenerable navigation

Scoping model.value: One project folder per project, with the memory-file router resolving symlinks and requiring the parent directory to be the project's own orbital directory; no scope key reaches a query

Agent integration.value: A desktop app for Windows and macOS with a daemon, a web Workbench, a calendar hub, and worker agents driven over Claude Code, Codex and Cursor transports

Background processing.value: A session-end pass: a deterministic size backstop that never calls a model, then an LLM memory editor that proposes archives, merges and ask closes by id, behind a mandatory backup and a single-flight lock

Trust/provenance model.value: No epistemic state on any entry. An ask carries a lifecycle — open, done, dropped, reopen — with the actor on every close; a durable entry carries only a pinned tag and its touched date

Notable strengths.value: A demotion path that refuses to move an entry with no id, on the stated ground that an unaddressable entry could not be recalled; an archive written before the live file shrinks, with the failure branch leaving the live file intact; and a set of rules written as comments beside the code that each name the incident that produced them

Main risks.value: The dropped-ask refusal keys on exact normalised text while the fuzzy matcher built for that job sits in a module with no callers; the format contract the agent reads is normalised over whatever the agent wrote, so a project cannot keep a local variant; and the budgets are tuned to one named model, with everything below roughly eighty thousand tokens falling back to a proportional scale

Memory unit.value: A Markdown file in the agent's scratch folder: CLAUDE.md as curated standing notes and breadcrumbs.md as an append-by-convention log. Archived sessions (knowledge bearers) and a hash-checked handoff record per session boundary sit beside them

Storage backend.value: Plain files under scratch/SLUG/NODE, shared by every generation of one seat; the node records, bearer lineage and the cheap_compacted marker live in the org's PostgreSQL store

Retrieval strategy.value: None by relevance. Write strategy.value: The agent edits its own files with its CLI's file or shell tools, prompted by the managed system prompt to append to breadcrumbs.md as events happen. No engine verb writes either file

Update/delete model.value: Edit or overwrite the file. A user-only delete removes the scratch folder; retiring keeps it. No tombstone, no version kept by the engine

Scoping model.value: Physical: one scratch folder per seat. Cross-agent reads pass an access check: self, descendants in the org chart, or earlier holders of an open docket item the reader is listed on

Agent integration.value: Managed system prompt for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and OpenRouter lanes; MCP tools orgtree_read_scratch, orgtree_read_transcript, orgtree_cheap_compact and orgtree_rehire; a warm-process identity hash that respawns an agent when its notes change

Background processing.value: None for memory content. An opt-in auto cheap compact replaces an idle session when its context passes a set fraction; the boundary exports the transcript and publishes a handoff record

Trust/provenance model.value: None on the notes. The handoff record labels every quoted line as a claim with a cited transcript line, and its prompt splice is behind a flag file nothing in the tree creates

Notable strengths.value: One promise made true on every provider lane by mirroring the notes into the prompt; first-turn-only breadcrumb splice with declared truncation and a no-fabrication fallback; memory edits move the warm-process hash; item-scoped cross-agent reads pinned by refusal tests

Memory unit.value: An object of a declared type with graded properties, links and provenance; an assertion is one source's claim about a property, chained to the one it replaced

Storage backend.value: PostgreSQL 16 with `pg_trgm`: objects, assertions split across a hot and a cold table, links, an `object_events` log, `audit_log`, a durable outbox, and embeddings as `real[]`; a Redis 7 event bus

Retrieval strategy.value: One search over active objects fusing strict full text, OR-relaxed full text, trigram and local static embeddings by reciprocal rank, weighted by evidence grade and recency; graph traversal and a per-object provenance timeline beside it

Write strategy.value: One actions layer; parsers declare an evidence class and the confidence is derived from it; a write that repeats a source's current value moves its observation time instead of adding a row

Update/delete model.value: Within-source supersession by a new row; merges, status changes and renames as events with a projection, undone by compensating events. A daily job deletes audit rows past 90 days, duplicate audit rows, no-op re-assertions and old layout rows

Scoping model.value: One graph for every agent and project; reflections alone are house-scoped on the search, provenance and select reads

Agent integration.value: A streamable-HTTP MCP server, Claude Code hooks for prompt, tool and compaction events, a CLI, and a bridge plugin for the DeepSeek Harness

Background processing.value: An arq worker running cron heartbeats: retention, storage housekeeping, embedding backfill, mining, crawl frontier and dissemination

Trust/provenance model.value: An evidence-class taxonomy behind every confidence, a lifecycle status every search route filters on, provenance on every property and link, and event rows for every identity and lifecycle change

Notable strengths.value: The evidence module names the defect it replaced: "every parser invented its own confidence number (0.4 → 0.99) with no shared meaning". A parser declares how it knew — self-declared, authoritative API, direct observation, derived, co-occurrence — and the confidence is "a *projection* of the class, not a guess". Corroboration is not a class a parser may store; the crawl frontier computes it from two or more distinct sources at read time. The lifecycle status is enforced where it matters: every route of the agent's search requires an active object, and the embedding index drops an object that leaves active, so a merged or retired object cannot return through the semantic route either. Supersession is within a source, so one source correcting itself never silences another. Merges, unmerges, status changes and renames are events carrying a justification, undone by compensating events. Reflections are house-scoped on the search path, with tests asserting that another house's caller gets no hit

Main risks.value: The append-only rule is stated in the module header and the README and relaxed by the system's own housekeeping: a default-on daily job deletes audit rows older than 90 days, retires audit rows that repeat an assertion, deletes superseded assertions that restate their predecessor, and deletes old layout assertions, all through raw SQL outside the actions layer. A repeated observation moves the existing row's `observed_at` in place. Work knowledge is fleet-readable by design. The reflection boundary is not applied by `dossier` or `list_assertions`, which return any object's current properties by reference, and the search and provenance functions take their reader from a `caller` argument that a saved composition can set to the operator. Search ranks by grade and withholds nothing by grade, and it never computes corroboration

Trust/provenance model.value: Eleven detectors with severities and block or flag actions, a source-class taxonomy, memory classification with protected keys, integrity checks, snapshots, and SIEM-shaped security events

Notable strengths.value: The self-reinforcement detector is the best statement in this corpus of a failure this atlas keeps finding: "an agent reads its own prior agent_authored memory, mildly elaborates on it, writes it back, then reads the elaborated version on the next turn and elaborates again. Over a few iterations a hallucination or attacker-suggestion is reinforced into a durable 'fact' the agent now relies on." Its two rules are the right ones — a cool-down on consecutive agent-authored writes to a key, and a self-similarity rule under which a write resembling a recent agent-authored value on the same key "is treated as reinforcement of the previous write, not independent corroboration" — with the key insight in the decay clause: only a separate `external_tool` or `user_input` write weakens the loop, because corroboration has to come from a different source class. The taxonomy around it is explicit: `external_tool` and `user_input` are "external inputs (untrusted by default)", `agent_authored` is "the self-poisoning surface", `system` is infrastructure. Eleven detectors cover injection, leakage, privilege escalation, tool abuse, excessive autonomy, ML injection, memory persistence injection, protected keys, cross-task contamination and anomaly

Main risks.value: The source class is declared by the integrating code, not derived, and the default is `UNKNOWN`. `self_reinforcement.py` states that it "[o]nly fires on writes whose source_class is AGENT_AUTHORED" and returns early otherwise, so a drop-in integration that never passes `source_class` — or maps it from the legacy `source_type`, where only `MODEL_INFERENCE` becomes `agent_authored` — gets none of the self-poisoning protection and no warning that it is off. The library cannot know the provenance itself, so this is a necessary design rather than a defect; it does mean the defence is a property of the integration's labelling discipline. Separately, the standalone `scanner/rules.py` is sixty-three lines of regex: its unprotected-write rule matches a variable literally named `memory` or `state` assigned on one line and requires `guard.wrap|check|protect` on that same line, so a guard call one line above reads as a violation and any other variable name reads as safe. Background processing.value: Decay ticks, cohere and dream passes, consolidation, hygiene scans, community detection

Trust/provenance model.value: A discrete `status`, a separate `epistemic_state` (`candidate`/`verified`/`corroborated`/`rejected`/`defensively_recalled`), a `verified` flag, a `certainty` float and a `source` field — four distinct axes rather than one score

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A record of kind note (title, body, category user, feedback, project or reference, global or project scope) or conversation (one finalized user or assistant message), with lane, session and event provenance and created and updated times; its id is a SHA-256 of the scoped normalized title, or of the event identity

Storage backend.value: One node:sqlite file under the Pi agent directory, mode 0600 in a 0700 directory, WAL: records with an external-content FTS5 index and a tombstones table of ids. A separate opt-in archive SQLite file holds raw session entries and can be encrypted

Retrieval strategy.value: FTS5 BM25 over title and body, title weighted 8 to 1, notes ahead of captures, terms quoted and ORed. Each request injects the 3 newest global notes, 5 notes by keyword and 2 captures from other sessions, capped at 6,000 bytes of escaped JSON. A search tool returns up to 10

Write strategy.value: The model calls jarvis_memory_remember, an upsert on the scoped title; finalized visible user and assistant text is captured at turn boundaries; a person uses /jarvis-memory remember and edit or the TUI editor. Synchronous SQLite, no model call, best-effort secret redaction

Update/delete model.value: Same-title upsert overwrites the body in place. Forget deletes the row and writes a tombstone on its id, which blocks every later automatic save under that scoped title until a person's explicit remember lifts it. The model's forget needs a human confirmation; bulk forget is human-only. Captures past 10,000 are pruned

Scoping model.value: A project key, the canonical cwd, on every record. The recall and the default search filter to global plus the current project, and get-by-id applies the same rule; the agent's search tool accepts scope all and widens to every project with no confirmation

Agent integration.value: A Pi extension mounted in the main session and in the Jarvis side session, three model tools, request-local context and policy injection, /jarvis-memory commands and a TUI editor; global, project and trust settings gate every tool call

Background processing.value: None. Captures are queued on message_end and written on turn_end or agent_settled; retention pruning runs inside the save transaction

Trust/provenance model.value: No status field. Recalled records are framed as untrusted historical data, with lane and session provenance, and the guidance tells the model to ask on conflicts

Notable strengths.value: Identity by scoped title, so a rename or forget leaves a tombstone that refuses the model's next save of that title; request-local recall that is never written to the transcript; trust and policy rechecked at each tool call; a schema and integrity validation that refuses to open a store it does not recognise

Main risks.value: The tombstone is keyed on the title, so the same fact under a new title is admitted; the model's upsert silently overwrites a note a person wrote; the agent's search tool reads every project with no gate, though the same repository gates the archive's identical widening; no record of prior values

Memory unit.value: An entry of a Pi session journal (a user, assistant, tool-result, bash, custom, compaction or branch-summary line), indexed by entry id, parent id, timestamp, kind, role, tool name, character count and the byte offset and length of its line

Storage backend.value: Pi's own JSONL session journals hold the text; a derived SQLite index holds file cursors, entry rows and a contentless FTS5 table of redacted terms, and can be deleted and rebuilt from the journals

Retrieval strategy.value: One on-demand tool: BM25 full-text search with all-terms-then-any-term fallback and a one-month recency discount, a newest-first listing, a list of compaction summaries, and a paged read of one entry reread from its journal line; filters by local-day or ISO date range, kind and a project, session or global scope

Write strategy.value: No memory writes by the agent. The index follows the current journal on session start, message end, compaction and tree moves, and one process at a time backfills other journals under a lease

Update/delete model.value: Index rows follow the journal: a journal that shrank is dropped and reindexed from the start. `/memory rebuild` deletes the index; `/memory gc` lists junk journals and `/memory gc confirm` hard-deletes exactly those, if unchanged since the preview, with their index rows

Scoping model.value: A project root derived from the session cwd is the default filter; the agent may pass session or global instead, and a read by entry id is not scoped

Agent integration.value: A Pi extension registering one tool, `memory_context`, and one command, `/memory`; it hooks no context, prompt or provider event

Background processing.value: Incremental indexing in 12 ms time slices with a yield between them, a delayed backfill of older journals under a two-minute lease, and a user-run junk-journal collector

Trust/provenance model.value: Secret redaction before terms are indexed and again on every returned text, FTS syntax quoted to literal terms, and a deletion that touches only the files a preview listed

Notable strengths.value: The store keeps no second copy of anything: the index holds search terms in a contentless FTS5 table and a byte pointer into the journal line, and every returned text is reread from the journal and redacted on the way out, so deleting the index loses nothing. Secrets are redacted before they become search terms, and a committed test asserts a key is neither searchable nor readable. Nothing reaches the model unless it calls the tool, and a test asserts the context, prompt and provider hooks are not registered. The junk collector deletes only the files its preview listed and keeps any that changed since

Main risks.value: The project scope is a default, not a boundary: `global` is a value of the agent's own `scope` argument, and a read by entry id is not filtered by project at all. A read seeks to the stored offset and returns whatever entry parses there without checking its id, and a journal is reindexed only when it shrinks. Redaction is pattern-based and the journal keeps the unredacted text. `/memory gc confirm` hard-deletes Pi's own journals, which are the only copy. The curated-fact databases of earlier versions are left on disk, and nothing in this tree reads or deletes them

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: An engram — an id, a version, a status, a commitment, a type and a scope; a statement with a rationale and contraindications; lineage through source, derivation count, pack and abstract; activation strengths; typed relations and weighted associations; provenance with an origin chain and a reserved signature; attribution naming the runtime, model and tool that asserted it; a claim class; feedback and usage counters; and an optional temporal block, episodic block and insight block

Retrieval strategy.value: BM25 with k1 1.2 and b 0.75 over a rewritten lexical query, optionally fused by reciprocal rank at k=60 with a local ONNX embedder over the original query, then an opt-in cross-encoder rerank. There is no relevance threshold in either leg; the fusion score is surfaced so a caller can apply one

Write strategy.value: The model authors the statement and it is stored verbatim — the only rewriting is stripping tool-call envelope artifacts and a derived eighty-character summary. Content-hash dedup against active engrams absorbs a repeat. A batch path lets a model decide add, update or merge, and a failure report has a model rewrite a procedural statement

Update/delete model.value: Three correction paths with different memories. The batch dedup and the failure report both preserve the prior text in a history event with the deciding model as the actor; the direct update overwrites in place with no history event and no version bump. Forget decrements a reference count and, at zero, sets status retired — the row and its full statement stay in the YAML, and no pruning of retired engrams exists

Scoping model.value: A free-form scope string with segment-aware containment, a personal-family pass-through, mounted-store grants, and a separate exact-membership authorization filter whose empty list matches nothing

Agent integration.value: 43 MCP tools, a CLI, a Claude Code and an OpenClaw plugin manifest, a read-only loopback dashboard, a migration package, and Python packages for Hermes and LangChain

Background processing.value: No consolidation pass on the memory. Sessions, packs and an outbox sync are explicit operations; the audit history is never synced

Trust/provenance model.value: A five-value commitment where draft withholds from injection, a four-value status where retired withholds from retrieval, a claim class naming how a statement was arrived at, an attribution block naming the asserting runtime and model, and activation strengths used for ranking

Notable strengths.value: A withholding state whose gate is enforced in the injector rather than in a caller; validity time separate from record time and filtered on both read paths; a scope filter whose empty grant matches nothing, stated in the source as a security rule; an append-only mutation history in the store's own directory; 4,893 committed test cases against 66,632 lines of source

Main risks.value: A retired engram is excluded from the content-hash dedup by design, so re-asserting it creates a new engram and a committed test pins that behaviour; nothing in this repository can approve a draft, and the schema points at a separate enterprise repository for the write sites; the direct update path destroys the prior statement without a history event; the `candidate` status is declared and assigned by nothing, which leaves a shipped promote tool with nothing to act on; the benchmark harness behind every published number was moved to another repository

Memory unit.value: One row in the events table: typed content (fact, qa, activity, preference, summary, goal and others), a metadata JSON blob, importance, access count, a decay tier and an archived_at stamp. Lessons, failures and keyed facts are facts told apart by metadata

Storage backend.value: One directory per workspace under ~/.pmb/workspaces: events.sqlite as the source of truth, a LanceDB vector table, and a pickled BM25 index. Entity graph, arcs, dedup queue and lesson-surface log are further SQLite tables in the same file

Write strategy.value: Explicit MCP tools (record_batch through a durable outbox, record_keyed_fact) plus hooks: a Stop hook journals the turn when the agent did not, and a prompt hook writes a draft lesson when a message reads as a correction. Exact and cosine dedup at write time; secrets redacted

Update/delete model.value: forget archives and is reversible; delete --hard purges the row, vector and graph links. A keyed fact supersedes the prior value by archiving it with superseded_by and valid_to. A negating statement archives the current keyed value. No tombstone

Scoping model.value: Physical: one SQLite file and one vector table per workspace, chosen by env var, a .pmb/workspace.yaml, a persisted default, or a hash of the git remote or path. A project filter over metadata and content exists on the MCP recall tool and is optional

Background processing.value: An embed queue and a write-outbox drainer. The daemon runs a maintenance tick every 24 hours of idle uptime: importance decay over every active row, archive of cold rows, conflict and declutter reports. Optional LLM passes for consolidation and borderline dedup

Trust/provenance model.value: None. No status field; a correction draft is excluded from lesson lists by source, and the server instructions tell the model to trust any result scoring above 0.2 over code

Notable strengths.value: Durable outbox makes the sub-millisecond async write crash-safe; every read path filters archived rows; hooks inject without the model calling a tool; lesson follow-through is measured with Wilson intervals and kept out of ranking; decay floors lessons and never deletes; secrets redacted at the persistence boundary

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A message row in Lance — `session_id`, `id`, `role`, `source_agent`, `project`, `content`, `search_text`, a `vector` and its `embedding_model`, a timestamp, and `parent_session_id`/`parent_message_id` so a forked or resumed session keeps its lineage. Beneath it a part row: an `ordinal`, a `type`, a `provenance` of `conversational` or `injected`, and for a tool call a `tool_name`, a `call_id` and an `is_failure` flag

Storage backend.value: Lance columnar datasets in storage the user owns — a local directory or their own S3 bucket — with a row-id map for hydration, snapshots, and a sync-state record per source. Ingest is described as lossless: the transcript goes in whole, including the parts that will never be searchable

Retrieval strategy.value: Two arms over the Lance datasets, hydrated from a row-id map so a hit takes the exact row rather than re-finding it with an `IN` predicate. `search_text` is the lexical column and a `vector` column with its `embedding_model` recorded beside it is the semantic one. A SQL surface exposes the corpus for arbitrary queries, and results reach an agent over MCP

Write strategy.value: Adapters per harness parse a session and upsert messages and parts, returning an `UpsertStatus` so a re-ingest is idempotent rather than duplicating. `search_text` is computed at write time from the conversational parts only, so what is indexed is decided at ingest and what is stored is everything

Update/delete model.value: Re-ingest upserts rather than appending duplicates, and a sync-state record tracks what each source has already contributed. The archive is the point, so there is no forgetting pass, no decay and no deletion verb for a memory; what exists is a store the user owns and can delete at the filesystem or bucket level

Scoping model.value: `project` and `source_agent` are stored on every message and are available as optional filters — the project filter is a contains-or-regex predicate a caller supplies. Nothing is applied by default: the corpus spans every tool and every project on the machine, which is the product's argument

Agent integration.value: An MCP server so an agent can query the corpus directly, a CLI, and Homebrew and Scoop packages. Sessions can be restored into any supported client and continued there, so a session is no longer locked to the tool that wrote it

Background processing.value: A scheduler for periodic ingest, snapshotting, and a prewarm that builds the row-id map so hydration can take rows directly. No consolidation, no summarisation and no decay — the corpus is meant to grow

Trust/provenance model.value: One discrete field, and it is about origin rather than truth: a part is `conversational` or `injected`, and an unknown value is a hard parse error rather than a default. Only conversational parts reach the index. Beside it, `is_failure` on a tool part records that a call failed. No confidence, no verification state and no validity interval anywhere

Notable strengths.value: Storing the whole transcript and indexing only the part a person actually said, so harness scaffolding is preserved for reconstruction and cannot be retrieved as speech; an unknown provenance value that fails the parse instead of defaulting; a paired test that drives the real function on both arms; Lance columnar storage in a bucket the user owns rather than a database the tool operates; session restore across clients, which makes the archive useful for continuation and not only for search

Main risks.value: No scope applied by default, so one corpus answers across every project and tool on the machine and the filters are a caller's option; session content is not redacted on the way in — the codebase redacts credentials in `pond config show` and does nothing of the kind at ingest, so a lossless archive of every session is a lossless archive of every secret pasted into one; no epistemic layer at all, so a wrong conclusion from a year ago ranks by relevance like anything else; the provenance field is two-valued and decided at ingest, so a harness whose adapter mislabels a part has no second chance to be corrected

Retrieval strategy.value: There is no query. `load` renders a fixed subset of the newest or named capsule into a briefing and reports how far the repository has moved; `--format json` and `export` return the whole document or its prose half

Write strategy.value: Two phases: `preflight` writes local git facts to a JSON file, the model writes a draft, `finalize` reads both back, re-hashes named files, redacts and budgets, and runs no git of its own; trust is capped against the provenance each claim declares

Update/delete model.value: A capsule is never rewritten and validation refuses an edited one; decisions carry `active`/`superseded`; there is no delete, and capsules are related only by filename order

Scoping model.value: One repository per capsule directory; the recorded root is re-checked on load and a mismatch is reported, not refused; no principal scope

Agent integration.value: A skill plus slash commands for Claude Code, Codex CLI and Cursor, a draft-only path for hosts with no shell, and read-only transcript adapters

Background processing.value: None — every step is a command

Trust/provenance model.value: Five discrete states; `verified` is downgraded to `claimed` at parse time beside a conversational or inferred provenance, while the draft author declares both fields and file and evidence records skip the cap

Notable strengths.value: Repository facts and file hashes come from local git calls, never from the draft; the briefing states the capsule's age, recorded publication state and drift; the secret scan records that it ran

Main risks.value: No state withholds anything, and `verified` is open to any draft author who names a deterministic provenance; finalize trusts a preflight file the agent can edit; what the budget dropped is printed at finalize and not kept in the capsule

Memory unit.value: A row holding one statement with a kind (profile, bot, episodic, procedural, lesson), a supporting quote, the source chat, a trust label, an importance and a soft-delete flag; beside it, indexed chat messages, and a separate per-bot index of document chunks

Storage backend.value: memory.db in the data directory: a memories table, an FTS5 index, a sqlite-vec vec0 table sized to the embedder, a journal and an FTS index of chat messages; one knowledge.db per bot for document chunks, FTS5 and vector blobs

Retrieval strategy.value: BM25 over FTS5 and a KNN over feature-hashed bag-of-words vectors, fused by reciprocal rank, boosted by importance and recency and cut to an 800-token budget; prepended to the user message each top-level turn and available as a search tool; lexical search over past messages; a separate knowledge_search tool over document chunks

Write strategy.value: After each successful chat turn a background task asks the bot's classifier model for candidates and code drops any without a verbatim quote from the excerpt, any question or hypothetical and any secret; the model's save tool must quote the user's own message of the current turn; the owner writes through REST and the settings panel

Update/delete model.value: A consolidation call picks add, update, delete or skip against five similar memories; untrusted content cannot rewrite or retract a user-trusted row; delete is a soft flag that removes the row from both indexes; every change is journaled and the newest change per memory can be undone; no hard delete

Scoping model.value: user_id and an optional bot_id on every row, filtered on recall, list and the tools; profile and episodic facts from extraction are shared across the user's bots, the rest belong to one bot; one knowledge database file per bot

Agent integration.value: Built into the agent loop of a Rust daemon with a Tauri desktop UI and a CLI; four model-callable tools; owner REST routes and a settings panel with list, edit, forget, undo and a recall preview

Background processing.value: One extraction task per turn, spawned after the reply and flushed at shutdown; no decay, compaction or scheduled pass over the store

Trust/provenance model.value: A two-value label, user or untrusted, set from whether the turn touched tools, other bots or tainted content; it picks the block a memory is rendered in and what it may overwrite, and filters nothing; recalling an untrusted memory taints the run so later writes ask for approval

Notable strengths.value: A save the model cannot make without quoting the user; ids resolved from the run and never from arguments; a journal with snapshots and undo written in the same transaction as each change

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A `session_ledger` row — project, conversation, user, a summary and title, the agent's name, JSON arrays of todos, files changed, decisions and keywords, a native 768-dimension `F32_BLOB` embedding beside a compressed copy, an `importance` score, `is_rollup`/`rollup_count` for consolidated entries, `session_date` beside `created_at`, and `archived_at`/`deleted_at` — with a separate `session_handoffs` row per project holding live state under an optimistic-concurrency `version`

Storage backend.value: One libSQL/SQLite file locally, or Supabase for a hosted multi-tenant deployment behind the same storage interface; fifteen tables covering the ledger, handoffs and their version history, an agent registry, memory links, a semantic knowledge store, an HDC dictionary, a retrieval access log, and verification harnesses and runs

Retrieval strategy.value: Three tiers with explicit fallback, documented in a reviewer note in the source: native `vector_distance_cos()` over the F32_BLOB column with a DiskANN index; on failure a JavaScript asymmetric TurboQuant scan over compressed embeddings; and FTS5 keyword search as the last resort. A similarity threshold filters the result, optional spreading activation expands it over `memory_links`, and the tier that produced each hit is carried into the rendering

Write strategy.value: `session_save_ledger` writes synchronously through an MCP tool the agent calls; the embedding is computed for the summary, PHI is scanned and redacted before storage, and importance decay is kicked off fire-and-forget afterwards. Consolidation is explicit rather than scheduled — `session_compact_ledger` rolls old entries into an `is_rollup` row, and `session_backfill_embeddings` repairs vectors the write path missed

Update/delete model.value: Soft delete throughout — `archived_at` and `deleted_at`, filtered on 29 read paths, and the interface calls the second a tombstone in its own comments. Correction of live state is versioned instead: every handoff save appends a full snapshot to `session_handoffs_history`, and `memory_history` plus `memory_checkout` let the agent list past versions and restore one, moving the version forward rather than rewinding it

Scoping model.value: `user_id` from the server's environment on every read, never from a tool argument, with `project` and `role` as optional narrowings; handoff writes additionally take an expected version and fail the update rather than clobber a concurrent one

Agent integration.value: An MCP server with 41 tool definitions over stdio, published to npm as `prism-mcp-server` and to the MCP registry, plus a Claude Code plugin marketplace entry, a Smithery packaging manifest, a local dashboard with authentication, a CLI, and Python and Vercel AI SDK adapters

Background processing.value: A background scheduler and an auto-update path run inside the server process; importance decay is fired and forgotten after a write; and a drift timer tracked on the session context nudges the agent to re-check rather than doing anything itself. Nothing rewrites the store on a timer

Trust/provenance model.value: Provenance is the agent name, the project and the conversation id, and the honest reporting of *how* a result was found. There is no epistemic status on a memory: `importance` is a number spent on ranking and decay, and nothing expresses that an entry is on record but not to be believed

Notable strengths.value: Nine contract and honesty tests whose subject is the accuracy of the system's own self-report — that a hybrid hit is not labelled semantic, that a lexical rescue never renders as `N/A similar`, and that a health check returns an explicit unknown rather than a fabricated zero, the last written after a hardcoded `missingEmbeddings: 0` reported HEALTHY through an outage in which 100% of 8,560 rows had no vector

Main risks.value: The ledger records no mutation anywhere — a soft delete writes nothing, and the one table named `..._log` records retrievals — so the correction story that exists for handoff state has no counterpart for the memories themselves; and 20.18.0 in seven months from one non-bot contributor, over a dependency surface of 33 floating ranges and a `postinstall`, is a lot of release velocity for a store holding a developer's project history

Write strategy.value: An agent's memory_save or the CLI, synchronous under one file lock. project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A `message` document — `message_id`, `message_type`, `source_id`, `memory_id`, `user_id`, `agent_id`, `session_id`, `content`, `content_embed`, `valid_at`, `invalid_at`, `forget_at`, `status`. Every agent turn produces one `raw` document plus zero or more extracted children pointing back at it through `source_id`

Storage backend.value: Two stores plus a counter. The `memory` configuration row is a Peewee model in RAGFlow's metadata database (MySQL by default, PostgreSQL and GaussDB supported); the messages live in the doc-store engine under a per-tenant index `memory_{tenant_id}` with adapters for Elasticsearch, Infinity, OceanBase/SeekDB and GaussDB; Redis holds the global message-id sequence and the per-memory byte total

Retrieval strategy.value: One hybrid pass — a `query_string` match over `tokenized_content_ltks` with synonym expansion and term weights, a kNN match on `q_{dim}_vec`, fused by `FusionExpr("weighted_sum", top_n, weights)` where slot 0 is the keyword weight and slot 1 is `1 - keyword_weight`, then sorted `valid_at` descending. `status = 1` and `forget_at` absent are added by default

Write strategy.value: The agent's `Message` component awaits `queue_save_to_memory_task`, which embeds and indexes the raw turn inline and then enqueues one Redis task per memory; the task executor runs the LLM extraction and a second embed-and-insert. There is no dedupe pass and no consolidation pass

Update/delete model.value: No update of an entry's content anywhere. `forget_at` hides a document from retrieval and moves it to the front of the eviction queue; `status = 0` withholds it from retrieval and leaves it listed; FIFO eviction hard-deletes forgotten documents first, then the oldest `valid_at`. Neither forget nor disable follows `source_id` to the extractions made from the entry

Scoping model.value: `tenant_id` on the memory and `permissions` of `me|team`, resolved to an accessible id list before every API query and forced into the doc-store predicate as `condition['memory_id']`; the index name is per tenant. `user_id`, `agent_id` and `session_id` are stored on the entry and are optional query filters, not boundaries

Agent integration.value: Two agent components on the workflow canvas — `Message` with `Save to Memory`, `Retrieval` with source `Memory` — plus a REST surface, a Python SDK, and a second complete implementation of the same API in Go. No MCP tool touches memory

Background processing.value: One Redis-queued task type, `memory`, consumed by `rag/svr/task_executor.py`; it performs the extraction that the inline write skipped. No consolidation, decay, re-embedding or nightly pass exists

Trust/provenance model.value: A boolean `status` the UI labels `Enable`, which filters retrieval, and nothing else. No confidence, no provenance beyond the writing agent's id, no record of who disabled what or when

Notable strengths.value: The access boundary is resolved before the query and re-forced inside every adapter; the capacity check refuses the write rather than silently dropping when it cannot decide what to evict; `forget` is a two-stage soft delete that hides first and evicts first; and the Go port ships committed cases asserting another tenant's memory never reaches the doc engine

Main risks.value: The four memory types are a prompt instruction and a string copied out of the LLM's JSON keys — nothing validates the type or checks it against the memory's own bit field; `invalid_at`, `zone_id` and `storage_type: graph` have no reader or no producer; a failed extraction reports success; the Go server validates `memory_size` and `forgetting_policy` and never enforces either; and `msgStoreConn` is left `None` for two of the seven supported doc engines

Memory unit.value: A claim with a kind, a five-state status, a sensitivity, a scope and structured subject, predicate and object keys; evidence rows beside it; separately, immutable revisions of the operator's diary files parsed into dated entries and passages

Storage backend.value: Postgres through SQLAlchemy, pgvector for claim and diary embeddings, a generated tsvector and optional pg_trgm index for diary passages

Retrieval strategy.value: Claims: hard filter on status, sensitivity, expiry and scope, then a 0.55 vector, 0.30 full-text, 0.15 entity blend. Diary: a room-bound diary_query with search, literal, timeline, read and continue modes; search fuses identifier, full-text, joined-word, fuzzy, variant and optional vector routes by weighted reciprocal rank

Write strategy.value: The assistant's memory_remember writes a room-scoped candidate through record_belief; the /memory review page activates, rejects, corrects and resolves conflicts; a confirm-tier memory_activate runs only after an operator approves it. Diary files enter only through the operator's diary CLI

Update/delete model.value: Reject, supersede, reactivate, expiry, sensitivity and scope edits on the claim row; rejection and supersession write a value-keyed tombstone; correct_belief supersedes and tombstones the old claim and records the replacement in one locked transaction. Diary: file exclusions by path, prune of old revisions, purge of a source

Scoping model.value: Global, agent, room and project scopes on claims; the query arm of memory_query, the chat context and the profile digest filter room and agent before ranking and exclude project; the uuid arm of memory_query applies no room or agent predicate; diary sources bound to one room and optionally one agent; sensitivity public, private or secret

Agent integration.value: A local-model assistant application: chat agents prepend a fenced profile, seed and memory block; the assistant calls memory_query and diary_query; an operator review page at /memory

Background processing.value: Embedding refresh on status change, backfill and prune; retrieval and feedback telemetry; feedback promotable to eval cases; no background extraction and no background diary sync

Trust/provenance model.value: A model actor's write is a candidate and a human actor's is active; value-keyed tombstones refuse a model's re-assertion; lattice-aware write-time conflict detection; confirm-tier writes bound by payload hash; recalled memory and diary passages fenced with angle brackets neutralised, failing closed

Notable strengths.value: Filter before rank in one shared function every query-driven claim read calls; a correction that supersedes, tombstones and replaces under one advisory lock; a candidate state no retrieval returns until a person activates it; a diary read gated by model locality, citing byte ranges into immutable revisions, and fenced as history rather than fact

Main risks.value: Explicit chat commands such as remember that and correct that have handlers in memory/ops.py and no caller, so the explicit_human_command actor has no producer; memory_forget by text matches claims in every room and, on an ambiguous match, lists their uuids, and the uuid arm of memory_query then returns any of them in full if active and non-secret, with no room, agent or expiry check, so two calls on the assistant's own surface read another room's claim; memory_forget by text or uuid also rejects and tombstones a claim in any room, recorded as confirmed_by_user; epistemic_confidence and retrieval_strength have writers and no reader; sensitivity, scope and expiry edits overwrite the row with no event record

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: An episode: one text note with an actor, a scope, optional source, session and tool names, a sensitivity of clean or redacted, a trust of trusted or orphaned, a JSON metadata object, a float32 embedding and the embedder's name

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file in WAL mode: a memories table, an FTS5 table over content, a refusals table, a mutations table, a tombstones table and a verb table for command aliases

Retrieval strategy.value: Every non-orphaned row of the actor and scope is loaded and scored in Python: 0.5 cosine, 0.3 keyword, 0.2 recency from creation time. A row under 0.05 on both the vector and keyword legs is dropped. The top k are packed into a token budget

Write strategy.value: The caller's keep. A gate inspects the text, source, tool name and metadata and returns store, redact or skip; a fingerprint lookup can turn any decision into a skip. A skip writes a refusal row, a tombstone and a mutation row and stores no memory

Update/delete model.value: No update. forget deletes memory rows and their FTS rows, marks rows derived from them orphaned, and appends a forget event. Refusals, tombstones and mutations are never deleted. It needs an actor, a session or an id

Scoping model.value: actor_id is required on keep, recall and audit and is an equality filter on every read, with scope beside it on recall. Tombstones are per actor across scopes. Both keys are caller-supplied strings

Agent integration.value: A Python class, a CLI and an optional MCP server exposing keep, recall, forget and audit under English, Hindi and German names. Nothing is injected; the caller asks

Background processing.value: None

Trust/provenance model.value: A two-value trust column that forget moves to orphaned for rows naming a deleted source, a write-time sensitivity label, and the refusal record. Provenance is free-text source fields and caller metadata

Notable strengths.value: The gate runs before the embedder, so a refused or redacted secret is never embedded or sent to a remote embedding API; refused text is fingerprinted and stays refused under any later gate; every mutation appends an event that forget does not remove; no required dependencies

Main risks.value: forget writes no tombstone; a secret in metadata permanently blocks the clean note beside it; fingerprints of refused secrets are unsalted and survive forget; a Luhn-valid Aadhaar number is stored in the clear; the injection gate is a phrase list that also refuses ordinary sentences
