project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A subject-relation-object triple in a sharded hyperdimensional (HRR/VSA) knowledge base, with provenance held in a separate dict keyed on the same triple

Storage backend.value: In-process hypervectors across shards, persisted by session snapshot, with an append-only JSONL write-ahead log per KB for crash recovery and JSONL sidecars for skills, provenance and query memory

Retrieval strategy.value: HRR cleanup against a codebook, multi-hop chain walking, rule instantiation and induction, with denied triples filtered out of candidates

Write strategy.value: Triples ingested from documents, dialogue or bulk load; corrections parse natural-language retractions into a store-and-forget pair; a second exact-index backend runs the same reasoning layer

Update/delete model.value: `deny` stores an explicit negative, corrections forget the value they replace, belief revision and fact pruning operate on the store, and conflicts resolve by source priority

Scoping model.value: None by principal. `universes.py` gives copy-on-write branches for counterfactual exploration, which isolates a hypothesis rather than a tenant

Agent integration.value: A CLI, an HTTP server, an MCP server, and a Python API frozen at 27 public methods

Background processing.value: Consolidation, dreaming, curiosity and skill promotion passes; a checkpoint that truncates the WAL only after the snapshot is confirmed

Trust/provenance model.value: Per-fact confidence, count and last-seen in provenance, plus a per-query epistemic state of KNOWN, AMBIGUOUS or IDK computed at read time rather than stored

Notable strengths.value: A denial blocks the inference that would regenerate the answer, not just the answer; and the project measured its own central architectural bet against a plain index and published that it lost

Main risks.value: The write-ahead log is truncated at every checkpoint, so it is a recovery mechanism and not a retained audit; the epistemic state is recomputed per query and never persisted; and the substrate the design is named for is, by the project's own measurement, slower and larger than an exact index at identical recall

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A source document chunked and indexed with declared validity, lineage and supersession; beside it an AtomicFact (namespace, subject, predicate, object, context, valid_from, valid_until) applied into an append-only fact ledger

Storage backend.value: The caller's own PostgreSQL with pgvector, every memory table under forced row-level security keyed on a tenant GUC; the rejection ledger and the agent stale-report queue are SQLite sidecars beside the markdown corpus

Retrieval strategy.value: Dense, sparse and graph legs fused, reranked, then judged: each hit returns a verdict, a score and provenance, and only ok hits become evidence. Two Claude Code hooks inject memos without the verdict

Write strategy.value: Generation builds from a manifest, an MCP fact write behind a deterministic evidence check, harness hooks that index sessions, and a review path where a person turns an agent report or a model proposal into a supersedes declaration in the memo

Update/delete model.value: A declared supersedes edge in the newer memo makes the older one superseded; a rejected claim is recorded by claim key and refused on every later write; forget() erases a source and writes a permanent per-source tombstone every build re-checks

Scoping model.value: Tenant isolation is an explicit predicate on every statement with forced row-level security behind it; folder and facet scope is a separate caller-supplied retrieval dimension; the prompt-time hook is scoped to one project's memo directory

Agent integration.value: A CLI, an MCP server, a Codex plugin, Claude Code hooks at session start, prompt submit, pre-tool-use, pre-compact and session end, a local review dashboard, a desktop packaging path and Docker compose files

Background processing.value: Generation builds, graph rebuilds, calibration fitting and invalidation, dependency invalidation, a garbage collector over superseded generations, and an opt-in model arbiter that proposes supersession pairs for review

Trust/provenance model.value: A closed ten-value verdict vocabulary, calibrated thresholds with a certification status, strict mode that refuses rather than answers, and a degraded mode with a verdict of its own so it cannot be mistaken for a judged result

Notable strengths.value: The off-topic pool is the passage to read: the subjects lived as Python literals, a code corpus rooted at the repository ingested them and disqualified all twenty-five, and the measurement against a third-party corpus of the same size, which kept eleven, is what showed the fault was self-ingestion. The pool moved to JSON, the distinctive words are never named in prose, and three committed guards hold it. The verdict vocabulary is argued rather than listed: unverified exists so a degraded hit cannot pass as a judged one. And the review path closes in both directions: an agent can report that one memo replaces another, a person decides off the agent's surface, and a rejection is keyed on the claim so neither the agent nor the model arbiter can raise it again

Main risks.value: Licence first: AGPL-3.0-only, with a commercial licence for closed products and unpublished hosted services, and the Claude marketplace manifest declares Apache-2.0. Then weight: a required PostgreSQL with pgvector, six auto-run surfaces and three build-time execution points at this pin, among them a setup.py that executes at install time and a conftest.py that runs on pytest collection. The two Claude Code injection hooks bypass the trust gate: the prompt-time hook ranks memo files by BM25 and tells the model to follow a hit that settles the question, and the write-time hook injects chunk text by raw SQL, so a superseded memo can reach the prompt through either. Development mode serves unverified results and generation_promoted_unsafe_development is a real audit event. The reviewer is a typed name. The decision ledger is off by default and best-effort, so the record of why a search abstained is as complete as the operator configured it

Memory unit.value: One Markdown file per fact with frontmatter — an immutable `ID` separate from a renameable `Name`, a monotonic `Revision`, a four-value `Type`, a `SubjectKey` naming which question it answers, an `Activation`, a `Volatility`, `ExpiresAt` and `LastVerifiedAt` — beside a `MEMORY.md` index

Storage backend.value: Plain files, no database: a per-project directory and a global one, each with its own index, plus an archive directory for forgotten facts and a revisions directory per fact

Retrieval strategy.value: The cached system prompt carries a fixed memory protocol and the bodies of pinned facts, and no index. Each user turn appends a BM25 recall block after the user's text, with expired facts left out and stale ones ranked down; the memory tool searches, lists and reads the rest

Write strategy.value: The model calls remember, behind a person's approval unless the write is a bounded new project fact; a # quick-add appends to an instruction doc; the Memory panel edits a fact in place. A second fact claiming a held SubjectKey is refused with the holder's id, so a new answer becomes a revision

Update/delete model.value: forget archives by name rather than deleting; every overwritten revision is kept as an immutable snapshot under .revisions/ID/, restorable as a new revision. A pinned body stays in the cached prompt until the next session

Scoping model.value: A per-project directory root plus a global tier that loads in every project; project facts shadow global ones on recall. One machine, one user — there is no tenant or principal boundary

Agent integration.value: A Go kernel reachable five ways — terminal CLI and TUI, the Reasonix Studio desktop app, a browser over its own HTTP server, and editors over ACP — with memory exposed as remember, forget and memory tools

Background processing.value: None on the memory path. Freshness is computed on read from volatility and the verification clock rather than swept by a job

Trust/provenance model.value: No epistemic status. Freshness classifies a fact fresh, current, stale or expired from its age and LastVerifiedAt; stale lowers a recall score and only expired withholds — a statement about age rather than belief

Notable strengths.value: A committed memory benchmark whose tasks are the failure modes a memory store should be asked about, with a paired memory-off arm that reports which tasks memory hurt and what recall cost in characters; a subject key that refuses a second answer to one question; a memory approval that no posture switch answers

Main risks.value: A forgotten fact stays in whichever text already carried it — the cached prompt for a pinned fact, an earlier turn for a recalled one; the contradiction task cannot pass; scope is a directory partition with no principal; and there is no mutation audit

Memory unit.value: A claim revision: kind (claim, decision, procedure, handover), subject, predicate, value, rationale, a repository, area and environment selection, a validity interval, freshness, an operational assessment, 1 to 20 exact evidence supports, plus review, lifecycle, admission, origin, actor, device and model derivation

Storage backend.value: PostgreSQL 17 with pgvector: claims, insert-only claim_revisions with a JSONB body, claim_supports, assertion_rules, memory_decisions and mutation_audit under row-level security; source text as artifact files on disk; Neo4j as a rebuildable projection for graph traversal

Retrieval strategy.value: One candidate SQL for exact and PostgreSQL full-text matching (websearch_to_tsquery over the simple configuration, ts_rank_cd), optional exact pgvector cosine over text-embedding-3-large and Neo4j graph neighbours, fused by RRF with k 60 and exact matches first; four modes (investigation, strict accepted, strict operational, history); 1 to 20 results in a 1 to 32 KiB budget

Write strategy.value: memory.contribute or the browser writes a proposed revision after evidence and scope validation; the learning worker extracts claims from sources and captured sessions through OpenAI and, under the autonomous policy, admits them as accepted_by_policy; every write checks rejection rules and stamps blocked_by_rule on a match

Update/delete model.value: Every change appends a revision. Browser review accepts, rejects, corrects, withdraws, revalidates or restores; reject, correct and withdraw write a value-keyed rule. The model may retire its own unreviewed claims as superseded with cited lines. Retention expiry and erasure blank bodies in place; Brain deletion removes every row

Scoping model.value: Brain as the tenant key under row-level security with reader, writer and admin grants; within a Brain, repository, area and environment selections applied as a recall predicate, with an empty selection meaning Brain-wide; agent operations pin a selection per task

Agent integration.value: Streamable HTTP MCP server per Brain with 22 tools (8 memory tools) behind a revocable device token; a native companion that installs capture hooks for Claude Code and Codex and runs private tool runners; a React desktop UI; an OpenAPI REST surface

Background processing.value: A durable job queue with leases and lanes; an autonomous pass every 10 seconds queues learning for up to 10 new sources per Brain and retries rate-limited runs; semantic indexing, graph projection, analytics cleanup and a privacy journal run beside it

Trust/provenance model.value: Review state and lifecycle filter every recall mode; rejected, withdrawn, superseded and rule-blocked claims are excluded from investigation and strict recall; strict modes need an acceptance authority, retained evidence and, for operational, a recorded observation; derived handovers inherit the weakest contribution

Notable strengths.value: Value-keyed rejection rules that also withhold raw source text repeating the rejected value; one scope and status predicate shared by every recall channel; a handover is strict-eligible only while every contribution is; row-level security with an insert-only revision table; review refused to bearer credentials

Main risks.value: Under the default autonomous policy, captured session text and device-imported sources become accepted memory without a person; default recall serves unreviewed claims; erasure lifts rejection rules; rules match normalised text only; most tests need a live PostgreSQL and no CI runs them; heavy stack (PostgreSQL, Neo4j, OpenAI for learning)

Update/delete model.value: Consolidation clusters similar memories and asks a model to merge, supersede or keep. A retired memory is not deleted: `superseded_by` points at its replacement and retrieval stops returning it. Each applied decision writes an undo-journal row carrying the SQL that reverses it

Scoping model.value: A project, carried in the memory's URI. The search applies a `rememora://projects/<name>/` prefix filter only when a project is supplied, so a caller that passes none searches across all of them

Agent integration.value: A Rust CLI any agent can call over Bash, a Tauri desktop app, a plugin directory, Docker packaging and a Homebrew tap — with lifecycle hooks deliberately removed in v1.7.0

Background processing.value: None wired by default. Curation and consolidation are commands a person runs — `rememora curate`, `rememora evolve`, or `rememora dream` for both

Trust/provenance model.value: A supersession pointer filtered on every retrieval arm, an audit log naming the model and reason behind each curation action, an undo journal carrying reversing SQL, a cluster-size refusal before the model is called, and a cap on how many memories one model decision may retire

Notable strengths.value: The guards are sized for the model being wrong rather than for it being right. `MAX_SUPERSEDE_PER_DECISION` is five and is documented as "the blast radius of a single LLM call ... so that even a fully-hallucinated decision can only retire a handful of records", deliberately set below the cluster limit rather than equal to it. An oversized cluster is refused before a token is spent, because clustering is transitive and a big cluster is more likely "one bad edge chaining unrelated memories than a genuine pile of duplicates" — and the refusal hands the work back with "review it by hand" rather than proceeding carefully. A decision that fails validation is discarded whole rather than partially applied. The undo row is written inside the decision's own transaction, so a rollback leaves no journal row claiming the decision happened. And v1.7.0 removed the automatic hooks the project had previously installed, with `setup --apply` self-healing an existing install by stripping them out

Main risks.value: The project key does not bind: the search applies its URI prefix only when a project is supplied, so a caller that passes none reads across every project in the shared database — and the database is explicitly shared by every agent on the machine, which is the design's whole point and also what makes the missing predicate matter. The epistemic vocabulary is one bit: a memory is superseded or it is not, with no way to record that a claim is disputed, unverified or believed on weak evidence, and the bit is set by a language model's judgement. Reversibility is narrower than it sounds — `evolve_undo` stores and prints the statement that would reverse a decision, and nothing executes it, so an undo is a person copying SQL; the constant guarding cluster size still describes consolidation as irreversible. Nothing is keyed on a memory's content, so a claim retired by consolidation can be saved again as a new row with nothing positioned to notice. And the audit surfaces cover curation and consolidation rather than every write

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Two. An ack is one deliberately accepted finding — a kind token, a 16-hex key over the symbol's path, scope and name, the magnitude it was accepted at, an optional content hash of the scrubbed body, an optional scope that wrote it, and a free-text reason. A note is a target — a canonical `path::scope::name` or a path — with a date, a text, and optionally the HEAD sha and branch it was written on

Storage backend.value: Two plain files at the analyzed root, both committed: `.ripwire_quality_acks` (1,310 rows) and `.ripwire_notes` (three rows). Both are sorted for merge friendliness; the ack file publishes atomically under a cross-process lock, the notes file truncates and rewrites without one

Retrieval strategy.value: Notes are surfaced by exact-string match on a canonical id or a root-relative path, riding along with the symbol or file in the task-scoped map, the default map, the expansion, the edit check and three MCP verbs. Acks are not retrieved; they are consulted as a filter when the quality delta is rendered

Write strategy.value: `--quality-ack[=REASON]` merges every finding the current delta reports into the ledger at its present magnitude; `--note-add` resolves a selector through the same resolver the read verbs use and refuses an ambiguous one, warning loudly on a target that resolves to nothing. Both are command-line acts; no MCP verb writes either store

Update/delete model.value: An ack is replaced in place by a later ack at a new magnitude, and its reason chain is capped at one hop so an older segment is dropped rather than accumulated. A rename or a move re-files an ack onto the current key through a healing pre-pass that rewrites the two sidecars before anything reads them — by the git-recorded rename map first, then by scrubbed-content-hash equality — and `--quality-ack` writes the healed rows back, so a rescued ack stops depending on the replay. A rewrite deliberately does not match. Nothing retires a stale row automatically — a past round retired 109 by hand

Scoping model.value: None enforced. An ack row can record the scope that wrote it and the field is read only to build a disclosure row; the suppression test never consults it, so an ack filed under one scope suppresses findings anywhere. The runtime `--scope` glob filters what is analysed, which is an argument rather than a stored key

Agent integration.value: A single compiled binary with a large flag surface, an MCP server of thirty-one verbs, editor and agent hooks, and a set of agent skills that tell a model when to ack and when to look

Background processing.value: None. Every read and every write is a command

Trust/provenance model.value: None on a stored memory. A stale ack is classified — its target is gone, its finding is gone, or it was filed from a foreign scope — and the classification is emitted as disclosure only; the suppression test consults presence and magnitude alone, so a stale ack keeps suppressing

Notable strengths.value: A ratchet rather than a suppression: an ack accepts a finding at its measured size and re-reports it the moment it worsens past that, with a zero-magnitude guard so a finding with no magnitude cannot become a blank check. The repair for a move is the part worth studying: rather than teaching nine call sites to try an alias — *"each an independent chance to get the direction backwards"* — the two sidecars are rekeyed forward into the identity the current tree uses, once, before anything reads them, so `computeDelta`, the ack ratchet, the stale-ack classifier and the ack writer become rename-aware with no edit at all, and it is self-healing because `--quality-ack` writes the rekeyed ledger back. The rescue route is kept per row rather than as a total, because surviving through a git-recorded rename and surviving through scrubbed-content equality are *"different claims with different trust"*. A ledger kept committed so what is suppressed is reviewable in a diff. And a survival measurement the project ran against its own history and published as the motivation for the repair

Main risks.value: A stale ack is classified and never acted on: its target is gone, its finding is gone, or it was filed from a foreign scope, and the classification is emitted as disclosure while the suppression test consults presence and magnitude alone, so a stale ack keeps suppressing. The rescue that carries an ack across a move is the most load-bearing machinery in the tool and the least visible to the person relying on it — a row rescued by scrubbed-content equality is a weaker claim than one rescued by a git-recorded rename, which is why the route is disclosed per row, but nothing refuses the weaker route. The notes store has no rescue route at all and no lock on its writer. The project's own skill instructs an agent to write acks unattended, and no CI job reads either sidecar, so the review the committed ledger makes possible is a review somebody still has to perform. And the surface is very large for six weeks of work: 172,653 lines across 167 files, with two auto-run surfaces and four unpinned dependency surfaces at this pin

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A `MemoryRecord` — id, submitting agent, content, content hash, embedding and its hash, a type of fact, observation, inference or task, a domain tag, a provider, a caller-asserted confidence, a status, an optional parent hash, task workflow fields, and created, committed and deprecated timestamps

Storage backend.value: Two tiers. BadgerDB holds the consensus state covered by the application hash — the content hash, status, domain, author and classification, and no content. SQLite for a personal node or PostgreSQL with pgvector for a cluster holds the serving projection with the content and the vectors, written only from the consensus path

Retrieval strategy.value: Cosine similarity over the candidate set with no minimum threshold, after a SQL prefilter on the embedding provider, the domain, the confidence and a committed status; a decayed-confidence floor is applied across all candidates before the top-K trim, then a per-record authorization pass. A BM25 text search and a hybrid mode sit beside it, with an off-by-default cross-encoder reranker

Write strategy.value: An agent submits through an MCP tool or the REST route; the node re-embeds the content itself rather than trusting the caller, derives a UUID and a content hash, builds a signed transaction and broadcasts it for commit. The block writes the Badger keys and buffers the SQL row, which is flushed at Commit through what the code calls the only path that writes memories to the offchain store

Update/delete model.value: No edit. A challenge transaction moves a memory to `challenged` or `deprecated` and a reinstate reverses it; deprecation leaves the row in place with a timestamp, and the voter's dedup refuses the deprecated memory's exact bytes under any new id until a reinstate. A cleanup pass can evict memories whose decayed confidence falls below a threshold, and it is disabled by default and requires an operator and an explicit dry-run flag

Scoping model.value: A required domain tag validated on write against a registered domain list, filtered in the query, and authorized per record against the caller's credential on the way out; agents may hold an owned home domain

Agent integration.value: 38 MCP tools, 119 REST routes, a CEREBRUM dashboard of 65 more, a Python SDK, a desktop shell, a tray app, a libp2p relay as a separate module, and a federation layer that syncs memories between chains under explicit policy

Background processing.value: A voter loop polling every two seconds for proposed memories to vote on, the CometBFT block loop, federation sync, and an opt-in cleanup pass

Trust/provenance model.value: Four produced statuses gating readability, a content-hash dedup that keeps a deprecated memory's bytes out, a caller-asserted confidence decaying on an exponential curve with a corroboration bonus, a per-domain decay rate, and a validator score table

Notable strengths.value: A status ladder that genuinely withholds — a memory is unreadable until something votes it in; a decay floor applied across the whole candidate set before the top-K trim rather than after; a node that re-embeds rather than trusting a caller's vector; consensus-first write ordering with a single documented path into the serving store; a dedup that excludes the candidate's own row rather than every unaccepted row; 4,941 test functions

Main risks.value: On the default install the vote is one validator key running three string heuristics, which the README's opening line states beside its consensus claim; the dedup is keyed on exact bytes, is a node-local opinion that fails open on a store error, admits two identical proposals in flight at once, and does not run on the co-commit path; the MCP client silently drops a write at 60% word overlap before the chain sees it; two of the four papers rest on an experiment pipeline excluded from the tree, which the papers index states; `access_logs`, the lifecycle state machine, the `validated` status and the record validator all have no production caller

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Several, in two repositories. In the team context: MEMORY.md, the server-written daily, weekly and monthly summaries, and observations, written as Fact JSONL, one new file per put. In the project ledger: session records, murmurs, plans with an events log, and plan feedback. Recorded discussions carry server-distilled atoms with valid_from, valid_to and superseded_by

Storage backend.value: Two git checkouts provisioned by the SageOx server: a team context per team holding MEMORY.md, SOUL.md, TEAM.md, memory/ and discussions/, and a sparse ledger per project repository holding sessions/ and data/

Retrieval strategy.value: MEMORY.md injected at session start up to 200 lines, with the summary directories advertised by file count. On a prompt that looks like recall, a hook injects up to four hits from an in-memory term-frequency search over the ledger's sessions, murmurs, plans and plan feedback from the last 90 days. ox query sends the query to the server's search by default

Write strategy.value: ox memory put writes its observations to a new UUID-named file under memory/.observations and commits it under the team-context repo lock; ox memory distill posts pending observations to the SageOx API, which writes the summaries

Update/delete model.value: Nothing in this repository rewrites a memory entry. Each put writes a new file; the summaries and discussion distillations are server-written; a plan revision overwrites plan.md and appends a lifecycle event; git keeps the history

Scoping model.value: Separate checkouts: one team context per team, one ledger per project repository, and a server-side team-membership check before discussions are read. ox query passes caller-supplied team and repo ids to the server, whose filter is not in this repository

Agent integration.value: A CLI with hooks for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and others, a Claude plugin, agent priming, session upload, and a daemon that pulls and pushes both repositories

Background processing.value: A daemon syncing both checkouts and, when an environment variable names an LLM binary, running a tiered conflict resolver on ledger pulls; server-side distillation of observations and discussions

Trust/provenance model.value: An LLM binary allowlist; a merge post-condition that refuses output missing any conflicted line or holding a duplicate key; a hard-deny list keeping MEMORY.md and memory/ out of accept-theirs; a lint test pinning the recall hook to local-only search; secret redaction before session upload

Notable strengths.value: The comment on the ledger's DefaultResolveRules is engineering judgement written to be checked: it names the failure (a deterministic wedge that never escalates and never self-heals), quantifies it (341 ahead and 1,055 behind for 13 days with 281 conflicts), names the canonical source of each auto-resolved artifact, and ends its SAFETY note with do not weaken that guard. The LLM merge tier counts every non-blank line on either conflict side and refuses output that drops one, and a conflict where both sides rewrote the same line is left for a person. Memory entries are conflict-free by construction: every put writes a new UUID-named file

Main risks.value: Distillation, the step that writes the summaries agents read, runs on the SageOx server, so what a team remembers is decided outside this repository. The merge post-condition counts lines kept and not lines added, so a merge that keeps both sides and inserts a sentence neither wrote passes. Recall and prior-art search read plans without their lifecycle status, so a superseded or abandoned plan resurfaces beside the live one. Discussion atoms honour a rejection on read, but the rejection is written by the server, and draft and finalized distillations are served identically

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A claim — subject, predicate, value and conditions — held as a chain of `claim_versions`, each with a state, a basis, a validity interval, a record interval and the exact source spans it quotes; beside it the `source_events` the claim was read out of, and episodes, artifacts and references built the same way

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file as the only authority — `source_events`, `claims`, `claim_versions`, `evidence_links`, `deletion_operations`, `entries` and the work queue, schema 1110 — with a vector companion in LanceDB holding metadata and a vector against an empty payload, deletable and rebuildable without losing a memory

Retrieval strategy.value: Five channels fused by reciprocal rank — exact reference, lexical index, claim, recent and vector — then assembled into a packet with an explicit answerability verdict that can say the corpus cannot answer the question

Write strategy.value: A turn is captured as a source event; a leased background work item consolidates what a person said or a document stated into claim proposals, never tool output; each proposal is stored only if the span it quotes is literally present in the source, and a deterministic ladder decides whether it lands proposed or active

Update/delete model.value: A change appends a claim version and closes the previous one's record interval; nothing overwrites content or state. Deletion is one operation record applied in dependency order across sources, claims, evidence links, episode membership and the vector rows, with the derived layer fenced so a rebuild cannot resurrect it

Scoping model.value: A `scope_id` bound from host identity and carried as `scope_id IN (allowed)` on every read; a vector hit is filtered by the trusted partition list and then re-read from SQLite under the same predicate before it can enter the packet

Agent integration.value: Host adapters rather than assumptions — a Hermes provider with eight tools and one MCP server with nine serving Codex and Claude Code, locally or as entries of a shared store over HTTP; the only write verbs are propose, revise and forget, and revise and forget must quote the session's own most recent human turn

Background processing.value: Durable work items with leases, attempt limits and at-most-once publication, for consolidation, embedding, projection rebuilds, purges and candidate evaluation; a crashed pass loses nothing and a provider outage parks work rather than failing it

Trust/provenance model.value: `state IN ('proposed','active','disputed','superseded','retracted')` as a SQL CHECK on every claim version, decided by a rule ladder the model is explicitly forbidden to influence — the candidate evaluator's own prompt says `Do not choose a fact state: Core qualification owns that decision`

Notable strengths.value: A stored claim can always name the sentence that caused it, and the check that the sentence is really there runs at the storage boundary rather than in a prompt

Main risks.value: Nothing in the tree measures recall quality: the README says every accuracy figure was measured by hand on the authors' own corpora, and the model-evaluation release gate meant to cover it was removed on 27 September 2026 rather than passed

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Two units that never meet. A `MemoryItem` — content, timestamp, a free-form metadata dict, extracted entities and relationships — living in a process dict with a JSON save file. And a `ContextNode`/`ContextEdge` in the context graph, each carrying `valid_from`/`valid_until`, with knowledge-graph relationships additionally carrying `recorded_at` and `superseded_at`

Storage backend.value: In-process dicts plus `agent_memory.json` for the memory store; an in-memory graph with Markdown-directory and JSON persistence for the context graph; SQLite for versions, tags and the mutation log; and adapters the operator points at — FAISS, sqlite-vec, pgvector, Qdrant, Milvus, Pinecone, Weaviate for vectors, Neo4j, FalkorDB, AGE and Neptune for graphs, Jena, RDF4J, Oxigraph, Blazegraph and Anzo for triples

Retrieval strategy.value: `ContextRetriever` fuses a vector arm and a BFS graph-expansion arm under a `hybrid_alpha` weight with a multi-source boost. `AgentMemory.retrieve` is meant to add a third: short-term buffer, then the vector store, then a keyword fallback — but its vector branch only consumes results when the store exposes `search` and not `search_vectors`, and the package's own `VectorStore` exposes both, so for the documented configuration the long-term arm contributes nothing and recall falls back to word-overlap keyword matching

Write strategy.value: Synchronous and immediate: `store()` appends to a short-term buffer, embeds into the vector store when one is bound, puts the item in the dict, pushes entities into the knowledge graph, and applies the retention policy — all on the caller's thread, all retrievable at once. No extraction model on the write path; graph construction is deterministic by design and an LLM is optional everywhere it appears

Update/delete model.value: The context graph distinguishes two operations and documents the difference: `retract_node` closes the validity window, leaving the record in history and in `state_at` before the cut, while `purge_node` removes it and leaves a tombstone that deliberately excludes the content. An `ErasureCoordinator` drives purge across the graph, the memory store and the vector store and returns a receipt naming which stores it reached. `AgentMemory` deletes outright, and its filtered deletion is where the boundary fails

Scoping model.value: Stored but not enforced where it matters. `user_id` and `conversation_id` live in item metadata and are filtered by the dedicated `get_by_user` and `get_conversation_history` accessors; `_matches_filters` — which `retrieve`, `clear_memory`, `count` and `list` all route through — recognises only `type`, `start_date` and `end_date` and returns True for everything else, so an unknown filter key is neither honoured nor rejected

Agent integration.value: A Python API, a 22-group CLI, a FastAPI Explorer with a React workspace UI, a JSON-RPC MCP server exposing graph, retrieval, extraction, reasoning, decision and export tools, and framework adapters for Agno, CrewAI, LangChain and others under `integrations/`

Background processing.value: None required. Ingestion, extraction, deduplication and export are explicit pipeline stages the operator runs; there is no scheduler, no worker loop and no consolidation timer. Retention is applied inline on every `store()`

Trust/provenance model.value: Provenance is the product and it is thorough — per-source credibility, conflict detection across five conflict types, decision records with causal chains, and a provenance manager with integrity checks. Epistemic status is not a field: a conflict resolves to a value with a confidence float, or returns `resolved=False` with a `requires_manual_review` flag that nothing in the tree reads

Notable strengths.value: The temporal model is the real thing — four timestamps, both axes queryable, retraction separated from erasure, and a purge tombstone that omits the content on purpose because keeping it would defeat the erasure it records

Main risks.value: `forget(conversation_id=...)` and `forget(user_id=...)` — both shown in the method's own docstring — delete every memory in the store, because the filter keys they build are ignored by the predicate they are passed to; the same root cause as the `days_old` inversion fixed one commit before this pin, in the same function, with the other two arms left untested

Memory unit.value: A `MemoryEntry` with an entry type, a key and a value, carrying the trust triple — `source_origin`, `channel_trust`, `confirmation_status` — and the `trust_band` and confidence derived from it, an `ingress_handle_id` binding it to the admission that let it in, an owner pair of `user_id` and `workspace_id`, an `importance_weight` and `decay_score`, a `superseded_by` pointer, and taint labels. Storage backend.value: SQLite, with tables for `memory_entries`, `memory_events`, `retrieval_records`, `retrieval_vectors`, `retrieval_keys` and `retrieval_metadata`. Retrieval strategy.value: Six compiled surfaces rather than one query: identity, active attention, recall, procedural, thread resume and evidence. Each is a `compile_*` call that filters by owner scope and, for identity, by trust band, ranks by importance weight times decay score, and fills a token budget. Recall reports a sufficiency assessment; thread resume carries prior-session context explicitly labelled untrusted evidence that *"does not authorize side effects"*

Write strategy.value: `MemoryManager.write` returns a decision rather than a row: `allow`, `require_confirmation` or `reject` with a reason. Before that, `derive_trust_band` looks the trust triple up in a validated matrix and raises on an unknown combination; PII is detected and redacted into the stored value; an external-origin write that is neither confirmed nor pending review is refused, as is a suspicious one. Trust fields are set by the runtime from the ingress handle, never accepted from the caller — and a `note.create` or `todo.create` the model proposes counts as user-confirmed only when every field it would store is structurally anchored in the sanitised text of the current user turn

Update/delete model.value: Supersession by pointer — a new entry names the one it replaces, the old keeps a `superseded_by` and drops out of the identity surface, and a supersession whose target is outside the caller's owner scope is rejected as not found. Soft deletion is a predicate the manager checks. Consolidation runs under a capability scope that forbids network, tool recursion and self-invocation, and its writes resolve to the untrusted band by construction

Scoping model.value: An owner pair, enforced together. A read or write that names a user without a workspace is rejected outright rather than falling back to a partial filter, and `_entry_matches_owner` gates every surface. Session-scoped entries are filtered separately, and channel participation binds an entry to the channel that produced it

Agent integration.value: A long-running daemon with a CLI, a TUI, channel adapters for messaging platforms, a scheduler, a sandboxed executor, a policy enforcement point in front of every action, and a self-modification subsystem. Memory is one subsystem of a security architecture rather than a standalone service

Background processing.value: A consolidation worker under an explicit capability scope; a summarizer; identity-candidate detection; a derived graph rebuilt from canonical entries; a decay score applied at read time; an adversarial metrics script and gate that a person runs

Trust/provenance model.value: The trust band is the epistemic field and it admits or withholds; confidence is a number the same rule carries and is used for weighting. The triple that produces both is validated rather than free-form, and an unenumerated combination is an exception rather than a default — except for `pending_review`, which short-circuits the lookup and is untrusted whatever carried it. Consolidation cannot raise trust — its writes are untrusted by construction. Historical thread content is surfaced with an explicit statement that it does not authorise action

Notable strengths.value: A trust band derived from a validated triple rather than asserted by a caller, with an unknown combination raising instead of defaulting; an owner scope that refuses a half-specified request rather than filtering on the half it was given; an identity surface whose test pins the exact returned set before asserting what is absent; an append-only event store keyed to the entry it describes; a consolidation worker that mathematically cannot upgrade trust; a review queue a person lists and adjudicates with `/identity`, on a channel check, while the model's thirty-five-tool surface carries no memory verb; a `note.create` that only counts as user-confirmed when every stored field is structurally anchored in the text of the current user turn; a security document that cites the memory-poisoning literature it is defending against

Memory unit.value: Five tier-specific rows rather than one record type. A warm `entity` is a tenant, category and name with a JSON-validated body and a free-form status; a hot `state_document` is a keyed JSON body; a cold `journal_event` is a timestamp with four optional JSON payloads; a `reference_document` is keyed text with metadata; an `archived_entity` preserves a body with an archive time and reason

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file at `~/.sibyl-memory/memory.db` in WAL mode, its directory created 0700 and the file 0600, with symlinked or hardlinked databases and sidecars refused; twelve base tables, five FTS5 virtual tables and a runtime-generated trigram shadow. The schema calls itself a port of a canonical Postgres schema held elsewhere

Retrieval strategy.value: FTS5 with a porter unicode tokeniser, one match per tier, unioned and sorted by a proximity bucket then rank then tier; on an empty head a ladder of relaxed query variants, then a folded-trigram shadow fallback. Over it a retrieve-then-verify layer with a coverage threshold, an anchor band, a document-frequency abstention and a negation policy of abstain. No embeddings anywhere

Write strategy.value: Four of eight MCP tools write: remember upserts an entity, forget archives one, set state replaces a keyed document, record event appends to the journal. Nothing extracts or summarises; the model supplies the body and a JSON validity check is the only gate besides a capacity check

Update/delete model.value: An entity is upserted in place by its unique tenant, category and name. Archiving copies the body into `archived_entities` with a reason and removes the original; a separate delete is a hard `DELETE` with nothing left behind. The MCP forget archives and the Hermes provider's forget hard-deletes, which is the same verb with opposite semantics

Scoping model.value: A tenant on every table and in every read query, validated at construction and switchable at runtime; in the LangGraph adapter a namespace tuple is stored as the entity category and applied as a prefix filter on read

Agent integration.value: Five published packages — a client engine, a CLI, an MCP server of eight stdio tools, a Hermes provider and plugin adapter, and a LangGraph store — plus a Dockerfile whose entrypoint is the stdio MCP server and a compose file that states it is not a network service

Background processing.value: None. A usage heartbeat fires every fifteen operations or ten minutes, and a capacity check may call out at the storage boundary; nothing rewrites memory

Trust/provenance model.value: None on a stored memory. The entity status is a free-form caller string with no withholding semantics and is filtered only when the caller passes one; the only constrained status vocabulary belongs to skill proposals, which are not yet memory

Notable strengths.value: A zero result that names which of five causes produced it rather than looking like an empty store; a negation policy that abstains instead of answering; an isolation weakness documented in a lock comment with a named regression test rather than left implicit; refusing to open a symlinked database file; 1,055 test functions against 16,000 lines

Main risks.value: Tenant isolation is a post-filter on an unindexed column, which the authors flag and defer; four of twelve declared tables have no writer and one of those is read with a column name it does not have behind a silent except; the review queue has no shipped interface and the CLI command the docs name does not exist; the README's claim that tier verification is the only outbound call omits a usage heartbeat the project's own other README discloses; no CI runs the 1,055 tests

Memory unit.value: Two layers that never merge: an immutable episodic row — content, type, tags, importance, `agent_id`, `visibility`, `scope`, `project`, a content hash, `memory_kind = 'episodic'` and a canonical `evidence_meta` payload — and a derived semantic layer of entities, aspects, grouped claim values with optional event and validity times, dependencies and epistemic assertions that Dreaming writes from those rows and projects back as `memory_kind = 'derived'`

Retrieval strategy.value: Hybrid: FTS5 lexical and sqlite-vec vector hits fused by reciprocal rank with k = 60, plus graph traversal, prospective-hint, temporal-facet and structured-evidence arms, dampened and reranked by a local ONNX cross-encoder by default; credential spans are redacted from every returned projection and nothing is withheld for content

Write strategy.value: Harness hooks stream transcripts into the store; `remember` over MCP, HTTP, CLI or a plugin writes an episodic row synchronously, deduplicated by content hash within agent, project, scope and visibility, and retrievable at once. No extraction on the hot path — the semantic layer is built later by Dreaming

Update/delete model.value: Soft delete with `is_deleted`/`deleted_at`, `superseded_by` and `stale_at`, all three excluded by one shared `currentMemorySql` predicate; a preview-then-execute forget; a source purge that also deletes the claim projections derived from it, while an edited source keeps its Dreaming claims and flags the ones whose quote vanished; the retention worker hard-deletes soft-deleted rows after 30 days and history after 180

Scoping model.value: `agent_id` plus a three-valued roster read policy (isolated, group, shared) applied as SQL on every recall arm and every memory read route, with `visibility != 'archived'`; project and a nullable `scope` column layer on top. In the default `local` auth mode no token binds a caller to an agent id; the Docker image starts in `team` mode

Agent integration.value: A daemon with a Hono HTTP API, a stdio and HTTP MCP server registering 62 tools, hooks for session start, prompt submit, pre-compaction and session end, connectors for eleven harnesses, a CLI, a dashboard, a tray and desktop app, a browser extension, a cross-agent message board, and a Docker image

Background processing.value: A dreaming worker sweeping every 5 minutes for content and hygiene passes, plus transcript capture, transcript recovery and import workers, embedding, embedding-repair and synthesis workers, reflection, a 6-hourly retention sweep, database integrity and vacuum

Trust/provenance model.value: Every Dreaming claim write must cite a quote that is a verbatim substring of a scoped episodic source, checked in code before any write; contradictions are recorded as durable observations rather than resolved into a winner; a deterministic credential detector redacts keys, tokens and secret-named assignments from every prompt- and agent-facing projection, while stored evidence keeps the raw text

Notable strengths.value: An exact-quote citation gate enforced in code before any claim write, an immutable evidence layer the derived layer can always be rebuilt from, valid-time ordering of claims under a test that fails on write order, agent scope in SQL on recall and every read route with tests that cannot pass vacuously and run in CI, and source deletion that reaches the derived claims

Main risks.value: The published 97.6% LongMemEval figure has no per-question artifact and the repository's own committed run ledger peaks at 45 correct out of 50; history is pruned at 180 days and agent purge deletes it; a forgotten value can be written straight back; `/api/memory/review-queue` selects three event names nothing writes; and captured transcripts are stored with no credential scrubbing

Trust/provenance model.value: A credential-pattern scan on ingest recording the kind and count per session without storing the match; redaction applied on the publication and remote paths; a `PublicationDraft` that counts the risks needing manual review before anything leaves the machine

Notable strengths.value: The privacy split is the right one and is stated honestly: `privacy.rs` says outright that it "deliberately only removes high-signal credential formats" and "is a reduction in accidental disclosure, not a security boundary: callers must still ask the user to review the resulting snapshot before publishing." On ingest, `replace_secret_findings` runs the same scan but discards the redacted text and keeps only the report, writing a `secret_findings` row of kind and occurrence count — so the index knows a session contains three GitHub-token-shaped strings without holding a copy, and the raw record stays local where the user needs it. Redaction then runs on the publication and remote paths. The schema comments are unusually disciplined about not storing what can be derived: costs "are NOT stored: they are computed at read time from the embedded pricing snapshot, so a pricing refresh re-prices history without touching these rows", the terminal/agent kind "is not stored: it derives from the record ref", and `blob_light` exists so a listing never pays for part text

Main risks.value: The retrieval eval cannot be reproduced from the repository. `sivtr eval` is documented as measuring "against a **snapshot of real data** (frozen corpus + labeled queries), so ranking changes are gated on measurable improvement over a fixed baseline instead of feel" — but no golden-query file and no frozen corpus are committed, so the baseline is each user's own machine and no reader can check a ranking claim or reproduce a regression. A `GoldenQuery` lists the records a query should surface and nothing lists records it must not, so the harness measures recall of the labelled set rather than exclusion. Redaction is pattern-based and the module says so; anything credential-shaped that misses the nine patterns reaches a published snapshot, and the stored raw text is unredacted by design. The workspace filter applies only when a non-empty key is supplied, so it narrows a query rather than bounding one

Retrieval strategy.value: Two different readers. The producer queries vectors only to find near-duplicates at write time. The consumer engine fans out over the host's skills directory (self-contained Okapi BM25 with CJK tokenisation and corpus-wide stopword pruning), the SkillHub catalog and optional ClawHub/skillhub.cn marketplaces, fuses by weighted RRF at `k = 60` with per-source trust weights, then an LLM gate reads name, description and a 300-character excerpt and returns at most two

Write strategy.value: Writes are a batch build, not an agent action: crawl, parse, regex safety block, structural thresholds, exact-hash duplicate check, LLM near-duplicate judgement, embed, copy the bundle, insert. Nothing an agent does at answer time writes back: no path in this tree persists a usage or outcome signal. The consumer plugin does emit one — it returns the injected skill ids in the segment metadata so the host can correlate skills shown against skills used — and nothing here consumes it. Retrieval latency is a rewrite call, a fan-out and a gate call, each with its own deadline, and a failure injects nothing rather than raising

Update/delete model.value: Exclusion is `deleted = 1` with the row retained: near-duplicate losers carry `superseded_by`, safety exclusions deliberately leave it NULL so the two are distinguishable. Both are re-derived on every build from caches keyed on the content hash rather than trusted from the row, which is what survives a re-crawl — the row itself is overwritten by `INSERT OR REPLACE` under a hash-derived id. `SkillStore.delete` and `SkillStore.update` have no caller in the repository

Scoping model.value: None on the read path. The engine's sources are physical partitions — a workspace directory, a packaged builtin directory, extra named directories, a remote catalog — each searched as its own pool and weighted, with no scope key on a record and no predicate on a query. The catalog arm applies a `hub_min_safety` quality floor of 0.7 and a keyword-relevance guard, both content filters

Agent integration.value: Five host plugins over two engines with the same file layout in Python and TypeScript: a `UserPromptSubmit` hook for automatic per-turn retrieval, an MCP stdio server exposing `skill_search` for on-demand retrieval, and packaged builds for OpenClaw 1.x and 2.0, WorkBuddy, Hermes, Raven and the DeepSeek Harness. Background processing.value: No workers and no scheduler. Everything heavy is a stage of `cli build` — quality judging, cross-source dedup, licence activation, the safety gate, export — run as subprocesses in a fixed order and re-run in full each time; there is no cadence or incremental refresh state

Trust/provenance model.value: Provenance is per-skill and durable — source repository, path, URL and licence, with an upstream licence audit that activates only sources on a GREEN whitelist. project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Three layers over one event store. A raw event is an appended session turn with its embedding, an optional agent-supplied source-event time, and the logic version it was ingested under. An episodic memory groups events with their text and provenance. A schema is the durable claim: content text, facets and tags, a scope id and kind, a status and stale reason, confidence and salience, an embedding with packed facet axes and strengths, supporting episode ids, a labile flag, a generalization stage, first-formed and last-updated stamps, and the logic version it was formed under. Beside the symbolic layer, semantic prototypes are latent cluster centroids

Storage backend.value: One local SQLite database, 33 tables and four FTS5 indexes, with a schema.sql carrying design commentary. Latent prototypes and their edges, symbolic schemas with normalised evidence, relation and co-activation edge tables, sessions and continuities, a raw_events spine appended per turn, retrieval and feedback event tables, a per-candidate retrieval-decision trail, feedback-derived learning projections, a derived procedure-search projection, replay checkpoints, worker runs, graph-health snapshots, and a scope registry. Embeddings are computed locally through ONNX encoders, one of them a multilingual model fetched at a pinned revision on first use

Retrieval strategy.value: Mode-gated hybrid recall with no LLM call. The MCP tools deliver from a declarative catalog: per-cue FTS and embedding candidates, both scope- and status-filtered in SQL, unioned with a multilingual dense channel, passed through the working-memory gate, and selected for coverage of the task's needs. Recall with full evidence also runs the older pipeline, which adds episode search ranked partly by source-event time and relation expansion under the same status and scope gate. Advisory procedures are retrieved separately, filtered to the exact scope, by reciprocal-rank fusion of applicability, strategy and FTS ranks

Write strategy.value: The agent decides what is durable and calls slowave_remember, which appends a raw event and writes a schema directly; slowave_activate opens a session, slowave_recall asks for context, slowave_feedback reports whether what came back helped, and slowave_commit closes the session. Every turn lands in raw_events, and the consolidated layer is built by replay and consolidation, both zero-LLM and geometric

Update/delete model.value: Feedback drives the lifecycle: a schema can be reinforced or marked stale with a reason and a named replacement, and salience and confidence are recomputed from the feedback ledger. Consolidation reinforces an existing engram in place, keyed on the primary prototype, and dedup_exact archives exact normalised duplicates into a canonical row. Removal is a hard delete from the dashboard: the schema row goes, and the recall items, feedback events and JSON references naming it are scrubbed in the same transaction. A procedure is deleted by stripping it from its raw_events payload; its row in the procedure-search projection and its FTS entry are left in place

Scoping model.value: scope_id and scope_kind on every schema, a scope_registry, and SQL filtering on the candidate queries when a scope is set. Cross-scope reach is earned rather than granted: a generalization stage from 0 (scoped, hard-blocked) through 1 (portable within the same scope kind, above a score floor) and 2 (contextual, admitted with a 0.70 score multiplier and the floor re-checked on recall) to 3 (global). The MCP tools fix the mode to strict_scope

Agent integration.value: An MCP server with five tools, published on PyPI with a Homebrew formula, with a setup command that configures every detected client — Claude Code, Copilot CLI, Codex, Cursor, Cline, Windsurf and Devin Desktop, OpenCode, and Claude Desktop — and installs daemon, worker and backup user services when run, or from the Homebrew formula's post_install, plus a local web dashboard with a Cytoscape graph view. No LLM API key is required for any memory operation

Background processing.value: A replay engine rebuilds derived memory from raw_events when the configured logic version differs from the store's, under an optimistic-lease claim so exactly one process rebuilds. Consolidation forms and reinforces schemas geometrically; unrecalled schemas older than 30 days lose salience each pass, remembered ones excepted; a daily timer snapshots the database with seven kept; co-activation edges are rebuilt from the recall and feedback ledgers and decay on a seven-day half-life; a generalization sweep advances or corrects stages; graph-health snapshots and worker runs are recorded

Trust/provenance model.value: Four lifecycle statuses, two of which withhold a schema from every shipped read path, with a stale reason drawn from contradicted, superseded, outdated, unsupported or withdrawn. Confidence and salience are separate numbers recomputed from accepted feedback, with a shared salience ceiling. is_labile marks a reactivated trace as temporarily uncertain, kept explicitly distinct from needs_review. Contradiction and supersession are described in the source as client-owned history that the store and consolidation never infer

Notable strengths.value: A cross-scope rule stated in the SQL rather than assembled by callers, with one gate function serving recall's direct and graph-expansion paths; an event store with a logic-version stamp so an algorithm change replays instead of migrating; a retrieval-gold contract with required, forbidden and history-only content in the same case, run over the real MCP boundary, with mutation tests that require the negative cases to fail when their guard is removed; a delete preview that counts the evidence links, relations and co-activations a removal will take with it; a schema file that argues for its own decisions; and a memory core with no LLM call and no API key anywhere in ingest, consolidation or recall

Main risks.value: The automatic rebuild that runs when an upgrade changes the logic version deletes every schema and re-consolidates from raw events, and consolidation skips any prototype whose episodes hold only remember events, so a memory the agent stored with slowave_remember is not re-formed, a stale or archived status is lost on the schemas that are, and a schema a person deleted at the dashboard can return because its raw events were kept and nothing records the deletion. A status the store does not recognise is coerced to active rather than refused. Event time exists but validity time does not: nothing records when a claim stopped being true and no read filters as of a past state. The dashboard's two delete routes accept a bare localhost POST with no token or Origin check. The published benchmark numbers are LLM-judged evidence containment with the run records behind them kept out of the repository, and the LongMemEval run is an oracle configuration. It is AGPL-3.0-or-later with a separate commercial licence offered. Deleting a procedure leaves its summary, step text and originating query in the procedure-search projection, which the Home activity chart counts. And the surface is wide: 33 tables, a dashboard of over 4,000 lines, and a client-setup module that writes into every detected client and installs user services, which the Homebrew formula runs on install

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Two kinds. An episode is one raw turn with session, role and timestamp. A fact is an extracted statement with a subject-predicate-object triple, kind, entities, optional applicability scope, a world validity window and a superseded_by pointer; observations are LLM digests stored as facts

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file in WAL mode: episodes, facts, entities, aliases, an ingest log, three FTS5 tables and float32 embedding blobs searched by an in-process numpy scan. The enterprise package migrates the same file and keeps receipts in a sidecar file

Retrieval strategy.value: Default evidence engine: BM25 and exact cosine over episodes fused by normalised score, a session roll-up, assistant, speaker, when and time-window priors, then budget-adaptive packing. Facts come from a rank-fusion pass over BM25, vectors, entity links to two hops and key expansion. Named profiles and a zero-token router choose the policy

Write strategy.value: Explicit add() of a session. Lite mode stores turns only; full mode makes one extraction call per session, checks each model-assigned scope against the source text with one bounded correction call, and consolidates. Ingest is idempotent on a hash of messages, timestamp and session

Update/delete model.value: Supersession, not overwrite: a single-valued subject-predicate-scope collision closes the old interval for zero tokens, a semantic collision gets one LLM arbitration call. Owner-only erase_session and erase_entity cascade through FTS, entity links, embeddings and derived digests. No tombstone

Scoping model.value: One database per file. A fact's scope string partitions consolidation and digests and is printed into context, but no read path filters on it

Agent integration.value: Python library; a stdlib MCP server with six tools, remember, recall, search, facts_about, add_fact and stats, lite mode unless model settings are given; erasure and aliasing are deliberately not exposed over MCP

Background processing.value: None scheduled. refresh_observations and the enterprise sweep run when a caller invokes them

Trust/provenance model.value: Core: none beyond CURRENT and SUPERSEDED labels. Enterprise: immutable origin and a mutable quarantine flag, filtered only by search with strict set

Notable strengths.value: Supersession chain re-sorted by event time on every write; scope validation that refuses to globalise a rejected scoped fact; exact lineage and hold-aware transactional erasure in the enterprise layer; embedder identity pinned per database; committed raw benchmark rows from which the headline accuracy recomputes

Main risks.value: Scope is a label on the read path; an MCP add_fact on a single-valued predicate supersedes the user's value with no origin check; trust filtering is opt-in and absent from context assembly; the default audit sink discards; the headline benchmark runs lite mode, so it never exercises facts or supersession

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A cache entry — an opaque string under a composed key, with a TTL and an ACL. The two that carry conversation are `messages` (the whole transcript array) and `systemPrompt`

Storage backend.value: In-process `Map` by default (`RAMCache`), with Redis, S3 and a local-file cache as drop-in connectors; persisted chats go to files on disk through SmythFS

Retrieval strategy.value: Exact key lookup only. Nothing ranks, scores or searches — the transcript is loaded whole and then trimmed newest-first to a token budget

Write strategy.value: Synchronous and total. Every message rewrites the entire transcript array to the store and to the cache mirror

Update/delete model.value: TTL expiry is the primary death: 3 hours for memory components, 1–3 hours for runtime context, 1 hour for the LLM cache. `MemoryDeleteKeyVal` removes a value and its scope pointer. `LLMCache.clear()` deletes a key that is never written

Scoping model.value: An ACL stamped on every entry naming an agent, user or team as owner, checked on the read path. The conversation mirror is written team-scoped; the default account connector resolves every candidate to one team

Agent integration.value: Four workflow components (`MemoryWriteKeyVal`, `MemoryReadKeyVal`, `MemoryDeleteKeyVal`, `MemoryWriteObject`) an agent author wires by hand, plus `agent.chat(id, { persist: true })` in the SDK

Background processing.value: One expiry sweep per minute in `RAMCache`, and a debounced context sync whose cooldown scales with serialized size. No consolidation, extraction or summarisation pass exists

Trust/provenance model.value: None. No field records where a value came from or whether it may be acted on; a tool result and a user statement enter the transcript identically

Notable strengths.value: Access control is a decorator on the connector method rather than a convention, so it cannot be forgotten at a call site; scope violations on the key-value components fail closed as 'key not found'

Main risks.value: The transcript handle travels in a client-supplied `X-CACHE-ID` header; the mirror's ACL is team-wide and the default account connector puts everyone in one team; the scope pointer is written unscoped, so two sessions sharing a memory name silently lose each other's data

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A debate row: question, both models' final positions, the synthesis, a human-facing answer, and a verification_result holding each dispute's verifier verdict, finding and rejected options; a workspace row holds settled decisions and tradeoffs as JSON lists

Storage backend.value: Two SQLite files relative to the working directory, answer_memory.db for debates and database/workspaces.db for workspaces and the human decision queue, plus per-build JSON under workspaces/

Retrieval strategy.value: By answer id for a build; a follow-up loads the whole workspace row and injects its last ten verified decisions as settled constraints; the LIKE search over debates reaches no CLI path

Write strategy.value: Every debate appends a row after synthesis with the verifier's per-dispute verdicts; a build registers a workspace row from decisions.json; a follow-up rewrites the workspace lists in place

Update/delete model.value: A follow-up reopens decisions whose words overlap it and re-debates them under a key a model assigns; the build finalizer overwrites the stored execution verdict; no shipped command deletes anything

Scoping model.value: One SQL row per workspace; the answer table is global and read by id; human decisions filter on workspace_id, and standalone debates file theirs under one literal id

Agent integration.value: A four-command CLI (debate, build, resume, status) driving ChatGPT and Gemini web sessions over Chrome DevTools, a verifier through Cerebras, Groq, OpenRouter or Ollama, and the OpenCode CLI

Background processing.value: None for memory; a follow-up debate runs in a non-daemon thread, and the build, repair and finalizer passes run inline

Trust/provenance model.value: RESOLVED, UNRESOLVED or EQUIVALENT per dispute from a verifier model, fixed at write; only RESOLVED claims become the build's immutable constraints, and unresolved claims stop the build

Notable strengths.value: Disagreements kept as keyed disputes with a verdict, a finding and rejected options; one canonical reader that admits only resolved claims; deterministic impact analysis that reopens only the decisions a follow-up touches

Main risks.value: Build-registered workspaces key decisions by dispute_key, which the follow-up path never reads, so a contradicted decision stays settled; a person's resolution is stored and never read; key tests need an uncommitted database

Retrieval strategy.value: Reciprocal rank fusion over three channels — FTS5 BM25 with the summary weighted about thirteen and themes about six, sqlite-vec cosine, and a separate theme channel — with per-channel k constants and a vector weight all set by a named tuning study. Post-fusion the score takes a UCB exploration bonus over the feedback prior, a Hebbian co-retrieval boost capped and floored, and Personalized PageRank expansion over the edge graph, which replaced naive adjacency for a measured gain. A 31-feature LightGBM reranker sits on top when its artifact is present, and a hand-tuned formula runs when it is not

Write strategy.value: `remember(content, category, priority, themes)` over MCP. The write path strips secrets against eleven patterns, embeds, then runs a same-category vector dedup: a near-duplicate with lower priority is superseded and its search rows dropped, and a near-duplicate that does not beat the incumbent is refused and logged. Auto-captured memories land as `pending`. Every write also emits a `write_shadow` event recording its three nearest same-category neighbours and the outcome

Update/delete model.value: `forget()` marks a row `deleted` and drops its vector, FTS and rowid rows. The supersede branch of `remember()` does the same to the incumbent and sets `superseded_by`. Per-category exponential decay runs on a half-life from thirty days for episodic to a hundred and seventy-three for meta, with `entity` timeless; dormancy is detected rather than deleted. Sleep's NREM phase clusters and merges, and its REM phase looks for gaps and generates questions

Scoping model.value: None. One database for one person, with no project, user or tenant key on a record and no scope predicate on any read. `session_id` is recorded on events for analysis, not applied as a filter

Agent integration.value: Eleven MCP tools for Claude Code, registered with `claude mcp add`. The README supplies a `CLAUDE.md` block prescribing the rhythm — `startup_load` at session start, `recall` with both a keyword query and a natural-language context, `recall_feedback` after every recall, `remember` at session end — and a separate guide on budgets, categories and pitfalls

Background processing.value: Sleep consolidation is a script rather than a daemon, in two phases named after the sleep stages: NREM clusters and merges similar memories and refreshes summaries, REM performs gap analysis and question generation. Decay and dormancy detection run with it. A shadow-load counter tracks memories that keep surfacing without being useful — tracked as metadata and deliberately not used in scoring, because tuning showed the impact was marginal

Trust/provenance model.value: A three-value `status` — `active`, `pending`, `deleted` — where `pending` withholds an auto-captured memory from every read until a person confirms it. Beside it a numeric `confidence` that feeds scoring, an EWMA-aggregated utility from explicit feedback with empirical Bayes priors, and a UCB exploration bonus so an unrated memory is not permanently buried by one bad score. Nothing records that a claim was contradicted; `superseded_by` records that one was replaced

Notable strengths.value: Every tuning constant carries the study that set it, its previous value and the measured delta, and deprecated constants say so rather than lingering silently. A codified missing-value policy: any feature whose missing value would masquerade as a real measurement is NaN-encoded so the model learns an explicit missing branch, while a feature whose zero means something keeps zero. Secrets are stripped before storage against eleven patterns with a visible `[REDACTED_*]` marker. A dimension guard that fails loud. And an architecture document that records the project's own three-month silent regression in full

Main risks.value: It is not open source — Apache-2.0 under a Commons Clause that forbids selling, hosting or supporting it. There is no test suite: eleven `assert` statements in the tree, all in a benchmark harness. No scope key of any kind. `valid_until` is written when a memory evolves and queried nowhere. The `dedup_rejected` event is explicitly measurement rather than gating, so a rejected write is recorded and never consulted. The learned reranker's model artifact is not in the repository, so a fresh install runs the formula — now with a loud warning, which is the fix that was applied to a failure that had been silent

Update/delete model.value: A nightly near-duplicate pruner deletes all but one lesson per cluster and writes a content-hashed tombstone; facts are superseded by closing their interval or deleted by exact id and project; preferences are upserted in place; playbook entries are approved, rejected, edited or removed by the owner

Agent integration.value: A terminal REPL, a headless service, an HTTP server and an MCP surface over one local database; the agent's leverage on lessons is outcome-mediated, while playbook_note and sonder_remember_fact are direct tools

Background processing.value: A nightly self-improvement job drains distillation, backfills embeddings and prunes near-duplicates in a window of the newest 1,024 lessons; quarantine and decay are computed at read time

Trust/provenance model.value: Lessons are active, quarantined or on probation by outcome statistics; every outcome records who judged it under a NOT NULL closed vocabulary; preferences carry an enabled flag; playbook entries carry a review status that only the owner moves to approved

Notable strengths.value: Honest deletion vocabulary: forget says the bytes remain, purge reports what it zeroed and what it cannot reach; a contradiction test that asserts the winner, the hidden loser and the forensic mode; physical namespace isolation with a cross-namespace test; append-only fact log with supersession chains

Memory unit.value: A verbatim turn in an append-only JSONL log; derived from it, a fact row (attribute, value, valid and recorded intervals), a dated event, and verbatim keeper sentences

Storage backend.value: Two append-only files in a project's .memory/ folder, log.jsonl and judgements.jsonl, replayed at start into in-memory SQLite views; an optional vectors.sqlite cache

Retrieval strategy.value: BM25 over turn units expanded with fact-key cue words, plus exact-cosine embeddings, BM25 over events and a Personalized PageRank walk, fused by RRF; an optional cross-encoder reorders; fact rows in force on the question's date are added by code

Write strategy.value: The Stop hook logs the turns at once; a tagger model then points at facts and events in the user's words, code drops any quote not in the turn, and each tag is routed fast, slow, skip or rejected and recorded before it applies

Update/delete model.value: A fact is closed, never edited, by a later value or a retraction; a reset is a ruling that closes every open fact at a time and can be undone. Nothing deletes a local turn and no local forget or purge exists; memory_delete removes uploaded sessions from the cloud only

Scoping model.value: One .memory folder per project, or one for every project with --scope user. No scope key on a record or a query

Agent integration.value: Claude Code hooks (UserPromptSubmit, Stop, PreCompact), a Codex hook script, an MCP server, a local HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:7447 and an optional cloud upload for team sharing

Background processing.value: Tagging runs after the Stop hook replies; a full rebuild of facts, events and the BM25 index runs before the next question whenever anything new arrived

Trust/provenance model.value: Quotes are checked letter for letter against the turn; flagged tags go to a second model call whose ruling can be marked disputed, which labels a fact without filtering it

Notable strengths.value: Verbatim log as the only truth, every model decision written before it acts and replayed deterministically, SQLite triggers that refuse edits to fact rows, and dates computed by code

Main risks.value: The prompt hook injects whenever any keyword matches, with no relevance bar; the asking session's own turns can come back; a default install is keyword-only; and nothing in the local store can be forgotten

Memory unit.value: A compiled `Memory` row — one of four kinds (`profile_fact`, `episode_summary`, `procedure`, `artifact_ref`) — carrying content, a summary, a `confidence` float, `valid_from` and `valid_to`, a `status`, a list of `source_episode_ids` pointing back to the raw events it was derived from, an optional embedding, a `subject_id` and a nullable `tenant_id`.
