Storage backend.value: PostgreSQL under Alembic migrations, thirteen tables — `episodes`, `memories`, `subject_entities`, `subject_snapshots`, `compile_jobs`, `resolutions`, `receipts`, `tenant_configs`, `policy_bundles`, `query_embedding_cache`, `webhook_events`, `rate_limit_hits`, `subject_health_cache`. Embeddings are stored beside the rows with a query cache. Shipped as a PyPI package, a Docker image, a Helm chart and a Fly config

Retrieval strategy.value: `assemble_context` fetches a bounded candidate pool per kind — fifty profile facts, thirty episode summaries, twenty procedures, thirty episodes newest-first — every query keyed on the subject and, when set, the tenant, with the validity and status predicates applied in the repository layer. Candidates are scored by a kind priority, recency and, when a real embedding provider is configured, semantic similarity; the result is packed into a token budget measured with tiktoken. The same subject and task at the same point in time is intended to produce the same bytes

Write strategy.value: `POST /v1/episodes` appends a raw event, idempotent on `(tenant_id, subject_id, idempotency_key)`. Compilation is a separate step: `compile_memories_from_episodes` derives typed memories once per subject change rather than at query time, running as a durable job with attach-and-drain semantics. A memory is written with a `valid_from`, a `valid_to` computed from a per-kind TTL when one is configured, a confidence, and the ids of the episodes it came from

Update/delete model.value: Nothing is edited in place on the memory path. Conflict resolution marks an older memory `superseded` when a newer one restates the same claim; the TTL sweep marks a memory whose `valid_to` has passed `tombstoned`; both leave the row and its provenance readable. Hard deletion exists as a subject-level operation — delete by subject, with a preview endpoint and a webhook — rather than as a per-memory verb. Episodes are never mutated

Scoping model.value: `subject_id` is the primary key of everything — a user, an account, an agent, a repo. `tenant_id` is a second key applied by `_tenant_filter` whenever it is set, and left off in single-tenant mode. The pairing is enforced structurally: an AST fitness function fails CI when a repository helper accepts a subject without a tenant, with an empty allowlist and a docstring forbidding additions to it

Agent integration.value: A FastAPI service with routes for episodes, context, memories, subjects, timeline, receipts, resolutions, templates, handoff, health, SLA and a large admin surface. Deployed as a container beside the application rather than embedded in it, or run from the PyPI package. Webhooks fire on subject deletion and health events

Background processing.value: A durable compile-job queue with attach, drain and latency observability; a TTL sweep that tombstones lapsed memories; embedding backfill; health checks with a per-subject cache and alerting; rate limiting. Compilation is the scheduled work, and it is what makes retrieval cheap

Trust/provenance model.value: `status` decides whether a memory may be assembled; `confidence` is a float used in ranking. Every memory names the episodes it was compiled from, so a bundle traces to raw events. A state-assembly receipt records the entries selected, the policy bundle in force and an `as_of`, and a replay can re-evaluate a past bundle against the policy snapshot from its receipt rather than the live one. A per-kind TTL and a conflict resolver keep the active set from accumulating restatements

Notable strengths.value: Compile-then-serve rather than retrieve-then-hope, with the determinism claim made explicit and receipts to check it against; validity time separate from record time and both queried; a tenant-scoping invariant enforced by parsing the repository module rather than by review; a guard that refuses to treat a stub embedding provider's deterministic-but-meaningless vectors as a relevance signal, written after those scores were observed dominating ranking in production; provenance from every memory back to its source episodes

Main risks.value: `tombstoned` is a TTL expiry target rather than a record of a rejected value, so nothing stops a lapsed claim being recompiled from the same episodes; there is no audit record of memory mutations, and the receipts record what was assembled rather than what changed; single-tenant mode applies no tenant filter at all, so the isolation the invariant protects is only live when a tenant is configured

Memory unit.value: A MemoryEntry — content plus a free-form metadata dict and the name of the store it came from. No id, no timestamp and no status at the protocol level; what a store keeps underneath is its own business

Storage backend.value: Whatever the bound store runs. Three are vended: markdown files under a storage namespace, a JSON file of records, and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases over S3

Retrieval strategy.value: Per store. Token-overlap keyword scoring for the two local stores, Bedrock semantic retrieval with an optional score bound for the third. The Python file store hands the query string to its storage backend's search, which only a backend accepting a string answers; the TypeScript file store scans with list and read. The manager fans out to every store concurrently and concatenates in registration order with no cross-store ranking

Write strategy.value: Background extraction every 5 turns by default: a model call distills the conversation into discrete facts, written through the store's add. Python's synchronous agent call flushes extraction after every invocation, so there the caller waits on it. An optional add_memory tool lets the model write directly, off by default

Update/delete model.value: Neither exists. The store protocol has no delete method, and no path in the memory subsystem calls the delete the storage layer underneath it provides. The design doc's correction story is recency weighting, which one of three vended stores implements, as a tie-break

Scoping model.value: A scope key on the Bedrock store, stamped on writes and sent as an equals filter on every search; per store instance rather than per request. The other two stores and the manager are unscoped

Agent integration.value: Two SDKs at parity (Python and TypeScript), a harness that turns memory on by default, a CLI over that harness, and an MCP server

Background processing.value: An ExtractionCoordinator with a per-store high-water mark, a per-store task chain, at-least-once delivery and backoff after 10 consecutive failures. No consolidation, no reindex, no sweep

Trust/provenance model.value: None stored. Metadata is a free-form dict no read path filters on; OpenTelemetry spans cover search, add and extract but land in a trace backend, not in the store

Notable strengths.value: The store protocol is small and its optional methods are detected by inspecting the type rather than by a capability flag; the subagent delegate gets a read-only view that drops write sinks and the store's own tools; extraction excludes tool traffic by default; the scope key is stamped by the writer and enforced by the reader in both SDKs

Main risks.value: Nothing can be deleted or superseded, and the harness writes to a local markdown store by default with extraction on; an explicit Bedrock filter silently unscopes search; the Python file store over a storage backend whose search does not take a string writes every fact and finds none, with only a warning logged; the default file store merges corrections into the same file as what they correct; extraction is at-least-once and the default store has no idempotency

Memory unit.value: A row with a content body, one of seven types — decision, preference, file context, error pattern, research, outcome, guideline — plus a summary, an importance float, an access count and an optional expiry

Update/delete model.value: `INSERT OR REPLACE` keyed on id — no version, no prior value kept and no record that a replacement happened. Expiry never deletes: the row stays and the read filters it out

Trust/provenance model.value: None. `importance` is a float applied as a floor filter, so a memory cannot be kept while being marked unreliable; the only state a memory can reach is expired

Notable strengths.value: The scope manager refuses rather than falling back when a project store is missing, so a project memory is never quietly filed where every project can read it; the expiry flag defaults closed and is forwarded to both stores instead of re-derived, so the two arms cannot drift; the FTS index is maintained by triggers on insert, update and delete; and the tests assert the label as well as the result

Main risks.value: Corrections are `INSERT OR REPLACE`, so the prior content is gone and nothing records that a replacement happened; `importance` is a float set at write time with nothing moving it afterwards, so a memory the agent learns to distrust can only be deleted; expired rows are filtered but never swept; and the global store is shared across every project on the machine, so a guideline learned in one repository surfaces in the next

Memory unit.value: A memory: an id, a user id, prose content, a created-at and an optional updated-at — and a link between two memories carrying a free-text `reason`

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file with `memories`, `links`, a singleton `syke_identity`, a singleton `current_memex` and an FTS5 index, beside a control directory of receipts, recovery points and an immutable MEMEX history

Retrieval strategy.value: FTS5 with a porter tokenizer over memory content, plus the whole `MEMEX.md` projection read directly by other agents

Write strategy.value: `syke record` from a person or agent, and a background synthesis cycle that reads local harness activity and rewrites the graph and the projection through an LLM

Update/delete model.value: The synthesis cycle may create, revise and delete memories; `links` declare `ON DELETE RESTRICT` on both endpoints, so a linked memory cannot be deleted without the link going first

Scoping model.value: A single local identity. Every table carries a `user_id`, `syke_identity` is a singleton with a CHECK constraint, and the post-cycle gate counts rows outside that identity and fails if any exist

Agent integration.value: A CLI — `syke ask`, `syke record`, `syke memex` — plus adapter seeds for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, opencode, Hermes, Pi and Antigravity, and a distributed `MEMEX.md`

Background processing.value: An ambient daemon that observes local harness sessions and runs synthesis cycles under a lock, with a recovery fence and reconciliation of an interrupted cycle before the next database use

Trust/provenance model.value: A recovery point per cycle with copy-on-write cloning where the filesystem allows it, integrity checks on the clone, a fingerprinted baseline of every memory and link, and a post-cycle gate whose invariants are enforced by rejecting the attempt

Notable strengths.value: The gate is the mechanism and its invariants are well chosen: a pre-existing memory's or link's `created_at` may not change, no link may reference a missing memory, the identity must stay a singleton with no rows outside it, the FTS index must match the memories table, and exactly one non-empty current MEMEX must survive. Rejections are marked repairable and the cycle is retried rather than abandoned. Before any of that, `capture_baseline` fingerprints every memory and link and `create_recovery_point` clones the database — copy-on-write when the filesystem supports it, a SQLite backup otherwise — with integrity checks on the copy, and an interrupted cycle is reconciled before the database is used again. The MEMEX history is immutable, content-hashed and receipt-linked

Main risks.value: The gate computes `memories_removed` and `removed_memory_ids`, records them in its stats, and raises no issue for them; no caller reads the number either — the synthesis backend branches only on `valid`, which is derived from `issues`. A cycle that deletes most of the graph passes. The recovery point taken beforehand means the state is restorable, but nothing notices that it should be restored, and the one number that would catch it is already in hand. The per-cycle graph change set — created, revised and removed ids for memories and links — is likewise assembled and never persisted, so the immutable history covers the rendered projection and not the mutations that produced it. A memory carries no status, no confidence and no provenance beyond its timestamps; the link's `reason` is free text

Update/delete model.value: `teamai recall maintenance --prune` removes learnings whose confidence falls under a threshold, or moves them to `learnings/_archive/`, which the collector never indexes; `promote` rewrites a mature learning into a skill, rule or doc through the AI CLI; the importer's `supersedes` list is logged and consumed by nothing; `teamai remove` appends a rule, skill, agent or MCP name to a committed `<type>/.removed` file that the next pull uses to delete every member's local copy and that the push scan consults so a stale copy is never re-uploaded — a mechanism learnings and docs are not part of, and one whose pull-side deletion of a skill is conditional: a tombstoned skill directory holding nested VCS metadata is kept with a warning, and a skill dropped by a role or tag change is deleted only when it is byte-identical to its team-repo source; a user-scope pull and a user-scope contribute reconcile `~/.teamai/learnings/` against the repository with `mirrorLearnings`, which deletes a shared root document, an inactive namespace directory and a file under an active namespace that the repository has dropped before the overwrite copy, so a prune or an archive reaches every member's cache and the index built from it

Scoping model.value: Project scope from the working directory's configuration, user scope from the home directory, chosen at read time with user results admitted only on opt-in; inside a scope, a project manifest maps an active project to learnings namespaces the index and the user-scope copy admit and every other subdirectory is skipped; roles map a member to knowledge and skill namespaces and tags subscribe a member to resources, both applied on pull

Agent integration.value: A CLI with `init`, `pull`, `push`, `recall`, `contribute`, `review`, `digest`, `dashboard` and more; hooks installed into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, CodeBuddy, OpenCode, Qoder and others, dispatched through one `hook-dispatch` command with a handler registry; a built-in `teamai-recall` subagent and a managed block in each agent's instructions; git hosts including GitHub, GitLab, GitCode, CNB and TGit; an HTTP local-agent backend as an alternative to the repository

Background processing.value: A SessionStart pull, a Stop-time friction score and vote sync, usage tracking on skill calls, a dashboard report; no scheduled consolidation; maintenance, promotion and quality drafts are commands a person runs

Trust/provenance model.value: A confidence per document — recalled and upvoted counts, recency of last recall, an upvote ratio — used for pruning, promotion and a health report; upvotes counted only for documents the transcript shows were recalled; a risk of medium or high on each review item; no state on a learning

Notable strengths.value: Votes that require the document to have been recalled before it can be credited; a relevance verdict that reports its threshold and the matched and missing terms; a review queue with a risk level for machine-written knowledge, behind a hidden opt-in flag; a namespace key applied at the copy, the index and the contribution, with a path-segment guard at three boundaries; scope isolation proved by tests; 3,020 test cases

Main risks.value: Supersession is computed and written to nothing; `teamai remove` has no learnings handler, so retiring a lesson by name is a repository edit rather than a record any later write consults; the skill deletion that does propagate is skipped for a deployed copy that differs from its source or cannot be compared against one, which is the copy a member is most likely to have edited; the learnings reconcile treats its source as authoritative, so a call site passing a partial snapshot deletes whatever the snapshot omits; retrieval is title and tag matching with a body fallback, no vector arm; the recall block tells the model it *should* invoke the subagent with four skip conditions, so recall is advisory; documents are required to be in Chinese by the share skill

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A `ContextEvent` on a node timeline: event time, ingestion time, type, confidence, importance, text and an inline embedding vector

Storage backend.value: An append-structured page store with its own WAL, block store, Raft replication and shared object storage; a Redis-compatible RESP surface on top

Retrieval strategy.value: A ranked, token-budgeted ContextPack — lexical scores mapped into the same micros scale as cosine similarity so embedded and un-embedded nodes merge into one ranking

Write strategy.value: Ingest events, extract entities and summaries, embed inline with a drainer for deferred or failed embeddings

Update/delete model.value: Resource lifecycle records carry `stale` and `deleted` flags used for counting and refresh; nothing in the event path supersedes or retires a memory

Scoping model.value: A tenant hash derived from `account_id:tenant_id` on the caller's own request, with `acct_local`/`tenant_local_agent` substituted when either is empty

Agent integration.value: Rust and Python SDKs, a proxy, Claude and Codex plugins, agent hooks, and any Redis client through the RESP surface

Background processing.value: An embedding drainer that retries deferred and failed embeddings, and resource watchers on an interval

Trust/provenance model.value: Confidence and importance as continuous filter floors, and a ContextPackAudit recording what a pack was assembled from

Notable strengths.value: The engineering below the memory layer is serious and legible: an append-structured page store with crash-safe reload, Raft, shared-storage clustering, 2,404 test functions, and constants documented with the reasoning behind their values rather than the values alone. `LEXICAL_MATCH_MICROS` is set at half the cosine ceiling with a written argument — so that "in a MIXED store, a strong semantic (embedded) match still outranks a purely lexical one, while un-embedded nodes remain rankable (never a flat 0) instead of collapsing to recency order" — which is a real hazard most hybrid rankers hit silently. A `bool` field carries a comment explaining why it is defaulted explicitly rather than with `#[serde(default)]`, because an absent field decoding to `false` would send a reader to an object URI the record does not carry. The benchmark documentation is likewise candid where it could have been quiet: it records that ingestion previously dropped tool messages entirely, "losing ~35% of real local context"; it states that grading against a recency slice is the wrong method and says so in italics; and its scope note admits a missing skills tier and instructs that "adoption claims should be scoped to memory + resources, not skills"

Main risks.value: The memory layer carries no epistemic or lifecycle state that retrieval acts on. `valid_until_ms` is the field that would close a world-time window, and every constructor in the tree sets it to `0` — the schema marks it "Deprecated hot-schema field: reserves this field", naming no replacement, while `context_event_matches_filter` still reads it under `#[allow(deprecated)]`, so the branch cannot fire for anything this code writes. The same filter's status check reads the in-row `status`, also deprecated and `skip_serializing`, after status filtering moved to a `status_hash` secondary index. `primary_time_ms()` prefers ingestion time when present, so the `as_of` comparison runs on arrival rather than on when anything was true, even though both columns exist on the row. `context_scope_matches` — the rule granting a global layer to everyone and letting an agent-layer request read user and workspace entries — has exactly one call site, in skill lookup, gated on `owner_scope_filter_enabled`, which is simply whether the caller sent a non-empty scope string. And the tenant key comes from `request.scope`, defaulting to `acct_local:tenant_local_agent`, so two callers that omit it share one tenant. Finally the headline: the 99.92% token saving divides a ~1,333-token pack by a 1,698,940-token corpus that the baseline arm never read, because the reproduce command caps it at 8,000 tokens for a reader whose window is 4,096 — a footnote says so directly, "[t]he saving headline is still computed against the full corpus", and the table keeps the number

Memory unit.value: A belief — subject, attribute, value, a valid interval, a recorded and a last-confirmed time, an authority level, sources, derivation lineage, a status and a supersession link — materialised from immutable lifecycle events

Storage backend.value: Append-only JSONL event files in a directory, either plain or with each belief's payload encrypted under its own key; Markdown projections and index snapshots rebuilt from them and optionally committed to Git; an independent SQLite oracle as a cross-check

Retrieval strategy.value: The oracle answers a subject and attribute at a transaction instant and a valid instant. A separate hybrid retriever fuses exact, lexical, hashed-vector and one-hop graph channels by reciprocal rank over a caller-supplied state, applying valid time only when its temporal channel is requested

Write strategy.value: Events appended through a store that refuses duplicate event ids, with both clocks supplied by the caller. No policy runs on the append path; the ingest and action gates are separate functions

Update/delete model.value: Reconfirm, supersede, expire and purge are events. A purge removes a belief from the projection and leaves its payload in the plain ledger; `redact_payloads` rewrites that payload in place and appends a receipt, and the protected store erases by destroying the belief's key

Scoping model.value: None in the store or on any read path. A tenant string exists only on the signed evidence envelope the action gate checks

Agent integration.value: A `temvera` CLI over the substrate and the experiment harness, plus adapters for Mem0, LangMem, Graphiti, Cognee and Hindsight

Background processing.value: None in the substrate. Decay and consolidation studies, a literature-freeze tool for the paper's prior-art review, LongMemEval label adjudication and artifact verification over sealed runs sit in the harness

Trust/provenance model.value: Five authority levels fixed at ingest and read only by action gates that refuse rather than discount, Ed25519-signed evidence envelopes, derivation-laundering detection, and adversarial probes whose one success is published

Notable strengths.value: Two things, and they are the same habit applied twice. The first is `bypass.py`, which publishes the attack that works: `compromised_trusted_signer` activates, is declared `expected_limitation=True`, and `tests/test_bypass.py` asserts that it is the only probe that activates, so a newly working bypass breaks the suite and the admission cannot be deleted without the test noticing. The second is the artifact discipline: "the whole paper can be checked without an API key, a database server, or a dataset download", and `verify_paper_claims.py` pairs each figure as printed with a recomputation from a sealed run and fails if either half moves, which catches a corrected number as readily as a corrupted one. The query protocol makes both instants mandatory, so each baseline is the oracle with one axis deleted in a single statement

Main risks.value: A research reference implementation at version 0.0.1 under a provisional API, and the README says "[n]o production readiness is claimed". The governance layer is not wired to the memory: authority is fixed at ingest and read only by action gates that no append and no retrieval calls, the tenant is never stored, and the superseded and expired statuses are written and never filtered on. The hybrid retriever and packet builder index superseded and expired beliefs and return them unless a caller asks for the temporal channel. Transaction time is supplied by the writer. A purge leaves the payload in the plain ledger, `redact_payloads` rewrites that ledger in place, and no ingest path reads the deletion receipts, so an erased value can return as a new belief. Regenerating the external comparisons needs an OpenAI key, a Neo4j server and a second interpreter

Memory unit.value: A typed atomic note — a *tessellum* — small enough to make a single point and tagged with what kind of point it makes, linked into Folgezettel trails

Storage backend.value: Authored notes as the source of truth under a one-way CQRS split; the searchable index is a projection rebuilt from them and never written back to

Retrieval strategy.value: Hybrid keyword and vector search over the projection, plus a query protocol that abstains when a claim's computed status is not answerable

Write strategy.value: Author notes, or hand over a source document and let the digester produce them; a dialectic cycle turns an observation into competing arguments, a counter and a revised rule

Update/delete model.value: Promotion turns an episodic derivation into durable knowledge; a scheduled re-derivation gate demotes, and an inconclusive finding quarantines rather than retracts

Scoping model.value: None — one knowledge base per installation

Agent integration.value: A Python package and CLI; it is not an agent-memory store and says so

Background processing.value: The scheduled re-derivation gate, consolidation, and a Dung grounded-semantics solver over the argument graph

Trust/provenance model.value: A blinded re-derivation protocol against a pinned model with an arithmetic verdict, five outcomes each carrying whether it is conclusive, and a labelling that treats an undecided dispute as having settled nothing

Notable strengths.value: The demotion module states the atlas's own central finding better than the atlas does: "a promoted claim that stops being true has no way to notice on its own, so a promotion path without a demotion path is a mechanism for entrenching whatever was believed first. That is not a hypothetical failure mode — it is the one the memory literature documents most consistently — which is why this gate ships ahead of consolidation rather than beside it." Its protocol is a blinded test in three parts, each closing a way the test could cheat. The claim is suppressed by construction — the request type "has nowhere to put" its text or id, and the gate refuses a caller who smuggles the claim into the question or cites the claim's own rendering as a source. The model is pinned with an explicit `model_id` and `frozen_at`, because one that re-tunes on the corpus it is checking "would eventually regenerate its own promoted claim from the promotion, and the gate would certify itself". And the verdict is arithmetic — a token-overlap ratio against a floor — because "[a] model must never decide the verdict: a demotion nobody can recompute is a demotion nobody can appeal." Three triggers fire independently, and the first is the one "an attack-driven system misses entirely": a claim can stop regenerating from its own sources with no attack against it anywhere in the log

Main risks.value: It is not an agent-memory store, and the README says so in its second sentence — a reader arriving for a memory backend will find a knowledge-construction system whose unit is an authored note. By this atlas's own scope rule it belongs here anyway, because it keeps claims that can turn out to be false and names which part of a losing argument broke; but the marks this atlas awards attach to a store's read path, and the statuses here are computed from the argument edge set rather than stored, so none apply. Two limits the project states about itself are worth carrying: by default the dialectic cycle "treats two arguments as conflicting when their claims are worded differently", with evidence-based incompatibility an opt-in mode — so the default conflict detector is textual, the failure chitta-field's claim-centric detector is built to avoid; and each cycle is labelled on its own, "so a later argument does not yet overturn an earlier cycle's verdict". There is also no scoping, and at 138,183 lines with a vocabulary drawn from Zettelkasten practice and formal argumentation, the entry cost is real

Memory unit.value: A knowledge item with an immutable revision chain — title, body, kind, namespace, status, trust level, sensitivity, owner, labels, scope paths, validity window, author and source anchors

Storage backend.value: SQLite derived from a directory of YAML migrations and Markdown bodies under each project's .theurian directory, with a separately built and published retrieval index

Retrieval strategy.value: Hybrid search over a published index — a word index, a trigram index and an optional hashed-trigram dense arm fused by reciprocal rank — with status and sensitivity asked before ranking and an optional asOf moment

Write strategy.value: Migrations applied by the migrate apply CLI. Agents draft proposals through three MCP tools; a proposal lands only through propose accept and migrate apply, both CLI commands

Scoping model.value: A per-project state file under the project root, and a project predicate on every canonical read; the project is a tool argument

Agent integration.value: A local MCP daemon with seven read tools and three proposal tools reporting writeTools true, a Claude Code plugin of slash commands granting the theurian CLI, and Codex over streamable HTTP

Trust/provenance model.value: Status, trust level, sensitivity and a validity window returned beside every result, a deployment sensitivity ceiling, and a content-identity gate that withholds a row whose body drifted from its revision's hash

One query is asked of a corpus holding a withheld record and of one that never held it, and the answers must match field for field — counts, token use, fused scores, budget drops and page boundaries — with a positive control proving the fixture reaches the withheld row. The visibility question is asked while the retrievers are read, because asking late let a withheld row occupy a candidate slot and move every number computed from those slots. A SQL validity filter was removed rather than patched once it was found comparing ISO-8601 timestamps as text. Accepting a proposal replays the whole migration set against a throwaway store and refuses one that would readmit a retired item or lower a sensitivity

An agent's proposal is written with status approved and whatever trust level the caller names, and the shipped Claude Code plugin grants the agent Bash(theurian:*), which covers propose accept and migrate apply; the plugin's own text calls that containment a documented rule, not a server-side check. The revision table's source_commit column has no writer. The project is chosen by the caller and there is one sensitivity ceiling per deployment, so the store separates projects, not people

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A node on a canvas — a question, answer versions with the model, time and context hash of each, a per-upstream record of what each input contributed, highlights, attachments with page provenance, a role, an archived flag, an import source and a frozen source snapshot — joined by wires that are the context; on a node that ran an agent turn or was imported from one, tool-step attachments excluded from context by default and a count of the thinking the turn spent, display only; beside it two profile documents, preferences and identity, one fact per line, each line with a note of the fact, canvas, time and evidence that wrote it; one dossier per topic in four sections whose sentences cite the turns they rest on; in the why layer, a fact index over other agents' session files and the memory files Claude Code and Codex keep

Storage backend.value: IndexedDB per canvas (idb-keyval) with a one-minute debounced `.thoughtdag.json` folder backup; `localStorage` for the profile documents, the memory inbox, the switches and each canvas's ask-the-canvas turns; `~/.thoughtdag/` for the why layer's fact index, text index, topic labels and dossiers, and a slim record of each canvas; a `.thoughtdag` folder in an agent turn's working directory for its guard file and copied materials; the source agents' session and memory files are read and never written

Retrieval strategy.value: For a generation, a deterministic walk of the graph — materials, dashed reference blocks, the solid chain in order, the question last — with archived nodes skipped, stale answers marked, an excluded tool record — an agent-lane footprint, or an imported turn's tool steps, which arrive switched off — reduced to one line naming its files, and a switched-on record folded into one execution record; with recall switched on, up to two topic dossiers whole and verbatim excerpts found by the question's exact words or by judged topic labels, ranked by a decision model when one answers over a light, deep or full reach, inside a 4k, 12k or 40k token ceiling; ask the canvas sends an outline of every live node and the focused node's chain; for the why layer, exact phrase and path lookup with reads hidden by default; no vectors anywhere

Write strategy.value: A person asks, edits, wires and imports; a model's answer lands as a version on its node; after an ordinary generation a decision model, or without one an API model from the shared background order, decides whether something durable was said, a preference or identity fact is merged into its document by a model rewrite whose new lines are re-checked for credentials and which may drop at most two lines, and a project fact is filed to a topic dossier's inbox or to the memory inbox; dossiers are written by a background API model from labelled turns; Session Atlas mirrors other agents' turns idempotently; the harness bridge forks, injects and queues into live sessions; Pi and Codex turns edit files in a working directory behind a guard

Update/delete model.value: Answers are versioned and never overwritten; a node can be archived — kept, dimmed, excluded from every context walk on its canvas and from the why layer's projection of the canvas at the next index refresh — or deleted; a wire can be removed or converted; an upstream change marks live dependants stale and replay regenerates them in dependency order; a profile rewrite can be undone at the toast or edited by hand; a dossier section can be edited, the dossier rebuilt from the turns or deleted; a recalled item can be struck from a node

Scoping model.value: One canvas per IndexedDB key and reachability by wire as the only filter inside it; the profile documents are global to the install; recall reads every project's sessions, canvases and agent memory files on the machine by design, leaving out only the active canvas's own record; the why layer's JSON find honours a working-directory filter that no in-tree caller passes; an agent turn is fenced to one working directory per canvas

Agent integration.value: A React canvas in the browser, an Electron desktop app with fenced session roots, an Express proxy for OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek and Zhipu endpoints plus MCP tools and a pass-through for decision endpoints, a Cloudflare Pages demo with no server state, a `dsh-thoughtdag` plugin mounting the canvas and the why layer inside DeepSeek Harness through its sidebar, a CLI exposing `why_check`, `why_file`, `find` and `recall_turn` over MCP and listed in the MCP Registry, and Pi, Codex and the harness's agents as runtimes behind the model picker

Background processing.value: A file watcher appends new turns of a subscribed session to its mirror; the why index refreshes when a source file's size or mtime moved; the memory judge runs fire-and-forget after ordinary generations; a labelling job asks the decision model one yes or no per topic for up to 600 turns per click; a stale judge asks whether an upstream change bears on each newly stale answer; a node with autoRerun regenerates when an ancestor completes; a dossier with six filed facts merges when the memory page opens

Trust/provenance model.value: A stale mark on any live answer whose upstream fingerprint drifted, prepended in downstream context; a judge can dismiss the mark, which leaves the badge, the preview, the request and Replay alike; a tool record whose contents are withheld names its files; a basis and completeness on every why-layer event, displayed and never filtered; an identity fact admitted only when the user stated it; a credential pattern checked on the fact and on every new line of the rewritten document; a stated, inferred, manual or folded note on each profile line, display only; conclusiveness levels on takeaways, display only

Notable strengths.value: The preview and the request share one compiler; a request hash written at dispatch; dossier sentences that carry the keys of the turns they rest on; recall items listed, priced and strikeable on the node; archive reaching the index recall reads; a benchmark whose conditions are graph operations, whose traces are immutable and whose scorer can re-score without an API call; source sessions and agent memory files read and never rewritten

Main risks.value: The canvas event log drops its oldest thousand events past 10,000, and sees no profile, dossier, recall or ask-the-canvas write; stale is a label and a judge's dismissal removes it outright; recall crosses every project on the machine, and an archived node's dossier sentences and a mirrored turn's session text survive its archive; topic labels and dossier coverage are keyed by a node's position, which an archive shifts; a node with autoRerun reruns while archived; the profile's stated label is the admitted fact's, carried onto every line a rewrite changed; ambient identity and preferences ride every canvas; the proxy's agent and judge endpoints accept any target from any localhost origin

Memory unit.value: A markdown note carrying a hand-written `Search for:` line of roughly thirty terms, plus front-matter provenance and a `stage` of raw, distilled or derived

Storage backend.value: The markdown where it already sits, with a SQLite index over it; one binary, no daemon, no account

Retrieval strategy.value: A deterministic keyword router that returns the files to open and the words that matched under each, with no embedding model and nothing in the path that improvises

Write strategy.value: Four outcomes — NOOP, ADD, UPDATE, DELETE — through a write gate, with provenance and stage recorded on the note and the agent holding a right to delete

Update/delete model.value: An update rewrites the note and a delete removes it; history is git, and a wrong answer is corrected by editing the file the router named

Scoping model.value: Several bases, each owned by a specialist; `kb boot` scores a message across them and routes, which selects a base rather than filtering rows inside one

Agent integration.value: A CLI, an MCP server over stdio for Claude Code and similar hosts, and a panel mode that seats reviewers from their own constitutions

Background processing.value: None over retrieval; promotion and distillation are invoked passes

Trust/provenance model.value: Refusal as a first-class outcome, matched words returned as the reason, a provenance ladder on every note, and a panel ledger where each objection is taken, refused with a reason, or escalated

Notable strengths.value: The thesis is a trade stated in full rather than a feature: "[r]etrieval is plain software: no embedding model, no network, nothing in the path that improvises. Same question, same answer, today and in a year, and when the answer is wrong you can read why in words you can act on" — and then, immediately, the cost: "[t]he price is writing, and it is paid per note. Each one carries a hand written `Search for:` line, roughly thirty terms… Nothing infers it for you." The abstention work follows the same discipline. It is measured because it is the differentiating claim, scored in both directions so a high decline rate cannot be bought with false declines, and bounded by a paragraph headed "[w]hat 'declined' means here, stated so nobody reads more into it". The panel is the third piece: reviewers must back objections with a mechanism rather than style, the round is priced before it is spent, every objection is "taken, refused with a reason, or escalated", and the governance rule is one sentence — "[o]ne agent stays accountable; nobody votes." Its own decision records carry `Search for:` lines, so the project is indexed by the convention it asks of its users

Main risks.value: The provenance ladder is recorded and never read. A note carries `stage: raw | distilled | derived` — with a `captured` stage kept deliberately distinct from `distilled` "so the provenance ladder does not quietly gain a rung" — and `provenance: agent`, and no read path filters on either: no comparison against a stage appears anywhere in the tool sources, so a raw capture and a distilled note rank by the same keyword score. That is the third system this atlas has read in short order whose epistemic vocabulary is validated and then ignored at retrieval. Scoping selects a base rather than filtering within one, so separation is a routing decision rather than a predicate on a row. The panel's reviewers are agents with constitutions, not people, so the ledger records adjudication by the same kind of thing that proposed the work — the accountability rule names an agent as owner, not a person. And the central cost is unavoidable and unhedged: a note without a good `Search for:` line is a note the router cannot reach, and nothing infers one, so the library's recall is exactly as good as its author's discipline

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: One row in a single `nodes` table, typed `context` or a message. Every node carries a `public_id`, the `project_id`, a JSONB `content` and `metadata`, a `created_at`, and three link columns — `parent_id` (the context this one was forked from), `prev_id` (the previous node in its chain) and `context_id` (the head it belongs to). A context is a chain of `context` nodes; each of those is a version, and owns a chain of messages

Storage backend.value: Postgres by default with a compose file and an `init.sql`, or Supabase, or SQLite through the same adapter interface; the API runs on Cloudflare Workers via wrangler or as a Node server. Indexes on `(project_id, type, context_id)`, on `context_id`, on `prev_id`, on `created_at`, and a GIN index on `metadata`. There is no vector column and no full-text index — retrieval is by id, by list, and by metadata filter

Retrieval strategy.value: By identity rather than by relevance. `get` resolves a context under the project and walks its chain, optionally at a version index, at a timestamp, or sliced at a message index; `list` pages a project's root contexts with metadata filters. There is no ranking, no embedding and no search — the MCP server hands an agent whole contexts, and the agent reads them

Write strategy.value: Two paths. A local sync daemon tails the session files of Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and OpenClaw, normalises each line through a per-agent parser, deduplicates against a local `seen_events` table with a TTL, and appends to a session context over the API. Separately, five SDK methods — create, get, append, update, delete — are the git-like Context API, with create accepting `from`, `version`, `at` and `before` to fork a source at a point

Update/delete model.value: Update and message-delete append a new version head recording the operation and the affected ids, so history survives and any earlier version can be read or forked from. Permanent delete is a separate path that removes the rows outright; it is chosen only by an empty body or an explicit `{permanent: true}`, and a body that combines `permanent` with `ids` is refused rather than resolved

Scoping model.value: `project_id` on every node, derived from the API key on every request and applied by the project-scoped resolvers. The gap is the fork source: `findRootContextByPublicId` takes no project, and it is how `create` resolves `from`

Agent integration.value: An MCP server, stdio or built into the API; npm and PyPI SDKs; a CLI with a terminal dashboard that runs the sync daemon. Parsers for five agents and *writers* for two, so a session can be written back out in another agent's own on-disk format and resumed there

Background processing.value: The sync daemon watches session directories in realtime, tracks per-file offsets, deduplicates by event hash with an expiry, and bulk-ingests in batches with per-session concurrency. Nothing consolidates, summarises, decays or re-ranks — the store grows and is read whole

Trust/provenance model.value: None. A search of the core, storage and API sources for a status, confidence, verified or stale vocabulary returns HTTP status codes and API-key verification and nothing else. A captured event carries its source, host, user id and session id as metadata; none of it is applied as a filter on truth

Notable strengths.value: Writers as well as parsers, so a session can genuinely continue in a different agent rather than merely being searchable; an `AGENT_COMPAT` matrix declaring which CLI versions each parser was verified against and which resume pairs have fixture coverage; a delete route that refuses an ambiguous body instead of guessing, so a typo cannot fall through to a permanent wipe; versioning that is the data model rather than a side table; a storage adapter thin enough that Postgres, Supabase and SQLite are genuinely interchangeable

Main risks.value: The fork path resolves its source without the project key, so a context id is a read grant across the project boundary. The redactor runs on the archival `raw` copy of a captured event and not on the `message` text derived from it, so a secret is masked in one field and shipped in the clear in the other — and no test mentions the redactor. The compatibility matrix is exported and consulted only by tests, while the writer is chosen by a bare ternary with no default, so any target that is not `codex` gets the Claude writer. And the hosted service is the default deployment: the SDK examples take a `uc_live_` key

The storage interface then splits in two: `findRootContext(projectId, publicId)`, `listRootContexts(projectId, …)` and the delete helpers take the key, and `getContext` resolves through the first of those, so a foreign project gets `not_found`. But `findRootContextByPublicId(publicId)` sits one line below it in the same interface and takes no project, and its single caller is the fork source resolution in `createContext` — where `projectId` is used only to stamp the new rows. Retrieval strategy.value: Tool-mediated. Write strategy.value: Bulk ingest is optimistic: parse, chunk, index, embed, then an LLM extraction that resolves entities and writes facts directly, with doubtful cases queued. A sentence recorded through `remember` appends a chunk to a per-base Memory log and is extracted into `pending_facts`, which never reaches the graph until a person confirms it

Update/delete model.value: Append-only. A functional relation's new value closes the old interval and links back via `supersedes`; below 0.75 confidence or with ambiguous timing it opens a conflict for a person. Deleting a document is a recorded event that invalidates only facts whose every source is gone and is revertible from a named list; purge is irreversible and leaves a tombstone row

Scoping model.value: Knowledge base, applied as a `kb_id` predicate on both retrieval arms and every graph read, with owner/admin/editor/viewer membership on top; personal tokens carry a base list and a read-or-write scope that is intersected with the holder's role on every MCP call

Agent integration.value: One binary serving a REST API, an SSE chat loop with a six-round tool budget, a Streamable-HTTP MCP endpoint per base exposing eleven read tools and `remember`, and a React console with graph browser, ontology workbench and review queues

Background processing.value: A Postgres job queue consumed in-process with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`: document processing, memory ingest, extraction, ontology bootstrap and embedding, vector index builds, scheduled forward chaining, source sync and an optional governance agent that adjudicates duplicate pairs by reading the audit ledger for precedent

Trust/provenance model.value: Four tables encode status rather than a score: pending, asserted, derived, rejected. Derived facts never close an asserted one; confidence gates auto-closing and fills the low-confidence queue but filters no retrieval result; an automatic merge is held for a person whenever undoing it could not recall what it already sent outside the graph

Notable strengths.value: A genuinely bidirectional pair of clocks with read predicates centralised in two modules, a rejected-triple key consulted before every memory proposal, an append-only ledger the database itself defends and the governance agent reads as precedent, and a committed 37-question bitemporal question set that asks both axes and excludes its own known gaps from the headline

Main risks.value: The nod and the rejected-triple key cover only the `remember` path — bulk ingest writes facts optimistically and can re-assert a rejected triple; the lexical arm has no historical version so record-time recall under-recalls; the whole extraction path needs an LLM endpoint, and every source comment is in Chinese

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A chunk of one Add message, up to 320 regex tokens with 40 overlap, stored verbatim with role, user_id, session_id, request_id, the caller's message timestamp and a float32 embedding

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file in WAL mode: memories with embedding BLOBs, add_requests holding one payload hash per request_id, and store_metadata pinning the embedding model identity; the offline benchmark path builds a separate FAISS flat index per directory

Retrieval strategy.value: Loads every row of the requested user_id, scores all of them by cosine, fuses BM25 over the same rows by weighted RRF at k = 60, optionally reranks with a cross-encoder, then adds same-session neighbours of the top 20 seeds; returns evidence, never an answer

Write strategy.value: Synchronous POST /add: chunk, embed every chunk under a process-wide lock, then insert under BEGIN IMMEDIATE after a second request_id check; idempotent on request_id and payload hash, 409 on a changed payload; no model call beyond the embedder

Update/delete model.value: No update or delete route; a CLI script deletes every row whose user_id starts with a prefix and keeps no record; nothing is superseded, expired or deduplicated across requests

Scoping model.value: user_id on every row and one WHERE user_id = ? on the search read, under which every ranking arm runs; user_id is a caller field under one shared API key; health counts span all users

Agent integration.value: Three HTTP routes, health, add and search, with X-Api-Key, Bearer or Token auth; a Dockerfile and compose file; smoke, load and replay scripts; an offline FAISS index, ask and evaluate CLI

Background processing.value: None

Trust/provenance model.value: None; every chunk is stored as sent and returned as evidence labelled with its role and timestamp

Notable strengths.value: One scope predicate at the row load that every arm inherits, BM25 statistics included; double-checked idempotent writes; an embedding identity that refuses a database written under another model or context setting; a populated cross-user negative test

Main risks.value: The tokenizer matches no Cyrillic, Hangul or kana, so such messages are not stored while Add returns 200; the Dockerfile's defaults are the 0.4.0 enhanced configuration, not the README's frozen 0.6.0 one; deletion is a prefix script with a race

Memory unit.value: A Markdown file in the vault, typed by its `type:` key (note, person, log, me), with frontmatter properties, wiki links, an optional origin label, and beside it in .vaultite/ a sidecar of the lines agents wrote

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A fact — `fact_id`, `claim`, `source`, `confidence`, `epistemic_state`, `claim_type`, `source_status`, `significance`, a `restricted` bit and metadata — in an L1 SQLite table, projected with its `truth_status` as a node with edges, entities and mentions into an L3 canonical graph, with evidence spans that bind a claim to a byte range of a source

Storage backend.value: SQLite for L1 facts, evidence spans, import and review sessions, the erasure log, the audit chain, the per-fact provenance chain and checkpoints; the L3 graph in on-disk SQLite unless the optional LadybugDB package is installed, with Neo4j selectable and a Postgres/pgvector migration written and not authorized; files and receipts beside them

Retrieval strategy.value: A bounded lexical pass when no embeddings are indexed; otherwise a hybrid cosine-plus-lexical retrieve over admitted memory with a graph walk that spreads activation along edges, blocks terminal and restricted facts and refuses to propagate through them; the public `search` and `query` paths resolve hits to canon, and `query` answers only from VERIFIED, evidenced, unrestricted canon or returns a named refusal

Write strategy.value: `ingest` classifies a claim, stores it as `Observed`, refuses it before the gate when it contains a recorded rejected pattern, and admits it through the truth gate — a source is required, model output can never be a world fact, and a fixed confidence floor of 0.05 applies to world facts and interpretations — into `Validated` and the canon; a blocked fact stays `Observed` for the curator. On HTTP an unprivileged caller is pinned to `USER_REPORTED` or `LLM_OUTPUT`, neither of which becomes VERIFIED

Update/delete model.value: `transition_esm` moves a fact along a declared state matrix with a revision compare-and-swap; `erase_fact` physically removes a fact from L1, the graph, evidence and sessions, cascades over `DERIVED_FROM` edges when asked, refuses Ring Zero, and writes a content-free erasure receipt whose content hash no write path reads; the rejected-value record is the separate `immune_memory` table, written by a curator or by the strict ingest path and read before the gate

Scoping model.value: One store per install; a `restricted` bit and a whole-session restriction implement a processing restriction per fact, not a partition by principal. Curator principals carry `fact:` scopes that authorize review writes, not reads

Agent integration.value: A FastAPI service with `/ingest`, `/ask`, `/receipt`, `/verify-receipt`, `/evidence/{fact_id}` and the `/review/*` routes behind one bearer token, a read-only stdio MCP server with six tools that never write, a CLI with ingest, ask, audit, review, erasure, immune and session commands, and source adapters for PDF, EPUB, BibTeX, RDF, Wikidata and YAML

Background processing.value: None on the memory; a curator runtime and a review session are explicit, the L3 outbox drains on the next access, reindexing is a command, and the `consolidate` decay pass has no caller

Trust/provenance model.value: Eight epistemic states and six truth statuses, a source status that names model output as such, a Ring Zero of immutable facts, a restricted bit that wins over every read, an immune memory of rejected claim patterns that blocks a matching claim before the gate, and a `CURATOR_OVERRIDE` status for force-approved facts that strict grounding refuses

Notable strengths.value: A truth gate whose one hard invariant cannot be configured away; canonical grounding as a pure predicate that fails closed on any missing or inconsistent field; a review that refuses to approve into a conflict; an audit chain with a checkpoint against suffix deletion; erasure that cascades over derived facts and is idempotent; a force approval that admits a blocked claim without letting it ground a strict answer

Main risks.value: No scope key inside a store. Erasure and rejection are separate records: an erased claim re-ingested from a source returns under the same value-derived id unless a curator has recorded its pattern, and erasure leaves a recorded pattern as normalized plaintext in the immune table. The immune match is whole-token containment, so a paraphrase passes. The bundled HTTP service maps one bearer token to one curator principal, so a client trusted to ingest is trusted to approve; unauthenticated local mode makes every caller the synthetic admin. `source_status` is a declared label on the Python path. The audit detail is content-free by convention, and approve records the curator's free-text note and reason in it

Memory unit.value: An atomic fact of at most 2,048 bytes with an embedding, optional typed links to other facts, ColumnStore metadata the caller supplies, a learned confidence from feedback and an optional TTL; plus entity hubs carrying extracted attributes and hub-to-hub relations

Retrieval strategy.value: Vector recall re-ordered by learned confidence; recall constrained by typed column predicates; fused recall combining vector hits with graph reach; `why` returning the nodes and edges behind an answer; entity profiles with outgoing and incoming relations; a dated timeline rendering from a caller-named date field

Write strategy.value: `remember` stores a fact with links and metadata and calls no model; `remember_extracted` and an optional asynchronous autograph worker use a local model to derive facts, entity hubs, attributes and relations; the context compiler stores sources and compilation events

Memory unit.value: A fact with a proposition, a status from a closed vocabulary, a writer role and writer principal, grounding evidence, an event time and an optional end of validity, beside episodes carrying task traces and outcomes

Storage backend.value: SQLite, with a local judge model fetched once for the admission gate and an audit table chained by tamper-evidence primitives

Retrieval strategy.value: BM25 and semantic recall whose SQL drops orphaned, quarantined and user-belief rows, with each exception a named opt-in keyword, and an as-of read over event time and supersession

Write strategy.value: Every write passes an admission gate with three tiers — off, fast substring detectors, and full with claim validation against semantic memory — and a local judge, before a fact is persisted

Update/delete model.value: Supersede, quarantine, forget, purge and reset; the destructive ones append an action-only row to the hash-chained mutation table in the same transaction, and a release from quarantine is refused to the principal recorded as the writer

Scoping model.value: A zero-schema topic-prefix convention, user, agent and run segments ahead of the base topic, applied when the caller passes the scope arguments; the gateway keeps one database file per API key

Agent integration.value: A CLI, an MCP server registered as io.github.aureliocpr-ctrl/verimem, an SDK client, a REST gateway, Docker compose files and Claude Code hook and plugin bundles

Background processing.value: Admission cleanup and requalification passes, source-trust demotion and rehabilitation, anomaly detection, and a sleep-consolidation family

Trust/provenance model.value: An admission gate with a local judge, grounding scores on the write receipt, a status vocabulary that withholds, a release from quarantine refused to the writer's own label, and a tamper-evident mutation chain

Notable strengths.value: Two habits, visible everywhere. The reasoning is written beside the code and names what it defends against: the mutation audit is action-only because "storing WHAT was deleted — even as a hash, brute-forceable on short text — inside an immutable chain makes GDPR Art.17 erasure a logical contradiction", and both that decision and the fail-closed one are attributed to two adversarial reviews with the finding ids they answer. And the project publishes its own corrections: the README's opening box names the version an old claim was true of, the function that caused it and the test that records the fix, and ends "[t]he fix shipped; the text did not follow it. Corrected here." The review queue does the same for its own shortfall under a DECLARED LIMIT heading, because "[m]easuring the real thing coarsely beats measuring a precise thing that does not"

Main risks.value: Two conveniences on the agent's MCP surface undo two guarantees. `hippo_quarantine_restore` refuses a release when the requesting label equals the stored writer label, but `hippo_transcript_promote` and `hippo_ingest_conversation` build facts with no writer label at all, both can land quarantined, and the guard needs two non-empty labels to refuse, so the agent releases what it wrote through those doors. Scope is a tool argument the agent may omit, an omitted scope reads every tenant, and the session-start banner applies no scope predicate. Nothing is keyed on a rejected value, so a purged claim can be written again as a new fact. The surface is very large for the guarantee it sells: 129,569 lines across nearly four hundred modules, a 711 MB judge model fetched on first gated write, and at this pin five auto-run surfaces and three build-time execution points

Memory unit.value: An entity keyed by its normalised name, a relationship keyed by its ordered pair of entity ids, and the source chunk each was extracted from, all as JSON bodies in SQLite; beside them glossary terms with a proposed, certified or deprecated status, answer receipts, and a per-agent buffer of the last 50 chat turns in a JSON file

Retrieval strategy.value: Seed entities whose name appears in the question or starts with one of its words longer than three letters, plus entities linked to any matched glossary term that is not deprecated; breadth-first expansion two hops to 25 nodes; every source chunk behind those nodes and edges goes to the model; no vector arm and no ranking

Write strategy.value: Synchronous: a document is chunked, a local model extracts entities and relationships per chunk before the write lock, and the merge, the vocabulary proposals and the audit row commit in one transaction; retrievable at commit. MCP agents write with ingest_document and import_graph

Update/delete model.value: An entity merge folds one entity into another; a whole-graph clear takes a snapshot first; a snapshot restore replaces the graph. No route deletes one entity, one relationship or one document, and a re-ingested correction replaces a description only when it is longer or carries a higher source_type

Scoping model.value: None on graph rows: one SQLite file per deployment, and bearer-token roles gate verbs, not rows. The Studio turn buffer is one list per agent id with no user key, so every caller of an agent shares its replayed history

Agent integration.value: A stdio MCP server whose read, write and admin tiers expose 14, 17 and 18 tools; a FastAPI Studio and REST API; a CLI for serve, mcp, migrate, compile, export and import

Background processing.value: An optional compile timer in the Studio process, and the same pipeline from the CLI: deterministic type and predicate normalisation against certified vocabulary, plus merge, term, rule-violation and orphan suggestions; no model call

Trust/provenance model.value: Facts carry no status. A source_type rank of curated over extracted over inferred decides only which write wins a merge, and the caller supplies it. Glossary terms move proposed, certified, deprecated, and governed mode answers only when a certified term appears in the question

Notable strengths.value: Every graph mutation appends a hash-chained audit row in the same transaction as the change, and destructive operations snapshot the graph first; answers carry receipts with the graph version they read

Main risks.value: No single fact can be deleted; MCP import labels agent writes curated by default; an MCP proposal resets a certified or deprecated term to proposed; one edge per entity pair keeps the longer description; the Studio's auth, role and certify modules are not in the tree

Agent integration.value: A CLI, a scheduled daemon, an MCP server of six read-only tools, a shipped agent skill, a JSON contract for an Obsidian plugin, and a writer for marked blocks in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: Three: a segment (a compacted span of turns with summary and full text), a fact (subject/verb/object with a temporal status, typed links and an author actor), and an actor-card entry (a kind-checked claim about a person citing the fact ids it rests on)

Storage backend.value: SQLite or Postgres with pgvector as the relational store — segments, facts, fact links and embeddings, actor cards, canonical turns, a tag graph, per-tag summaries and a cost ledger — beside Neo4j and FalkorDB fact-link backends, a filesystem backend and Redis for session state

Retrieval strategy.value: Tag-directed with a local embedding tagger on the request path, so recall never waits on a model call, plus eight paging tools the model calls to open a topic, search the verbatim record, query facts or restore a stubbed tool output, and a temporal `remember_when` mode that resolves a date window and can anchor on a state as of a target date

Write strategy.value: Turns are tagged by an LLM after the response, compacted under budget pressure, and superseded when contradicted — with every accept and reject written to `fact_decisions` inside the same transaction

Update/delete model.value: A supersession checker sets `superseded_by` and fact search appends `IS NULL`; an actor-card entry can also expire out of the read path on its own validity window; conversations tombstone in Redis with a day-long TTL, and a conversation delete removes its rows, ledger included

Scoping model.value: `conversation_id` is a predicate on every proxy read and paging tool, with `tenant_id` above it on `conversations` and `audience_conversation_id` on canonical turns; the MCP server's `domain_status` tool and topic resources read every conversation in the store, and the audience check withholds a summary drawing on another audience but never a fact

Agent integration.value: A proxy in front of the provider API, an MCP server, a CLI, a TUI, a Discord community surface and an OpenClaw integration. A typed-judgment layer can route thirteen named decision seams — rerank, query and temporal intent, safety, actor-card admission, tag reuse, tag selection, tag split, tag consolidation, supersession, fact curation, topic selection and summary grounding — to an external service, globally or per seam, in three modes: `legacy` (never called, the default), `shadow` (the legacy answer is used and the external one logged for comparison) and `jev` (the external answer is used, falling back to legacy on any failure). The config comment says it is not tenant-settable in the hosted product

Background processing.value: Tag generation, vocabulary canonicalisation, tag splitting, per-tag summarisation, compaction and a due-queue of actor-card rebuilds

Trust/provenance model.value: None epistemic. `facts.status` is a temporal status — is this still happening — and `actor_card_entries.confidence` is a float nothing filters on — it appears in two `ORDER BY e.kind, e.confidence DESC` clauses and in no `WHERE`, and its only comparison anywhere is a write-time range check that the value is finite and within 0.0–1.0. The discrete verdict is on the *decision*, in the ledger, not on the fact

Notable strengths.value: An append-only decision ledger a database trigger refuses to let anyone edit, recording the before, the after, the proposal and the reason for every accept and every reject

Main risks.value: The ledger has no production reader — `get_fact_decisions` is carried through the store protocol and the composite store, and every caller outside the storage layer is a test — so the same wrong fact can be proposed and refused forever; and the MCP server's `virtualcontext://domains/{tag}` resource returns the stored summaries of every conversation in the store carrying that tag

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A chunk with a typed schema — identity, preference, decision, lesson, gotcha or fact — carrying required and optional structured fields, a retrieval cue, and an event date when its text names one

Storage backend.value: libSQL/SQLite with F32_BLOB embeddings inline in the memories table, a knowledge graph, page maps, a page history, and Markdown pages projected to disk as the user-facing artifact

Retrieval strategy.value: Hybrid retrieval with an optional cross-encoder reranker, community routing, a temporal channel over event dates, and confidence decay applied at search time

Write strategy.value: A rule-based quality gate rejects noise, credentials and non-novel text before embedding; typed schema validation follows. A machine write to a page lands only on the AI's own sentences and stages changes to the person's as proposals

Update/delete model.value: An agent's supersede applies unless the user lowered that agent's trust below full, in which case it is staged with pending_revision. Daemon merges are graded by stability tier, with identity and preference queued for review. Forget is a hard delete

Scoping model.value: A ReadScope enum of Global, Space and Uncategorized compiled into the SQL. An omitted Space resolves to Global, so a standard-profile MCP caller chooses its own scope; only a WENLAN_SPACE pin set by the launcher fixes it

Agent integration.value: An MCP server with standard, query-only and web-write profiles, a CLI, a desktop app, a relay for web AI apps, and an HTTP server, all over one local libSQL file

Background processing.value: Steep (enrichment and page refresh), refinement, citation backfill, claim derivation, re-embedding and decay-driven archival, queued rather than inline

Trust/provenance model.value: A confirmed flag, a pending_revision flag that hides a staged replacement from every read, per-sentence authorship on pages, and a page support state whose hiding branch no production code switches on

Notable strengths.value: A dismissed suggestion cannot be re-proposed, enforced by a unique index on a derived fingerprint; a machine write cannot overwrite a sentence the person wrote, and the accept routes for those proposals refuse any caller that names an agent

Main risks.value: An omitted Space reads every Space. The agent holds accept_refinement, confirm_memory and accept_revision on local MCP, and a revision card carries its full content, so accepting one replaces the person's sentences the sentence gate would have kept. The changelog is a 20-entry FIFO and deleting a page deletes its history

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A fact version: a memory_chunks row with text, entity name, scope path, writer, optional role, event time and a 384-dimension embedding; beside it Graphiti edges distilled from the text, conventions and decisions, short-lived working notes, and briefs

Storage backend.value: Postgres with pgvector and ltree for versions, rules, notes, the change feed, grants, tokens and the audit log; Neo4j through graphiti-core for entities and temporal edges, one group_id per scope path; private blob storage for uploaded files

Retrieval strategy.value: Vector search over rows and passages plus a trigram match on quoted text, fused by reciprocal rank with k 60; Graphiti edge search fusing BM25 and cosine; entity lookup in the graph. Legs run in parallel under a per-tier latency ceiling, the page is filled by provenance tier and cut to a per-tier token budget

Write strategy.value: memory_ingest, app routes, connectors and uploads all call one ingest path. The row is embedded and stored in the request, with its change event and applied audit row in one transaction; distillation and graph extraction run in a queued job that never blocks the reply

Update/delete model.value: A write naming baseVersion replaces that version or is refused as stale; a write without one is refused if the writer has not read the newest version. Two writers inside one second: first stored wins, the loser is kept as superseded. Deletion is an app route for signed-in people; person erasure removes every copy and leaves a digest list

Scoping model.value: An ltree scope tree per org. A grant or token on a scope covers its subtree. check() decides every guarded call, the SQL repeats the containment, the graph is asked by exact partition, and a write into a scope after reading outside its subtree is refused unless declared

Agent integration.value: An MCP server over Streamable HTTP and stdio with thirteen tools, a four-tool coding set, server instructions and Claude Code hooks for change notices and session capture; a Next.js app and REST routes; connectors for GitHub, Drive, Slack, Figma, PostHog and websites

Background processing.value: Inngest jobs for ingest, file extraction, connector sync, graph extraction retry, erasure and org deletion. No pass rewrites the store; no model takes part in an access, ranking or staleness decision

Trust/provenance model.value: Writer tier (person, agent, extraction) orders the page; a claim's status (proposed, untested, failing, tested, verified) is computed per read from who wrote it and what its session's captured test run showed; an agent's decision is a lead until a person confirms it

Notable strengths.value: One audited check before every store call; value-level leak, conflict and deletion tests on real Postgres; lost updates refused server-side even without a base version; a tamper-evident audit; erasure that survives re-sync and restore; documentation that lists its own bypass credentials and limits

Main risks.value: Enforcement is application code, with no row-level security and a graph service that trusts its caller; an agent can make a standing rule by calling it a convention; dispute resolution changes no graph edge; query text sits in an audit table erasure cannot touch; eight public commits from a bot leave the design history unreadable

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: One message row — id, conversation id, parent message id, role, content, metadata, created_at — with ordered `message_parts` beneath it for text and image content

Storage backend.value: One SQLite database. Messages form a tree by parent link; sessions, session events, session inputs, compactions, tool schemas and provider state sit beside it

Retrieval strategy.value: No search of any kind. A selected head is resolved to its root-to-head path by one recursive parent traversal, and that path is the model's context

Write strategy.value: Synchronous inserts on the parent link. A fork adds a branch without copying ancestors; an edit is an in-place UPDATE of the message content

Update/delete model.value: `replace_message` overwrites content and keeps no prior version; `remove_message` splices children onto the removed node's parent and deletes a whole tool-call group together; `truncate_after_message` cuts a subtree

Scoping model.value: Conversation id checked on every message read and write, and the selected-head path is what bounds a request. No user, tenant or agent key — this is one person's machine

Agent integration.value: A local desktop runtime with a CLI, an MCP surface, and per-tool approval; sessions point at a head rather than owning messages

Background processing.value: None running. `save_compaction` exists as a stored primitive and is marked dead code with a note that nothing writes compactions yet

Trust/provenance model.value: None as a field. `sessions.status` carries `WaitingForApproval`, but that gates a tool call rather than the standing of a memory

Notable strengths.value: Shared-node tree so a branch costs one row; message mutation refused while a session depends on it; a compaction checkpoint deleted in the same transaction as the edit that invalidates it; deleting any part of a tool-call group deletes the group

Main risks.value: An edit is a destructive UPDATE with no prior version anywhere, so the product's own promise holds for forking and not for editing; no audit record of message mutations; no search, so recall is whatever the selected path contains

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: An episodic interaction row (a completed turn) in episodic.db, and the semantic fact-summary row it is later rolled up into in semantic.db, each with an optional FAISS vector id

Storage backend.value: One local file set — episodic.db, semantic.db, episodic.faiss.index, semantic.faiss.index, watermark_state.json and embedding_space.json — under the OS app-data directory, shared by every user_id on the machine; the backend only computes embeddings and summaries

Retrieval strategy.value: FAISS inner-product search per memory type, filtered by user_id, returning nothing (non-fatally) when embeddings are unavailable

Write strategy.value: The SDK requests an embedding from the backend and hands it to the local store; a write with no embedding still lands in SQLite with a NULL vector id and is backfilled later

Update/delete model.value: Hard delete per row; episodic and semantic delete independently with no cross-cascade, and a partial delete drops the row's vector mapping but leaves the FAISS vector in place until the index empties

Scoping model.value: A user_id column indexed on the memories table, a SQL predicate on the row-addressed reads and a Python post-filter on the vector read; conversation rows keyed (user_id, conversation_id)

Agent integration.value: A local-runtime Python memory boundary behind JSON-RPC, with the desktop app as the client; embeddings and summaries fetched from a FastAPI backend over HTTP

Background processing.value: A summarizer that rolls episodic interactions into semantic summaries on a startup pass and a fixed interval, resuming from a watermark

Trust/provenance model.value: No status on a row. Low-value material is rejected at summarization time, not marked; there is no verified, rejected or confidence field

Notable strengths.value: Every FAISS index is stamped with the embedding space that built it, and a space change clears and rebuilds rather than silently comparing incompatible vectors

Main risks.value: Partial deletes leave orphaned vectors in the FAISS file until the type empties, and there is no episodic-to-semantic delete cascade, so a summary outlives the interactions it was derived from
