project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A Markdown note under a git-tracked memory root, its title the identity and its directory only filing, with Basic-Memory-style `- [category] text` observation lines parsed out of the body

Storage backend.value: Markdown files as the sole truth; SQLite (metadata, FTS5 trigram, collisions, guard events, audit dispositions and an execution timeline) and LanceDB vectors are derived indexes under `.index/`, rebuildable and untracked

Retrieval strategy.value: FTS5 trigram and vector search fused by RRF, filtered to the caller's identity, with archived notes dropped for MCP clients, settled curator proposals dropped for every caller, and a ⚠ warning attached to any hit that has an open collision

Write strategy.value: `memory_write(title, content, force, force_confirm)` creates only: an existing path is refused, a near-duplicate title is refused unless forced, and the force is itself rate-limited

Update/delete model.value: `memory_edit` on a unique anchor, `memory_edit_section` by heading, move, archive and unarchive, and an explicit delete. Every one commits to git, so the memory repository is always clean and any deletion is recoverable

Scoping model.value: A separate store root and MCP mount per user; inside it, a private zone per agent and device selected by a token in the request header and applied by one predicate on every MCP read

Agent integration.value: One streamable-HTTP server that any MCP client joins by URL with nothing installed locally, plus a bundled Vue web console at `/ui/` behind an optional password

Background processing.value: A weekly LLM curator on a systemd timer that writes a proposal report, and an incremental observation-collision detector on the write path

Trust/provenance model.value: A deterministic duplicate guard with a counted override, collision warnings only a person can dismiss, per-call usage logging, and git history over every mutation

Notable strengths.value: The duplicate guard anticipates the evasion. `normalize_title` strips trailing dates, compact MMDD and YYYYMMDD stamps, `-2`-style counters, `v1`, `更新` and `（新）` before comparing, so the rename that would slip a second copy past a naive check is exactly what it collapses, and the refusal names the near-matches with their scores and says to edit instead. The override ladder makes the bypass possible, visible and self-limiting: `force=true` is counted in `guard_events`, and once forced writes in the last 24 hours cross a configured threshold a second flag becomes mandatory. A person's verdict on a collision is stored, kept through edits, moves and rebuilds, and read by every search, and the agent's tools cannot set it. Identity scoping is one predicate shared by every MCP read rather than a filter copied into each

Main risks.value: No record covers every mutation. Git commits do, and git history is not an audit record this atlas credits, because it lives outside the store and anyone with the directory can rewrite it. `guard_events` holds refusals and forced bypasses only, and `call_log` trims itself to the newest 20,000 rows and is not written by the console's archive, tag or disposition routes. The identity token is a self-asserted header, and `memory_audit` prints other identities' private paths with 60-character excerpts. The agent can declare a curator proposal settled by writing a marker, after which every item a person did not dismiss is recorded as executed. The duplicate guard is keyed on title similarity only, so the same fact under two genuinely different titles is two memories. The console and the MCP endpoint have no authentication by default; the stated boundary is the home LAN

The vault purge is the most careful erasure in the tree: it overwrites a leaked audit line in the memories table and in the oplog payload that recorded it, then runs VACUUM and a WAL truncate because an UPDATE frees a page without erasing it. The recall tool's audit-line filter carries a committed must-not-appear case with a positive control on a real engine

LLM consolidation's tombstone sets `half_life = 1.0` on every row with that text and leaves the status active, and the pinned engine ranks on a constant half-life, so a superseded memory stays recallable beside its replacement. Memory unit.value: A memory row keyed by UUIDv7 with a type of episodic, semantic, procedural or emotional, an embedding, decay parameters, a namespace, certainty, domain, source, an event-time range, and typed write-resolution provenance

Storage backend.value: One SQLite database per store, with HNSW vectors, an oplog, `record_revisions`, `record_links`, idempotency claims, and a cognition layer of propositions, variables, state assertions and rule edges

Retrieval strategy.value: Hybrid vector and lexical recall with decay-weighted scoring, graph expansion, thread reconstruction, and `recall_as_of` for point-in-time reads

Write strategy.value: `remember` with actor-scoped idempotency keys and a confidence-basis write gate; `correct` mutates in place while archiving the prior state; `link` records supersession as an edge

Update/delete model.value: Correction archives `prior_text`, `prior_metadata`, `prior_importance` and `prior_valence` into `record_revisions` with an `applied_at`; supersession is an edge in `record_links`; forgetting sets `consolidation_status = 'tombstoned'` with a caller-supplied `tombstone_reason` and removes the row from the recall path

Scoping model.value: A `namespace` column with a `NOT NULL DEFAULT 'default'`, appended as `AND m.namespace = ?` on recall — but the engine's own signature is `namespace: Option<&str>`, so a caller that passes `None` gets no predicate

Agent integration.value: An embeddable Rust library with Python, WASM and TUI crates; wrapped by yantrikdb-server for HTTP and HA, and embedded in process by the YantrikDB Hermes plugin

Background processing.value: Decay sweeps over stored half-lives, autonomous consolidation into semantic memories, contradiction detection, a reembed pipeline with staging columns and generation stamps, and a materializer draining the oplog

Trust/provenance model.value: Consolidation and synthesis statuses as read predicates, a confidence-basis justification tier in a write-gate consistency matrix, actor-scoped idempotency claims, an append-only oplog, HLC ordering, and encryption at rest with a documented erasure step

Notable strengths.value: The bitemporal module states its own limits in its header rather than leaving them to be discovered: ranking is present-day, forgotten records stay forgotten, and the as-of pool runs with `skip_reinforce` because "archaeology must not masquerade as usage". A superseding edge only hides a record from an as-of read if the edge already existed at that instant. The audit op is written inside the caller's transaction rather than beside it. The reembed path stages new vectors in separate columns with a generation stamp because in-place mutation "would dim-mismatch concurrent recalls". An index comment carries a signed honesty note that the index does not satisfy its query's ORDER BY and that SQLite may sort the full eligible set

Main risks.value: Scope is offered rather than enforced: `recall` takes `namespace: Option<&str>` and emits the predicate only when a namespace is supplied, so the boundary is the wrapper's to keep, not the engine's — which is why the mark sits on the Hermes plugin and not here. The v26 write-resolution columns — `resolution_kind`, `dismissal_reason`, `prior_rid`, `confidence_at_write` — record the epistemic operation chosen at write time and no read path consults them to refuse a re-assertion; the schema comment frames them as a foundation for a future API. `synthesis_granularity` and `synthesis_state` carry CHECK constraints while `consolidation_status`, `type`, `storage_tier` and `resolution_kind` do not, so those four accept any string. The schema is `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` with no migration constants, so a column added to the constant reaches an existing database only through the separate `ensureColumn`-style paths

Storage backend.value: Postgres, SQLite or DuckDB behind one connection layer, with a graph and embeddings

Retrieval strategy.value: 0.5 × normalised BM25 + 0.5 × cosine plus a +0.25 temporal boost, then graph BFS to depth 2

Write strategy.value: Semantic dedup by similarity band — reinforce, replace on contradiction, merge, or insert

Update/delete model.value: `memory_history` logs old content before an update; Ebbinghaus decay drives a 24-hour prune at strength 0.05, and ranking ignores it

Scoping model.value: user_id is a WHERE clause on retrieval, compaction and the audit read

Agent integration.value: An MCP server, hook templates, a FastAPI service, a Cloudflare worker, Docker

Background processing.value: Compaction, decay, temporal analysis, a 24-hour prune, recall reinforcement

Trust/provenance model.value: importance and recall_count as floats; nothing discrete and nothing epistemic

Notable strengths.value: A hash-chained audit that logs ids and metadata but never memory content or query text

Main risks.value: The dedup `replace` branch overwrites without a `memory_history` row, nothing reads the log back, and `BENCHMARKS.md` publishes ranking weights the service does not use

The design decision worth the mark is stated in the module header: it deliberately logs *no raw memory content or query text*, 'so the audit log itself isn't a data-leak vector', which is the opposite of the usual failure where the audit trail becomes a second uncontrolled copy of the data | nothing reads the chain back to verify it — there is no verify function, only `get_events` for listing — and `prune_expired` drops rows past a retention window the app calls at startup, so the chain is prunable from its tail. Memory unit.value: A message pair — one user turn and one character turn — reduced to a list of word ids with the common words pruned out

Storage backend.value: Three JSON files under `RAG_Database/`: a word table with counts and values, per-pair word ids and scores, and the raw text

Retrieval strategy.value: Six highest-value query words scored against every stored pair by shared-word count, with a length penalty; the best pair and its two neighbours are injected

Write strategy.value: Every message pair is tokenised into the word table after it is sent; no model is involved at any point

Update/delete model.value: An undo pops the word-id rows and documents that it does not uncount the words; a manual recalculate rebuilds everything

Scoping model.value: None. One global corpus per installation

Agent integration.value: The companion app's own prompt builder; the result is injected as a `[System M]` block

Background processing.value: A thread recomputes word values every 120 seconds, plus a roughly one-in-three chance of recomputing on any given turn

Trust/provenance model.value: None. Every stored pair is equally eligible and nothing records where it came from

Notable strengths.value: Inverse document frequency, length normalisation and a cap on the character's own words steering retrieval — all derived from scratch

Main risks.value: A three-message window score is computed and never used; the licence is not open source, and one of its three conditions constrains what a memory system may store

Memory unit.value: One Markdown file per fact, carrying name, description and metadata.type frontmatter, beside a MEMORY.md index that is explicitly not a memory

Memory unit.value: A text row in one of four tables: learned_facts with a confidence float and FSRS scheduling fields, episodic_memories with a context string and emotional weight, procedural_memories with steps and a success rate, core_memory_blocks keyed by a label. No status, no validity interval

Storage backend.value: SQLite through better-sqlite3 with JSON-array embeddings and a cosine UDF, or Postgres with pgvector and HNSW indexes; working and session memory are in process only

Retrieval strategy.value: Per layer: pgvector-style cosine distance when an EmbeddingProvider is configured, otherwise an IDF-weighted token overlap over the 500 newest rows with a recency fallback at score 0. Every core block is added to every recall at a fixed 0.5 or 0.8. Results merged by raw score, Jaccard-deduplicated, cut to the limit

Write strategy.value: Explicit store call from MCP, the Vercel AI SDK middleware or the library. Routing by regex for procedures, an emotion lexicon above 0.5 for episodes, confidence above 0.9 for core blocks, otherwise a fact. Every store is an INSERT except core blocks, which upsert on a label cut from the first 50 characters

Update/delete model.value: Core blocks overwrite by label. Layer classes expose delete by id, and the coordinator, MCP server and middleware expose none. Nothing expires; consolidate reports pruned as a constant 0

Scoping model.value: None on the recall path. Episodes store a context string, and only EpisodicMemory.getRecent filters on it, with no caller passing one. Facts drop the context. Postgres can run each adapter under its own search_path, a physical partition

Agent integration.value: MCP server over stdio with four tools (store, recall, consolidate, health); Vercel AI SDK middleware that recalls on the last user message, prepends results as a system message and stores each user turn; examples for LangChain, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, Mastra and Claude

Background processing.value: None scheduled. consolidate() is a tool call that promotes every episode above 0.5 emotional weight among the latest 100 to a new fact, optionally summarised by an LLM, and decays the in-process working memory

Trust/provenance model.value: None. A confidence float filters recall only when the caller passes minConfidence; core blocks report confidence 1.0 regardless of source

Notable strengths.value: Small, readable coordinator; a lexical fallback that says when nothing matched by scoring 0; a SQLite adapter that runs the same vector SQL through a cosine UDF; a CI step that re-runs the paper's ablation and diffs every point estimate against the published JSON; a README that retracted its own benchmark claim with the arithmetic

Main risks.value: No forget or update verb on any agent surface; consolidate re-promotes the same episodes on every call; core blocks enter every recall whatever the query; includeContext and taskType do nothing because no writer sets encodingContext; the cross-context layer reads a table nothing writes and pairs each entity with itself; the paper's ablation measures hand-set multipliers in a simulation, not the shipped code

Memory unit.value: An episode submitted to a hosted graph, and the typed fact edge it later becomes — carrying valid_at and invalid_at for world time and created_at and expired_at for the graph's own

Main risks.value: The mechanism is a closed hosted service, and an episode submitted without created_at is silently dated to ingestion time

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A section of operator-written Markdown on one side — categories, durable summaries and cross-topic pointers — and whatever mem0 stores for the same text on the other

Storage backend.value: Two layers: Markdown files the operator maintains, and a local Chroma store written through mem0, with Ollama supplying embeddings

Retrieval strategy.value: Delegated to mem0. The package supplies a CLI and a local server, and its own citation abstract states that wiring the query into model calls remains an agent-host step

Write strategy.value: Seeding, not capture: Markdown is collected by extension, split at level-two headings and capped at 2,000 characters, then pushed into the store

Update/delete model.value: None modelled. A correction means editing the Markdown and re-seeding, and nothing reconciles the store against a changed source, so a deleted paragraph's chunk stays retrievable until the store is rebuilt

Scoping model.value: One key, and not spelled `scope` — every read and write forwards a `user_id` into mem0, and `--user-id` defaults to the literal `agent`, collapsing the per-user partition into one shared bucket unless the operator sets it

Agent integration.value: A CLI, a local background server, a skill directory and an `AGENTS.md`, plus a TypeScript hook shipped as example source rather than as a package

Background processing.value: A background server whose state record the CLI detects and removes when stale or invalid, without touching any process

Trust/provenance model.value: None. No status, no confidence and no validity window; the Markdown layer is trusted because the operator wrote it

Notable strengths.value: The citation abstract states which half the adopter still has to build — that wiring the query into model calls remains an agent-host step — which is a disclosure most READMEs avoid; the heading splitter emits a section only when the buffer holds a non-heading line, removing the empty-section bug common to such splitters; a stale server-state record is removed without touching any process; and a thirty-line test asserts the documentation still matches the code

Main risks.value: Retrieval is `mem0ai>=0.1.0` — a floating lower bound on a 0.1 release, and the dependency is the memory rather than a detail of it; nothing detects drift between the Markdown source and the seeded copy, so an edited or deleted paragraph stays retrievable until a rebuild; and the package holds no status, scope or lifecycle of its own, so every epistemic decision belongs to the layer beneath or to the host above

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A lesson card: a title of at most 96 bytes, a recommendation of at most 640, a repository or graph-node scope with its match associations, and evidence pointers; id and revision, no timestamp

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file outside every checkout, shared by all repositories on the machine or Docker target: a records table, a generation counter and initialization receipts. Hosts may install another backend through a trait; none is in the tree

Retrieval strategy.value: Exact-term inverted indexes over a snapshot frozen at run start: file 1000, containing folder 800, whole identifier 700, complete keyword group 500; strongest match per card, ties by id. Graph cards are selected by node id. No model, embedding or network call

Write strategy.value: After the main graph settles, four model specialists propose and maintain lessons; the host validates citations against the run ledger and current files, derives ids, stamps the checkout commit and publishes one compare-and-swap transaction

Update/delete model.value: Maintenance keeps, adapts, retires or defers every card it was given. Adapt and retire need the card's recorded commit to be an ancestor of a clean HEAD. Retirement nulls the body and keeps id and revision. No person-facing edit or delete verb

Scoping model.value: Repository key hashed from the checkout's forge identity, or authored graph hash plus node id with an optional repository qualifier; applied in the snapshot SQL and rechecked per lesson

Agent integration.value: PreToolUse hooks for Claude Code and Codex, an RPC callback for Copilot, a session entry for Pi, a stored session message for OpenCode and a plugin notice on the tool message for Hermes, all over a loopback broker with a per-invocation token; graph cards join the private provider prompt; one CLI verb for backfill

Background processing.value: The postmortem runs inside the finishing run under a shared deadline of at most ten minutes; nothing is scheduled between runs

Trust/provenance model.value: No state on a lesson. Admission is a host check that a proposal cites an observed completion or tool receipt of its own node and an existing tracked file; cards are injected as guidance subordinate to authored instructions

Notable strengths.value: Workers hold no write path; proposals are validated against host-recorded evidence; revisions with whole-snapshot compare-and-swap; delivery receipts decide what maintenance may touch; a model cannot forge the source commit; bounded everything; dense tests

Main risks.value: A lesson admitted from a dirty checkout can never be adapted or retired; one rediscovered retired id discards the run's whole publication; no person can list, edit or delete a lesson; replaced text is not kept; store-wide caps are shared by all repositories

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A Markdown file — the global `MEMORY.md`, a per-project `SCRATCHPAD.md`, project notes, and a daily log per date

Storage backend.value: Plain files on disk under a store root, with project-scoped subdirectories and `YYYY-MM-DD.md` daily logs

Retrieval strategy.value: An injected block of open scratchpad items, the two newest non-empty daily logs and `MEMORY.md` under a 32 KB budget; `memory_read` by source; `memory_search` with literal case-insensitive terms, files ranked `MEMORY.md` first and then by distinct terms matched

Write strategy.value: `memory_write` and `memory_edit` as agent tools behind the permission checker; the pre-compaction flush appends the model-written summary to today's log outside it; `/memory` for the operator

Update/delete model.value: An edit without `old_str` deletes a whole note and is refused for other targets; `long_term` and `scratchpad` overwrites and edits, and note deletions, copy the file to a single `.bak` first; note overwrites and daily or note edits take no backup; the TUI's `/memory editor` empties `MEMORY.md` before opening it

Scoping model.value: A project slug derived from the working directory's full path scopes scratchpad, notes and daily logs by directory; `MEMORY.md` is deliberately global and shared across projects

Agent integration.value: Four tools when built with the memory feature, a read-only pair for subagents, system-prompt guidance, and a `/memory` command in the TUI and the headless engine

Background processing.value: No worker. Every compaction appends its summary to today's daily log: /compact on demand, and automatic compaction when compact_enabled is set, off by default

Trust/provenance model.value: None. A line is in a file or it is not; the injected block is wrapped as reference-only

Notable strengths.value: Atomic write-then-rename, a `.bak` whose extension keeps it out of listing and search, truncation-with-warning on oversized writes, whitespace-normalised dedup on long-term appends, and a context budget that truncates by priority with markers

Main risks.value: The TUI's `/memory editor` empties the global `MEMORY.md` with no backup; backups are one version deep and skip note overwrites and daily or note edits; the default permission mode allows all four tools; appends race across sessions; a `MEMORY.md` over 128 KB drops out of injection silently

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: A MemoryNote row: raw text, source type and ref, regex entities, keywords, a 768-dim fastembed vector, supersession links, domain, tier, confidence, TLP and STIX confidence

Storage backend.value: One SQLite file under ~/.amem holding notes, knowledge-graph nodes and edges, an entity index and an enrichment job ledger; a LanceDB table per domain for vectors; rotating JSON logs and daily telemetry JSONL

Retrieval strategy.value: Intent-weighted fusion of LanceDB vector hits and a two-hop graph walk from regex query entities, plus entity-index lookups and causal edges, then a cross-encoder over the top 8; recall() drops superseded and expired notes

Write strategy.value: remember() runs governance, an injection guard and an audit-mode anomaly gate, then stores the text with regex entities and heuristic edges; with evolve=true, the MCP default, it stores up to five LLM-extracted facts instead

Update/delete model.value: A later note sharing one CVE, tool, actor, person or location value supersedes the older; the LLM updater supersedes on UPDATE or DELETE; a background evolver rewrites neighbours' text; no delete route

Scoping model.value: A caller-chosen domain filters the vector arm only; one store per data directory; the web API's tenant hook returns the one default manager, and multi-tenancy is in an enterprise package outside the tree

Agent integration.value: Python MemoryManager, a seven-tool stdio MCP server, a FastAPI web UI behind an API-key guard, LangChain and CrewAI adapters, Sigma and YARA ingest CLIs

Background processing.value: One in-process thread drains a 500-job queue of causal-triple extraction, LLM NER and neighbour evolution; a consolidation thread on semantic shift; an hourly LanceDB version cleanup per table

Trust/provenance model.value: Every constructed note is tier A with confidence 1.0; the anomaly gate audits by default and its quarantine file has no reader; the injection guard filters stored text only in get_context output

Notable strengths.value: A calibrated write-time anomaly gate with block and quarantine modes, an injection guard on every LLM prompt builder, a fan-out gate that keeps speaker names out of graph recall, and a bounded rerank head

Main risks.value: Supersession on a single shared entity value, which the MCP and web recall then ignore; a 30-day expiry every note inherits; evolved text never re-indexed in LanceDB; mutation events only in a rotating log

project_benchmark_results.note: Profile descriptions and Atlas capability evidence are not benchmark results.

Memory unit.value: An event row: agent, type, a JSON data payload, an optional parent event, session, metadata carrying importance and supersedes, timestamp, sequence number, a SHA-256 checksum and a per-agent chain hash

Storage backend.value: Postgres as the source of truth for events, tombstones, receipts and chain heads, with a GIN full-text index; optional Qdrant for vectors when embeddings are on; Redis for caches and rate limits; one all-in-one container or a compose stack

Retrieval strategy.value: context_for packs the ten newest events, then keyword or vector hits weighted by relevance, importance and a 30-day recency half-life, into a 2,000-token block; search fuses Postgres full-text and Qdrant by RRF; superseded events are dropped after retrieval

Write strategy.value: The application, framework callbacks or the MCP log_event tool post events; each insert is synchronous with its checksum and chain link; secret-named keys are redacted before storage; no extraction or model call

Update/delete model.value: A new event naming an old one in supersedes, or a later STATE_SET or STATE_DELETE of every key, hides the old event from memory without deleting it; forget deletes events whose top-level data key equals a string; retention deletes by age; both leave sealed tombstones

Scoping model.value: tenant_id from the credential on every query; agent_id bound to the API key on first use and enforced on reads and writes; self-hosted runs one agent per install

Agent integration.value: REST API, Python and TypeScript SDKs, LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI and LiveKit loggers, a stdio MCP server with log, search, context, why, time-travel and forget tools, a CLI and a Next.js dashboard

Background processing.value: An embedding worker polling every two seconds for pending events, with retries and a dead state; an hourly retention purge inside the API process when a period is set; no consolidation or summarisation pass

Trust/provenance model.value: Integrity, not belief: a checksum and per-agent hash chain prove the record unchanged, and erasures are sealed; nothing marks an event candidate or verified, and every logged event is served

Notable strengths.value: Credential-derived scope on every read; deletions that leave a verifiable trace without keeping content; tamper tests that inject the fault through raw SQL; vectors deleted before rows under the embed worker's lock

Main risks.value: A supersedes link set through raw metadata skips the same-agent check and can hide any event in the tenant; import keeps old ids in supersedes, so superseded facts return after a move; context values are cut to 80 characters; telemetry defaults on
